knowledge_statements.title: Sequential Quadratic Programming
knowledge_statements.scope_note: Canonical line-search SQP iteration for smooth finite-dimensional nonlinear programs with equality and inequality constraints; no finite-termination or convergence claim is made.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex:
Consider \(\min_{x\in\mathbb R^n} f(x)\) subject to \(h(x)=0\) and \(g(x)\ge 0\), with Lagrangian \(\mathcal L(x,y,z)=f(x)+y^\top h(x)-z^\top g(x)\). Define
\[R(x,y,z)=\max\!\left\{\|\nabla_x\mathcal L(x,y,z)\|_\infty,\ \|h(x)\|_\infty,\ \|[-g(x)]_+\|_\infty,\ \|[-z]_+\|_\infty,\ \|z\odot g(x)\|_\infty\right\},\]
where \([\cdot]_+\) is the componentwise positive part and \(\odot\) denotes componentwise multiplication. Given \((x_0,y_0,z_0)\), \(\varepsilon>0\), and a symmetric matrix \(B_0\), perform the following iteration for \(k=0,1,\ldots\). If \(R(x_k,y_k,z_k)\le\varepsilon\), return \((x_k,y_k,z_k)\). Otherwise compute a primal-dual solution \((d_k,\widehat y_k,\widehat z_k)\), with \(\widehat z_k\ge0\), of
\[\min_{d\in\mathbb R^n}\ \nabla f(x_k)^\top d+\tfrac12 d^\top B_kd\quad\text{subject to}\quad h(x_k)+\nabla h(x_k)^\top d=0,\quad g(x_k)+\nabla g(x_k)^\top d\ge0.\]
Choose an accepted step length \(\alpha_k\in(0,1]\) using the prescribed merit-function or filter line search, set \(x_{k+1}=x_k+\alpha_kd_k\), \((y_{k+1},z_{k+1})=(\widehat y_k,\widehat z_k)\), construct a symmetric Hessian approximation \(B_{k+1}\), and continue.
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: At each nonterminal iteration, this line-search SQP method solves a quadratic objective model subject to first-order constraint linearizations, globalizes the primal step with a merit-function or filter line search, updates the multiplier and Hessian estimates, and continues. If it terminates, its returned primal-dual iterate has KKT residual at most the prescribed tolerance.
assumptions_latex: \(f:\mathbb R^n\to\mathbb R\), \(h:\mathbb R^n\to\mathbb R^p\), and \(g:\mathbb R^n\to\mathbb R^q\) are twice continuously differentiable.
At every nonterminal iteration, the displayed quadratic subproblem has a computed primal-dual solution.
At every nonterminal iteration, the prescribed globalization procedure returns an accepted step length \(\alpha_k\in(0,1]\).
knowledge_statements.conclusion_latex: If the algorithm terminates at iteration \(k\), then its returned iterate satisfies \(R(x_k,y_k,z_k)\le\varepsilon\); every direction computed before termination is a primal solution of the displayed quadratic subproblem.

notation.meaning: Lagrangian f(x)+y^T h(x)-z^T g(x), where y and z are equality- and inequality-constraint multipliers
symmetric approximation to the Hessian of the Lagrangian at iteration k
maximum of the infinity norms of the stationarity, equality-feasibility, inequality-feasibility, dual-feasibility, and complementarity residuals
componentwise positive part of a vector v

knowledge_statements.slot_contract: State the canonical mathematical definition of the source node, with its domain, quantifiers, notation, and a precise source locator.
knowledge_statements.ambient_context_latex: Let \(f:\mathbb R^n\to\mathbb R\), \(c:\mathbb R^n\to\mathbb R^{m_e}\), and \(g:\mathbb R^n\to\mathbb R^{m_i}\) be twice continuously differentiable, and consider \(\min f(x)\) subject to \(c(x)=0\) and \(g(x)\leq0\). Write \(L(x,\lambda,\mu)=f(x)+\lambda^Tc(x)+\mu^Tg(x)\).
knowledge_statements.scope_note: Finite-dimensional, smooth, local SQP. The definition classifies foundational interpretations, constraint regimes, and classical local lineages; globalization and subproblem-solver taxonomies are outside this slot.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex: An SQP foundational lineage is a class of iterations whose local step \(s_k\) and multiplier estimate \((\lambda_{k+1},\mu_{k+1})\) satisfy the KKT conditions of a quadratic program of the form \[\min_s\ \nabla f(x_k)^Ts+\tfrac12s^TB_ks\quad\text{subject to}\quad c(x_k)+J_c(x_k)s=0,\quad g(x_k)+J_g(x_k)s\leq0,\] followed locally by \(x_{k+1}=x_k+s_k\), where \(B_k\) is the exact Lagrangian Hessian or a symmetric approximation. The foundations taxonomy assigns such a class the triple \((\mathcal I,\mathcal R,\mathcal L)\): \(\mathcal I\) records its Newton interpretation (coupled KKT, Lagrange-Newton, or reduced-space Newton), \(\mathcal R\) records its constraint regime (equality, mixed equality-inequality, or explicit bounds), and \(\mathcal L\) records a historically identified local construction distinguished by its curvature update, activity rule, or correction mechanism.
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: For a smooth finite-dimensional nonlinear program, an SQP foundational lineage is a class of iterations that computes its step and new multipliers from the KKT system of a quadratic objective model with affine constraint models. Its defining classification is the triple \((\mathcal I,\mathcal R,\mathcal L)\), recording the Newton interpretation, constraint regime, and historically identified local construction. The curvature matrix \(B_k\) may be the exact Lagrangian Hessian or a symmetric approximation, but the defining local model retains the objective gradient and first-order constraint linearizations.
assumptions_latex: \(f,c,g\) are \(C^2\) on an open neighborhood of the iterates.
Each member of the classified family computes at least one local quadratic-programming step from first-order constraint models.
For an inequality-constrained member, the QP multipliers satisfy the sign and complementarity conditions associated with its affine inequalities.
knowledge_statements.conclusion_latex: \(\mathfrak S_{\mathrm{foundation}}=\{\text{local SQP classes indexed by }(\mathcal I,\mathcal R,\mathcal L)\}\), with every member represented by the displayed SQP quadratic program.
equivalent_formulations_latex: For equality constraints, the QP KKT equations are a Newton or Newton-like linear system for \((\nabla_xL(x,\lambda),c(x))=0\).
When the equality Jacobian has full row rank, the same step admits a range-space/null-space decomposition, giving a reduced-space representative of \(\mathcal I\).
special_cases_latex: If \(m_i=0\), then \(\mathcal R\) is the equality-constrained regime.
If \(m_e=0\) and every inequality is a variable bound, then \(\mathcal R\) is the explicit-bound interface regime.
immediate_consequences_latex: The taxonomy does not identify two methods merely because they solve the same nonlinear program; their Newton representation, constraint treatment, or defining local mechanism may differ.
Exact-Hessian and quasi-Newton members share the same affine constraint model while differing in the choice of \(B_k\).
boundary_notes: This is a mathematical organization of local SQP foundations, not a claim that the three labels form a unique historical classification.
Merit functions, filters, trust regions, restoration phases, and numerical QP architectures require separate classifications.

notation.meaning: Symmetric exact or approximate Hessian used in the quadratic objective model.

knowledge_statements.statement_title: Newton Interpretation of an Equality-Constrained SQP Step
knowledge_statements.ambient_context_latex: Consider \(\min_{x\in\mathbb R^n}f(x)\) subject to \(c(x)=0\), with \(f,c\in C^2\), \(A(x)=J_c(x)\), and \(L(x,\lambda)=f(x)+\lambda^Tc(x)\). Define the KKT residual \(F(x,\lambda)=(\nabla_xL(x,\lambda),c(x))\).
knowledge_statements.scope_note: Smooth equality-constrained SQP with an exact Lagrangian Hessian. Approximate-Hessian schemes are Newton-like variants rather than exact Newton steps.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex:
The Newton interpretation of SQP is the identification of a Newton correction \((s_k,\delta\lambda_k)\) for \(F(x,\lambda)=0\), \[ egin{pmatrix}H_k&A_k^T\A_k&0\end{pmatrix} egin{pmatrix}s_k\\delta\lambda_k\end{pmatrix}=- egin{pmatrix}
abla_xL(x_k,\lambda_k)\c(x_k)\end{pmatrix},\qquad H_k=
abla_{xx}^2L(x_k,\lambda_k),\] with the KKT point of the equality-constrained quadratic program \[\min_s\ 
abla f(x_k)^Ts+	frac12s^TH_ks\quad	ext{subject to}\quad c(x_k)+A_ks=0.\] With \(\lambda_{k+1}=\lambda_k+\delta\lambda_k\), the QP stationarity equation is \(H_ks_k+
abla f(x_k)+A_k^T\lambda_{k+1}=0\). Thus Newton on the nonlinear KKT residual, Lagrangian quadratic modeling with affine constraints, and the QP KKT system are representations of the same local correction whenever the bordered matrix is nonsingular.
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: For a smooth equality-constrained problem, the Newton interpretation of SQP identifies the Newton correction for the nonlinear KKT equations with the primal step and multiplier update obtained from the KKT conditions of an equality-constrained quadratic program. The quadratic objective uses the gradient of \(f\) and the Hessian of the Lagrangian, while the constraint is the first-order affine model of \(c(x_k+s)=0\). The equivalence is defined only when sign conventions for the multipliers are used consistently.
assumptions_latex: \(f\) and every component of \(c\) are twice continuously differentiable near \(x_k\).
\(H_k=\nabla_{xx}^2L(x_k,\lambda_k)\) and \(A_k=J_c(x_k)\).
The bordered KKT matrix \(\begin{pmatrix}H_k&A_k^T\\A_k&0\end{pmatrix}\) is nonsingular when a unique correction is asserted.
knowledge_statements.conclusion_latex: The Newton correction for \(F(x,\lambda)=0\) and the primal-dual KKT solution of the displayed SQP subproblem define the same \((s_k,\lambda_{k+1})\).
equivalent_formulations_latex: The Newton equations may be written with \(\delta\lambda_k\) or directly with the next QP multiplier \(\lambda_{k+1}\).
Replacing \(H_k\) by a symmetric approximation defines a Newton-like SQP interpretation with the same affine constraint equation.
special_cases_latex: If \(c(x_k)=0\), then \(s_k\) lies in \(\ker A_k\).
If \(m_e=0\), the system reduces to the unconstrained Newton equation \(H_ks_k=-\nabla f(x_k)\).
immediate_consequences_latex: The QP multiplier is naturally a new estimate of the nonlinear-program multiplier.
The SQP model contains constraint curvature through \(\nabla_{xx}^2L\), although its explicit constraint model is affine.
boundary_notes: Inequality KKT systems require activity, complementarity, or another nonsmooth reformulation and are not covered by this equality-only definition.
Nonsingularity is not guaranteed solely by differentiability.

knowledge_statements.title: Primal-Dual KKT Newton View
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: An equality-constrained SQP KKT point is a coupled Newton or quasi-Newton correction for primal feasibility and Lagrangian stationarity.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex:
For the problem \(\min_{x\in\mathbb R^n} f(x)\) subject to \(c(x)=0\), where \(c:\mathbb R^n\to\mathbb R^m\), define \(L(x,\lambda)=f(x)+\lambda^\top c(x)\) and the row-oriented Jacobian \(J(x)=Dc(x)\in\mathbb R^{m\times n}\). At a primal-dual iterate \((x,\lambda)\), an SQP correction \((p,\delta\lambda)\) satisfies
\[
\begin{bmatrix}B&J(x)^\top\\J(x)&0\end{bmatrix}
\begin{bmatrix}p\\\delta\lambda\end{bmatrix}
=-\begin{bmatrix}\nabla_xL(x,\lambda)\\c(x)\end{bmatrix}.
\]
This is Newton's linearized KKT system when \(B=\nabla_{xx}^2L(x,\lambda)\), and a quasi-Newton KKT system when \(B\) approximates that Hessian. Equivalently, \((p,\lambda+\delta\lambda)\) is the KKT point of the equality-constrained quadratic model with objective \(\nabla f(x)^\top p+\tfrac12p^\top Bp\) and constraint \(c(x)+J(x)p=0\).
assumptions_latex: \(f:\mathbb R^n\to\mathbb R\) and \(c:\mathbb R^n\to\mathbb R^m\) are twice continuously differentiable near \(x\).
\(J(x)\) has full row rank.
\(B\in\mathbb R^{n\times n}\) is symmetric.
The displayed saddle-point matrix is nonsingular.
knowledge_statements.conclusion_latex: \((p,\delta\lambda)\) is simultaneously a primal-dual KKT Newton or quasi-Newton correction and the correction represented by the SQP quadratic model's KKT system.
knowledge_statements.scope_note: Equality-constrained primal-dual interpretation with a symmetric SQP Hessian model.

knowledge_statements.slot_contract: State the canonical mathematical definition of the source node, with its domain, quantifiers, notation, and a precise source locator.
knowledge_statements.ambient_context_latex: Let \(f:\mathbb R^n\to\mathbb R\) and \(c:\mathbb R^n\to\mathbb R^m\) be \(C^2\). For \(L(x,\lambda)=f(x)+\lambda^Tc(x)\), define \(R(x,\lambda)=\binom{\nabla_xL(x,\lambda)}{c(x)}\).
knowledge_statements.scope_note: Coupled primal-dual Newton representation for smooth equality constraints, with the multiplier treated as an iterate rather than eliminated.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex:
The primal-dual KKT Newton view defines an SQP correction as the simultaneous solution \((s_k,d_k)\in\mathbb R^n	imes\mathbb R^m\) of \[DR(x_k,\lambda_k) inom{s_k}{d_k}=-R(x_k,\lambda_k),\qquad DR(x_k,\lambda_k)= egin{pmatrix}
abla_{xx}^2L(x_k,\lambda_k)&J_c(x_k)^T\J_c(x_k)&0\end{pmatrix}.\] The associated update is \((x_{k+1},\lambda_{k+1})=(x_k+s_k,\lambda_k+d_k)\). Equivalently, \((s_k,\lambda_{k+1})\) satisfies \[
abla_{xx}^2L(x_k,\lambda_k)s_k+
abla f(x_k)+J_c(x_k)^T\lambda_{k+1}=0,\qquad c(x_k)+J_c(x_k)s_k=0.\] The defining feature is that primal feasibility and dual stationarity residuals are corrected in one bordered linear system.
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: In the primal-dual KKT Newton view, the primal variable and Lagrange multiplier are joint unknowns of the nonlinear KKT residual. An SQP step is the Newton correction obtained from the bordered Jacobian containing the Lagrangian Hessian, constraint Jacobian, its transpose, and a zero multiplier block. Updating both components gives the next primal-dual estimate. The same equations are the KKT conditions of the local equality-constrained quadratic program, but this view is distinguished by treating them as one Newton equation for a coupled residual.
assumptions_latex: \(f,c\in C^2\) near \(x_k\).
The sign convention in \(L\) and in the bordered matrix is fixed consistently.
If a unique correction is required, \(DR(x_k,\lambda_k)\) is nonsingular.
knowledge_statements.conclusion_latex: \((s_k,d_k)=-DR(x_k,\lambda_k)^{-1}R(x_k,\lambda_k)\), and \(\lambda_{k+1}=\lambda_k+d_k\), whenever the bordered derivative is invertible.
equivalent_formulations_latex: Using \(\lambda_{k+1}\) instead of \(d_k\) yields the QP stationarity and affine feasibility equations displayed above.
With the opposite Lagrangian sign convention, the multiplier columns and multiplier correction change sign without changing the primal step.
special_cases_latex: At a feasible iterate, \(J_c(x_k)s_k=0\), so the primal correction is tangent to the linearized constraint manifold.
At a KKT pair, \(R(x_k,\lambda_k)=0\) and the Newton correction is zero.
immediate_consequences_latex: The QP dual variables furnish a multiplier update rather than merely an auxiliary certificate.
A quasi-Newton primal-dual SQP method replaces only the upper-left block while retaining the residual coupling.
boundary_notes: For inequalities, complementarity introduces additional variables and equations or an active-set restriction.
The definition does not assert convergence of undamped full Newton steps.

notation.meaning: Newton correction to the multiplier iterate.

knowledge_statements.statement_title: Equivalence of the Equality-SQP QP Step and the Primal-Dual KKT Newton Step
knowledge_statements.scope_note: Local exact-Hessian SQP interpretation for a smooth equality-constrained nonlinear program.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex:
Let \(H_k=\nabla^2_{xx}\mathcal L(x_k,\lambda_k)\). If \(A_k\) has full row rank and \(d^TH_kd>0\) for every nonzero \(d\in\ker A_k\), then the quadratic program
\[
\min_p\ f_k+\nabla f_k^Tp+\tfrac12p^TH_kp
\quad\text{subject to}\quad A_kp+c_k=0
\]
has a unique primal-dual solution \((p_k,l_k)\), characterized by
\[
H_kp_k+\nabla f_k-A_k^Tl_k=0,\qquad A_kp_k+c_k=0.
\]
Its KKT system is the Newton system for the nonlinear KKT equations, written as
\[
\begin{bmatrix}H_k&-A_k^T\\A_k&0\end{bmatrix}
\begin{bmatrix}p_k\\\lambda_{k+1}\end{bmatrix}
=
\begin{bmatrix}-\nabla f_k\\-c_k\end{bmatrix}.
\]
Consequently \(l_k=\lambda_{k+1}\), and the same \(p_k\) is obtained from either the SQP subproblem or the primal-dual Newton equations.
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: Under full constraint rank and positive curvature on the constraint tangent space, the equality-constrained SQP quadratic model has a unique primal-dual solution. Its KKT equations are exactly the primal-dual Newton equations for the nonlinear problem's KKT system; the QP multiplier is the next multiplier iterate and both views produce the same primal step.
assumptions_latex: A_k\text{ has full row rank}
d^T\nabla^2_{xx}\mathcal L_kd>0\quad\forall d\in\ker A_k\setminus\{0\}
knowledge_statements.conclusion_latex: p_k^{\mathrm{QP}}=p_k^{\mathrm{Newton}},\qquad l_k=\lambda_{k+1}.

knowledge_statements.title: Lagrange-Newton View
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: SQP minimizes a quadratic Lagrangian model over linearized equalities; with the exact Lagrangian Hessian, the QP optimality equations are the Newton equations for stationarity and feasibility.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex:
Consider \(\min_{x\in\mathbb R^n}f(x)\) subject to \(c(x)=0\), where \(c:\mathbb R^n\to\mathbb R^m\), and define \(L(x,\lambda)=f(x)+\lambda^\top c(x)\) and \(J_k=Dc(x_k)\). At \((x_k,\lambda_k)\), let \(B_k\in\mathbb R^{n\times n}\) be symmetric and model \(\nabla_{xx}^2L(x_k,\lambda_k)\). The Lagrange-Newton primal step is obtained from
\[
\min_{p\in\mathbb R^n}\;\nabla f(x_k)^\top p+\tfrac12p^\top B_kp
\quad\text{subject to}\quad c(x_k)+J_kp=0.
\]
If \(\lambda_{k+1}\) is the QP multiplier, the first-order conditions are \(B_kp+\nabla f(x_k)+J_k^\top\lambda_{k+1}=0\) and \(c(x_k)+J_kp=0\). With \(B_k=\nabla_{xx}^2L(x_k,\lambda_k)\), these equations are the Newton linearization of Lagrangian stationarity and primal feasibility, where \(\delta\lambda_k=\lambda_{k+1}-\lambda_k\).
assumptions_latex: \(f:\mathbb R^n\to\mathbb R\) and \(c:\mathbb R^n\to\mathbb R^m\) are twice continuously differentiable near \(x_k\).
\(J_k\) has full row rank.
\(B_k\) is positive definite on \(\ker J_k\).
knowledge_statements.conclusion_latex: The unique SQP-QP minimizer and its multiplier satisfy the Lagrange-Newton system when \(B_k=\nabla_{xx}^2L(x_k,\lambda_k)\).
knowledge_statements.scope_note: Classical equality-constrained SQP as Newton minimization of a quadratic Lagrangian model.

notation.meaning: row-oriented constraint Jacobian at the current iterate

knowledge_statements.ambient_context_latex: For \(\min f(x)\) subject to \(c(x)=0\), let \(L(x,\lambda)=f(x)+\lambda^Tc(x)\), \(A_k=J_c(x_k)\), and \(H_k=\nabla_{xx}^2L(x_k,\lambda_k)\).
knowledge_statements.scope_note: Smooth equality-constrained local modeling. This view emphasizes the Lagrangian quadratic model and QP multiplier, rather than the coupled residual map itself.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex: The Lagrange-Newton view defines the SQP model at \((x_k,\lambda_k)\) by retaining the second-order primal variation of the Lagrangian and the first-order variation of feasibility: \[q_k(s)=f(x_k)+\nabla f(x_k)^Ts+\tfrac12s^TH_ks,\qquad \ell_k(s)=c(x_k)+A_ks.\] A Lagrange-Newton step is a KKT pair \((s_k,\lambda_{k+1})\) of \[\min_s q_k(s)\quad\text{subject to}\quad \ell_k(s)=0,\] namely \[H_ks_k+\nabla f(x_k)+A_k^T\lambda_{k+1}=0,\qquad A_ks_k+c(x_k)=0.\] The multiplier attached to the affine constraint is interpreted as the next nonlinear-program multiplier estimate. With exact \(H_k\), these conditions reproduce the primal component of Newton's method for the nonlinear KKT equations.
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: The Lagrange-Newton view of SQP constructs a quadratic model using the objective gradient and the Hessian of the Lagrangian, while replacing each nonlinear equality by its affine Taylor model. The step and the next multiplier estimate are defined as a KKT pair of this quadratic program. Unlike the explicitly coupled primal-dual formulation, the defining object here is the constrained quadratic model and its Lagrangian stationarity system.
assumptions_latex: \(f,c\in C^2\) near \(x_k\).
The curvature matrix is \(H_k=\nabla_{xx}^2L(x_k,\lambda_k)\) for the exact Lagrange-Newton view.
A KKT pair of the QP exists; uniqueness additionally requires appropriate constraint qualification and reduced-Hessian nonsingularity.
knowledge_statements.conclusion_latex: The Lagrange-Newton SQP step is exactly a pair \((s_k,\lambda_{k+1})\) satisfying the two displayed model KKT equations.
equivalent_formulations_latex: The constant \(f(x_k)\) may be removed from \(q_k\) without changing \(s_k\).

Adding \(\tfrac12s^TA_k^TCA_ks\) to the objective for any symmetric \(C\) does not change objective values over the affine feasible set except for terms fixed by \(A_ks=-c(x_k)\), although multiplier representations may change.
special_cases_latex: If \(x_k\) is feasible, the QP constraint is \(A_ks=0\).
Replacing \(H_k\) by a symmetric quasi-Newton matrix gives a Lagrange-Newton-like SQP model.
immediate_consequences_latex: Constraint curvature enters the objective through the multiplier-weighted Hessian terms in \(H_k\).
The affine QP multiplier provides the next multiplier estimate needed to form the following Lagrangian Hessian.
boundary_notes: The quadratic model need not be convex because the exact Lagrangian Hessian may be indefinite.
The definition does not specify step acceptance or a globalization device.

knowledge_statements.title: Reduced-Space Newton View
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: The equality-constrained SQP step decomposes into a normal feasibility correction and a tangent-space correction governed by the reduced Hessian; it is a reduced Newton step when the exact Lagrangian Hessian is used.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex:
Consider \(\min_{x\in\mathbb R^n}f(x)\) subject to \(c(x)=0\), where \(c:\mathbb R^n\to\mathbb R^m\), and let \(J_k=Dc(x_k)\in\mathbb R^{m\times n}\) have full row rank. Let the columns of \(Z_k\in\mathbb R^{n\times(n-m)}\) span \(\ker J_k\), choose a normal step \(p_k^N\) satisfying \(J_kp_k^N=-c(x_k)\), and write \(p_k=p_k^N+Z_ks_k\). For \(g_k=\nabla f(x_k)\) and a symmetric Hessian model \(B_k\in\mathbb R^{n\times n}\), tangent-space projection of QP stationarity gives
\[
Z_k^\top B_kZ_ks_k=-Z_k^\top(g_k+B_kp_k^N).
\]
If \(Z_k^\top B_kZ_k\) is nonsingular, this equation uniquely determines the tangential SQP correction. It is a reduced-space Newton equation when \(B_k=\nabla_{xx}^2L(x_k,\lambda_k)\), and a reduced quasi-Newton equation when \(B_k\) approximates that Hessian. A QP multiplier can subsequently be recovered from the unprojected stationarity equation.
assumptions_latex: \(f:\mathbb R^n\to\mathbb R\) and \(c:\mathbb R^n\to\mathbb R^m\) are differentiable at \(x_k\).
\(J_k\) has full row rank.
\(Z_k\) has full column rank and satisfies \(J_kZ_k=0\).
\(B_k\) is symmetric and \(Z_k^\top B_kZ_k\) is nonsingular.
knowledge_statements.conclusion_latex: \(p_k=p_k^N+Z_ks_k\) satisfies the reduced equality-constrained SQP KKT equations, with the exact-Newton interpretation applying when \(B_k\) is the Lagrangian Hessian.

knowledge_statements.slot_contract: State the canonical mathematical definition of the source node, with its domain, quantifiers, notation, and a precise source locator.
knowledge_statements.ambient_context_latex: Let \(A_k=J_c(x_k)\in\mathbb R^{m\times n}\) have full row rank. Choose \(N_k\in\mathbb R^{n\times(n-m)}\) with \(A_kN_k=0\), and a range-space matrix \(R_k\in\mathbb R^{n\times m}\) such that \(A_kR_k\) is nonsingular. Let \(H_k\) be the exact or approximate Lagrangian Hessian.
knowledge_statements.scope_note: Smooth equality-constrained SQP with full-row-rank constraint Jacobian. The definition concerns algebraic reduction of the local Newton/QP equations.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex: The reduced-space Newton view decomposes the SQP step uniquely as \(s_k=R_ku_k+N_kv_k\). The normal or range-space component is defined by \[(A_kR_k)u_k=-c(x_k),\] and the tangential component is defined by the reduced Newton equation \[(N_k^TH_kN_k)v_k=-N_k^T\bigl(\nabla f(x_k)+H_kR_ku_k\bigr).\] The matrix \(Z_k=N_k^TH_kN_k\) is the reduced Hessian. When \(Z_k\) and \(A_kR_k\) are nonsingular, these equations define the same primal step as the full KKT system for the equality-constrained SQP quadratic program. A multiplier can subsequently be recovered from \(A_k^T\lambda_{k+1}=-(\nabla f(x_k)+H_ks_k)\).
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: In the reduced-space Newton view, the SQP step is split into a range-space component that satisfies the affine constraint and a null-space component tangent to that constraint. The tangent component solves a Newton equation involving the reduced Hessian \(N_k^TH_kN_k\). Under full row rank and the stated nonsingularity conditions, recombining the two components yields the same primal step as the unreduced saddle-point KKT system; the multiplier is recovered afterward.
assumptions_latex: \(A_k\) has full row rank \(m\leq n\).
The columns of \(N_k\) span \(\ker A_k\), and \(A_kR_k\) is nonsingular.
For a unique reduced step, both \(A_kR_k\) and \(N_k^TH_kN_k\) are nonsingular.
knowledge_statements.conclusion_latex: \(s_k=R_ku_k+N_kv_k\) defined by the normal and reduced equations is the primal SQP/Newton step associated with the full bordered KKT equations.
equivalent_formulations_latex: If \(Y_k=R_k(A_kR_k)^{-1}\), then the normal step may be written \(s_k^{N}=-Y_kc(x_k)\).
For a feasible iterate, \(u_k=0\) and only the reduced equation on \(\ker A_k\) remains.
special_cases_latex: If \(m=n\) and \(A_k\) is nonsingular, the null space is trivial and the affine constraint alone determines \(s_k\).
If \(m=0\), then \(N_k=I\) and the reduced equation is the ordinary Newton equation.
immediate_consequences_latex: Positive definiteness of \(N_k^TH_kN_k\), rather than of \(H_k\) on all of \(\mathbb R^n\), is the relevant curvature condition along feasible tangent directions.
Reduced-Hessian approximations can be maintained without explicitly approximating every block of the full Hessian.
boundary_notes: Rank-deficient Jacobians require a different decomposition or regularization.
The definition does not prescribe a particular null-space basis or factorization.

knowledge_statements.slot_contract: State the canonical mathematical definition of the source node, with its domain, quantifiers, notation, and a precise source locator.
knowledge_statements.ambient_context_latex: Let \(f:\mathbb R^n\to\mathbb R\), \(c:\mathbb R^n\to\mathbb R^{m_e}\), and \(g:\mathbb R^n\to\mathbb R^{m_i}\) be smooth. Optional bounds are \(l\leq x\leq u\), where components of \(l\) or \(u\) may be infinite.
knowledge_statements.scope_note: Finite-dimensional smooth nonlinear programs, classified by the geometry represented in each SQP subproblem.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex: The SQP nonlinear-program regime is the constraint signature \(\mathcal R=(m_e,m_i,\mathcal B)\), where \(m_e\) counts nonlinear equalities, \(m_i\) counts general nonlinear inequalities, and \(\mathcal B=\{i:l_i> -\infty\text{ or }u_i<+\infty\}\) records explicit variable bounds. At iterate \(x_k\), the signature induces the local feasible model \[\mathcal F_k=\{s:c(x_k)+J_c(x_k)s=0,\ g(x_k)+J_g(x_k)s\leq0,\ l-x_k\leq s\leq u-x_k\}.\] Equality-constrained, mixed-constraint, and bound-interface SQP are respectively the regimes \((m_e,0,\varnothing)\), \((m_e,m_i,\mathcal B)\) with \(m_i>0\), and a regime in which \(\mathcal B\neq\varnothing\) is retained explicitly in the QP rather than absorbed into generic nonlinear inequalities.
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: A nonlinear-program regime for SQP is determined by the numbers of nonlinear equalities and inequalities and by the set of explicit finite variable bounds. This signature determines whether the local QP contains affine equalities, affine inequalities with complementary multipliers, and shifted box constraints. The distinction is mathematical because it changes the local feasible set, multiplier conditions, and activity structure even when all constraints could be encoded syntactically as inequalities.
assumptions_latex: All constraint functions used in affine models are differentiable at \(x_k\).
The bound vectors satisfy \(l_i<u_i\) whenever both endpoints are finite.
Inequalities use the convention \(g(x)\leq0\).
knowledge_statements.conclusion_latex: Each iterate has the regime-specific affine feasible set \(\mathcal F_k\), and the three named SQP regimes are the stated subclasses of the signature \((m_e,m_i,\mathcal B)\).
equivalent_formulations_latex: A lower bound \(x_i\geq l_i\) is the affine inequality \(l_i-x_i\leq0\), but retaining it as a bound exposes box structure.
An equality may be encoded as two inequalities, but doing so changes the multiplier representation and is not the equality regime used here.
special_cases_latex: \((0,0,\varnothing)\) is unconstrained Newton or quasi-Newton optimization, not constrained SQP in the narrow sense.
\((0,0,\mathcal B)\) gives a bound-constrained quadratic subproblem.
immediate_consequences_latex: The mixed regime requires complementarity for QP inequality multipliers.
Only equality regimes admit the basic smooth square KKT residual without explicit complementarity variables or activity selection.
boundary_notes: Nonsmooth constraints, complementarity constraints, conic constraints, and integer restrictions are outside this classification.
The signature records constraint form, not regularity or convexity.

notation.meaning: Indices having at least one finite explicit bound.
Regime-dependent feasible set of the local SQP subproblem.

knowledge_statements.title: Equality-Constrained SQP
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: Each equality-constrained SQP iteration solves a quadratic objective model over linearized equalities, accepts a possibly damped step, and updates the Lagrangian Hessian model; termination is based on approximate KKT residuals.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex:
For \(\min_{x\in\mathbb R^n}f(x)\) subject to \(c(x)=0\), where \(c:\mathbb R^n\to\mathbb R^m\), define \(L(x,\lambda)=f(x)+\lambda^\top c(x)\) and \(J_k=Dc(x_k)\). Given \(x_0\in\mathbb R^n\), \(\lambda_0\in\mathbb R^m\), and a symmetric matrix \(B_0\), repeat: compute \((p_k,\lambda_{k+1})\) by solving
\[
\min_{p\in\mathbb R^n}\;\nabla f(x_k)^\top p+\tfrac12p^\top B_kp
\quad\text{subject to}\quad c(x_k)+J_kp=0;
\]
choose \(\alpha_k\in(0,1]\) using the specified local or globalization rule; set \(x_{k+1}=x_k+\alpha_kp_k\); and construct \(B_{k+1}\) as an exact or quasi-Newton model of \(\nabla_{xx}^2L(x_{k+1},\lambda_{k+1})\). Stop when the primal-feasibility and Lagrangian-stationarity residuals meet the selected tolerances, and output the corresponding \((x_k,\lambda_k)\).
assumptions_latex: \(f:\mathbb R^n\to\mathbb R\) and \(c:\mathbb R^n\to\mathbb R^m\) are twice continuously differentiable on the region where exact Hessians are used.
Each quadratic subproblem has a selected solution and multiplier.
A step-acceptance rule and an exact or quasi-Newton Hessian-update rule are specified.
knowledge_statements.conclusion_latex: If the stopping test is reached, the returned pair approximately satisfies \(c(x)=0\) and \(\nabla_xL(x,\lambda)=0\) to the prescribed tolerances.
knowledge_statements.scope_note: Canonical local SQP iteration for smooth nonlinear equality constraints.

notation.meaning: row-oriented Jacobian of the equality constraints

knowledge_statements.ambient_context_latex: Consider \(\min_{x\in\mathbb R^n}f(x)\) subject to \(c(x)=0\), with \(f,c\in C^2\), Lagrangian \(L(x,\lambda)=f(x)+\lambda^Tc(x)\), and \(A_k=J_c(x_k)\).
knowledge_statements.scope_note: Local smooth SQP for nonlinear equality constraints, allowing exact or symmetric approximate Lagrangian curvature.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex:
An equality-constrained SQP iteration is a sequence \(\{(x_k,\lambda_k)\}\) for which a primal step and next multiplier are obtained from a KKT pair of \[\min_{s\in\mathbb R^n}\ 
abla f(x_k)^Ts+	frac12s^TB_ks\quad	ext{subject to}\quad c(x_k)+A_ks=0,\] so that \[B_ks_k+
abla f(x_k)+A_k^T\lambda_{k+1}=0,\qquad c(x_k)+A_ks_k=0.\] The local full-step update is \(x_{k+1}=x_k+s_k\). Exact-Hessian SQP takes \(B_k=
abla_{xx}^2L(x_k,\lambda_k)\); equality-constrained quasi-Newton SQP uses a symmetric approximation intended to represent Lagrangian curvature on feasible tangent directions.
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: Equality-constrained SQP repeatedly solves a quadratic program whose objective contains the current objective gradient and an exact or approximate Lagrangian Hessian, and whose equality constraint is the affine Taylor model of the nonlinear equality. The QP solution supplies the primal step, and its equality multiplier supplies the next multiplier estimate. A local full step adds the QP step to the current primal iterate.
assumptions_latex: \(f,c\in C^2\) near the iterates.
\(B_k\in\mathbb R^{n\times n}\) is symmetric.
The affine equality system is consistent and the QP has a KKT pair; uniqueness requires additional rank and reduced-curvature conditions.
knowledge_statements.conclusion_latex: For every defined iteration, \((s_k,\lambda_{k+1})\) satisfies the displayed equality-QP KKT equations and \(x_{k+1}=x_k+s_k\) locally.
equivalent_formulations_latex: With exact curvature, the QP KKT equations are Newton's equations for the nonlinear KKT system.
If \(A_k\) has full row rank, the primal step may be computed through a normal/tangential or null-space decomposition.
special_cases_latex: At a feasible iterate, the step satisfies \(A_ks_k=0\).
For linear \(c\), the affine constraint model is exact.
immediate_consequences_latex: No complementarity conditions occur in the equality-QP subproblem.
The QP multiplier can be used in the next Lagrangian Hessian or quasi-Newton update.
boundary_notes: The definition does not guarantee that the affine constraint is consistent at rank-deficient iterates.
Line searches, trust regions, filters, and restoration phases are additional mechanisms.

notation.meaning: Symmetric exact or approximate Lagrangian-curvature matrix.
Multiplier of the affine QP equality and next nonlinear multiplier estimate.

knowledge_statements.slot_contract: State the canonical mathematical definition of the source node, with its domain, quantifiers, notation, and a precise source locator.
knowledge_statements.ambient_context_latex: Consider \(\min f(x)\) subject to \(c(x)=0\) and \(g(x)\leq0\), where \(f,c,g\) are \(C^2\). Let \(L(x,\lambda,\mu)=f(x)+\lambda^Tc(x)+\mu^Tg(x)\).
knowledge_statements.scope_note: Smooth finite-dimensional SQP with simultaneous nonlinear equalities and inequalities, using a QP to determine activity and complementary multipliers.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex:
A mixed-constraint SQP iteration computes \((s_k,\lambda_{k+1},\mu_{k+1})\) as a KKT triple of \[\min_s\ 
abla f(x_k)^Ts+	frac12s^TB_ks\] \[	ext{subject to}\quad c(x_k)+J_c(x_k)s=0,\qquad g(x_k)+J_g(x_k)s\leq0.\] Thus \[B_ks_k+
abla f(x_k)+J_c(x_k)^T\lambda_{k+1}+J_g(x_k)^T\mu_{k+1}=0,\] together with affine equality feasibility, affine inequality feasibility, \(\mu_{k+1}\geq0\), and \[\mu_{k+1,i} igl(g_i(x_k)+
abla g_i(x_k)^Ts_k igr)=0\quad(i=1,\ldots,m_i).\] The QP active set is \(\mathcal A_k^{QP}=\{i:g_i(x_k)+
abla g_i(x_k)^Ts_k=0\}\).
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: Mixed-constraint SQP forms one quadratic subproblem containing affine models of both nonlinear equalities and nonlinear inequalities. Its solution consists of a primal step, unrestricted equality multipliers, and nonnegative inequality multipliers satisfying complementarity with the affine slacks. The active inequalities are those whose affine models bind at the QP solution. This complementary activity structure distinguishes the regime from equality-only SQP.
assumptions_latex: \(f,c,g\in C^2\) near \(x_k\).
\(B_k\) is symmetric.
The mixed QP is feasible and possesses a KKT triple under an appropriate QP constraint qualification.
knowledge_statements.conclusion_latex: The mixed SQP step and multipliers are exactly the variables satisfying the displayed QP stationarity, feasibility, sign, and complementarity relations.
equivalent_formulations_latex: Introducing affine slack variables \(z_k\geq0\) gives \(g(x_k)+J_g(x_k)s_k+z_k=0\) and \(\mu_{k+1}^Tz_k=0\).
After an active set is fixed, the primal-dual equations reduce to an equality-constrained bordered system using \(c\) and the active rows of \(g\).
special_cases_latex: If \(m_i=0\), the definition reduces to equality-constrained SQP.
If \(m_e=0\), it gives inequality-constrained SQP.
immediate_consequences_latex: Inactive QP inequalities have zero QP multiplier.
The curvature model may depend on both equality and inequality multiplier estimates through the Lagrangian Hessian.
boundary_notes: A QP active set need not equal the active set at the nonlinear-program solution away from the solution.
Degenerate complementarity and inconsistent linearizations require safeguards not included here.

notation.meaning: Set of affine inequalities active at the QP solution.

knowledge_statements.title: Inequality-Constrained SQP
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: Inequality-constrained SQP solves a QP with affine inequality models, uses its nonnegative multipliers as nonlinear multiplier estimates, and terminates according to approximate KKT residuals.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex:
For \(\min_{x\in\mathbb R^n}f(x)\) subject to \(g(x)\leq0\), where \(g:\mathbb R^n\to\mathbb R^q\), define \(L(x,\mu)=f(x)+\mu^\top g(x)\) and \(G_k=Dg(x_k)\). Initialize \(x_0\in\mathbb R^n\), \(\mu_0\in\mathbb R_+^q\), and a symmetric matrix \(B_0\). At iteration \(k\), solve
\[
\min_{p\in\mathbb R^n}\;\nabla f(x_k)^\top p+\tfrac12p^\top B_kp
\quad\text{subject to}\quad g(x_k)+G_kp\leq0,
\]
obtaining \(p_k\) and QP multipliers \(\mu_{k+1}\geq0\). Choose \(\alpha_k\in(0,1]\) using a specified acceptance rule, set \(x_{k+1}=x_k+\alpha_kp_k\), and construct \(B_{k+1}\) as an exact or quasi-Newton model of \(\nabla_{xx}^2L(x_{k+1},\mu_{k+1})\). Stop when stationarity, feasibility, complementarity, and dual-feasibility residuals meet their prescribed tolerances.
assumptions_latex: \(f:\mathbb R^n\to\mathbb R\) and \(g:\mathbb R^n\to\mathbb R^q\) are twice continuously differentiable on the region where exact Hessians are used.
Each quadratic subproblem has a selected primal-dual solution.
A step-acceptance rule and an exact or quasi-Newton Hessian-update rule are specified.
knowledge_statements.conclusion_latex: If the stopping test is reached, the output approximately satisfies \(\nabla f(x)+Dg(x)^\top\mu=0\), \(g(x)\leq0\), \(\mu\geq0\), and \(\mu_i g_i(x)=0\) to the prescribed tolerances.
knowledge_statements.scope_note: Canonical SQP iteration for smooth constraints written with the nonpositive sign convention.

knowledge_statements.statement_title: IQP and EQP Architectures for Active-Set SQP
knowledge_statements.scope_note: Extraction-grounded taxonomy of active-set SQP architectures for nonlinear programs with inequality constraints; it states the subproblem and globalization alternatives but makes no convergence or complexity claim.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex: For an active\text{-}set SQP method applied to an inequality\text{-}constrained nonlinear program, the step computation has two principal architectures. In the IQP architecture, each iteration solves a general inequality\text{-}constrained quadratic program both to compute a step and to estimate the optimal active set. In the EQP architecture, the method first estimates the optimal active set and then computes the step by solving an equality\text{-}constrained quadratic program. Either architecture may be embedded in a line\text{-}search or trust\text{-}region framework and may be designed for small or large problems.
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: Active-set SQP methods for inequality-constrained nonlinear programs have two principal architectures. IQP methods solve a general inequality-constrained quadratic program at each iteration to compute the step and estimate the optimal active set jointly. EQP methods first estimate the optimal active set and then solve an equality-constrained quadratic program for the step. Either architecture can be used with line-search or trust-region globalization and can be designed for small or large problems.
assumptions_latex: \text{The problem is a nonlinear program with inequality constraints.}
\text{The SQP method uses an active-set strategy.}
knowledge_statements.conclusion_latex: \text{The step architecture is IQP or EQP as described, and either admits line-search or trust-region globalization.}

knowledge_statements.title: Mixed Equality-Inequality SQP
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: Mixed-constraint SQP places affine equality and inequality models in one QP, updates the iterate with an accepted step, and uses both QP multiplier blocks in its Lagrangian Hessian model and KKT stopping test.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex:
For \(\min_{x\in\mathbb R^n}f(x)\) subject to \(c(x)=0\) and \(g(x)\leq0\), where \(c:\mathbb R^n\to\mathbb R^m\) and \(g:\mathbb R^n\to\mathbb R^q\), define \(J_k=Dc(x_k)\), \(G_k=Dg(x_k)\), and \(L(x,\lambda,\mu)=f(x)+\lambda^\top c(x)+\mu^\top g(x)\). At iteration \(k\), solve
\[
\min_{p\in\mathbb R^n}\;\nabla f(x_k)^\top p+\tfrac12p^\top B_kp
\quad\text{subject to}\quad c(x_k)+J_kp=0,\qquad g(x_k)+G_kp\leq0.
\]
Let \((\lambda_{k+1},\mu_{k+1})\), with \(\mu_{k+1}\geq0\), be selected QP multipliers. Choose \(\alpha_k\in(0,1]\) using a specified acceptance rule, set \(x_{k+1}=x_k+\alpha_kp_k\), and construct \(B_{k+1}\) as an exact or quasi-Newton model of \(\nabla_{xx}^2L(x_{k+1},\lambda_{k+1},\mu_{k+1})\). Terminate when all mixed KKT residuals meet their prescribed tolerances.
assumptions_latex: \(f\), \(c\), and \(g\) are twice continuously differentiable on the region where exact Hessians are used.
Each mixed quadratic subproblem has a selected primal-dual solution.
A step-acceptance rule and an exact or quasi-Newton Hessian-update rule are specified.
knowledge_statements.conclusion_latex: If the stopping test is reached, the returned iterate approximately satisfies equality feasibility, inequality feasibility, stationarity, dual feasibility, and complementarity to the prescribed tolerances.

knowledge_statements.statement_title: Mixed-Constraint IQP Step and Active-Set Newton Reduction
knowledge_statements.scope_note: Local SQP model for nonlinear programs with equality and inequality constraints, including its active-set interpretation.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex:
For
\[
\min_x f(x)\quad\text{subject to}\quad c_i(x)=0\ (i\in\mathcal E),\qquad c_i(x)\ge 0\ (i\in\mathcal I),
\]
a local IQP-SQP step at \((x_k,\lambda_k)\) is obtained by solving
\[
\begin{aligned}
\min_p\;&f_k+\nabla f_k^Tp+\tfrac12p^T\nabla^2_{xx}\mathcal L_kp,\\
\text{subject to }&\nabla c_i(x_k)^Tp+c_i(x_k)=0 &&(i\in\mathcal E),\\
&\nabla c_i(x_k)^Tp+c_i(x_k)\ge0 &&(i\in\mathcal I).
\end{aligned}
\]
If \((p_k,\lambda_{k+1})\) is its primal-multiplier solution, the new primal iterate is \(x_{k+1}=x_k+p_k\). The QP-active set is used as the estimate of the nonlinear program's optimal active set. If that set is identified correctly and remains unchanged, the iteration reduces to equality-constrained Newton behavior and hence exhibits the corresponding rapid local convergence. Strict complementarity at \((x^*,\lambda^*)\) means
\[
\nexists i\in\mathcal I:\quad \lambda_i^*=0\ \text{and}\ c_i(x^*)=0.
\]
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: For a nonlinear program with equalities and inequalities, IQP-SQP linearizes every constraint and minimizes a quadratic Lagrangian model. The QP solution supplies the primal step and next multiplier estimate. Its active constraints predict the solution's active set; once the correct set is identified and remains fixed, the method behaves like equality-constrained Newton iteration and converges rapidly. Strict complementarity excludes an active inequality with zero multiplier.
assumptions_latex: f\text{ and }c_i\text{ admit the derivatives appearing in the local quadratic model}
\mathcal E\text{ and }\mathcal I\text{ index equality and inequality constraints, respectively}
\mathcal A_k\text{ is correctly identified and remains unchanged for the Newton-reduction conclusion}
knowledge_statements.conclusion_latex: x_{k+1}=x_k+p_k;\quad \mathcal A_k=\mathcal A^*\text{ persistently }\Longrightarrow\text{ equality-constrained Newton behavior and rapid local convergence}.

knowledge_statements.title: Mixed-Constraint Activity Regimes
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: A mixed SQP step is classified by which affine inequalities bind, whether their multipliers are positive, and whether activity is exact or tolerance-based.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex:
For a mixed SQP subproblem with inequality model \(g(x_k)+G_kp\leq0\), define the predicted active set at a QP solution \((p_k,\mu_{k+1})\) by
\[
\mathcal A_k=\{i:g_i(x_k)+\nabla g_i(x_k)^\top p_k=0\}.
\]
The regime is strictly complementary when \(\mu_{k+1,i}>0\) for every \(i\in\mathcal A_k\) and \(g_i(x_k)+\nabla g_i(x_k)^\top p_k<0\) for every \(i\notin\mathcal A_k\). It is degenerate when some \(i\in\mathcal A_k\) has \(\mu_{k+1,i}=0\), and weakly active when activity is judged using a prescribed numerical tolerance rather than exact equality.
assumptions_latex: The mixed SQP QP has a primal-dual solution \((p_k,\lambda_{k+1},\mu_{k+1})\).

knowledge_statements.title: Bound-Constrained SQP Interfaces
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: Variable bounds become exact step bounds in the SQP QP, so damped updates preserve box feasibility while nonlinear constraints are linearized.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex:
For a nonlinear program with box bounds \(\ell\leq x\leq u\), an SQP interface preserves the bounds by imposing
\[
\ell-x_k\leq p\leq u-x_k
\]
directly in the quadratic subproblem, together with any affine models \(c(x_k)+J_kp=0\) and \(g(x_k)+G_kp\leq0\). Thus the QP feasible set is the intersection of the step box with the linearized nonlinear constraints. If \(x_k\) is box feasible and \(\alpha_k\in[0,1]\), every update \(x_{k+1}=x_k+\alpha_kp_k\) generated from a bound-feasible QP step remains within \([\ell,u]\).
assumptions_latex: \(\ell,u\in(\mathbb R\cup\{-\infty,+\infty\})^n\) satisfy \(\ell\leq u\).
The current iterate satisfies \(\ell\leq x_k\leq u\).
The accepted step length satisfies \(\alpha_k\in[0,1]\).
knowledge_statements.conclusion_latex: \(\ell-x_k\leq p_k\leq u-x_k\) implies \(\ell\leq x_k+\alpha_kp_k\leq u\).
knowledge_statements.scope_note: Explicit box bounds retained as linear constraints in each SQP quadratic subproblem.

knowledge_statements.statement_title: Explicit-Bound Interface in an SQP Subproblem
knowledge_statements.ambient_context_latex: Consider a smooth nonlinear program with optional constraints \(c(x)=0\), \(g(x)\leq0\), and componentwise bounds \(l\leq x\leq u\). Let \(x_k\) satisfy its finite bounds.
knowledge_statements.scope_note: SQP formulations that preserve simple variable bounds as shifted bounds on the step. This slot does not define a particular bound-QP solver.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex: A bound-constrained SQP interface preserves each finite variable bound exactly in step coordinates by imposing \[l-x_k\leq s\leq u-x_k.\] Its local subproblem is \[\min_s\ \nabla f(x_k)^Ts+\tfrac12s^TB_ks\] \[\text{subject to}\quad c(x_k)+J_c(x_k)s=0,\quad g(x_k)+J_g(x_k)s\leq0,\quad l-x_k\leq s\leq u-x_k.\] If \(\alpha_k\in[0,1]\), then the accepted update \(x_{k+1}=x_k+\alpha_ks_k\) remains within the box whenever \(x_k\) and \(x_k+s_k\) do. The bound-active sets are \(\mathcal A_k^L=\{i:x_{k,i}+s_{k,i}=l_i\}\) and \(\mathcal A_k^U=\{i:x_{k,i}+s_{k,i}=u_i\}\).
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: A bound-constrained SQP interface keeps simple variable bounds in their native form. Translating from the new variable \(x_k+s\) to the step gives the exact shifted bounds \(l-x_k\leq s\leq u-x_k\), which are appended to any affine nonlinear-constraint models. This exposes lower- and upper-active sets to the QP solver and ensures that any convexly shortened feasible step preserves the box.
assumptions_latex: The bounds are componentwise and satisfy \(l_i<u_i\) whenever both endpoints are finite.
The current iterate satisfies \(l\leq x_k\leq u\).
The accepted step length lies in \([0,1]\) when bound preservation by interpolation is asserted.
knowledge_statements.conclusion_latex: The exact bound model in SQP step variables is \(l-x_k\leq s\leq u-x_k\), with active sets \(\mathcal A_k^L\) and \(\mathcal A_k^U\) as displayed.
equivalent_formulations_latex: The lower bound is \(-s_i\leq x_{k,i}-l_i\), and the upper bound is \(s_i\leq u_i-x_{k,i}\).
Bounds may be represented as linear inequalities, but the explicit interface retains their box identity.
special_cases_latex: If all endpoints are infinite, the bound interface contributes no constraints.
If there are no general nonlinear constraints, the local problem is a box-constrained quadratic program.
immediate_consequences_latex: A full QP step feasible for the shifted bounds produces a bound-feasible new iterate.
Projected, active-set, and bound-QP methods can exploit the separate lower and upper active sets.
boundary_notes: General linear inequalities are not variable bounds unless each row selects a single variable with coefficient \(1\) or \(-1\).
The definition does not handle integrality or disjunctive bounds.

knowledge_statements.title: Wilson-Han-Powell SQP Methods
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: This classical template combines an SQP QP, exact-penalty line search, multiplier estimates, and a safeguarded quasi-Newton Lagrangian Hessian update.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex:
Given \((x_k,\lambda_k,B_k)\), solve the linearly constrained quadratic model with objective \(\nabla f(x_k)^\top p+\tfrac12p^\top B_kp\), obtain its multiplier estimate \(\lambda_{k+1}\), and choose \(\alpha_k\in(0,1]\) by sufficient decrease of an exact-penalty merit function. Set \(x_{k+1}=x_k+\alpha_kp_k\). Form the Lagrangian-gradient displacement
\[
y_k=\nabla_xL(x_{k+1},\lambda_{k+1})-\nabla_xL(x_k,\lambda_{k+1}),
\]
and apply a positive-definite quasi-Newton update to \(B_k\), with damping or skipping when the curvature test fails. Stop when the nonlinear KKT residual is below tolerance.
assumptions_latex: The SQP quadratic subproblem is solvable.
The merit function, penalty update, and quasi-Newton safeguard are specified.
The constraint sign convention is fixed consistently.
knowledge_statements.conclusion_latex: The iteration produces a merit-globalized quasi-Newton SQP sequence \(\{(x_k,\lambda_k,B_k)\}\).
knowledge_statements.scope_note: Generic quasi-Newton, merit-function SQP template associated with the named classical lineage.

enrichment_metadata.review_comment: The generic merit-function quasi-Newton SQP template is plausible, but no evidence identifies it as the Wilson-Han-Powell lineage or supports the particular multiplier displacement, penalty globalization, and safeguarding choices. A primary or authoritative historical source with a precise locator is required.

knowledge_statements.title: Maratos-Mayne-Polak SQP Methods
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: These methods supplement the SQP step with a higher-order feasibility correction to account for constraint curvature during acceptance testing.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex:
After computing a primary SQP step \(p_k\), form a correction \(d_k\) that compensates for nonlinear constraint curvature. In the equality-constrained form, a representative correction satisfies
\[
J_kd_k=-c(x_k+p_k),
\]
possibly in a least-norm or regularized sense; active inequalities may be included analogously. Test the corrected trial point \(x_k+p_k+d_k\), or its damped version, using the method's prescribed feasibility and merit acceptance rule. Accept the corrected step when it meets that rule; otherwise shorten or recompute it. The correction is required to be of higher order than \(p_k\) locally so that it does not alter the leading Newton step.
assumptions_latex: The primary SQP subproblem has a solution \(p_k\).
The correction equation is solvable or regularized.
A feasibility or merit acceptance rule is specified.
knowledge_statements.conclusion_latex: The corrected trial step \(p_k+d_k\) addresses the nonlinear feasibility error left by the affine constraint model.
knowledge_statements.scope_note: SQP template augmented by a feasible or second-order correction before step acceptance.

enrichment_metadata.review_comment: A second-order feasibility correction is a standard SQP construction, but the record merges potentially distinct Maratos, Mayne, and Polak variants and gives no source for the displayed correction or acceptance behavior. The named lineage cannot be reviewed reliably without precise primary or authoritative sources.

The corrected trial point is \(x_k+s_k+d_k\), and the member's acceptance rule must compare this point with the uncorrected trial point or with a merit criterion. The family is distinguished by the correction being higher order locally and directed at the nonlinear feasibility defect left by the first-order SQP step.
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: Provisionally, a Maratos-Mayne-Polak-type method computes the usual equality-constrained SQP step and then adds a higher-order correction aimed at the nonlinear constraint residual at the trial point. A representative correction solves \(A_kd_k=-c(x_k+s_k)\) and is required to be of order \(\|s_k\|^2\) locally. A complete family member must also state when the correction is computed and how corrected and uncorrected trials are accepted.

The SQP step satisfies \(c(x_k)+A_ks_k=0\).

For linear constraints, the ordinary affine-feasible SQP step has zero nonlinear feasibility residual, so no correction is required.
immediate_consequences_latex: The corrected trial need not be exactly feasible unless the correction equation or an additional solve enforces exact feasibility.
The correction is mathematically distinct from merely shortening \(s_k\) by a scalar line-search parameter.

knowledge_statements.title: Pang SQP Methods
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: The identifiable common structure is inequality SQP with QP multipliers and activity information; the precise Pang variant remains source-dependent.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex:
For \(\min f(x)\) subject to \(g(x)\leq0\), compute a quadratic-programming step \((p_k,\mu_{k+1})\) from an objective Hessian model \(B_k\) and the affine constraints \(g(x_k)+G_kp\leq0\). Define the QP active set
\[
\mathcal A_k=\{i:g_i(x_k)+\nabla g_i(x_k)^\top p_k=0\},
\]
use \(\mathcal A_k\) and \(\mu_{k+1}\geq0\) in the method's prescribed step-acceptance and multiplier-update rules, and update \(B_k\) from Lagrangian-gradient information. Stop when stationarity, feasibility, dual-feasibility, and complementarity residuals meet tolerance. The specific Pang globalization and active-set rules require source disambiguation.

knowledge_statements.ambient_context_latex: For a smooth nonlinear program \(\min f(x)\) subject to \(c(x)=0\) and \(g(x)\leq0\), define \(L(x,\lambda,\mu)=f(x)+\lambda^Tc(x)+\mu^Tg(x)\).
knowledge_statements.scope_note: Taxonomy of the mathematical models used to form an SQP subproblem, not of globalization or numerical QP solution methods.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex:
An SQP local model at \((x_k,\lambda_k,\mu_k)\) is the tuple \[\mathcal M_k=(
abla f(x_k),B_k,c(x_k),J_c(x_k),g(x_k),J_g(x_k)),\] inducing \[\min_s\ 
abla f(x_k)^Ts+	frac12s^TB_ks\quad	ext{subject to}\quad c(x_k)+J_c(x_k)s=0,\quad g(x_k)+J_g(x_k)s\leq0.\] Its curvature class is exact if \(B_k=
abla_{xx}^2L(x_k,\lambda_k,\mu_k)\), quasi-Newton if \(B_k\) is generated by a symmetric secant update, derivative-approximation if Hessian or Jacobian information is obtained through finite differences or another stated approximation, and hybrid if distinct blocks or iterations use different such constructions. Multiplier-activity coupling is present when the choice of \(B_k\), its update data, or included constraint rows depends on multiplier or activity estimates.
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: An SQP local model consists of the objective gradient, a symmetric curvature matrix, constraint values, and constraint Jacobians at the current iterate. These data define a quadratic objective and affine constraint models. The taxonomy classifies the curvature as exact Lagrangian, quasi-Newton, derivative-approximated, or hybrid, and separately records whether multiplier and activity estimates influence curvature or the selected constraint rows.
assumptions_latex: The functions whose derivatives appear in \(\mathcal M_k\) are differentiable at \(x_k\).
\(B_k\) is symmetric for the canonical quadratic model.
Every approximation class specifies which exact derivative quantity it approximates.
knowledge_statements.conclusion_latex: Every canonical local SQP subproblem is induced by a tuple \(\mathcal M_k\) and receives the stated curvature and coupling classifications according to the construction of \(B_k\) and the affine constraints.
equivalent_formulations_latex: The constant term \(f(x_k)\) may be included in or omitted from the quadratic objective.
Using the KKT equations of the induced QP gives an equivalent primal-dual representation of the model.
special_cases_latex: With no constraints, \(\mathcal M_k\) reduces to the ordinary quadratic Newton or quasi-Newton model.
For linear constraints, their affine models are exact even when the objective curvature is approximate.
immediate_consequences_latex: Two SQP algorithms may share a local model class while using different globalization mechanisms.
Exact Lagrangian curvature depends on current multiplier estimates whenever constraints are nonlinear.
boundary_notes: A nonsymmetric matrix is outside the canonical quadratic model unless its symmetric part is explicitly used.
Models with nonlinear subproblem constraints are sequential nonlinear models rather than canonical SQP models in this definition.

knowledge_statements.statement_title: Canonical Quadratic Programming Model for SQP
knowledge_statements.ambient_context_latex: Let \(f:\mathbb R^n\to\mathbb R\), \(c:\mathbb R^n\to\mathbb R^{m_e}\), and \(g:\mathbb R^n\to\mathbb R^{m_i}\) be \(C^2\). Let \(L(x,\lambda,\mu)=f(x)+\lambda^Tc(x)+\mu^Tg(x)\).
knowledge_statements.scope_note: Smooth finite-dimensional SQP with first-order constraint models and exact or approximate Lagrangian curvature.
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: The canonical SQP model minimizes a quadratic function of the step over affine Taylor models of the current nonlinear constraints. Its linear objective term is the current objective gradient. Its quadratic term uses either the exact Hessian of the Lagrangian, including multiplier-weighted constraint curvature, or a specified symmetric approximation. The constant objective value may be retained for model interpretation or omitted computationally.
assumptions_latex: \(f,c,g\in C^2\) when the exact Lagrangian Hessian is used.
\(B_k\) is symmetric.
A solution or KKT point is asserted only when the affine feasible set and quadratic program admit one.
knowledge_statements.conclusion_latex: The canonical local SQP subproblem is \(\min_{s\in\mathcal F_k}Q_k(s)\) with \(Q_k\), \(\mathcal F_k\), and exact \(B_k\) defined by the displayed formulas.
equivalent_formulations_latex: Dropping \(f(x_k)\) gives the equivalent objective \(\nabla f(x_k)^Ts+\tfrac12s^TB_ks\).
The QP KKT conditions provide the equivalent primal-dual Newton-like model.
special_cases_latex: For equality-only problems, omit the affine inequalities.
For linear constraints, the affine feasible set is the exact translated constraint set.
For unconstrained problems, the model is the ordinary quadratic Newton model.
immediate_consequences_latex: Nonlinear constraint curvature appears in \(B_k\), not in the affine constraint equations.
The exact model may be nonconvex because the Lagrangian Hessian need not be positive semidefinite.
boundary_notes: Replacing affine constraints by second-order nonlinear constraint models produces a different sequential model family.
Convexity and uniqueness are not part of the canonical definition.

notation.meaning: Quadratic objective model in step coordinates.

children.title: Constraint Linearization Models
children.top_down_role: Local affine representations of nonlinear equality and inequality constraints.

knowledge_statements.title: Constraint Linearization Models
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: SQP replaces each smooth nonlinear constraint by its first-order affine expansion in the trial step, preserving equality or inequality sense.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex:
Let \(c:\mathbb R^n\to\mathbb R^m\) and \(g:\mathbb R^n\to\mathbb R^q\) be differentiable, with constraints \(c(x)=0\) and \(g(x)\leq0\). At \(x_k\), their SQP affine models in a step \(p\) are
\[
c(x_k)+J_kp=0,\qquad g(x_k)+G_kp\leq0,
\]
where the rows of \(J_k\) and \(G_k\) are the corresponding constraint gradients. For \(p\to0\), differentiability gives \(c(x_k+p)=c(x_k)+J_kp+o(\lVert p\rVert)\) and \(g(x_k+p)=g(x_k)+G_kp+o(\lVert p\rVert)\), componentwise for the inequalities.
assumptions_latex: \(c\) and \(g\) are differentiable at \(x_k\).
Inequalities use the convention \(g(x)\leq0\).
knowledge_statements.conclusion_latex: The affine constraints approximate the nonlinear constraints with residual \(o(\lVert p\rVert)\) as \(p\to0\).
knowledge_statements.scope_note: First-order affine local models for smooth equality and inequality constraints.

source_witnesses.locator: 3.5.3 Sequential quadratic programming (SQP) p. 107
2.4 Quadratic Models p. 24

knowledge_statements.slot_contract: State the canonical mathematical definition of the source node, with its domain, quantifiers, notation, and a precise source locator.
knowledge_statements.ambient_context_latex: Let \(c:\mathbb R^n\to\mathbb R^{m_e}\) and \(g:\mathbb R^n\to\mathbb R^{m_i}\) be differentiable at \(x_k\). The local variable is the displacement \(s\in\mathbb R^n\), so the trial point is \(x_k+s\).
knowledge_statements.scope_note: First-order local models of smooth equality and inequality constraints in canonical SQP.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex: The constraint linearization model at \(x_k\) is the pair of affine maps \[\ell_k^c(s)=c(x_k)+J_c(x_k)s,\qquad \ell_k^g(s)=g(x_k)+J_g(x_k)s.\] The canonical linearized feasible set is \[\mathcal L_k=\{s\in\mathbb R^n:\ell_k^c(s)=0,\ \ell_k^g(s)\leq0\}.\] Componentwise, \(\ell_{k,j}^c(s)=c_j(x_k)+\nabla c_j(x_k)^Ts\) and \(\ell_{k,i}^g(s)=g_i(x_k)+\nabla g_i(x_k)^Ts\). If the functions are differentiable, then \(c(x_k+s)=\ell_k^c(s)+o(\|s\|)\) and \(g(x_k+s)=\ell_k^g(s)+o(\|s\|)\) as \(s\to0\).
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: The SQP constraint model replaces every smooth equality or inequality by its affine first-order Taylor model in the step. Equalities are imposed as affine equations, inequalities as componentwise affine inequalities, and their intersection is the linearized feasible set \(\mathcal L_k\). Differentiability makes the modeling error little-o of the step norm. This definition concerns only constraint modeling; it does not specify the quadratic objective or guarantee consistency of the affine system.
assumptions_latex: \(c\) and \(g\) are differentiable at \(x_k\).
Vector inequalities are interpreted componentwise.
The Jacobian convention is such that \(J_c(x_k)s\) and \(J_g(x_k)s\) have constraint-space dimensions.
knowledge_statements.conclusion_latex: The canonical SQP constraint model is \(\mathcal L_k=\{s:c(x_k)+J_c(x_k)s=0,\ g(x_k)+J_g(x_k)s\leq0\}\), with first-order residual errors \(o(\|s\|)\).
equivalent_formulations_latex: Using the trial variable \(z=x_k+s\), the equality model is \(c(x_k)+J_c(x_k)(z-x_k)=0\), with the analogous inequality model.
Explicit bounds linearize exactly to \(l-x_k\leq s\leq u-x_k\).
special_cases_latex: If a constraint is affine, its linearization equals the exact constraint at every trial point.
At an equality-feasible iterate, \(\ell_k^c(s)=J_c(x_k)s\).
immediate_consequences_latex: The linearized equality system may be inconsistent when the Jacobian is rank deficient.
A sufficiently small trust region does not by itself guarantee intersection with a displaced affine equality manifold.
boundary_notes: Second-order constraint corrections and nonlinear subproblem constraints are outside the first-order model.
Differentiability does not imply that a step feasible for \(\mathcal L_k\) is feasible for the original nonlinear constraints.

notation.meaning: Affine equality and inequality constraint models.

children.title: Lagrangian Hessian SQP Model
children.top_down_role: The canonical multiplier-dependent second-order SQP curvature family.

knowledge_statements.slot_contract: State the canonical mathematical definition of the source node, with its domain, quantifiers, notation, and a precise source locator.
knowledge_statements.ambient_context_latex: Let \(f:\mathbb R^n\to\mathbb R\) and \(c=(c_i)_{i\in\mathcal E\cup\mathcal I}\) be twice continuously differentiable, with constraints \(c_i(x)=0\) for \(i\in\mathcal E\) and \(c_i(x)\ge 0\) for \(i\in\mathcal I\). Use \(\mathcal L(x,\lambda)=f(x)-\sum_i\lambda_i c_i(x)\).
knowledge_statements.scope_note: Finite-dimensional smooth nonlinear programming; the definition concerns the local SQP subproblem and does not prescribe globalization or a QP solver.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex:
At a primal-multiplier pair \((x_k,\lambda_k)\), the Lagrangian-Hessian SQP model is the quadratic program in \(p\in\mathbb R^n\)
\[
\min_p\;m_k(p):=f(x_k)+\nabla f(x_k)^Tp+\tfrac12p^TB_kp
\]
subject to
\[
c_i(x_k)+\nabla c_i(x_k)^Tp=0\quad(i\in\mathcal E),\qquad c_i(x_k)+\nabla c_i(x_k)^Tp\ge0\quad(i\in\mathcal I),
\]
where the canonical curvature choice is \(B_k=\nabla_{xx}^2\mathcal L(x_k,\lambda_k)\). More generally, the same model family permits a symmetric matrix \(B_k\) intended to represent that Lagrangian Hessian. A QP solution \(p_k\) is the SQP primal step, while the multipliers of its linearized constraints provide the next multiplier estimate.
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: At the current primal and multiplier estimates, an SQP Lagrangian-Hessian model minimizes a quadratic Taylor model of the objective whose curvature is the Hessian of the Lagrangian, subject to first-order linearizations of all equality and inequality constraints. The QP minimizer is the primal step, and its constraint multipliers furnish a new multiplier estimate. Symmetric approximations to the Lagrangian Hessian belong to the same model family.
knowledge_statements.conclusion_latex: \(m_k(p)=f_k+\nabla f_k^Tp+\tfrac12p^T\nabla_{xx}^2\mathcal L(x_k,\lambda_k)p\), with every nonlinear constraint replaced by its affine linearization at \(x_k\).
equivalent_formulations_latex: For equality constraints, the KKT equations of the QP are the Newton equations for \(\nabla_x\mathcal L(x,\lambda)=0\) and \(c(x)=0\).
On the affine feasible set, \(\nabla f(x_k)^Tp\) may be replaced by \(\nabla_x\mathcal L(x_k,\lambda_k)^Tp\) up to a constant independent of \(p\).
special_cases_latex: If \(\mathcal I=\varnothing\), the model is an equality-constrained QP.
If \(c\) is affine and \(f\) is quadratic, the local model reproduces the original problem up to constants.
immediate_consequences_latex: Positive definiteness of \(B_k\) on the null space of the active constraint Jacobian makes the equality-constrained model strictly convex along feasible directions.
boundary_notes: The definition does not require the full-space Hessian to be positive definite.
Trust-region bounds, merit functions, filters, and elastic variables are separate globalization additions.

notation.meaning: Symmetric exact or approximate Lagrangian-Hessian matrix used in the QP.
Primal step obtained from the SQP subproblem.

knowledge_statements.title: Exact Lagrangian Hessian Models
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: The canonical SQP subproblem linearizes the constraints and uses the exact primal Hessian of the Lagrangian as its quadratic curvature matrix.
assumptions_latex: \(f\) and \(c\) are twice continuously differentiable near \(x_k\).
\(x_k\in\mathbb R^n\) and \(\lambda_k\in\mathbb R^m\).
knowledge_statements.conclusion_latex: \(B_k=\nabla_{xx}^2L(x_k,\lambda_k)\) in the SQP quadratic model.
knowledge_statements.scope_note: Equality-constrained SQP model using exact second derivatives at the current primal-dual iterate.

source_witnesses.locator: 3.5.3 Sequential quadratic programming (SQP) p. 107

knowledge_statements.slot_contract: State the canonical mathematical definition of the source node, with its domain, quantifiers, notation, and a precise source locator.
knowledge_statements.ambient_context_latex: Consider the smooth nonlinear program and Lagrangian \(\mathcal L(x,\lambda)=f(x)-\lambda^Tc(x)\), with current estimates \((x_k,\lambda_k)\in\mathbb R^n\times\mathbb R^m\).
knowledge_statements.scope_note: The adjective exact refers solely to the curvature matrix; constraint functions remain first-order linearized in the SQP subproblem.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex:
An exact Lagrangian-Hessian SQP model is an SQP quadratic model whose curvature matrix is evaluated without a quasi-Newton or finite-difference replacement:
\[
B_k:=
abla_{xx}^2\mathcal L(x_k,\lambda_k)=
abla^2f(x_k)-\sum_{i=1}^m(\lambda_k)_i
abla^2c_i(x_k).
\]
Thus its objective is \(m_k(p)=f(x_k)+
abla f(x_k)^Tp+	frac12p^TB_kp\), and its feasible set consists of the affine constraint linearizations at \(x_k\). Exactness is an operator identity: any algebraically equivalent full-space, null-space, or factorized realization qualifies only when it represents the restriction or action of this same \(
abla_{xx}^2\mathcal L(x_k,\lambda_k)\), rather than a secant approximation.
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: An exact Lagrangian-Hessian model uses the actual second derivative of the current Lagrangian as its quadratic curvature. This matrix equals the objective Hessian minus the multiplier-weighted sum of the constraint Hessians. The constraints are still linearized, so exact curvature does not mean that the entire nonlinear program is represented exactly. Equivalent factorizations or reduced restrictions remain exact only if they reproduce the true Lagrangian-Hessian action.
knowledge_statements.conclusion_latex:
\(B_k=
abla_{xx}^2\mathcal L(x_k,\lambda_k)=
abla^2f(x_k)-\sum_i(\lambda_k)_i
abla^2c_i(x_k)\).
equivalent_formulations_latex: For any \(d\in\mathbb R^n\), exact curvature means \(d^TB_kd=d^T\nabla_{xx}^2\mathcal L(x_k,\lambda_k)d\).
For a null-space basis \(Z_k\), its exact reduced realization is \(Z_k^TB_kZ_k=Z_k^T\nabla_{xx}^2\mathcal L(x_k,\lambda_k)Z_k\).
special_cases_latex: With affine constraints, \(\nabla^2c_i=0\), so \(B_k=\nabla^2f(x_k)\).
For an unconstrained problem, the model reduces to the ordinary Newton quadratic model.
immediate_consequences_latex: The curvature depends on the multiplier estimate whenever at least one constraint has a nonzero Hessian.
boundary_notes: Analytic evaluation and an algebraically exact automatic-differentiation evaluation define the same mathematical model.
A regularized matrix \(B_k+\delta I\) is no longer exact unless \(\delta=0\).

notation.meaning: Hessian of the Lagrangian with respect to primal variables.

knowledge_statements.title: Exact-curvature SQP model

children.title: Full-Space Lagrangian Hessian Models
children.top_down_role: Lagrangian curvature represented in the full primal space.

knowledge_statements.title: Full-Space Lagrangian Hessian Models
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: A full-space model stores Lagrangian curvature as an n-by-n matrix. Writing the new QP multiplier as the current multiplier plus a correction gives the displayed saddle-point system for the primal step and multiplier correction.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex: Let \(f:\mathbb R^n\to\mathbb R\) and \(c:\mathbb R^n\to\mathbb R^m\), let \(x_k\in\mathbb R^n\) and \(\lambda_k\in\mathbb R^m\), and set \(A_k=J_c(x_k)\). Let \(B_k\in\mathbb S^n\) represent Lagrangian curvature in the full primal space. The full-space SQP model is \[\min_{d\in\mathbb R^n}\;\nabla f(x_k)^{\mathsf T}d+\tfrac12d^{\mathsf T}B_kd\quad\text{subject to}\quad A_kd=-c(x_k).\] If its QP multiplier is written as \(\lambda_k+\delta\lambda\), its KKT equations are \[\begin{pmatrix}B_k&A_k^{\mathsf T}\\A_k&0\end{pmatrix}\begin{pmatrix}d\\\delta\lambda\end{pmatrix}=-\begin{pmatrix}\nabla f(x_k)+A_k^{\mathsf T}\lambda_k\\c(x_k)\end{pmatrix}.\] Thus \(B_k\) is stored and applied in the full primal space, without requiring a tangent-space basis.
assumptions_latex: \(f:\mathbb R^n\to\mathbb R\) and \(c:\mathbb R^n\to\mathbb R^m\) are continuously differentiable at \(x_k\).
\(B_k\in\mathbb S^n\) and \(A_k\in\mathbb R^{m\times n}\).
The linearized equality constraints are consistent.
knowledge_statements.conclusion_latex: \(The\ SQP\ step\ is\ represented\ by\ the\ full\text{-}space\ KKT\ system\ in\ (d,\delta\lambda).\)
knowledge_statements.scope_note: Equality-constrained SQP curvature represented by an n-dimensional symmetric matrix before any null-space projection.

notation.meaning: constraint Jacobian at the current iterate
correction such that the QP multiplier is lambda_k plus delta lambda

knowledge_statements.slot_contract: State the canonical mathematical definition of the source node, with its domain, quantifiers, notation, and a precise source locator.
knowledge_statements.ambient_context_latex: Let \(p\in\mathbb R^n\) be an SQP step and let \(A_k\in\mathbb R^{m\times n}\) denote the current active or equality-constraint Jacobian.
knowledge_statements.scope_note: This is a representation classification: the curvature operator is maintained on all primal directions, whether exact or approximate.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex:
A full-space Lagrangian-Hessian model is an SQP model represented by a symmetric operator \(B_k:\mathbb R^n\to\mathbb R^n\), equivalently \(B_k\in\mathbb S^n\), and quadratic term \(\tfrac12p^TB_kp\) for every \(p\in\mathbb R^n\). The exact member has \(B_k=\nabla_{xx}^2\mathcal L(x_k,\lambda_k)\); a full-space quasi-Newton member instead approximates that operator but still stores or applies it on the complete primal space. The associated equality-constrained step and QP multiplier solve
\[
\begin{bmatrix}B_k&-A_k^T\\A_k&0\end{bmatrix}
\begin{bmatrix}p_k\\\lambda_{k+1}\end{bmatrix}
=
\begin{bmatrix}-\nabla f(x_k)\\-c(x_k)\end{bmatrix}.
\]
Full-space status is therefore distinct from exactness and from positive definiteness.
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: A full-space Lagrangian-Hessian model maintains a symmetric curvature operator on all primal directions and inserts that operator into the complete saddle-point KKT system. The matrix may be the exact Lagrangian Hessian or a full-space approximation. What distinguishes the model is its domain and representation, not its accuracy or definiteness.
knowledge_statements.conclusion_latex: \(B_k\in\mathbb S^n\) acts on every \(p\in\mathbb R^n\), and the SQP quadratic term is \(\tfrac12p^TB_kp\).
equivalent_formulations_latex: The full-space operator is the primal-primal block of the SQP KKT matrix.
For any null-space basis \(Z_k\), its induced reduced Hessian is \(Z_k^TB_kZ_k\), but storing only this projection is a reduced-space model.
special_cases_latex: If \(m=0\), the KKT system reduces to \(B_kp_k=-\nabla f(x_k)\).
If \(B_k\succ0\), the full-space quadratic objective is strictly convex.
immediate_consequences_latex: A full-space matrix also supplies normal-tangential cross curvature that a reduced-only matrix does not represent.
boundary_notes: Positive definiteness is not part of the definition.
A matrix-free routine computing \(B_kv\) for arbitrary \(v\in\mathbb R^n\) is still full-space.

notation.meaning: Space of real symmetric matrices of order \(n\).

knowledge_statements.scope_note: Null-space projection of the KKT equations and its implication for full-space quasi-Newton models.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex:
Let \(A_k\) have full row rank, let the columns of \(Z_k\in\mathbb R^{n	imes(n-m)}\) be an orthonormal basis of \(\ker A_k\), and define \(P_k=I-A_k^T(A_kA_k^T)^{-1}A_k=Z_kZ_k^T\). The KKT step satisfies \[Z_k^T
abla_{xx}^2\mathcal L_kp_k=-Z_k^T
abla f_k,\qquad A_kp_k=-c_k,\] equivalently \[P_k
abla_{xx}^2\mathcal L_kp_k=-P_k
abla f_k,\qquad A_kp_k=-c_k.\] Near the solution these equations determine \(p_k\); hence only the one-sided null-space projection \(P_k
abla_{xx}^2\mathcal L_k\) affects the step. A full-space quasi-Newton model therefore needs to approximate this projection, rather than the range-space component of the Lagrangian Hessian.

Near the solution these equations determine the step, so a full-space quasi-Newton matrix need only reproduce the one-sided null-space projection of the Lagrangian Hessian accurately.

Z_k^TZ_k=I,\qquad \operatorname{range}(Z_k)=\ker A_k.
P_k=I-A_k^T(A_kA_k^T)^{-1}A_k=Z_kZ_k^T.
(x_k,\lambda_k)\text{ is sufficiently near }(x^*,\lambda^*)\text{ for local step determination.}

\{Z_k^T

abla f_k,\ A_kp_k=-c_k\}\iff\{P_k

knowledge_statements.title: Reduced-Hessian Models
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: A null-space basis eliminates the linearized constraints and projects full Lagrangian curvature to the tangent coordinates through Z-transpose B Z.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex: Suppose \(A_k\in\mathbb R^{m\times n}\) has full row rank, and choose \(Z_k\in\mathbb R^{n\times(n-m)}\) with \(A_kZ_k=0\) and \(Z_k^{\mathsf T}Z_k=I\). For any particular step \(d_k^p\) satisfying \(A_kd_k^p=-c(x_k)\), write \(d=d_k^p+Z_kp\). A full curvature model \(B_k\) then induces the reduced Hessian \(H_k=Z_k^{\mathsf T}B_kZ_k\), and the quadratic objective becomes, up to a constant, \[\tfrac12p^{\mathsf T}H_kp+\bigl(Z_k^{\mathsf T}(\nabla f(x_k)+B_kd_k^p)\bigr)^{\mathsf T}p.\]
assumptions_latex: \(A_k\) has full row rank.
\(B_k\in\mathbb S^n\).
\(d_k^p\) satisfies the linearized constraints.
knowledge_statements.conclusion_latex: \(H_k=Z_k^{\mathsf T}B_kZ_k\) is the curvature matrix of the reduced SQP model.
knowledge_statements.scope_note: Equality-constrained SQP curvature restricted to the null space of the active constraint Jacobian.

notation.meaning: orthonormal null-space basis of the constraint Jacobian
