knowledge_statements.slot_contract: State the canonical mathematical definition of the source node, with its domain, quantifiers, notation, and a precise source locator.
knowledge_statements.ambient_context_latex: Let \(A_k\in\mathbb R^{m\times n}\) have full row rank and let \(Z_k\in\mathbb R^{n\times(n-m)}\) have full column rank with \(A_kZ_k=0\). Choose \(Y_k\) so that \([Y_k\ Z_k]\) is nonsingular.
knowledge_statements.scope_note: Equality-constrained or fixed-working-set SQP in finite dimensions; inequalities enter after a working set has been selected.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex:
A reduced-Hessian SQP model represents Lagrangian curvature only on the tangent space \(\ker A_k\). Writing
\[
p_k=Y_kp_Y+Z_kp_Z,
\]
the exact reduced Hessian is
\[
R_k:=Z_k^T\nabla_{xx}^2\mathcal L(x_k,\lambda_k)Z_k\in\mathbb S^{n-m}.
\]
A reduced model replaces or represents \(R_k\) by \(M_k\in\mathbb S^{n-m}\) and determines the tangential component from a reduced equation such as \(M_kp_Z=-Z_k^T\nabla f(x_k)\), while the normal component satisfies \((A_kY_k)p_Y=-c(x_k)\). Thus only curvature along feasible first-order directions is modeled; full-space cross curvature is omitted or treated separately.
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: A reduced-Hessian model projects the Lagrangian Hessian onto the null space of the active constraint Jacobian. The step is split into a normal component, determined by linearized feasibility, and a tangential component, determined using a smaller symmetric curvature matrix. Only curvature along first-order feasible directions is represented.
knowledge_statements.conclusion_latex: \(R_k=Z_k^T\nabla_{xx}^2\mathcal L(x_k,\lambda_k)Z_k\), acting on reduced coordinates \(p_Z\in\mathbb R^{n-m}\).
equivalent_formulations_latex: For every tangent direction \(d=Z_kz\), \(d^T\nabla_{xx}^2\mathcal L_kd=z^TR_kz\).
Changing the null-space basis to \(\widehat Z_k=Z_kT\) transforms the matrix by congruence: \(\widehat R_k=T^TR_kT\).
special_cases_latex: If \(m=0\), one may take \(Z_k=I\), and the reduced model is full-space.
If \(n=m\) and \(A_k\) is nonsingular, the tangent space is zero-dimensional.
immediate_consequences_latex: Positive definiteness of \(R_k\) is precisely positive definiteness of Lagrangian curvature on \(\ker A_k\).
boundary_notes: The matrix depends on the chosen coordinates, although the tangent-space quadratic form does not.
Dropping normal-tangential cross terms is an additional modeling choice.

notation.meaning: Basis matrix for the null space of the active constraint Jacobian.
Exact reduced Hessian in the chosen null-space coordinates.

children.title: Multiplier-Activity Model Coupling
children.top_down_role: Model families distinguished by multiplier estimation and predicted inequality activity.

knowledge_statements.slot_contract: State the canonical mathematical definition of the source node, with its domain, quantifiers, notation, and a precise source locator.
knowledge_statements.statement_title: Coupled multiplier and activity SQP model
knowledge_statements.ambient_context_latex: Consider constraints \(c_i(x)=0\) for \(i\in\mathcal E\) and \(c_i(x)\ge0\) for \(i\in\mathcal I\), with current point \(x_k\), multiplier estimate \(\lambda_k\), and predicted working set \(W_k\subseteq\mathcal I\).
knowledge_statements.scope_note: Active-set SQP models for smooth inequality-constrained nonlinear programs.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex:
A multiplier-activity coupled SQP model is a family indexed by a pair \((\lambda_k,W_k)\) in which multiplier information controls curvature and activity information controls the constraint model. Its quadratic term uses
\[
B_k=B(x_k,\lambda_k)\approx\nabla_{xx}^2\mathcal L(x_k,\lambda_k),
\]
while its equality-constrained realization imposes
\[
c_i(x_k)+\nabla c_i(x_k)^Tp=0\quad(i\in\mathcal E\cup W_k)
\]
and omits inactive inequalities. In an inequality-QP realization, all linearized inequalities are retained and \(W_k\) is defined by those active at the QP solution; their QP multipliers become \(\lambda_{k+1}\). Consequently, changing either the multiplier estimate or the predicted activity set changes the local model, even at the same primal point.
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: A multiplier-activity coupled model is determined jointly by multiplier estimates and an active-set prediction. Multipliers enter the Lagrangian curvature, while the predicted active inequalities determine which constraint linearizations are imposed as equalities. In an inequality-QP variant, activity is inferred from the QP solution and the associated QP multipliers update the multiplier estimate.
knowledge_statements.conclusion_latex: The local model is indexed by \((\lambda_k,W_k)\), with curvature \(B(x_k,\lambda_k)\) and equality Jacobian formed from \(\mathcal E\cup W_k\).
equivalent_formulations_latex: IQP coupling defines \(W_k\) as the active set of the inequality-constrained QP.
EQP coupling chooses \(W_k\) first, using multiplier estimates or an auxiliary subproblem, and then solves an equality-constrained QP.
special_cases_latex: For equality-only problems, \(W_k=\varnothing\), so coupling remains only through \(\lambda_k\).
With affine constraints, multiplier changes do not alter exact curvature because \(\nabla^2c_i=0\).
immediate_consequences_latex: Correct identification of the optimal active set makes the local inequality problem behave as an equality-constrained SQP model.
boundary_notes: The definition does not prescribe a particular working-set selection rule.
Complementarity and sign conventions for inequality multipliers must match the chosen constraint convention.

notation.meaning: Predicted active subset of the inequality indices.

knowledge_statements.title: Working-Set Prediction Models
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: Predict an inequality as active when its slack is small and its estimated nonnegative multiplier exceeds a chosen threshold.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex: Let \(g_i(x)\geq0\), let \(\widehat\mu_{k,i}\geq0\) be multiplier estimates, and choose thresholds \(\tau_k^g\geq0\) and \(\tau_k^\mu\geq0\). The predicted working set is \[W_k=\{i:g_i(x_k)\leq\tau_k^g\ \text{and}\ \widehat\mu_{k,i}\geq\tau_k^\mu\}.\] Equality constraints are always included. The model predicts an inequality as active only when it is nearly binding and has sufficiently positive estimated multiplier; setting \(\tau_k^\mu=0\) gives a slack-only boundary with a sign check.
assumptions_latex: The inequality convention is \(g_i(x)\geq0\).
\(\widehat\mu_{k,i}\) and both thresholds are nonnegative.
knowledge_statements.conclusion_latex: \(W_k\) is the threshold-predicted active inequality set.
knowledge_statements.scope_note: Threshold predictor for inequalities written as \(g_i(x)\geq0\), using slack and multiplier estimates.

enrichment_metadata.review_comment: The threshold rule is a plausible working-set predictor and the condition content kind fits the container, but the particular conjunction of slack and multiplier thresholds is an algorithm-specific claim with no cited source.

knowledge_statements.title: Coupled Multiplier-Activity Models
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: Alternate multiplier estimation and active-set prediction until the two agree, then build the SQP model from the stabilized pair.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex: Initialize an inequality set \(W^{(0)}\). For \(j=0,1,\ldots\), form the Jacobian \(A(W^{(j)})\), compute \(\nu^{(j)}\) by least-squares stationarity, and update \[W^{(j+1)}=\{i:g_i(x_k)\leq\tau_g\ \text{and}\ \widehat\mu_i^{(j)}\geq\tau_\mu\}.\] Stop when \(W^{(j+1)}=W^{(j)}\), or at a prescribed iteration limit. Output the stabilized pair \((W_k,\widehat\nu_k)\), and use both the selected constraint Jacobian and these multipliers in the SQP quadratic model.
assumptions_latex: Inequalities are written as \(g_i(x)\geq0\).
The multiplier subproblem is solved for every trial working set.
\(\tau_g,\tau_\mu\geq0\).
knowledge_statements.conclusion_latex: At successful termination, \(W_k\) is invariant under the predictor generated by \(\widehat\nu_k\).
knowledge_statements.scope_note: Finite active-set/multiplier consistency iteration for an SQP local model.

notation.meaning: working set at coupling iteration j

enrichment_metadata.review_comment: The alternating finite-set procedure is a specific coupled algorithm with no source. At an iteration limit the output need not be stabilized, so the instruction to output the stabilized pair is also not valid for every stated stopping case.

children.title: Quasi-Newton SQP Methods
children.top_down_role: SQP families replacing exact Lagrangian curvature with secant approximations.

top_down_textbook_witnesses.source_query: Bertsekas, Constrained Optimization and Lagrange Multiplier Methods

knowledge_statements.slot_contract: State the canonical mathematical definition of the source node, with its domain, quantifiers, notation, and a precise source locator.
knowledge_statements.ambient_context_latex: Let \((x_k,\lambda_k)\) be successive SQP estimates for a twice differentiable constrained problem, and let \(B_k\in\mathbb S^n\).
knowledge_statements.scope_note: Smooth finite-dimensional SQP; this definition covers full- and reduced-space secant variants.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex:
A quasi-Newton SQP method replaces \(\nabla_{xx}^2\mathcal L(x_k,\lambda_k)\) in the SQP quadratic model by a symmetric approximation \(B_k\) updated from first-derivative information. In the canonical full-space construction,
\[
s_k=x_{k+1}-x_k,
\qquad
y_k=\nabla_x\mathcal L(x_{k+1},\lambda_{k+1})-\nabla_x\mathcal L(x_k,\lambda_{k+1}),
\]
and an update map \(\mathcal U\) defines \(B_{k+1}=\mathcal U(B_k,s_k,y_k)\), normally so that the secant equation \(B_{k+1}s_k=y_k\) holds whenever the update is accepted. The next SQP step is computed from the usual linearly constrained quadratic subproblem with \(B_k\) as its curvature matrix.
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: A quasi-Newton SQP method uses a symmetric approximation to the Lagrangian Hessian rather than recomputing exact second derivatives. The approximation is updated from a primal displacement and a change in the Lagrangian gradient evaluated with a common multiplier estimate. Accepted updates normally satisfy a secant equation. The resulting matrix supplies curvature to the next SQP subproblem.
knowledge_statements.conclusion_latex: \(B_{k+1}=\mathcal U(B_k,s_k,y_k)\) with canonical pairs \(s_k=x_{k+1}-x_k\) and \(y_k=\nabla_x\mathcal L(x_{k+1},\lambda_{k+1})-\nabla_x\mathcal L(x_k,\lambda_{k+1})\).
equivalent_formulations_latex: The method applies ordinary quasi-Newton updating to \(x\mapsto\mathcal L(x,\lambda_{k+1})\) with the multiplier held fixed across the gradient difference.
A reduced-space variant imposes a secant equation on a projected Lagrangian-gradient difference.
special_cases_latex: Choosing \(\mathcal U\) as BFGS gives a BFGS-SQP model.
Choosing \(\mathcal U\) as SR1 gives an SR1-SQP model.
immediate_consequences_latex: Only first derivatives of the objective and constraints are required to form the canonical correction pair.
boundary_notes: A generic approximation unrelated to derivative differences is not quasi-Newton merely because it replaces the Hessian.
Safeguarding may modify the secant vector or skip an unsafe update.

children.title: Full-Space Quasi-Newton SQP
children.top_down_role: Secant approximations maintained in the full primal space.

knowledge_statements.slot_contract: State the canonical mathematical definition of the source node, with its domain, quantifiers, notation, and a precise source locator.
knowledge_statements.ambient_context_latex: Let the primal variable lie in \(\mathbb R^n\), and let \(s_k,y_k\in\mathbb R^n\) be the full-space Lagrangian correction pair.
knowledge_statements.scope_note: Dense, sparse, factored, or matrix-free representations qualify if they define the approximate operator on all of \(\mathbb R^n\).
knowledge_statements.statement_latex:
A full-space quasi-Newton SQP model maintains \(B_k\in\mathbb S^n\) as an approximation to the complete primal operator \(\nabla_{xx}^2\mathcal L(x_k,\lambda_k)\). With
\[
s_k=x_{k+1}-x_k,
\qquad y_k=\nabla_x\mathcal L(x_{k+1},\lambda_{k+1})-\nabla_x\mathcal L(x_k,\lambda_{k+1}),
\]
the accepted update is defined on \(\mathbb R^n\) and ordinarily enforces \(B_{k+1}s_k=y_k\). The entire matrix or operator is then used in the primal block of the SQP KKT system. This distinguishes the model from one that stores only \(Z_k^TB_kZ_k\) on a tangent subspace.
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: Full-space quasi-Newton SQP maintains a symmetric secant approximation on every primal direction. Its correction vectors are full-dimensional Lagrangian-gradient data, and the resulting operator occupies the primal curvature block of the complete SQP KKT system. It is distinct from reduced-space updating, which retains only projected tangent curvature.
knowledge_statements.conclusion_latex: \(B_k:\mathbb R^n\to\mathbb R^n\) is updated from full-space pairs and used through \(\tfrac12p^TB_kp\) for arbitrary \(p\in\mathbb R^n\).
equivalent_formulations_latex: A factored representation is full-space if it permits \(B_kv\) for every \(v\in\mathbb R^n\).
The induced reduced approximation for a basis \(Z_k\) is \(Z_k^TB_kZ_k\), but it is not the stored object defining this family.
special_cases_latex: Full-space BFGS and full-space SR1 are obtained by their respective update maps.
immediate_consequences_latex: Dense storage generally requires \(O(n^2)\) memory unless structure or a compact representation is used.
boundary_notes: Full-space does not imply dense storage.
A positive-definite update may fail to reproduce negative curvature of the true Lagrangian Hessian.

knowledge_statements.title: BFGS SQP Models
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: BFGS updates the full-space Lagrangian Hessian approximation from primal and Lagrangian-gradient differences while preserving positive definiteness under positive curvature.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex: Given \(B_k\in\mathbb S_{++}^n\), set \(s_k=x_{k+1}-x_k\) and \(y_k=\nabla_xL(x_{k+1},\lambda_{k+1})-\nabla_xL(x_k,\lambda_{k+1})\). If \(s_k^{\mathsf T}y_k>0\), update \[B_{k+1}=B_k-\frac{B_ks_ks_k^{\mathsf T}B_k}{s_k^{\mathsf T}B_ks_k}+\frac{y_ky_k^{\mathsf T}}{s_k^{\mathsf T}y_k}.\] Otherwise apply a prescribed safeguard or retain \(B_k\). Use \(B_{k+1}\) as the full-space Lagrangian curvature matrix in the next SQP subproblem.
assumptions_latex: \(B_k\) is symmetric positive definite.
\(s_k\neq0\) and the displayed Lagrangian gradients exist.
\(s_k^{\mathsf T}y_k>0\) for the undamped update.
knowledge_statements.conclusion_latex: The update satisfies \(B_{k+1}s_k=y_k\) and \(B_{k+1}\in\mathbb S_{++}^n\).
knowledge_statements.scope_note: Full-space BFGS approximation to the primal Hessian of the Lagrangian.

knowledge_statements.slot_contract: State the canonical mathematical definition of the source node, with its domain, quantifiers, notation, and a precise source locator.
knowledge_statements.ambient_context_latex: Let \(B_k\in\mathbb S^n\), \(s_k=x_{k+1}-x_k\), and \(y_k=\nabla_x\mathcal L(x_{k+1},\lambda_{k+1})-\nabla_x\mathcal L(x_k,\lambda_{k+1})\).
knowledge_statements.scope_note: Full-space direct-Hessian BFGS updating for smooth SQP; reduced-coordinate BFGS uses the same formula with projected pairs.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex:
A BFGS SQP model uses the curvature update
\[
B_{k+1}=B_k-\frac{B_ks_ks_k^TB_k}{s_k^TB_ks_k}+\frac{y_ky_k^T}{y_k^Ts_k},
\]
whenever its denominators are nonzero and the update is accepted. It satisfies \(B_{k+1}s_k=y_k\) and preserves symmetry. If \(B_k\succ0\) and \(y_k^Ts_k>0\), then \(B_{k+1}\succ0\). The matrix \(B_{k+1}\) supplies the quadratic curvature in the next linearly constrained SQP subproblem. A damped BFGS SQP model replaces \(y_k\) by a safeguarded vector before applying the same rank-two formula.
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: A BFGS SQP model updates the Lagrangian-Hessian approximation by the direct BFGS rank-two formula using the primal displacement and Lagrangian-gradient change. The update is symmetric, satisfies the secant equation, and preserves positive definiteness when the old matrix is positive definite and the curvature inner product is positive. Damped BFGS modifies the gradient-difference vector before this formula is applied.
knowledge_statements.conclusion_latex: \(B_{k+1}=B_k-(B_ks_ks_k^TB_k)/(s_k^TB_ks_k)+(y_ky_k^T)/(y_k^Ts_k)\).
equivalent_formulations_latex: The inverse update is \(H_{k+1}=(I-\rho_ks_ky_k^T)H_k(I-\rho_ky_ks_k^T)+\rho_ks_ks_k^T\), where \(H_k=B_k^{-1}\) and \(\rho_k=(y_k^Ts_k)^{-1}\).
special_cases_latex: If the correction pair is expressed in reduced coordinates, the same formula updates the reduced Hessian approximation.
immediate_consequences_latex: For \(B_k\succ0\), the curvature condition \(y_k^Ts_k>0\) keeps the SQP quadratic curvature positive definite.
boundary_notes: Undamped BFGS may be unsuitable when the true Lagrangian Hessian is indefinite.
The formula is undefined when either denominator vanishes.

knowledge_statements.title: SR1 SQP Models
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: SR1 adds a symmetric rank-one correction only when the secant residual is nonzero and its denominator is safely separated from zero; the resulting model can retain negative curvature.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex:
Given \(B_k\in\mathbb S^n\), define \(s_k=x_{k+1}-x_k\), \(y_k=
abla_xL(x_{k+1},\lambda_{k+1})-
abla_xL(x_k,\lambda_{k+1})\), and \(r_k=y_k-B_ks_k\). For a prescribed \(\varepsilon\in(0,1)\), perform \[B_{k+1}=B_k+ rac{r_kr_k^{\mathsf T}}{r_k^{\mathsf T}s_k}\] when \(r_k
eq0\) and \[|r_k^{\mathsf T}s_k|\geq\varepsilon\|r_k\|_2\|s_k\|_2.\] Otherwise set \(B_{k+1}=B_k\). An accepted update is symmetric, satisfies the secant equation, and may be indefinite.

\(s_k\neq0\) and the displayed Lagrangian gradients exist.
\(\varepsilon\in(0,1)\).
knowledge_statements.conclusion_latex: \(An\ accepted\ update\ satisfies\ B_{k+1}s_k=y_k\ and\ need\ not\ be\ positive\ definite.\)

knowledge_statements.slot_contract: State the canonical mathematical definition of the source node, with its domain, quantifiers, notation, and a precise source locator.
knowledge_statements.ambient_context_latex: Let \(B_k\in\mathbb S^n\) and let \((s_k,y_k)\) be the full-space Lagrangian correction pair used by SQP.
knowledge_statements.scope_note: Smooth SQP with a symmetric rank-one curvature approximation; indefinite matrices are permitted.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex:
An SR1 SQP model updates the Lagrangian-Hessian approximation by
\[
B_{k+1}=B_k+\frac{(y_k-B_ks_k)(y_k-B_ks_k)^T}{(y_k-B_ks_k)^Ts_k},
\]
provided the denominator is sufficiently separated from zero; otherwise the update is skipped. Whenever defined, the update is symmetric, has rank-one correction, and satisfies \(B_{k+1}s_k=y_k\). Unlike BFGS, SR1 does not impose positive definiteness, so it can retain negative-curvature information from an indefinite Lagrangian Hessian. The resulting \(B_{k+1}\) is used as the curvature operator in a subsequent SQP subproblem, commonly within a trust-region framework capable of handling indefiniteness.
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: An SR1 SQP model applies the symmetric rank-one formula to Lagrangian-gradient correction data. The formula satisfies the secant equation when its denominator is safely nonzero. It need not preserve positive definiteness and can therefore encode negative curvature, which is useful in trust-region SQP. A near-zero denominator triggers a skipped update.
knowledge_statements.conclusion_latex: \(B_{k+1}=B_k+((y_k-B_ks_k)(y_k-B_ks_k)^T)/((y_k-B_ks_k)^Ts_k)\) whenever the safeguarding test accepts the denominator.
equivalent_formulations_latex: Writing \(r_k=y_k-B_ks_k\), the correction is \(r_kr_k^T/(r_k^Ts_k)\).
special_cases_latex: Projected correction pairs yield a reduced-space SR1 model.
If \(y_k=B_ks_k\), the current matrix already satisfies the new secant equation and no correction is needed.
immediate_consequences_latex: The sign of \((y_k-B_ks_k)^Ts_k\) may make the rank-one correction positive or negative semidefinite.
boundary_notes: Indefinite SR1 curvature may require a trust region or another mechanism that makes the QP step well defined.
The denominator safeguard is part of a numerically meaningful SR1 model.

knowledge_statements.scope_note: The canonical representative is damped BFGS; denominator tests and skipped SR1 updates are related members of the broader safeguarded family.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex:
A safeguarded SQP update is a quasi-Newton update equipped with an acceptance, damping, or regularization rule preventing unsuitable correction data from producing an undefined or undesired curvature model. Canonical damped BFGS sets
\[
r_k=\theta_ky_k+(1-\theta_k)B_ks_k,
\]
where
\[
\theta_k=1\ \text{if }s_k^Ty_k\ge0.2s_k^TB_ks_k,
\]
and otherwise
\[
\theta_k=\frac{0.8s_k^TB_ks_k}{s_k^TB_ks_k-s_k^Ty_k}.
\]
It then applies BFGS with \(r_k\):
\[
B_{k+1}=B_k-\frac{B_ks_ks_k^TB_k}{s_k^TB_ks_k}+\frac{r_kr_k^T}{s_k^Tr_k}.
\]
For \(B_k\succ0\), this rule enforces \(s_k^Tr_k\ge0.2s_k^TB_ks_k>0\).
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: A safeguarded SQP update tests or modifies curvature data before updating the Lagrangian-Hessian approximation. In canonical damped BFGS, the raw gradient difference is blended with the current matrix action whenever its curvature is too small. The resulting vector has a guaranteed positive curvature inner product and is inserted into the ordinary BFGS formula, preserving positive definiteness.
knowledge_statements.conclusion_latex: Damped BFGS produces \(s_k^Tr_k\ge0.2s_k^TB_ks_k>0\) and updates \(B_k\) using \(r_k\) instead of \(y_k\).
equivalent_formulations_latex: When the curvature test passes, \(\theta_k=1\) and the safeguarded update equals ordinary BFGS.
When damping is active, \(s_k^Tr_k=0.2s_k^TB_ks_k\).
special_cases_latex: An SR1 denominator test that skips the update when \(|(y_k-B_ks_k)^Ts_k|\) is too small is another safeguard.
immediate_consequences_latex: If \(B_k\succ0\), damped BFGS yields \(B_{k+1}\succ0\).
boundary_notes: Safeguarding changes the exact secant equation from \(B_{k+1}s_k=y_k\) to \(B_{k+1}s_k=r_k\) when damping is active.
Positive-definiteness safeguards can suppress genuine negative curvature.

knowledge_statements.title: Damped Quasi-Newton Updates
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: Powell damping forms the secant displacement from Lagrangian gradients evaluated with the same new multiplier, then blends that displacement with the current model prediction until the BFGS curvature condition is safely positive.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex: Let \(L(x,\lambda)\) denote the SQP Lagrangian, let \(B_k\in\mathbb S_{++}^n\), choose \(\eta\in(0,1)\), and define \(s_k=x_{k+1}-x_k\) and \(y_k=\nabla_xL(x_{k+1},\lambda_{k+1})-\nabla_xL(x_k,\lambda_{k+1})\). Set \[\theta_k=\begin{cases}1,&s_k^{\mathsf T}y_k\geq\eta s_k^{\mathsf T}B_ks_k,\\\dfrac{(1-\eta)s_k^{\mathsf T}B_ks_k}{s_k^{\mathsf T}B_ks_k-s_k^{\mathsf T}y_k},&\text{otherwise},\end{cases}\] and set \(\bar y_k=\theta_ky_k+(1-\theta_k)B_ks_k\). Apply the BFGS formula with \(\bar y_k\) in place of \(y_k\). Then \[s_k^{\mathsf T}\bar y_k\geq\eta s_k^{\mathsf T}B_ks_k>0.\]
assumptions_latex: \(B_k\) is symmetric positive definite.
\(s_k=x_{k+1}-x_k\neq0\), and the displayed Lagrangian gradients exist.
knowledge_statements.conclusion_latex: \(Damped\ BFGS\ is\ well\ defined\ and\ produces\ B_{k+1}\in\mathbb S_{++}^n.\)
knowledge_statements.scope_note: Powell-damped BFGS update enforcing positive curvature relative to the current SQP Hessian model.

knowledge_statements.title: Curvature-Safeguarded Updates
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: Safeguards accept BFGS-type updates only with adequate positive curvature and accept SR1 updates only when the secant residual is nonzero and the rank-one denominator is not relatively small.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex: For a secant pair \((s_k,y_k)\) with \(s_k\neq0\), a positive-definite BFGS-family update is curvature-safeguarded when a modified vector \(\bar y_k\) is chosen so that \[s_k^{\mathsf T}\bar y_k\geq\delta\,s_k^{\mathsf T}B_ks_k>0\] for a fixed \(\delta\in(0,1)\). Define the SR1 residual by \(r_k=y_k-B_ks_k\). An SR1-family update is denominator-safeguarded when \(r_k\neq0\) and \[|r_k^{\mathsf T}s_k|\geq\varepsilon\|r_k\|_2\|s_k\|_2\] for a fixed \(\varepsilon\in(0,1)\). Only updates satisfying their corresponding predicate are accepted.
assumptions_latex: \(B_k\) is symmetric and \(s_k\neq0\).
\(\delta\in(0,1)\) and \(\varepsilon\in(0,1)\).
knowledge_statements.conclusion_latex: \(Accepted\ updates\ avoid\ the\ designated\ curvature\ or\ denominator\ degeneracy.\)
knowledge_statements.scope_note: Acceptance conditions preventing inadequate positive curvature in BFGS-family updates and unstable denominators in SR1-family updates.

knowledge_statements.title: Update Rejection Boundaries
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: Reject undamped BFGS at nonpositive curvature. Reject the SR1 correction when its residual is zero or when its correction denominator is relatively too small, because the quotient is then undefined or unstable.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex: For BFGS, the term \(y_ky_k^{\mathsf T}/(s_k^{\mathsf T}y_k)\) is undefined when \(s_k^{\mathsf T}y_k=0\), and positive definiteness is not guaranteed when \(s_k^{\mathsf T}y_k\leq0\). For SR1, define \(r_k=y_k-B_ks_k\). Its correction is undefined when \(r_k^{\mathsf T}s_k=0\) and can be arbitrarily large near that boundary. Hence reject undamped BFGS when \[s_k^{\mathsf T}y_k\leq0,\] and reject the SR1 correction when \[r_k=0\quad\text{or}\quad |r_k^{\mathsf T}s_k|<\varepsilon\|r_k\|_2\|s_k\|_2,\] where \(\varepsilon\in(0,1)\).
assumptions_latex: \(s_k\neq0\) and \(B_k\) is symmetric.
\(\varepsilon\in(0,1)\) is a prescribed rejection tolerance.
knowledge_statements.conclusion_latex: \(The\ displayed\ predicates\ define\ rejection\ boundaries\ for\ the\ corresponding\ undamped\ updates.\)
knowledge_statements.scope_note: Algebraic boundaries at which standard undamped BFGS or SR1 updates lose their guarantees or become undefined or unstable.

knowledge_statements.slot_contract: State the canonical mathematical definition of the source node, with its domain, quantifiers, notation, and a precise source locator.
knowledge_statements.ambient_context_latex: Let \(A_kZ_k=0\), where \(Z_k\in\mathbb R^{n\times r}\) is a tangent-space basis and \(r=n-\operatorname{rank}(A_k)\).
knowledge_statements.scope_note: Equality-constrained or working-set SQP with quasi-Newton curvature maintained in tangent coordinates.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex:
A reduced-space quasi-Newton SQP model maintains \(M_k\in\mathbb S^r\) as an approximation to
\[
Z_k^T\nabla_{xx}^2\mathcal L(x_k,\lambda_k)Z_k.
\]
For a step \(x_{k+1}-x_k=\alpha_k(Y_kp_Y+Z_kp_Z)\), canonical reduced correction vectors are
\[
s_k^{R}=\alpha_kp_Z,
\qquad y_k^{R}=Z_k^T[\nabla_x\mathcal L(x_{k+1},\lambda_{k+1})-\nabla_x\mathcal L(x_k,\lambda_{k+1})].
\]
A symmetric update, such as BFGS or SR1, produces \(M_{k+1}\) and ordinarily enforces \(M_{k+1}s_k^R=y_k^R\). The tangential step is then computed from a reduced system such as \(M_kp_Z=-Z_k^T\nabla f(x_k)\).
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: Reduced-space quasi-Newton SQP updates only the Lagrangian curvature seen along tangent directions. The primal displacement and Lagrangian-gradient change are expressed or projected into null-space coordinates, and a symmetric secant formula updates a smaller matrix. That matrix determines the tangential component of the SQP step, while linearized feasibility determines the normal component.
knowledge_statements.conclusion_latex: \(M_k\approx Z_k^T\nabla_{xx}^2\mathcal L_kZ_k\) and accepted updates satisfy \(M_{k+1}s_k^R=y_k^R\).
equivalent_formulations_latex: The update acts on the tangent-space quadratic form rather than on a complete \(n\times n\) approximation.
Under a fixed orthonormal basis, reduced BFGS or SR1 is the ordinary formula applied in \(\mathbb R^r\).
special_cases_latex: If \(Z_k=I\), reduced-space updating coincides with full-space updating.
immediate_consequences_latex: The stored matrix has \(r(r+1)/2\) independent entries rather than \(n(n+1)/2\).
boundary_notes: When \(Z_k\) changes, correction pairs must be expressed consistently in the selected reduced coordinates.
The standard reduced model omits a normal-tangential cross term.

knowledge_statements.title: Explicit Reduced-Hessian Updates
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: Store curvature only in null-space coordinates, transport it when the basis changes, and apply a reduced BFGS update to reduced secant data.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex: Let \(Z_k\) span \(\ker A_k\), let \(p_k\) be the reduced step, and let \(H_k\in\mathbb S^{r}\) be stored explicitly. Form a reduced gradient displacement \(q_k\), expressed in the same reduced coordinates as \(p_k\). When \(p_k^{\mathsf T}q_k>0\), apply \[H_{k+1}=H_k-\frac{H_kp_kp_k^{\mathsf T}H_k}{p_k^{\mathsf T}H_kp_k}+\frac{q_kq_k^{\mathsf T}}{p_k^{\mathsf T}q_k}.\] If the null-space basis changes, first transport \(H_k,p_k,q_k\) to a common basis. Output \(H_{k+1}\) for the next reduced SQP subproblem.
assumptions_latex: \(Z_k\) has orthonormal columns spanning the current tangent space.
\(H_k\) is symmetric positive definite.
\(p_k^{\mathsf T}q_k>0\) for the undamped update.
knowledge_statements.conclusion_latex: The update satisfies \(H_{k+1}p_k=q_k\) and preserves positive definiteness in reduced coordinates.
knowledge_statements.scope_note: Quasi-Newton curvature updated and stored directly in current null-space coordinates.

enrichment_metadata.review_comment: The fixed-coordinate reduced BFGS formula is standard, but the record additionally claims that H_k, p_k, and q_k can first be transported whenever the null-space basis changes. No transport map is defined, and changing tangent subspaces generally requires more than a coordinate change. The cited broad quasi-Newton locators do not establish this implementation-dependent construction.

knowledge_statements.statement_title: Explicit matrix update in reduced coordinates
knowledge_statements.ambient_context_latex: Let \(Z_k\in\mathbb R^{n\times r}\) be an explicitly available null-space basis, and let reduced vectors \(s_k^R,y_k^R\in\mathbb R^r\) be expressed in its coordinates.
knowledge_statements.scope_note: Reduced-space SQP methods that form and retain the reduced curvature matrix itself.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex:
An explicit reduced-Hessian update stores a symmetric matrix \(M_k\in\mathbb S^r\) directly in tangent coordinates and applies a finite-dimensional secant formula to it:
\[
M_{k+1}=\mathcal U_R(M_k,s_k^R,y_k^R),
\qquad M_{k+1}s_k^R=y_k^R
\]
when the update is accepted. The matrix \(M_k\) is intended to approximate \(Z_k^T\nabla_{xx}^2\mathcal L_kZ_k\), and the reduced step equation is formed explicitly as
\[
M_kp_Z=-Z_k^T\nabla f(x_k).
\]
For reduced BFGS or SR1, \(\mathcal U_R\) is the corresponding standard formula in \(\mathbb R^r\). Explicitness means that entries or factors of \(M_k\), not merely products with an unreduced operator, constitute the maintained curvature state.
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: An explicit reduced-Hessian method stores the symmetric tangent-space curvature matrix in reduced coordinates. It updates that matrix directly using reduced secant vectors and forms the smaller tangential linear system from it. This differs from an implicit method that obtains reduced products by projecting a full-space operator without storing the reduced matrix itself.
knowledge_statements.conclusion_latex: The maintained state contains \(M_k\in\mathbb S^r\) explicitly, with \(M_k\approx Z_k^T\nabla_{xx}^2\mathcal L_kZ_k\).
equivalent_formulations_latex: Storing a Cholesky or symmetric-indefinite factorization of \(M_k\) is explicit reduced storage because the factorization represents the reduced matrix itself.
special_cases_latex: Reduced BFGS gives the direct rank-two update of \(M_k\).
Reduced SR1 gives the direct rank-one update of \(M_k\).
immediate_consequences_latex: If \(r\ll n\), direct reduced storage may be substantially smaller than full-space storage.
boundary_notes: An explicit matrix must be transformed or reinitialized when the reduced-coordinate basis changes incompatibly.
The definition does not require \(M_k\) to be positive definite.

knowledge_statements.scope_note: Equality-constrained SQP construction using a null-space decomposition, least-squares multipliers, omission of vanishing cross terms, and a reduced secant update.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex:
Let $A_k$ have full row rank, and let the columns of $Y_k$ and $Z_k$ span $\operatorname{range}(A_k^T)$ and $\ker(A_k)$, respectively. Decompose
\[
p_k=Y_kp_Y+Z_kp_z,
\]
where
\[
(A_kY_k)p_Y=-c_k,
\]
and the exact tangential equation is
\[
(Z_k^T\nabla_{xx}^2\mathcal L_kZ_k)p_z=-Z_k^T\nabla_{xx}^2\mathcal L_kY_kp_Y-Z_k^T\nabla f_k.
\]
With $Y_k=A_k^T$, deleting the Hessian-step term from the multiplier equation gives the least-squares estimate
\[
\widehat\lambda_{k+1}=(A_kA_k^T)^{-1}A_k\nabla f_k
=\arg\min_\lambda\|\nabla f_k-A_k^T\lambda\|_2^2.
\]
Dropping the normal-tangential cross term gives
\[
(Z_k^T\nabla_{xx}^2\mathcal L_kZ_k)p_z=-Z_k^T\nabla f_k.
\]
Approximate the reduced Hessian by $M_{k+1}$ satisfying
\[
M_{k+1}s_k=y_k,\quad s_k=\alpha_kp_z,
\]
\[
y_k=Z_k^T\!\left[\nabla_x\mathcal L(x_k+\alpha_kp_k,\lambda_{k+1})-\nabla_x\mathcal L(x_k,\lambda_{k+1})\right],
\]
and obtain $M_{k+1}$ with BFGS or SR1. The omitted terms are asymptotically justified when $p_k\to0$ and the normal component tends to zero faster than the tangential component; outside that regime the simplified equations are only approximations.
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: For equality-constrained SQP, split the step into range-space and null-space components. The constraints determine the range-space component, while Lagrangian curvature determines the null-space component. Full row rank permits a least-squares multiplier estimate. Omitting the normal–tangential curvature term leaves only the reduced Hessian to approximate, and BFGS or SR1 can update that matrix using projected Lagrangian-gradient differences. The omissions are justified near a solution under the stated vanishing-step behavior, not as exact identities in general.
assumptions_latex: A_k\in\mathbb R^{m\times n}\text{ has full row rank}
\operatorname{range}(Y_k)=\operatorname{range}(A_k^T)
\operatorname{range}(Z_k)=\ker(A_k)
p_k=Y_kp_Y+Z_kp_z
\text{For the asymptotic simplifications: }p_k\to0\text{ and }\|p_Y\|\text{ tends to zero faster than }\|p_z\|.
knowledge_statements.conclusion_latex: \text{The SQP curvature model can be maintained solely as a quasi-Newton approximation to }Z_k^T\nabla_{xx}^2\mathcal L_kZ_k\text{, with the stated least-squares multiplier and projected secant pair.}

knowledge_statements.title: Implicit Reduced-Hessian Updates
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: Reduced curvature is stored in a full-space operator and accessed by projection onto feasible tangent directions; projected displacement and gradient-change vectors impose the secant equation.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex: At iterate \(x_k\), let \(A_k\) be the active-constraint Jacobian and let \(P_k\) be a projector onto \(\ker A_k\). A symmetric full-space operator \(B_k\) implicitly represents the reduced Hessian by \[H_k^{\mathrm{red}}[p,q]=p^{\mathsf T}B_kq,\qquad p,q\in\ker A_k.\] If a factorization applies \(P_k\) without forming a basis, then the reduced quasi-Newton action is \(p\mapsto P_kB_kP_kp\). A projected secant update uses \(s_k=P_k(x_{k+1}-x_k)\) and \(y_k=P_k(\nabla_xL_{k+1}-\nabla_xL_k)\), enforcing \(P_kB_{k+1}P_ks_k=y_k\) when the projected curvature condition holds.
assumptions_latex: \(A_k\in\mathbb R^{m\times n}\) has constant rank locally.
\(B_k\in\mathbb R^{n\times n}\) is symmetric.
\(P_k^2=P_k=P_k^{\mathsf T}\) and \(\operatorname{range}(P_k)=\ker A_k\).
knowledge_statements.conclusion_latex: \(P_kB_kP_k\) supplies the reduced-Hessian action without explicitly forming reduced coordinates.
knowledge_statements.scope_note: Operator representation of reduced Lagrangian curvature without explicitly forming a null-space matrix or reduced Hessian.

knowledge_statements.scope_note: Large-scale reduced SQP where tangent curvature is accessed through operator products or projections rather than an explicitly stored reduced matrix.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex:
An implicit reduced-Hessian model represents the reduced operator through
\[
\mathcal R_k z:=Z_k^T\mathcal B_k(Z_kz),\qquad z\in\mathbb R^r,
\]
without forming or storing the matrix \(Z_k^T\mathcal B_kZ_k\). The underlying state may be a full-space quasi-Newton operator, a compact secant representation, a factorization, or routines applying \(Z_k\), \(Z_k^T\), and \(\mathcal B_k\). A reduced linear solver obtains the tangential step using only products \(z\mapsto\mathcal R_kz\). The model is an implicit reduced-Hessian update when changes to the underlying state alter these projected products and thereby update tangent curvature, while no independent \(r\times r\) reduced matrix is maintained.
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: An implicit reduced-Hessian method accesses tangent curvature by projecting the action of another operator: map a reduced vector into the primal space, apply the curvature operator, and project back. The reduced matrix is never assembled. Updating the underlying operator, compact representation, or factors updates the induced reduced curvature used by an iterative tangential solver.
knowledge_statements.conclusion_latex: \(\mathcal R_kz=Z_k^T\mathcal B_kZ_kz\) is available for every \(z\in\mathbb R^r\), while \(Z_k^T\mathcal B_kZ_k\) need not be formed.
equivalent_formulations_latex: A projected Krylov method using only \(Z_k^T\mathcal B_kZ_kz\) products is an implicit realization.
If projection is implemented without an explicit \(Z_k\), the model remains implicit provided it applies the same tangent-space operator.
special_cases_latex: A full-space L-BFGS compact representation induces an implicit reduced L-BFGS operator by projection.
immediate_consequences_latex: Memory can be reduced when neither \(Z_k\) nor the reduced matrix is stored densely.
boundary_notes: Implicit representation does not mean inexactness; the projected action may equal the exact reduced Hessian.
The quality of the model depends on the underlying operator and not merely on the projection mechanism.

knowledge_statements.title: Limited-Memory SQP Models
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: A bounded history of Lagrangian secant pairs defines the SQP curvature model through compact BFGS recursions, avoiding storage of a dense Hessian approximation.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex: Given retained pairs \((s_i,y_i)\) for \(i=k-r,\ldots,k-1\), define \(\rho_i=(y_i^{\mathsf T}s_i)^{-1}\) and an initial symmetric positive-definite operator \(B_k^{(0)}=\gamma_k I\), where \(\gamma_k>0\). Applying, in chronological order, \[B^{+}=B-\frac{Bss^{\mathsf T}B}{s^{\mathsf T}Bs}+\frac{yy^{\mathsf T}}{y^{\mathsf T}s}\] to only the retained pairs defines the limited-memory SQP curvature operator \(B_k\). The SQP model is \(\nabla f(x_k)^{\mathsf T}d+\tfrac12d^{\mathsf T}B_kd\) subject to linearized constraints; products or inverse products are evaluated through the compact recursion without storing a dense matrix.
assumptions_latex: \(s_i=x_{i+1}-x_i\) and \(y_i=\nabla_xL(x_{i+1},\lambda_{i+1})-\nabla_xL(x_i,\lambda_{i+1})\).
\(y_i^{\mathsf T}s_i>0\) for every retained pair.
The memory parameter satisfies \(1\le r\ll n\).
knowledge_statements.conclusion_latex: The curvature model requires storage proportional to \(nr\), rather than \(n^2\).
knowledge_statements.scope_note: Compact limited-memory BFGS representation of SQP Lagrangian curvature.

notation.meaning: maximum number of retained secant pairs

An authoritative locator is needed for the limited-memory SQP specialization, including the stated Lagrangian secant-pair multiplier convention and compact storage claim.

knowledge_statements.slot_contract: State the canonical mathematical definition of the source node, with its domain, quantifiers, notation, and a precise source locator.
knowledge_statements.ambient_context_latex: Let \((s_i,y_i)\in\mathbb R^n\times\mathbb R^n\) be accepted Lagrangian correction pairs, and choose a memory parameter \(q\ge1\) independent of the iteration count.
knowledge_statements.scope_note: Large-scale SQP using compact quasi-Newton curvature; full- or reduced-space pairs may be used consistently.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex:
A limited-memory SQP model represents its quasi-Newton curvature using only the most recent \(q\) accepted correction pairs
\[
\{(s_i,y_i):i=k-q,\ldots,k-1\}
\]
and a simple initial operator \(B_k^0\) or \(H_k^0\), rather than storing a dense accumulated Hessian approximation. In limited-memory BFGS, these pairs define the result of applying the last \(q\) BFGS updates to the initial operator; matrix-vector or inverse-matrix-vector products are evaluated by a compact formula or two-loop recursion. After accepting a new pair, the oldest retained pair is discarded. The induced operator supplies the quadratic curvature or preconditioning action in the SQP subproblem.
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: A limited-memory SQP model retains a fixed number of recent Lagrangian secant pairs and a simple initial scaling instead of storing a dense Hessian approximation. These data implicitly represent a truncated sequence of quasi-Newton updates. Products required by the SQP subproblem are computed from the compact representation, and the oldest pair is discarded when a new pair is accepted.
knowledge_statements.conclusion_latex: The curvature state at iteration \(k\) consists of at most \(q\) correction pairs plus a simple initial operator, giving storage \(O(qn)\) in full coordinates.
equivalent_formulations_latex: L-BFGS inverse actions may be evaluated by the two-loop recursion without forming \(H_k\).
A compact direct-Hessian representation may instead supply \(B_kv\) products.
special_cases_latex: With \(q\ge k\) and no discarded pairs, the construction reproduces the corresponding full-history update from the selected initial operator.
Projected reduced pairs define a limited-memory reduced-space SQP model.
immediate_consequences_latex: For fixed \(q\), storage and product costs scale linearly with \(n\).
boundary_notes: Limited-memory refers to retained secant history, not merely sparse storage.
Curvature acceptance or damping remains necessary when pair quality is unsuitable.

children.title: Derivative-Approximation SQP Models
children.top_down_role: SQP models distinguished by numerical or operator-based derivative information.

knowledge_statements.slot_contract: State the canonical mathematical definition of the source node, with its domain, quantifiers, notation, and a precise source locator.
knowledge_statements.statement_title: SQP model with approximate derivative operators
knowledge_statements.ambient_context_latex: Let \(f:\mathbb R^n\to\mathbb R\) and \(c:\mathbb R^n\to\mathbb R^m\) be smooth, but suppose one or more derivative arrays are supplied only approximately.
knowledge_statements.scope_note: Deterministic smooth SQP with numerical, automatic, matrix-free, or structured approximations to first- or second-order derivative information.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex:
A derivative-approximation SQP model replaces at least one exact derivative in the canonical SQP subproblem by an approximation
\[
g_k\approx\nabla f(x_k),\qquad J_k\approx J_c(x_k),\qquad B_k\approx\nabla_{xx}^2\mathcal L(x_k,\lambda_k),
\]
and defines
\[
\min_p\;f(x_k)+g_k^Tp+\tfrac12p^TB_kp
\]
subject to the corresponding affine constraints \(c(x_k)+J_kp=0\) and/or inequalities. An operator-only model may specify \(J_kv\), \(J_k^Tw\), or \(B_kv\) without forming matrices. Finite differences, automatic differentiation, quasi-Newton secant updates, and structure-exploiting formulas are distinct constructions within this family; the approximation mechanism and its domain are part of the model definition.
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: A derivative-approximation SQP model substitutes approximate objective gradients, constraint Jacobians, Lagrangian curvature, or their operator actions into the standard quadratic subproblem. The approximations may be numerical, automatically differentiated, secant-based, matrix-free, or structure-specific. The model must specify which derivatives are approximated and how their actions enter the objective and affine constraints.
knowledge_statements.conclusion_latex: The SQP data are \((g_k,J_k,B_k)\) with at least one component differing from its exact derivative counterpart, and these data define the quadratic objective and affine constraint model.
equivalent_formulations_latex: A matrix-free model is defined by consistent derivative-vector products rather than explicit arrays.
A finite-difference Jacobian model constructs columns or products from perturbed constraint evaluations.
special_cases_latex: If only \(B_k\) is secant-updated, the model is quasi-Newton SQP.
If \(g_k\) and \(J_k\) are finite-differenced while \(B_k\) is quasi-Newton, both approximation mechanisms are present.
immediate_consequences_latex: Approximation errors affect both predicted stationarity and predicted feasibility when \(g_k\) and \(J_k\) are inexact.
boundary_notes: Exact automatic differentiation is not numerically approximate at the mathematical level, although finite-precision evaluation remains.
The definition alone imposes no convergence-accuracy condition.

notation.meaning: Exact or approximate constraint Jacobian used in the local model.

source_refs.locator: Chapter 18, §18.1, models (18.7) and (18.11); §18.3, derivative replacement in “Full Quasi-Newton Approximations”; Chapter 8, §8.1

children.title: Finite-Difference SQP Models
children.top_down_role: SQP models using numerically approximated derivative information.

knowledge_statements.title: Finite-Difference SQP Models
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: Function and constraint evaluations supply finite-difference gradients and Jacobians, which replace exact derivatives in the quadratic SQP subproblem.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex: For \(f:\mathbb R^n\to\mathbb R\), equality constraints \(c:\mathbb R^n\to\mathbb R^m\), iterate \(x_k\), and increments \(h_{k,j}>0\), compute \[g_{k,j}=\frac{f(x_k+h_{k,j}e_j)-f(x_k)}{h_{k,j}},\qquad (A_k)_{ij}=\frac{c_i(x_k+h_{k,j}e_j)-c_i(x_k)}{h_{k,j}}.\] Choose a symmetric curvature approximation \(B_k\), solve the SQP model \[\min_d\ g_k^{\mathsf T}d+\tfrac12d^{\mathsf T}B_kd\quad\text{subject to}\quad c(x_k)+A_kd=0,\] apply the method's globalization rule, and stop when its approximate feasibility and stationarity residuals meet prescribed tolerances.
assumptions_latex: \(f\) and \(c\) are continuously differentiable near \(x_k\).
\(h_{k,j}>0\) are chosen above the function-evaluation noise scale.
\(B_k=B_k^{\mathsf T}\).
knowledge_statements.conclusion_latex: The displayed finite-difference quantities define a derivative-approximation SQP model at \(x_k\).
knowledge_statements.scope_note: Forward-difference derivative construction for a smooth finite-dimensional SQP subproblem.

source_witnesses.locator: 2.3.5. Finite-Difference Approximations to Derivatives p. 54
3.5.3 Sequential quadratic programming (SQP) p. 107

knowledge_statements.slot_contract: State the canonical mathematical definition of the source node, with its domain, quantifiers, notation, and a precise source locator.
knowledge_statements.ambient_context_latex: Let \(F=(f,c):\mathbb R^n\to\mathbb R^{m+1}\) be evaluable near \(x_k\), let \(e_j\) be the \(j\)-th coordinate vector, and choose nonzero differencing intervals \(h_{k,j}\).
knowledge_statements.scope_note: Deterministic finite-dimensional SQP whose required derivatives are obtained from nearby function or gradient evaluations.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex:
A finite-difference SQP model constructs one or more derivative arrays from finite perturbations. The forward-difference objective gradient and constraint-Jacobian columns are
\[
(g_k)_j=\frac{f(x_k+h_{k,j}e_j)-f(x_k)}{h_{k,j}},
\qquad (J_k)_{:j}=\frac{c(x_k+h_{k,j}e_j)-c(x_k)}{h_{k,j}}.
\]
A centered model replaces each numerator by the difference between values at \(x_k+h_{k,j}e_j\) and \(x_k-h_{k,j}e_j\), divided by \(2h_{k,j}\). A Hessian-vector action may likewise be approximated by
\[
B_kv=\frac{\nabla_x\mathcal L(x_k+hv,\lambda_k)-\nabla_x\mathcal L(x_k,\lambda_k)}{h}.
\]
These approximate quantities replace their exact counterparts in the SQP quadratic objective and affine constraints.
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: A finite-difference SQP model estimates objective gradients, constraint-Jacobian columns, or Lagrangian-Hessian products from evaluations at perturbed points. Forward differences use a base value and one displaced value; centered differences use symmetric displacements. The resulting approximate derivatives are inserted into the standard SQP objective and constraint linearizations.
knowledge_statements.conclusion_latex: The model uses finite-difference data \(g_k\), \(J_k\), or \(B_kv\) computed from nonzero perturbations of \(x_k\).
equivalent_formulations_latex: For a vector function \(c\), a directional Jacobian product is \(J_c(x_k)v\approx[c(x_k+hv)-c(x_k)]/h\).
Centered first derivatives use \([F(x_k+he_j)-F(x_k-he_j)]/(2h)\).
special_cases_latex: Forward differences have truncation error \(O(h)\) under bounded second derivatives.
Centered first differences have truncation error \(O(h^2)\) when the required higher regularity holds.
immediate_consequences_latex: Forming a dense forward-difference Jacobian columnwise requires a base evaluation and one perturbed evaluation per variable.
boundary_notes: Choosing \(h\) too small amplifies floating-point cancellation; choosing it too large increases truncation error.
Noisy evaluations may require differencing intervals and error models different from the smooth deterministic formulas.

notation.meaning: Approximate column \(j\) of the constraint Jacobian.

children.title: Matrix-Free SQP Curvature Models
children.top_down_role: SQP curvature represented through operator actions rather than explicit matrices.

knowledge_statements.title: Matrix-Free SQP Curvature Models
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: The SQP quadratic model is exposed through Hessian-vector actions, enabling Krylov solution of large subproblems without forming or storing a curvature matrix.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex: At \((x_k,\lambda_k)\), a matrix-free curvature model is a self-adjoint linear operator \(\mathcal B_k:\mathbb R^n\to\mathbb R^n\) accessed only through products \(v\mapsto\mathcal B_kv\). The quadratic term is defined by \[q_k(d)=\tfrac12\langle d,\mathcal B_kd\rangle.\] An admissible finite-difference Lagrangian Hessian action is \[\mathcal B_kv=\frac{\nabla_xL(x_k+\tau_kv,\lambda_k)-\nabla_xL(x_k,\lambda_k)}{\tau_k},\qquad \tau_k>0,\] optionally symmetrized or replaced by a quasi-Newton product. A Krylov subproblem solver may use these actions and Jacobian products without assembling \(\mathcal B_k\).
assumptions_latex: \(L(\cdot,\lambda_k)\) is twice continuously differentiable near \(x_k\).
\(\mathcal B_k\) is self-adjoint for the quadratic model.
\(\tau_k>0\) is compatible with evaluation accuracy.
knowledge_statements.conclusion_latex: All curvature information required by the local quadratic model is obtainable from products \(\mathcal B_kv\).
knowledge_statements.scope_note: Hessian-vector product representation of SQP curvature for iterative subproblem solution.

enrichment_metadata.review_comment: No source is supplied, and the finite-difference gradient action displayed for finite \(\tau_k\) is generally nonlinear in \(v\) and need not define the self-adjoint linear operator asserted earlier. The phrase 'optionally symmetrized' does not specify a mathematically defined replacement. A sourced and internally consistent matrix-free variant is required.

knowledge_statements.slot_contract: State the canonical mathematical definition of the source node, with its domain, quantifiers, notation, and a precise source locator.
knowledge_statements.statement_title: Matrix-Free Curvature Model for an SQP Subproblem
knowledge_statements.ambient_context_latex:
Let \(f:\mathbb R^n	o\mathbb R\) and \(c:\mathbb R^n	o\mathbb R^m\) be twice continuously differentiable, let \(x_k\) be an SQP iterate, and write \(g_k=
abla f(x_k)\), \(A_k=
abla c(x_k)\), and \(c_k=c(x_k)\). Let \(B_k:\mathbb R^n	o\mathbb R^n\) be a self-adjoint linear operator modeling \(
abla_{xx}^2L(x_k,\lambda_k)\).
knowledge_statements.scope_note: Finite-dimensional smooth SQP with curvature accessed by operator products; no explicit dense or sparse Hessian matrix is required.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex: A matrix-free SQP curvature model is the quadratic local model \[m_k(p)=f(x_k)+g_k^Tp+\tfrac12p^TB_kp\] together with linearized constraints \(A_kp+c_k=0\), or the corresponding equality-and-inequality linearizations, where every inner computation is permitted to access \(B_k\) only through products \(v\mapsto B_kv\). The model is therefore represented by the data \((g_k,c_k,A_k,\mathcal B_k)\), where \(\mathcal B_k(v)=B_kv\), rather than by stored entries of \(B_k\). In an equality-constrained step, projected Krylov iterations may equivalently access the reduced operator \(z\mapsto Z_k^TB_kZ_kz\), where \(A_kZ_k=0\), or an implicit projector onto \(\ker A_k\).
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: A matrix-free SQP curvature model is the usual quadratic SQP model, but its symmetric curvature operator is supplied only through Hessian-vector or approximation-vector products. The constraints are linearized at the current iterate. Equality-constrained inner iterations may act on the reduced curvature operator in the null space of the constraint Jacobian or use an implicit null-space projector. Storing or factoring the curvature matrix itself is not part of the definition.
assumptions_latex: \(f\) and the modeled constraints are differentiable at \(x_k\).
\(B_k\) is a self-adjoint linear operator on \(\mathbb R^n\).
The inner solver can evaluate \(B_kv\) for every requested \(v\in\mathbb R^n\).
knowledge_statements.conclusion_latex: The SQP curvature term is well defined by \(p^TB_kp/2\) using operator actions alone, and projected iterative solution can be performed without explicitly forming \(B_k\) or a null-space basis.
equivalent_formulations_latex: For equality constraints, the reduced model is \(m_k(Z_kz+p_k^N)\), whose reduced Hessian action is \(z\mapsto Z_k^TB_kZ_kz\).
An implicit projected formulation replaces explicit \(Z_k\) by a projector \(P_k\) satisfying \(\operatorname{range}(P_k)=\ker A_k\).
special_cases_latex: If \(B_kv=\nabla_{xx}^2L(x_k,\lambda_k)v\), the model is exact-curvature matrix-free SQP.
If \(B_k\) is a limited-memory quasi-Newton operator, the same definition gives limited-memory matrix-free SQP.
immediate_consequences_latex: Storage for curvature can be subquadratic in \(n\), depending on the operator implementation.
Projected conjugate-gradient or related Krylov methods can serve as inner equality-QP solvers.
boundary_notes: Matrix-free representation does not itself imply that the constraint Jacobian or its preconditioner is matrix-free.
Positive definiteness, forcing tolerances, and globalization are additional conditions, not part of this definition.

notation.meaning: A matrix whose columns span \(\ker A_k\).
An implicit projection onto the linearized tangent space.

source_refs.locator: Chapter 16, §16.3, “Iterative Solution of the KKT System,” especially Algorithms 16.1–16.2 and the implicit projection discussion following equation (16.27)

review_flags: The source directly supports operator-based projected iterative QP solution; the term “matrix-free SQP curvature model” is a scoped synthesis of that representation with the SQP model.

children.title: Structured Least-Squares SQP Models
children.top_down_role: Curvature models exploiting constrained nonlinear least-squares structure.

knowledge_statements.title: Structured Least-Squares SQP Models
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: Linearizing residuals produces a constrained linear least-squares subproblem, equivalently an SQP model with Gauss-Newton curvature.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex: Consider \(f(x)=\tfrac12\|r(x)\|_2^2\) with equality constraints \(c(x)=0\). At \(x_k\), let \(J_k=Dr(x_k)\) and \(A_k=Dc(x_k)\). The structured least-squares SQP subproblem is \[\min_d\ \tfrac12\|r(x_k)+J_kd\|_2^2\quad\text{subject to}\quad c(x_k)+A_kd=0.\] Equivalently, after discarding the constant term, its gradient and curvature are \(g_k=J_k^{\mathsf T}r(x_k)\) and \(B_k=J_k^{\mathsf T}J_k\). Thus residual-Jacobian products furnish positive-semidefinite Gauss-Newton curvature while retaining the linearized nonlinear constraints.
assumptions_latex: \(r:\mathbb R^n\to\mathbb R^p\) and \(c:\mathbb R^n\to\mathbb R^m\) are continuously differentiable.
The objective is exactly \(f(x)=\tfrac12\|r(x)\|_2^2\).
knowledge_statements.conclusion_latex: The structured curvature matrix is \(B_k=J_k^{\mathsf T}J_k\succeq0\).
knowledge_statements.scope_note: Gauss-Newton SQP model for equality-constrained nonlinear least squares.

source_witnesses.locator: 5.3 Linear Least-Squares Problems p. 106
3.5.3 Sequential quadratic programming (SQP) p. 107

knowledge_statements.slot_contract: State the canonical mathematical definition of the source node, with its domain, quantifiers, notation, and a precise source locator.
knowledge_statements.ambient_context_latex: Consider \(\min_x F(x)=\tfrac12\|r(x)\|_2^2\) subject to smooth constraints \(c_E(x)=0\) and \(c_I(x)\geq0\), where \(r:\mathbb R^n\to\mathbb R^q\). Let \(J_k=\nabla r(x_k)\), \(r_k=r(x_k)\), and let \(A_k\) denote the constraint Jacobian.
knowledge_statements.scope_note: Finite-dimensional constrained nonlinear least squares using Gauss–Newton or structured second-order curvature inside an SQP subproblem.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex: A structured least-squares SQP model is an SQP local problem whose objective model preserves the residual structure: \[m_k(p)=\tfrac12\|r_k+J_kp\|_2^2+\tfrac12p^TS_kp,\] subject to the linearized original constraints. Equivalently, after discarding the constant \(\|r_k\|_2^2/2\), \[m_k(p)=J_k^Tr_k{}^Tp+\tfrac12p^T(J_k^TJ_k+S_k)p,\] where \(S_k\) models the residual-weighted second-order term \(\sum_{i=1}^q r_i(x_k)\nabla^2r_i(x_k)\), possibly together with constraint-curvature terms required by the Lagrangian. The choice \(S_k=0\) is the constrained Gauss–Newton SQP model.
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: A structured least-squares SQP model linearizes the residual vector and minimizes the squared norm of that residual model while imposing linearized nonlinear constraints. Its curvature is the Gauss–Newton matrix plus an optional symmetric correction representing residual and Lagrangian second derivatives. Setting the correction to zero gives constrained Gauss–Newton SQP; retaining or approximating it gives a structured second-order model.
assumptions_latex: \(r\), \(c_E\), and \(c_I\) are continuously differentiable near \(x_k\).
The correction \(S_k\in\mathbb R^{n\times n}\) is symmetric.
The linearized constraints use the same step variable \(p\in\mathbb R^n\) as the residual model.
knowledge_statements.conclusion_latex: The SQP curvature matrix has the structured form \(B_k=J_k^TJ_k+S_k\), and the local objective is equivalently a corrected linear least-squares model.
equivalent_formulations_latex: \(\tfrac12\|r_k+J_kp\|_2^2=\tfrac12\|r_k\|_2^2+(J_k^Tr_k)^Tp+\tfrac12p^TJ_k^TJ_kp\).
With \(S_k=0\), computing the objective-model step is a linearly constrained linear least-squares problem.
special_cases_latex: Zero residual at a solution eliminates the residual-weighted objective Hessian term.
For affine residuals, \(S_k=0\) gives the exact objective Hessian.
immediate_consequences_latex: The positive-semidefinite Gauss–Newton component can be applied through products with \(J_k\) and \(J_k^T\).
Least-squares factorizations can be used without forming \(J_k^TJ_k\).
boundary_notes: The definition does not assert positive definiteness when \(J_k\) is rank deficient.
A generic SQP Hessian that ignores the decomposition \(J_k^TJ_k+S_k\) is not structured in this sense.

notation.meaning: Residual vector at the current iterate.
Residual Jacobian at the current iterate.

children.title: Hybrid Sequential Model Family
children.top_down_role: Closely related sequential models that retain the SQP architecture while modifying the canonical quadratic model.

top_down_textbook_witnesses.source_query: Conn, Gould, and Toint, Trust Region Methods

knowledge_statements.slot_contract: State the canonical mathematical definition of the source node, with its domain, quantifiers, notation, and a precise source locator.
knowledge_statements.ambient_context_latex: Let an iteration for a smooth nonlinear program produce a step \(p_k\) from one or more local subproblems built at \(x_k\), followed by a globalization and update rule.
knowledge_statements.scope_note: A proposed umbrella definition for sequential methods retaining SQP linearized constraints while using more than one objective-model class or modeling phase.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex: A hybrid sequential model family is a collection of iterations for which each \(p_k\) is selected from a finite sequence of local subproblems \(\mathcal M_k^{(1)},\ldots,\mathcal M_k^{(s)}\), \(s\geq2\), sharing the linearized constraint data at \(x_k\), while at least two phases use mathematically different objective models. Typical phases may use a linear model, a quadratic Lagrangian model, or another smooth local model. The phase outputs are combined by a specified map \(p_k=\Psi_k(p_k^{(1)},\ldots,p_k^{(s)})\), or a switching rule selects one output. The defining feature is retention of sequential constraint linearization and SQP-style step acceptance while the canonical single quadratic objective model is replaced or supplemented.
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: A hybrid sequential model method forms at least two distinct local objective models at an iterate, uses the same local constraint information, and either combines their steps or switches between them by a stated rule. It remains SQP-like because constraints are locally linearized and the resulting trial step is globalized, but it is not defined by one quadratic model alone.
assumptions_latex: At least two distinct local objective-model classes are used.
All phases refer to the same nonlinear program and current iterate.
A deterministic combination or switching rule specifies the final trial step.
knowledge_statements.conclusion_latex: The family is characterized by \(s\geq2\) model phases and a step rule \(p_k=\Psi_k(p_k^{(1)},\ldots,p_k^{(s)})\), rather than by a single canonical quadratic subproblem.
special_cases_latex: A linear working-set identification phase followed by an equality-constrained quadratic phase is a two-model instance.
A rule that switches between quadratic and nonquadratic local models is an instance when its switching criterion is explicit.
immediate_consequences_latex: The local model family must specify both the phase models and their coupling rule.
boundary_notes: Merely changing a Hessian approximation within one quadratic model does not by itself create a hybrid model family.
No inspected source supplied a canonical umbrella definition matching the full breadth of this tree node.

notation.meaning: The local subproblem used in phase \(j\).

review_flags: A precise canonical source for the umbrella term “Hybrid Sequential Model Family” was not located.
The formalization follows the supplied blueprint but requires independent source validation.

children.title: Sequential Linear-Quadratic Programming
children.top_down_role: Hybrid sequential models separating linear and quadratic modeling roles.

knowledge_statements.title: Sequential Linear-Quadratic Programming
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: A linear least-squares phase reduces constraint violation, then a quadratic tangential phase improves the objective without undoing first-order feasibility.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex: For equality-constrained \(\min f(x)\) subject to \(c(x)=0\), first compute a normal step \(n_k\) from a linearized feasibility problem, for example \[n_k\in\arg\min_n\ \|c(x_k)+A_kn\|_2\quad\text{subject to}\quad\|n\|_2\le\Delta_k^{n}.\] Then compute a tangential correction \(t_k\) from \[\min_t\ g_k^{\mathsf T}(n_k+t)+\tfrac12(n_k+t)^{\mathsf T}B_k(n_k+t)\quad\text{subject to}\quad A_kt=0,\ \|n_k+t\|_2\le\Delta_k.\] Set \(d_k=n_k+t_k\), accept or reject it by the prescribed globalization test, update \(x_{k+1}=x_k+d_k\) when accepted, and stop at feasibility and stationarity tolerances.
assumptions_latex: \(f\) and \(c\) are continuously differentiable near \(x_k\).
\(A_k=Dc(x_k)\), \(g_k=\nabla f(x_k)\), and \(B_k=B_k^{\mathsf T}\).
\(0<\Delta_k^{n}\le\Delta_k\).
knowledge_statements.conclusion_latex: The trial step decomposes as \(d_k=n_k+t_k\), with \(A_kt_k=0\).
knowledge_statements.scope_note: Hybrid step using a linear feasibility model followed by a quadratic tangential optimality model.

enrichment_metadata.review_comment: The displayed normal-tangential trust-region procedure is a recognizable constrained-optimization architecture, but no source establishes that this particular construction is the intended 'Sequential Linear-Quadratic Programming' family. The exact model, globalization, and nomenclature therefore remain unreliable without an authoritative locator.

knowledge_statements.slot_contract: State the canonical mathematical definition of the source node, with its domain, quantifiers, notation, and a precise source locator.
knowledge_statements.ambient_context_latex: For a smooth nonlinear program, let \(g_k\), \(c_k\), \(A_k\), and \(B_k\) be the objective gradient, constraint values, constraint Jacobian, and symmetric Lagrangian-curvature model at \(x_k\). Let \(\Delta_k^{LP},\Delta_k^{QP}>0\).
knowledge_statements.scope_note: Trust-region SLQP in which an LP identifies a working set and a subsequent EQP supplies curvature refinement.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex: A sequential linear-quadratic programming iteration computes its step in two stages. First it solves a trust-region linear program obtained from the SQP subproblem by omitting \(p^TB_kp/2\), using \(\|p\|_\infty\leq\Delta_k^{LP}\), and defines a working set \(\mathcal W_k\) from constraints active at the LP solution \(p_k^{LP}\). Second it solves an equality-constrained quadratic problem for a correction \(d\): \[\min_d\ (g_k+B_kp_k^{LP})^Td+\tfrac12d^TB_kd,\qquad A_{k,\mathcal W_k}d=0,\quad\|d\|\leq\Delta_k^{QP}.\] The trial step is \(p_k=p_k^{LP}+d_k\), with the EQP phase preserving the working constraints identified by the LP phase.
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: SLQP first solves a trust-region linear program to predict the active constraints. It then fixes those predicted constraints and solves an equality-constrained quadratic problem to add a curvature-based correction. The final step is the sum of the LP identification step and the EQP correction.
assumptions_latex: The objective and constraint functions are differentiable at \(x_k\).
\(B_k\) is symmetric.
The LP phase has a finite solution and yields a specified working set \(\mathcal W_k\).
The EQP correction is constrained to remain tangent to the working constraints.
knowledge_statements.conclusion_latex: The SLQP step decomposes as \(p_k=p_k^{LP}+d_k\), separating linear active-set prediction from quadratic tangent-space refinement.
equivalent_formulations_latex: The LP phase is the SQP model with \(B_k=0\) and an infinity-norm trust region.
The EQP phase minimizes the quadratic model restricted to the affine face predicted by the LP phase.
special_cases_latex: If \(d_k=0\), the accepted trial step is the LP step.
If the predicted working set is correct, the EQP phase is the local equality-constrained SQP refinement on that face.
immediate_consequences_latex: Large-scale LP software and projected iterative EQP solvers can be used in separate phases.
boundary_notes: SLQP is not the same as solving a single inequality-constrained QP.
Trust-region updates and acceptance tests are algorithm controls beyond the defining two-phase model.

notation.meaning: Working-set identification step from the LP phase.
Quadratic correction from the EQP phase.
Working set predicted by the LP phase.

children.title: Nonquadratic Local-Model SQP
children.top_down_role: Sequential constrained methods using nonquadratic local models within an SQP-like architecture.

knowledge_statements.title: Nonquadratic Local-Model SQP
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: An SQP-like method retains linearized constraints and globalization but replaces the quadratic objective approximation by a first-order-consistent nonquadratic local model.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex: At iterate \(x_k\), choose a differentiable local model \(m_k:\mathbb R^n\to\mathbb R\) satisfying \(m_k(0)=f(x_k)\) and \(\nabla m_k(0)=\nabla f(x_k)\), without requiring \(m_k\) to be quadratic. Compute \[d_k\in\arg\min_d\ m_k(d)\quad\text{subject to}\quad c(x_k)+A_kd=0,\quad\|d\|_2\le\Delta_k.\] Compare actual reduction in a specified merit or filter measure with the reduction predicted by the local model, accept or reject \(d_k\), update the model and radius, and terminate when prescribed feasibility and first-order stationarity residuals are below tolerance.
assumptions_latex: \(f\) and \(c\) are continuously differentiable on a neighborhood of the iterates.
Each subproblem has a computed approximate minimizer within \(\|d\|_2\le\Delta_k\).
knowledge_statements.conclusion_latex: The local objective model is first-order consistent at \(d=0\), while its higher-order shape may be nonquadratic.
knowledge_statements.scope_note: SQP-like iteration whose smooth local objective model need not be quadratic.

The architecture must return a primal step \(p_k\), multiplier estimate \(\widehat\lambda_k\), and working-set or complementarity information sufficient for the outer SQP iteration. Representations include the full KKT system, Schur-complement range-space equations, and reduced null-space equations; solvers include active-set, interior-point, and Krylov procedures.
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: An SQP subproblem solution architecture consists of the local QP, its chosen linear-algebra representation, the inner QP or linear solver, and the stopping rule. Its output includes a step and the multiplier or active-set information needed by the outer SQP method. Full KKT, range-space, and null-space representations, as well as active-set, interior-point, and iterative solvers, are different architectures for the same local model.

The selected representation is algebraically consistent with the local QP.
The solver termination rule identifies what constitutes an exact or acceptable inexact subproblem output.

equivalent_formulations_latex: For an equality QP, \(\mathcal R_k\) may be the saddle-point KKT equations or an algebraically equivalent range-space or null-space reduction.
special_cases_latex: An exact active-set QP solve is an architecture with KKT termination.

children.title: IQP-EQP Strategy Duality
children.top_down_role: The principal distinction between inequality-retaining and working-set equality subproblems.

knowledge_statements.slot_contract: State the canonical mathematical definition of the source node, with its domain, quantifiers, notation, and a precise source locator.
knowledge_statements.ambient_context_latex: Consider a smooth nonlinear program with equalities indexed by \(\mathcal E\) and inequalities indexed by \(\mathcal I\). At \(x_k\), let \(q_k(p)\) denote the SQP quadratic model and let the constraints be linearized.
knowledge_statements.scope_note: Active-set SQP design for general nonlinear programs with inequalities.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex: The IQP strategy solves the inequality-constrained quadratic subproblem containing every equality linearization and every inequality linearization; the active set at its solution simultaneously defines the step and predicts the nonlinear program's active set. The EQP strategy first selects a working set \(\mathcal W_k\subseteq\mathcal E\cup\mathcal I\), with \(\mathcal E\subseteq\mathcal W_k\), and then solves \[\min_p q_k(p)\quad\text{subject to}\quad c_i(x_k)+\nabla c_i(x_k)^Tp=0,\ i\in\mathcal W_k,\] while omitting inequalities outside \(\mathcal W_k\) from that EQP. Thus IQP couples active-set identification and step computation, whereas EQP separates them.
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: IQP retains all linearized inequalities in the local quadratic program, so solving that QP both computes a step and predicts which inequalities are active. EQP predicts a working set first and then treats only those constraints as equalities in a cheaper equality-constrained QP. The distinction is whether active-set identification is internal to or precedes the main quadratic solve.
assumptions_latex: A quadratic SQP model is defined at \(x_k\).
Every equality constraint is included in either strategy.
An EQP strategy supplies a working-set selection rule.
knowledge_statements.conclusion_latex: IQP and EQP differ by the logical order of active-set identification and quadratic step computation, not by the underlying nonlinear program.
equivalent_formulations_latex: IQP: solve the full linearized inequality QP and read \(\mathcal W_k\) from its solution.
EQP: choose \(\mathcal W_k\) first and solve the quadratic model on the resulting affine subspace.
special_cases_latex: For equality-only nonlinear programs, the IQP and EQP subproblem forms coincide.
Once IQP identifies a stable active set, its local solve behaves as an equality-constrained Newton-type step.
immediate_consequences_latex: EQP subproblems can be less expensive for large problems when working-set prediction is reliable.
boundary_notes: The term “duality” here denotes a strategy contrast, not Lagrange or Fenchel duality.
Neither strategy alone specifies globalization.

knowledge_statements.statement_plain: Each SQP iteration solves a quadratic program containing all linearized equalities and inequalities, obtaining both a trial step and multiplier estimates.

\(B_k=B_k^{\mathsf T}\) approximates Lagrangian curvature.

knowledge_statements.title: Equality-QP SQP
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: A predicted active set converts selected inequalities to equalities; violated omitted constraints or incorrectly signed multipliers trigger working-set changes.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex: For \(\min f(x)\) subject to \(c(x)=0\) and \(g(x)\le0\), select a predicted working set \(W_k\). Compute \(d_k\) and equality-QP multipliers from \[\min_d\ \nabla f(x_k)^{\mathsf T}d+\tfrac12d^{\mathsf T}B_kd\quad\text{subject to}\quad c(x_k)+Dc(x_k)d=0,\quad g_i(x_k)+\nabla g_i(x_k)^{\mathsf T}d=0\ \ (i\in W_k).\] Test omitted linearized inequalities and multiplier signs; modify \(W_k\) when either test fails. Globalize the resulting step, update \(x_k\) and multiplier estimates, and stop when nonlinear feasibility, complementarity, and stationarity tolerances hold.

\(B_k=B_k^{\mathsf T}\).

knowledge_statements.statement_title: IQP and EQP architectures for SQP subproblems
knowledge_statements.scope_note: Extraction-grounded description of two practical SQP architectures, with emphasis on equality-QP SQP and its working-set selection mechanisms.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex: For a general nonlinear program, an IQP-SQP iteration solves an inequality-constrained quadratic subproblem and uses its active set as an estimate of the solution's optimal active set; although a general QP can be expensive at large scale, warm-starting from the preceding subproblem becomes effective as the SQP iterates converge. In an EQP-SQP iteration, a working set \(W_k\) is selected, the constraints in \(W_k\) are imposed as equalities, the remaining constraints are omitted, and an equality-constrained QP is solved; \(W_k\) may be updated from multiplier estimates or an auxiliary subproblem, and the resulting QP is generally cheaper at large scale. In SLQP, an LP formed by omitting the quadratic term and imposing \(\lVert p\rVert_\infty\leq\Delta_k\) identifies \(W_k\), after which the quadratic term is restored in the equality-constrained QP. A gradient-projection alternative identifies \(W_k\) by minimizing the quadratic model along the path obtained by projecting steepest descent onto the feasible region.
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: IQP-SQP solves the full inequality-constrained quadratic subproblem and uses its active set as an estimate of the optimal active set; it can be expensive on large problems, but warm starts become effective near convergence. EQP-SQP instead selects and updates a working set, imposes only those constraints as equalities, and solves a cheaper equality-constrained quadratic subproblem. SLQP selects the working set with a trust-region linear program and then restores the quadratic term, while gradient projection can select it along a projected steepest-descent path.
assumptions_latex: \text{The problem is a general nonlinear program treated by sequential quadratic programming.}
W_k\text{ denotes the working set selected at iteration }k.
\text{For the SLQP construction, }\lVert p\rVert_\infty\leq\Delta_k\text{ is imposed on the linear subproblem.}
knowledge_statements.conclusion_latex: \mathrm{IQP}:\ \text{solve the inequality-constrained QP and estimate the optimal active set from its solution};\qquad \mathrm{EQP}:\ \text{select }W_k\text{ and solve the QP with constraints in }W_k\text{ imposed as equalities}.

knowledge_statements.title: Hybrid IQP-EQP SQP
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: An inequality QP predicts the active set, after which an equality QP refines the step; validation determines whether refinement or fallback is used.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex: At \(x_k\), first solve or approximately solve the IQP containing all linearized constraints to obtain \((d_k^{I},\mu_k^{I})\). Predict \[W_k=\{i:g_i(x_k)+\nabla g_i(x_k)^{\mathsf T}d_k^{I}\ge-\tau_k\}\cup\{i:\mu_{k,i}^{I}>\tau_k^{\mu}\}.\] Next solve an EQP using the equalities \(c(x_k)+Dc(x_k)d=0\) and \(g_i(x_k)+\nabla g_i(x_k)^{\mathsf T}d=0\) for \(i\in W_k\). Accept the EQP step only if omitted inequalities and multiplier-sign tests pass; otherwise retain the IQP step or revise \(W_k\). Globalize the selected step and stop at feasibility, complementarity, and stationarity tolerances.
assumptions_latex: \(f\), \(c\), and \(g\) are continuously differentiable near \(x_k\).
Both phases use a symmetric curvature approximation \(B_k\).
\(\tau_k\ge0\) and \(\tau_k^{\mu}\ge0\) are active-set thresholds.
knowledge_statements.conclusion_latex: Each iteration selects a validated EQP refinement or an IQP fallback step.
knowledge_statements.scope_note: Two-phase SQP combining inequality-QP identification with equality-QP refinement.
