knowledge_statements.ambient_context_latex: Let \(Q_k^I\) be the full inequality-constrained SQP subproblem and, for a working set \(\mathcal W\), let \(Q_k^E(\mathcal W)\) be its equality-constrained restriction.
knowledge_statements.scope_note: SQP strategies that use an inequality-aware identification phase and an equality-constrained refinement phase within one iteration or across explicitly controlled modes.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex: A hybrid IQP–EQP SQP strategy is an SQP iteration that uses both maps \[Q_k^I\longmapsto(\widetilde p_k,\mathcal W_k),\qquad Q_k^E(\mathcal W_k)\longmapsto p_k,\] or switches between them by an explicit rule. The IQP component retains inequalities to produce a feasible or inequality-aware step and an active-set estimate. The EQP component fixes the resulting working constraints as equalities and computes a curvature-refined step on that face. A switching form is hybrid only if its state and criterion specify when the principal step is obtained from \(Q_k^I\) and when from \(Q_k^E\).
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: Hybrid IQP–EQP SQP uses both full inequality-QP information and equality-QP refinement. An inequality-aware phase predicts a working set or produces a preliminary step; an EQP phase then optimizes on the predicted face. Alternatively, an explicit state rule switches the main solve between IQP and EQP modes.
assumptions_latex: Both the full inequality QP and working-set EQP are defined from the same local SQP model.
The IQP phase supplies or updates \(\mathcal W_k\).
A combination or switching rule uniquely identifies the trial step.

equivalent_formulations_latex: Gradient-projection QP solution is hybrid in interpretation when projection identifies a face and subspace minimization solves the EQP on that face.
special_cases_latex: A projected identification step followed by reduced-space conjugate-gradient minimization is a hybrid instance.
If the EQP refinement is omitted permanently, the method reduces to IQP; if inequality identification is external and no IQP is solved, it reduces to EQP.
immediate_consequences_latex: The architecture can exploit inequality robustness during identification and cheaper reduced linear algebra during refinement.
boundary_notes: SLQP's LP phase is not literally an IQP phase, although its two-stage identification/refinement pattern is closely related.

knowledge_statements.statement_title: KKT Linear System for an SQP Equality Subproblem
knowledge_statements.ambient_context_latex: Consider \(\min_p g_k^Tp+p^TB_kp/2\) subject to \(A_kp=-c_k\), where \(A_k\in\mathbb R^{m\times n}\), \(B_k=B_k^T\), and \(c_k\in\mathbb R^m\).
knowledge_statements.scope_note: Linear algebra for equality-QP steps or fixed-working-set SQP steps.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex: The KKT linear-algebra representation of the SQP subproblem is the saddle-point system \[\begin{bmatrix}B_k&A_k^T\\A_k&0\end{bmatrix}\begin{bmatrix}p_k\\\delta\lambda_k\end{bmatrix}=\begin{bmatrix}-g_k\\-c_k\end{bmatrix}.\] Its coefficient matrix is the KKT matrix. Full-system factorization, elimination into a multiplier-space Schur complement, and null-space reduction are equivalent solution representations whenever their stated rank and invertibility conditions hold. If \(A_k\) has full row rank and \(Z_k^TB_kZ_k\) is positive definite for \(A_kZ_k=0\), the KKT matrix is nonsingular.
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: The equality-constrained SQP step and its multiplier correction satisfy a symmetric saddle-point KKT system. One may solve this coupled system directly or reduce it to range-space or null-space equations. Full row rank of the working constraint Jacobian together with positive definiteness of the reduced Hessian gives a nonsingular KKT matrix.
assumptions_latex: \(A_k\) represents equality or currently working constraints.
For the stated nonsingularity condition, \(A_k\) has full row rank and \(Z_k^TB_kZ_k\succ0\).
knowledge_statements.conclusion_latex: The primal-dual SQP step is represented by a symmetric KKT system, with direct, range-space, and null-space solution forms.
equivalent_formulations_latex: If \(B_k\succ0\), eliminating \(p_k\) yields a system in \(\delta\lambda_k\) with coefficient \(A_kB_k^{-1}A_k^T\).
Writing \(p_k=p_k^N+Z_kz_k\) yields a reduced system with coefficient \(Z_k^TB_kZ_k\).
special_cases_latex: For \(c_k=0\), the step is tangent to the current working constraints.
For no constraints, the system reduces to \(B_kp_k=-g_k\).
immediate_consequences_latex: The KKT matrix is symmetric and generally indefinite when constraints are present.
boundary_notes: Rank-deficient constraints require specialized regularization or dependent-row handling.
The equations characterize a stationary QP pair; minimization additionally depends on curvature on the feasible tangent space.

notation.meaning: Multiplier associated with the equality-QP step.

knowledge_statements.title: Full KKT Factorization
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: The SQP step and multiplier correction solve one symmetric saddle-point system, which can be handled by a direct symmetric-indefinite factorization.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex: For the equality-constrained QP \[\min_d\ g_k^{\mathsf T}d+\tfrac12d^{\mathsf T}B_kd\quad\text{subject to}\quad A_kd+b_k=0,\] its primal-dual stationary equations are the full KKT system \[\begin{pmatrix}B_k&A_k^{\mathsf T}\\A_k&0\end{pmatrix}\begin{pmatrix}d_k\\\delta\lambda_k\end{pmatrix}=-\begin{pmatrix}g_k\\b_k\end{pmatrix}.\] A symmetric-indefinite factorization of the displayed matrix computes the coupled step directly. If \(A_k\) has full row rank and \(B_k\) is positive definite on \(\ker A_k\), then the KKT matrix is nonsingular and the primal-dual solution is unique.
assumptions_latex: \(B_k=B_k^{\mathsf T}\).
\(A_k\in\mathbb R^{m\times n}\) has full row rank.
\(z^{\mathsf T}B_kz>0\) for every nonzero \(z\in\ker A_k\).
knowledge_statements.conclusion_latex: The full KKT matrix is nonsingular and uniquely determines \((d_k,\delta\lambda_k)\).
knowledge_statements.scope_note: Coupled saddle-point system for an equality-constrained SQP step and its multiplier correction.

knowledge_statements.ambient_context_latex: Let \(K_k=\begin{bmatrix}B_k&A_k^T\\A_k&0\end{bmatrix}\) be a nonsingular symmetric KKT matrix for an equality-QP SQP step.
knowledge_statements.scope_note: Direct coupled-system computation retaining both primal and multiplier variables.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex: A full KKT factorization method computes a symmetric permutation and block factorization \[P_k^TK_kP_k=L_kD_kL_k^T,\] where \(P_k\) is a permutation, \(L_k\) is unit lower triangular, and \(D_k\) is block diagonal with \(1\times1\) and \(2\times2\) pivot blocks. The primal-dual right-hand side is solved by permutation, forward substitution, block-diagonal solution, backward substitution, and inverse permutation. The factorization acts on the complete \((n+m)\)-dimensional saddle-point matrix rather than first forming a Schur complement or reduced Hessian.
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: Full KKT factorization directly factors the entire symmetric saddle-point matrix using a stability- and sparsity-oriented permutation and an indefinite LDL-transpose factorization with one-by-one or two-by-two pivots. The primal step and multipliers are then recovered through triangular and block-diagonal solves.
assumptions_latex: \(K_k\) is symmetric.
A pivoting strategy is available for symmetric indefinite factorization.
For a unique step, \(K_k\) is nonsingular.
knowledge_statements.conclusion_latex: Both \(p_k\) and \(\delta\lambda_k\) are obtained from one factorization of the complete KKT matrix.
equivalent_formulations_latex: The notation \(L_kD_kL_k^T\) is equivalent to a symmetric-indefinite \(L_kB_k^{\mathrm{blk}}L_k^T\) factorization when the block diagonal factor is renamed.
special_cases_latex: For sparse SQP systems, \(P_k\) may be chosen to balance numerical stability and fill reduction.
When all stable pivots are scalar, \(D_k\) is diagonal.
immediate_consequences_latex: No explicit inverse of the curvature matrix is required.
The computed factor inertia can help diagnose reduced-Hessian definiteness under suitable assumptions.
boundary_notes: Ordinary Cholesky factorization is generally inapplicable because a constrained KKT matrix is indefinite.
Poor ordering can cause substantial fill even when the original KKT matrix is sparse.

knowledge_statements.title: Range-Space SQP Methods
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: Eliminating the primal step yields a multiplier-space Schur-complement system; back-substitution then recovers the SQP step.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex: Suppose \(B_k\) is symmetric positive definite and \(A_k\) has full row rank. Eliminating \(d_k\) from \[B_kd_k+A_k^{\mathsf T}\delta\lambda_k=-g_k,\qquad A_kd_k=-b_k\] gives the range-space system \[(A_kB_k^{-1}A_k^{\mathsf T})\delta\lambda_k=b_k-A_kB_k^{-1}g_k.\] After solving this \(m\)-dimensional system, recover the primal step by \[d_k=-B_k^{-1}(g_k+A_k^{\mathsf T}\delta\lambda_k).\] The Schur complement \(A_kB_k^{-1}A_k^{\mathsf T}\) is symmetric positive definite, so the reduced multiplier equation has a unique solution.
assumptions_latex: \(B_k=B_k^{\mathsf T}\succ0\).
\(A_k\in\mathbb R^{m\times n}\) has full row rank.
The products with \(B_k^{-1}\) are computed exactly or to the linear-solver tolerance.
knowledge_statements.conclusion_latex: \(A_kB_k^{-1}A_k^{\mathsf T}\succ0\), and the range-space equations uniquely determine \((d_k,\delta\lambda_k)\).
knowledge_statements.scope_note: Multiplier-space Schur-complement reduction of an equality-constrained SQP KKT system.

knowledge_statements.statement_title: Range-Space Reduction of an SQP KKT System
knowledge_statements.ambient_context_latex: Let \(B_k\succ0\), let \(A_k\in\mathbb R^{m\times n}\) have full row rank, and consider \(B_kp_k+A_k^T\lambda_k=-g_k\), \(A_kp_k=-c_k\).
knowledge_statements.scope_note: Multiplier-space Schur-complement solution of an equality-QP or fixed-working-set SQP system.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex: A range-space SQP method eliminates the primal step from the KKT equations and solves the Schur-complement system \[(A_kB_k^{-1}A_k^T)\lambda_k=c_k-A_kB_k^{-1}g_k,\] with signs adjusted consistently if the multiplier convention in the KKT equations is reversed. It then recovers \[p_k=-B_k^{-1}(g_k+A_k^T\lambda_k).\] The principal reduced system therefore has dimension \(m\) and lies in multiplier or constraint space. Implementations apply \(B_k^{-1}\) through solves with a factorization or preconditioned operator rather than by explicitly forming an inverse.
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: A range-space SQP method eliminates the primal variable from the equality-QP KKT equations. It solves a Schur-complement equation in the multipliers and then recovers the primal step through a curvature-system solve. Its reduced dimension is the number of working constraints.
assumptions_latex: \(B_k\) is positive definite and suitable for repeated linear solves.
\(A_k\) has full row rank.
The right-hand-side signs follow the stated KKT convention.
knowledge_statements.conclusion_latex: The coupled KKT system reduces to the symmetric positive-definite multiplier system with coefficient \(A_kB_k^{-1}A_k^T\).
equivalent_formulations_latex: The Schur complement of \(B_k\) in the KKT matrix is \(-A_kB_k^{-1}A_k^T\); multiplying by \(-1\) gives the positive-definite form.
The method computes the component of the step in \(\operatorname{range}(B_k^{-1}A_k^T)\) through multiplier variables.
special_cases_latex: If \(B_k\) is diagonal or block diagonal, its inverse actions are inexpensive.
The method is attractive when \(m\ll n\) and the Schur complement remains manageable.
immediate_consequences_latex: The reduced multiplier matrix is positive definite under the stated assumptions.
boundary_notes: The basic reduction is not valid when \(B_k\) is singular or indefinite without modification.
Forming the Schur complement may destroy sparsity.

children.title: Null-Space SQP Methods

knowledge_statements.title: Null-Space SQP Methods
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: A particular feasible step plus a null-space basis converts the equality-constrained SQP subproblem into a reduced-Hessian quadratic problem with unique reduced coordinates.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex: Let \(g\in\mathbb R^n\), \(B=B^\top\in\mathbb R^{n\times n}\), \(A\in\mathbb R^{m\times n}\), and \(c\in\mathbb R^m\), where \(A\) has full row rank and \(m\le n\). Consider \[\min_{p\in\mathbb R^n} g^\top p+\tfrac12p^\top Bp\quad\text{subject to}\quad Ap=-c.\] Let \(Z\in\mathbb R^{n\times(n-m)}\) have columns forming a basis of \(\ker A\), and choose \(p_N\in\mathbb R^n\) satisfying \(Ap_N=-c\). Every feasible step has the unique form \(p=p_N+Zq\), with \(q\in\mathbb R^{n-m}\). Hence the subproblem reduces to \[\min_{q\in\mathbb R^{n-m}}\ \tfrac12q^\top(Z^\top BZ)q+\bigl[Z^\top(g+Bp_N)\bigr]^\top q.\] After computing a reduced minimizer \(q\), recover \(p=p_N+Zq\). A multiplier \(\lambda\in\mathbb R^m\) then satisfies \(A^\top\lambda=-(g+Bp)\). If \(Z^\top BZ\) is positive definite, the reduced minimizer and the resulting primal step are unique.
assumptions_latex: \(A\in\mathbb R^{m\times n}\) has full row rank.
\(B=B^\top\in\mathbb R^{n\times n}\).
The columns of \(Z\in\mathbb R^{n\times(n-m)}\) form a basis of \(\ker A\).
knowledge_statements.conclusion_latex: \(p=p_N+Zq\), where \(q\) solves the reduced-Hessian quadratic program.
knowledge_statements.scope_note: Equality-constrained SQP subproblem reduced to the tangent space of the linearized constraints.

notation.meaning: Basis matrix for the null space of the constraint Jacobian.
Particular feasible normal step satisfying the linearized constraints.
Reduced Hessian on the tangent space.

knowledge_statements.statement_title: Null-Space Reduction of an SQP Equality Subproblem
knowledge_statements.ambient_context_latex: Let \(A_k\in\mathbb R^{m\times n}\) have full row rank, let \(Z_k\in\mathbb R^{n\times(n-m)}\) have full column rank with \(A_kZ_k=0\), and let \(Y_k\) complete \(Z_k\) to a basis.
knowledge_statements.scope_note: Tangent-space solution of equality-QP or working-set SQP systems; the full curvature matrix need not be positive definite.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex: A null-space SQP method decomposes the step as \[p_k=Y_ky_k+Z_kz_k,\] chooses the normal component \(Y_ky_k\) to satisfy \(A_kp_k=-c_k\), and determines the tangent component from \[(Z_k^TB_kZ_k)z_k=-Z_k^T(g_k+B_kY_ky_k).\] The matrix \(Z_k^TB_kZ_k\) is the reduced Hessian. After computing \(p_k\), multipliers are recovered from the remaining KKT equation. The defining solve has dimension \(n-m\) and requires positive definiteness only of the reduced Hessian for a unique minimizing tangent correction.
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: A null-space SQP method first computes a normal step satisfying the linearized constraints and then optimizes in the null space of the working constraint Jacobian. The tangent coordinates solve a system involving the reduced Hessian. Multipliers are recovered afterward from the stationarity equation.
assumptions_latex: \(A_k\) has full row rank.
\(A_kZ_k=0\) and \(Z_k\) spans \(\ker A_k\).
For a unique reduced minimizer, \(Z_k^TB_kZ_k\succ0\).
knowledge_statements.conclusion_latex: The equality-QP step is obtained from a feasibility component plus a tangent correction governed by the reduced Hessian \(Z_k^TB_kZ_k\).
equivalent_formulations_latex: An implicit projected method may apply the tangent-space projector without explicitly forming \(Z_k\).
For a feasible current iterate, the normal component can be zero and \(p_k=Z_kz_k\).
special_cases_latex: The method is attractive when \(n-m\) is small.
Projected conjugate gradient gives an iterative null-space implementation.
immediate_consequences_latex: The full \(B_k\) may be indefinite while the reduced QP remains strictly convex if \(Z_k^TB_kZ_k\succ0\).
boundary_notes: Constructing a stable sparse null-space basis can itself be expensive.
Rank-deficient working constraints require a generalized basis or preprocessing.

knowledge_statements.statement_title: Mathematical Interface between SQP and an Inner QP Solver
knowledge_statements.ambient_context_latex: At SQP iteration \(k\), let the local QP data be \(B_k,g_k,A_{E,k},b_{E,k},A_{I,k},b_{I,k}\), with optional bounds and warm-start state \(w_k\).
knowledge_statements.scope_note: An abstract mathematical interface covering active-set, interior-point, and iterative inner QP solvers.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex: A QP solver interface for SQP is a map \[\mathcal S_k:(B_k,g_k,A_{E,k},b_{E,k},A_{I,k},b_{I,k},w_k,\tau_k)\mapsto(p_k,\lambda_k^Q,s_k,\sigma_k),\] where \(p_k\) is a primal step, \(\lambda_k^Q\) are QP multipliers, \(s_k\) contains active-set, slack, or primal-dual state reusable by the outer iteration, and \(\sigma_k\) reports termination, infeasibility, unboundedness, or an accepted inexact status. For an exact convex solve, the returned primal-dual variables satisfy QP feasibility, stationarity, multiplier sign, and complementarity. An inexact interface replaces these equalities and inequalities by explicitly specified residual tolerances \(\tau_k\).
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: The inner QP interface maps the local SQP model, constraints, warm-start information, and tolerances to a primal step, QP multipliers, reusable solver state, and a status. Exact solvers return a QP KKT point; inexact solvers must define residual-based acceptance. This common contract can be implemented by active-set, interior-point, or iterative methods.
assumptions_latex: All QP matrices and vectors have compatible dimensions.
The multiplier sign convention is fixed by the inequality convention.
If inexact output is allowed, \(\tau_k\) defines each required residual threshold.
knowledge_statements.conclusion_latex: The outer SQP method receives both a primal step and dual/working information, together with a mathematically interpretable solve status.
equivalent_formulations_latex: For an active-set solver, \(s_k\) may be a working set and factorization state.
For an interior-point solver, \(s_k\) may contain positive slack and dual variables.
For an iterative equality-QP solver, \(s_k\) may contain Krylov and preconditioner state.
special_cases_latex: With \(\tau_k=0\), the interface requests an exact KKT solution.
Warm starting sets \(w_k\) from the preceding SQP subproblem's final state.
immediate_consequences_latex: Multiplier and working-set outputs can be used for outer active-set prediction and Hessian updates.
boundary_notes: This is a mathematical interface, not a software calling convention.
A solver failure status requires an outer safeguard and does not itself define one.

knowledge_statements.title: Active-Set QP Solvers for SQP
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: The solver alternates equality-constrained QP steps with adding blocking constraints or deleting active constraints having negative multipliers; a terminating KKT point is globally optimal, and prior SQP working sets can provide warm starts.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex: Let \(B=B^\top\in\mathbb R^{n\times n}\), \(g\in\mathbb R^n\), \(A\in\mathbb R^{m_e\times n}\), \(b\in\mathbb R^{m_e}\), \(C\in\mathbb R^{m_i\times n}\), and \(d\in\mathbb R^{m_i}\). Consider \[\min_{p\in\mathbb R^n}\ \tfrac12p^\top Bp+g^\top p\quad\text{subject to}\quad Ap=b,\quad Cp\le d.\] Initialize a feasible point \(p_0\) and a working set \(W_0\). At inner iteration \(j\), solve the equality-constrained quadratic model in a displacement \(q_j\) subject to \(Aq_j=0\) and \(C_{W_j}q_j=0\). If \(q_j\ne0\), choose the largest \(\alpha_j\in(0,1]\) for which \(C(p_j+\alpha_jq_j)\le d\), set \(p_{j+1}=p_j+\alpha_jq_j\), and add a blocking constraint when \(\alpha_j<1\). If \(q_j=0\), stop when the active inequality multipliers are nonnegative; otherwise remove an active inequality having a negative multiplier. Any terminating iterate satisfies the convex-QP KKT conditions and is globally optimal. In SQP, the preceding subproblem's solution and working set may warm-start the next solve.
assumptions_latex: \(B=B^\top\succeq0\), and \(B\) is positive definite on \(\ker A\).
The QP feasible set is nonempty and \(p_0\) is feasible.
The equality rows together with each working set used by the method are linearly independent.
Equality-constrained subproblems and their multipliers are computed exactly for the stated KKT conclusion.
knowledge_statements.conclusion_latex: If the method terminates by the multiplier test, its iterate satisfies the convex-QP KKT conditions and is globally optimal.
knowledge_statements.scope_note: Feasible working-set method for convex SQP quadratic subproblems with linear inequalities.

notation.meaning: Indices of inequalities treated as equalities at inner iteration j.
Rows of the inequality matrix indexed by the working set.
Feasibility-preserving step fraction toward the equality-constrained QP minimizer.

knowledge_statements.statement_title: Active-Set QP Inner Solver for SQP
knowledge_statements.ambient_context_latex: Consider the convex QP \(\min_p q(p)=g^Tp+p^TBp/2\) subject to \(A_Ep=b_E\) and \(A_Ip\geq b_I\), with \(B\succeq0\).
knowledge_statements.scope_note: Primal working-set QP solution used for successive SQP subproblems, including warm starts.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex: An active-set QP solver maintains feasible iterates \(p_j\) and linearly independent working sets \(\mathcal W_j\) containing all equality constraints and selected active inequalities. At inner iteration \(j\), it solves the equality-constrained QP search problem with \(A_{\mathcal W_j}d=0\). If \(d\neq0\), it moves by the largest feasible step along \(d\), adding a blocking inequality when encountered. If \(d=0\), it inspects working-set multipliers: nonnegative inequality multipliers certify the convex-QP KKT conditions, while a constraint with an inadmissible multiplier is removed. For SQP, the initial \(\mathcal W_0\) may be the final working set of the preceding subproblem.
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: A primal active-set QP solver repeatedly solves equality-constrained QPs on a working face. A nonzero direction is followed until its minimizer or a blocking constraint is reached; a zero direction triggers a multiplier test that either certifies optimality or removes a working inequality. Successive SQP subproblems can be warm-started from the previous final working set.
assumptions_latex: The QP is convex, with \(B\succeq0\).
The starting point is QP-feasible, or a separate feasibility phase supplies one.
Working constraint gradients are maintained linearly independent.
Inequality multipliers use the sign convention consistent with \(A_Ip\geq b_I\).
knowledge_statements.conclusion_latex: The solver identifies a QP KKT point by finitely changing a working set and solving equality-constrained quadratic subproblems on its faces, subject to standard noncycling safeguards.
equivalent_formulations_latex: The working set is a linearly independent subset of the active constraints.
Each inner direction is the minimizer of the quadratic model restricted to the current working face.
special_cases_latex: If the initial working set is optimal, one EQP and multiplier test may suffice.
Warm starting reuses the previous SQP subproblem's active-set estimate.
immediate_consequences_latex: Adding or deleting one constraint permits factorization updates instead of complete refactorization.
Active-set solvers can provide accurate active-set and multiplier estimates to the outer SQP method.
boundary_notes: Degeneracy can cause cycling or ambiguous active-set identification and requires safeguards.
The stated convex-QP form does not cover all modifications required for indefinite QPs.

notation.meaning: Working set at inner QP iteration \(j\).
Equality-constrained QP search direction on the working face.

knowledge_statements.title: Interior-Point QP Solvers for SQP
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: A primal-dual solver follows perturbed QP KKT equations while maintaining positive slacks and multipliers, then returns an approximate step and multipliers.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex: For \\(\min_p \tfrac12p^\top Bp+g^\top p\\) subject to \\(Ap=b\\) and \\(Cp+s=d\\), initialize \\(s>0\\) and inequality multipliers \\(\mu>0\\). At each inner iteration, apply Newton's method to primal feasibility, stationarity, and the perturbed complementarity equations \\(S\mu=\tau\mathbf1\\), together with \\(Ap=b\\). Choose a fraction-to-the-boundary step preserving \\(s>0\\) and \\(\mu>0\\), update the primal-dual variables, and reduce \\(\tau>0\\). Stop when the primal and dual residuals and the duality measure \\(s^\top\mu/r\\) meet prescribed tolerances; return \\(p\\) and the multiplier estimates to SQP.
assumptions_latex: \\(B=B^\top\succeq0\\).
A strictly interior primal-dual starting point or an infeasible-start formulation is available.
knowledge_statements.conclusion_latex: The returned variables approximately satisfy primal feasibility, dual feasibility, stationarity, and complementarity.
knowledge_statements.scope_note: Primal-dual path-following solution of an inequality-rich convex SQP quadratic subproblem.

notation.meaning: Slack vector for the QP inequalities.

enrichment_metadata.review_comment: The algorithm fits the terminal container, but no source is supplied for the particular primal-dual path-following equations, initialization alternatives, fraction-to-boundary rule, or stopping criteria. These method-specific choices require an authoritative QP interior-point locator.

knowledge_statements.slot_contract: State the canonical mathematical definition of the source node, with its domain, quantifiers, notation, and a precise source locator.
knowledge_statements.statement_title: Primal-Dual Interior-Point Solution of an SQP Quadratic Subproblem
knowledge_statements.ambient_context_latex: At an SQP iterate \(x_k\), consider the quadratic program \(\min_d q_k(d)=\nabla f(x_k)^Td+\tfrac12d^TB_kd\) subject to \(c_k+A_kd=0\) and \(g_k+G_kd\geq0\), where \(B_k=B_k^T\). Introduce slack \(s=g_k+G_kd\), equality multiplier \(y\), inequality multiplier \(z\geq0\), and \(S=\operatorname{Diag}(s)\), \(Z=\operatorname{Diag}(z)\).
knowledge_statements.scope_note: Finite-dimensional primal-dual, path-following solution of equality-and-inequality SQP subproblems; the definition permits convex or locally regularized QP models but does not assert global convergence for an indefinite model.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex: An interior-point QP solver for SQP is an inner iteration that maintains \(s_j>0\) and \(z_j>0\) and approximately solves the perturbed KKT system \[B_kd_j+\nabla f(x_k)-A_k^Ty_j-G_k^Tz_j=r_{d,j},\quad c_k+A_kd_j=r_{c,j},\quad g_k+G_kd_j-s_j=r_{g,j},\quad S_jz_j=\mu_j\mathbf1+r_{\mu,j},\] with \(\mu_j>0\), while driving \(\mu_j\to0\) and the residual tuple to a prescribed SQP inner tolerance. A returned QP step is any \((d_k,y_k,z_k,s_k)\) satisfying positivity and \(\max\{\|r_{d,k}\|,\|r_{c,k}\|,\|r_{g,k}\|,\|S_kz_k\|\}\leq\varepsilon_k\).
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: The solver introduces positive inequality slacks and dual variables, follows perturbed complementarity equations \(S_jz_j\approx\mu_j\mathbf1\), and reduces primal, dual, and complementarity residuals. It returns an approximate KKT point of the complete SQP quadratic subproblem when those residuals meet the selected inner tolerance \(\varepsilon_k\).
knowledge_statements.conclusion_latex: \((d_k,y_k,z_k,s_k)\) is the interior-point QP output precisely when it is produced through positive perturbed-KKT iterates and satisfies the stated residual stopping test.
equivalent_formulations_latex: In the exact inner-solve limit, \(r_{d,j}=r_{c,j}=r_{g,j}=r_{\mu,j}=0\) and \(\mu_j\downarrow0\), so every finite limit satisfies primal feasibility, dual feasibility, stationarity, and \(S z=0\).
special_cases_latex: With no inequalities, the slack, positivity, and complementarity equations disappear and the inner system is the equality-constrained KKT system.
For a convex QP with \(B_k\succeq0\), the limiting KKT conditions characterize a global QP solution whenever the standard constraint qualification holds.
immediate_consequences_latex: Strict positivity prevents premature identification of an inequality active set during the inner iterations.
The SQP outer method may control computational work through the tolerance sequence \((\varepsilon_k)\).
boundary_notes: The definition does not include active-set methods whose inner iterates need not remain strictly interior.
A precise authoritative locator supporting this SQP-specific formulation was not inspected; the supplied interior-point locators alone do not establish the complete definition.

knowledge_statements.title: Iterative QP Solvers for SQP
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: Projection eliminates active linear constraints, after which a gradient or Krylov method solves the reduced system using products and optional preconditioning.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex:
For a fixed equality or working-set matrix \\(A\\), first compute \\(p_N\\) approximately satisfying \\(Ap_N=-c\\). Let \\(Z\\) span \\(\ker A\\). Starting from \\(q_0\\), apply a gradient or Krylov iteration to the reduced system \\[Z^\top BZq=-Z^\top(g+Bp_N),\
\\] using matrix-vector products and, when available, a preconditioner. Terminate when the reduced residual norm is at most the prescribed inner tolerance, or when negative curvature is detected. Return \\(p=p_N+Zq\\); on negative curvature, return a safeguarded boundary or trust-region step along the detected direction. Inequality working sets may be updated outside the iterative linear solve.
assumptions_latex: \\(A\\) has constant row rank for the selected working set.
knowledge_statements.conclusion_latex: The returned step is approximately feasible and has a controlled projected optimality residual, or identifies reduced negative curvature.
knowledge_statements.scope_note: Projected Krylov solution of a structured SQP subproblem for a fixed working set.

notation.meaning: Null-space basis or implicit tangent-space projector.
Approximate normal component of the QP step.

enrichment_metadata.review_comment: The record combines projected gradient, Krylov, working-set, and trust-region boundary behavior without a source identifying one precise algorithmic regime. The negative-curvature return rule and its relationship to the SQP globalization mechanism are method-specific and cannot be validated from the supplied inventory.

knowledge_statements.statement_title: Residual-Terminated Iterative QP Solver for SQP
knowledge_statements.ambient_context_latex: Let \(Q_k\) be the SQP quadratic program \(\min_{d\in\mathbb R^n}\nabla f(x_k)^Td+\tfrac12d^TB_kd\) subject to \(c_k+A_kd=0\) and \(g_k+G_kd\geq0\). Let \(N_{Q_k}(d)\) denote the normal cone of its polyhedral feasible set and define the primal-dual KKT residual using feasibility, stationarity, and complementarity components.
knowledge_statements.scope_note: Finite-dimensional structured SQP subproblems solved by projection, first-order, Krylov, or related matrix-free iterations; this class is distinguished by iterative approximation and residual termination, not by a particular globalization mechanism.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex: An iterative QP solver for SQP is a map that, from an initial inner state \(w_{k,0}\), generates \(w_{k,j+1}=\mathcal I_k(w_{k,j})\) using matrix-vector products, projections, or preconditioned linear operations and returns a step \(d_k=d_{k,j_k}\) at the first accepted index \(j_k\) for which \[\operatorname{dist}\bigl(0,\nabla f(x_k)+B_kd_{k,j}+N_{Q_k}(d_{k,j})\bigr)\leq\varepsilon_k\] together with primal infeasibility at most \(\varepsilon_k\). In an explicit primal-dual representation, this means that stationarity, equality feasibility, inequality feasibility, dual feasibility, and complementarity residuals are jointly bounded by \(\varepsilon_k\).
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: An iterative QP solver constructs a sequence of approximate SQP subproblem solutions using projection, gradient, Krylov, or other repeated linear-algebra operations. It stops when a computable KKT residual and the constraint infeasibility are no larger than the prescribed tolerance \(\varepsilon_k\), and returns the associated approximate step rather than requiring an exact QP solution.
knowledge_statements.conclusion_latex: The returned \(d_k\) is an iterative QP solution exactly in the residual-controlled sense specified above; the definition imposes no finite-termination or direct-factorization requirement.
equivalent_formulations_latex: For equality constraints only, the criterion can be written \(\left\|\begin{bmatrix}B_k&A_k^T\\A_k&0\end{bmatrix}\begin{bmatrix}d\\y\end{bmatrix}+\begin{bmatrix}\nabla f(x_k)\\c_k\end{bmatrix}\right\|\leq\varepsilon_k\), up to the chosen multiplier sign convention.
For a simple convex feasible set \(C_k\), a projected-gradient residual such as \(\|d-\Pi_{C_k}(d-\nabla q_k(d))\|\) may replace the normal-cone distance.
special_cases_latex: Preconditioned conjugate gradients apply to a positive-definite reduced Hessian after equality null-space elimination.
MINRES or GMRES may be applied to a symmetric-indefinite or nonsymmetric preconditioned KKT system.
immediate_consequences_latex: The tolerance \(\varepsilon_k\) separates outer SQP accuracy from inner QP work.
Matrix-free implementations need only operator actions when the selected residual and projection are computable without forming \(B_k\).
boundary_notes: An interior-point iteration is covered only when treated generically as a residual-controlled iteration; path-following positivity and centrality are not defining requirements here.
The definition alone supplies no convergence rate for the inner sequence and no outer SQP convergence guarantee.

top_down_textbook_witnesses.locator: An Inexact SQP Method for Equality Constrained Optimization, SIAM Journal on Optimization 19, 2008

knowledge_statements.slot_contract: State the canonical mathematical definition of the source node, with its domain, quantifiers, notation, and a precise source locator.
knowledge_statements.ambient_context_latex: Consider \(\min f(x)\) subject to \(c(x)=0\) and \(g(x)\geq0\), with Lagrangian \(L(x,y,z)=f(x)-y^Tc(x)-z^Tg(x)\). Let \(F_k(w)=0\) denote a KKT system for the SQP quadratic model at \(x_k\), where \(w\) contains the step and model multipliers.
knowledge_statements.scope_note: Finite-dimensional smooth nonlinear programming in which the SQP subproblem or its KKT equations are solved only approximately. The definition is local-algebraic and does not select a line search, trust region, or filter.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex: An inexact SQP method is an iteration \(x_{k+1}=x_k+\alpha_kd_k\) in which the computed primal-dual model variable \(w_k\) satisfies \[F_k(w_k)=r_k,\qquad \|r_k\|\leq\eta_k\,\mathcal R_k+\delta_k,\] where \(\mathcal R_k\geq0\) is a specified outer KKT residual scale, \(0\leq\eta_k<1\) is a forcing parameter, and \(\delta_k\geq0\) is an absolute error allowance. The model step must also satisfy every feasibility or trust-region condition designated as hard by the chosen SQP formulation. Exact SQP is recovered when \(r_k=0\).
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: Inexact SQP permits an approximate solution of the quadratic subproblem or its primal-dual KKT equations. The allowed error is explicitly controlled by a forcing term proportional to an outer optimality residual, optionally plus an absolute allowance. Constraints declared hard by the SQP model must still be met to their separately specified tolerance.
knowledge_statements.conclusion_latex: A method belongs to the inexact SQP class when its inner error admits the stated residual equation and quantitative forcing bound at every computed outer step.
equivalent_formulations_latex: The error may be expressed as a perturbed model first-order condition \(0\in\nabla q_k(d_k)+N_{C_k}(d_k)+e_k\) with \(\|e_k\|\leq\eta_k\mathcal R_k+\delta_k\).
For an equality-constrained KKT system \(K_kw_k=-b_k\), the condition becomes \(\|K_kw_k+b_k\|\leq\eta_k\mathcal R_k+\delta_k\).
special_cases_latex: A fixed forcing bound \(\eta_k\leq\bar\eta<1\) defines a uniformly inexact regime.
A vanishing forcing sequence \(\eta_k\to0\) and \(\delta_k=o(\mathcal R_k)\) defines an asymptotically increasingly accurate regime.
immediate_consequences_latex: The definition separates inner algebraic accuracy from the outer acceptance rule \(\alpha_k\).
Full-QP, composite-step, and iterative-KKT realizations correspond to different choices of \(F_k\), \(w_k\), and residual blocks.
boundary_notes: Merely using floating-point arithmetic does not make an SQP method inexact in this technical sense; a stated error model or stopping rule is required.
The forcing bound alone does not imply global or superlinear convergence.
No source was inspected that supports this precise umbrella definition across all three named realizations.

knowledge_statements.title: Inexact Full-QP SQP
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: The complete SQP quadratic program is solved only until its primal-dual residual is reduced by a prescribed forcing factor.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex:
At outer iterate \\(x_k\\), form the complete SQP quadratic subproblem and its primal-dual KKT residual mapping \\(R_k(z)\\), where \\(z\\) contains the step, multipliers, and any slacks. Starting from \\(z_k^0\\), compute an approximate subproblem solution \\(z_k\\) satisfying \\[\lVert R_k(z_k)\rVert\le\eta_k\lVert R_k(z_k^0)\rVert,\qquad 0\le\eta_k<1.\
\\] Use its primal component as the trial SQP step, subject to the chosen globalization acceptance test. Stop the inner solve once the forcing inequality holds. For increasingly accurate local solves, choose \\(\eta_k\to0\\); a fixed upper bound below one gives uniformly reduced KKT residuals.
assumptions_latex: The subproblem KKT residual \\(R_k\\) uses a fixed compatible norm.
knowledge_statements.conclusion_latex: The accepted inner iterate supplies a full-QP step whose KKT residual satisfies the prescribed relative accuracy.
knowledge_statements.scope_note: SQP iteration using a residual-controlled approximate solution of the entire quadratic subproblem.

notation.meaning: Primal-dual KKT residual mapping for the kth SQP subproblem.

enrichment_metadata.review_comment: The full-QP residual mapping, treatment of complementarity, compatible norm, and forcing rule depend on the selected inexact SQP framework. No source is supplied to establish that this relative residual test is an adequate definition or stopping condition for the claimed method.

knowledge_statements.statement_title: Inexact Solution of the Complete SQP Quadratic Program
knowledge_statements.ambient_context_latex: At \(x_k\), let \(Q_k\) be the complete SQP subproblem \(\min_d q_k(d)=\nabla f(x_k)^Td+\tfrac12d^TB_kd\) subject to \(c_k+A_kd=0\) and \(g_k+G_kd\geq0\). Let \(w=(d,y,z,s)\) and let \(F_k^{\mathrm{QP}}(w)\) collect stationarity, primal feasibility, dual feasibility, and complementarity residuals.
knowledge_statements.scope_note: Finite-dimensional inexact SQP in which one approximate solve is applied to the complete quadratic program, rather than separately computing normal and tangential components.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex: An inexact full-QP SQP iteration computes a single primal-dual tuple \(w_k=(d_k,y_k,z_k,s_k)\) for the entire subproblem such that \[\|F_k^{\mathrm{QP}}(w_k)\|\leq\varepsilon_k,\qquad s_k\geq-\varepsilon_k\mathbf1,\qquad z_k\geq-\varepsilon_k\mathbf1,\] or, in relative form, \(\|F_k^{\mathrm{QP}}(w_k)\|\leq\eta_k\mathcal R_k\). The same tuple determines the outer trial point \(x_k+\alpha_kd_k\); no exact QP minimizer or exact active set is required.
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: Inexact full-QP SQP approximately solves all coupled optimality conditions of the complete quadratic subproblem in one inner solve. One residual tolerance controls the returned primal step, multipliers, feasibility, and complementarity, and that approximate full-QP step is passed to the SQP globalization procedure.
knowledge_statements.conclusion_latex: The defining output is one approximate KKT tuple for the complete QP whose joint residual and relaxed sign violations satisfy the prescribed tolerance.
equivalent_formulations_latex: For equality constraints, \(F_k^{\mathrm{QP}}(d,y)=\bigl(B_kd+\nabla f(x_k)-A_k^Ty,\ c_k+A_kd\bigr)\).
A computable primal-dual QP gap may replace the joint residual when the model is convex and the gap controls the required feasibility and stationarity errors.
special_cases_latex: When \(\varepsilon_k=0\), the definition reduces to exact full-QP SQP.
An interior-point or active-set QP solver can realize this class if it is stopped before exact solution using the stated full-system test.
immediate_consequences_latex: Coupling is retained between feasibility improvement and objective-model reduction within a single approximate QP solution.
The definition differs from composite-step SQP because it does not assign separate error budgets to normal and tangential computations.
boundary_notes: For an indefinite QP, a small KKT residual need not identify a global QP minimizer; curvature safeguards are outside this definition.
The relaxed sign bounds are residual conventions, not permission for uncontrolled inequality violation.
A precise source locator for this exact full-QP residual definition was not verified.
review_flags: No inspected source supports the exact joint residual and relaxed-sign formulation.

children.title: Inexact Composite-Step SQP
children.top_down_role: Separate approximation regimes for feasibility and tangential computations.

knowledge_statements.title: Inexact Composite-Step SQP
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: A composite-step method approximates feasibility and tangential optimization separately, using independent inner tolerances before combining both components.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex:
At \\(x_k\\), compute a normal step \\(v_k\\) that approximately reduces the linearized constraint residual, with \\(\lVert c_k+A_kv_k\rVert\le\eta_k^N\lVert c_k\rVert\\). Then compute a tangential step \\(t_k\\) approximately satisfying \\(A_kt_k=0\\) and reducing the quadratic model on the tangent space, with projected residual \\[\bigl\lVert Z_k^\top\bigl(g_k+B_k(v_k+t_k)\bigr)\bigr\rVert\le\eta_k^T\Delta_k.\
\\] Set \\(p_k=v_k+t_k\\), apply the chosen globalization test, and return the accepted step. The forcing factors \\(\eta_k^N\\) and \\(\eta_k^T\\) may be chosen independently according to feasibility and optimality progress.
assumptions_latex: \\(A_k=c'(x_k)\\) has a well-defined tangent space.
\\(0\le\eta_k^N,\eta_k^T<1\\).
knowledge_statements.conclusion_latex: \\(p_k=v_k+t_k\\) has separately controlled linearized-feasibility and projected-optimality residuals.
knowledge_statements.scope_note: Separate residual budgets for normal feasibility reduction and tangential objective reduction.

notation.meaning: Normal step for reducing constraint violation.
Tangential step for reducing the quadratic model.
Basis for the null space of the constraint Jacobian.

enrichment_metadata.review_comment: The normal-step and tangential-step tolerances are method-specific, and Delta_k is not defined. A source is needed to determine the intended scaling, feasibility condition, projected residual, and globalization compatibility before a reliable replacement can be made.

knowledge_statements.slot_contract: State the canonical mathematical definition of the source node, with its domain, quantifiers, notation, and a precise source locator.
knowledge_statements.ambient_context_latex: For the equality-constrained problem \(\min f(x)\) subject to \(c(x)=0\), write \(A_k=\nabla c(x_k)^T\). A composite SQP step has the decomposition \(d_k=n_k+t_k\), where \(n_k\) targets the linearized constraint residual and \(t_k\) targets objective reduction approximately within \(\ker A_k\).
knowledge_statements.scope_note: Finite-dimensional smooth equality-constrained SQP with separately controlled feasibility and tangential computations. Inequalities require an active-set, slack, or normal-cone extension not fixed here.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex: An inexact composite-step SQP method computes \(n_k\) and \(t_k\) with separate tests \[\|A_kn_k+c(x_k)\|\leq\varepsilon_k^{N},\qquad \|A_kt_k\|\leq\varepsilon_k^{T},\] and a tangential model-stationarity test \[\|Z_k^T(\nabla f(x_k)+B_k(n_k+t_k))\|\leq\varepsilon_k^{S},\] where the columns of \(Z_k\) span \(\ker A_k\). The outer trial step is \(d_k=n_k+t_k\). Equivalent projected tests are allowed when no explicit null-space basis is formed.
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: The method splits the approximate SQP step into a normal component that reduces linearized infeasibility and a tangential component that improves the quadratic objective while remaining approximately tangent to the constraints. Independent tolerances govern normal feasibility, tangency, and reduced model stationarity.
knowledge_statements.conclusion_latex: A step is an inexact composite SQP step when it admits the stated normal-tangential decomposition and satisfies all three independently specified residual bounds.
equivalent_formulations_latex: The tangency and stationarity conditions can be written with the orthogonal projector \(P_k\) onto \(\ker A_k\) as \(\|(I-P_k)t_k\|\) small and \(\|P_k(\nabla f(x_k)+B_kd_k)\|\leq\varepsilon_k^S\).
If \(A_k\) has full row rank, the minimum-norm exact normal step is \(n_k=-A_k^T(A_kA_k^T)^{-1}c(x_k)\); an inexact normal step approximates its defining feasibility equation.
special_cases_latex: Setting all three tolerances to zero gives an exact normal-tangential decomposition of an equality-constrained SQP step.
A trust-region composite step may additionally require \(\|n_k+t_k\|\leq\Delta_k\).
immediate_consequences_latex: Feasibility work can be terminated by a criterion different from the reduced-Hessian solve.
The formulation permits matrix-free null-space projections without solving the complete KKT system to one uniform tolerance.
boundary_notes: The definition does not prescribe how incompatible linearized constraints are relaxed.
Without a specified inequality extension, it does not define normal and tangential cones for general inequalities.
No authoritative source was inspected for these exact three stopping conditions.

children.title: Iterative KKT SQP
children.top_down_role: SQP using iterative KKT solvers and residual-controlled inner accuracy.

knowledge_statements.title: Iterative KKT SQP
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: An iterative KKT solve stops after its preconditioned residual falls below a prescribed fraction of the right-hand-side norm.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex:
Let the SQP Newton or equality-constrained QP equations be \\(K_ky=b_k\\), with symmetric saddle-point matrix \\(K_k\\). An iterative KKT solve is acceptable when its iterate \\(y_k\\) satisfies \\[r_k=b_k-K_ky_k,\qquad \lVert P_k^{-1}r_k\rVert\le\eta_k\lVert P_k^{-1}b_k\rVert,\qquad 0\le\eta_k<1,\
\\] where \\(P_k\\) is the identity or a nonsingular preconditioner. The primal block of \\(y_k\\) defines the SQP step and the dual block defines the multiplier correction. For local Newton accuracy, the forcing sequence is tightened, commonly with \\(\eta_k\to0\\).
assumptions_latex: \\(K_k\\) and \\(P_k\\) are nonsingular on the subspace used by the iteration.
knowledge_statements.conclusion_latex: The computed primal-dual correction has a relative preconditioned KKT residual bounded by \\(\eta_k\\).
knowledge_statements.scope_note: Residual stopping condition for iterative solution of an SQP KKT linear system.

enrichment_metadata.review_comment: The condition kind fits this residual-stopping leaf, but no source supports the particular left-preconditioned norm, denominator, nonsingularity assumptions, or assertion that eta_k tending to zero supplies the intended local Newton accuracy.

knowledge_statements.slot_contract: State the canonical mathematical definition of the source node, with its domain, quantifiers, notation, and a precise source locator.
knowledge_statements.ambient_context_latex: For an equality-constrained SQP model, define \(K_k=\begin{bmatrix}B_k&-A_k^T\\A_k&0\end{bmatrix}\), \(u_k=(d_k,y_k)\), and \(b_k=(\nabla f(x_k),c(x_k))\). The exact model equations are \(K_ku_k=-b_k\). Inequality variants arise after an active-set choice or primal-dual linearization.
knowledge_statements.scope_note: Finite-dimensional SQP whose inner computation is an iterative linear solve of a KKT system, ordinarily Krylov-based and possibly preconditioned. The definition concerns algebraic residual control.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex:
An iterative KKT SQP method generates inner iterates \(u_{k,j}\) in affine Krylov or comparable iterative-solver spaces and returns \(u_k=u_{k,j_k}\) when \[r_{k,j_k}=K_ku_{k,j_k}+b_k,
\qquad \|P_k^{-1}r_{k,j_k}\|\leq\eta_k\|P_k^{-1}b_k\|+\delta_k,\] where \(P_k\) is a nonsingular preconditioner, \(0\leq\eta_k<1\), and \(\delta_k\geq0\). The primal component of \(u_k\) is the SQP step; the dual component is the model multiplier estimate.
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: Iterative KKT SQP obtains the step and multiplier by stopping an iterative linear solver before the KKT equations are solved exactly. A relative-plus-absolute bound on the preconditioned KKT residual controls inner accuracy, and the primal block of the accepted linear-system iterate becomes the SQP step.
knowledge_statements.conclusion_latex: The method is iterative KKT SQP precisely when the accepted SQP step is extracted from an iteratively generated KKT-system approximation satisfying the stated residual test.
equivalent_formulations_latex: With \(P_k=I\) and \(\delta_k=0\), the test is the standard relative residual condition \(\|K_ku_k+b_k\|\leq\eta_k\|b_k\|\).
A reduced-space iterative solve is equivalent when its reconstructed primal-dual pair satisfies the full KKT residual bound.
special_cases_latex: MINRES applies when the preconditioned representation preserves symmetry; GMRES permits a nonsymmetric preconditioned operator.
For an exact inner solve, \(\eta_k=\delta_k=0\) and \(r_k=0\).
immediate_consequences_latex: The preconditioner changes the measured residual and computational behavior but not the exact KKT solution when it is nonsingular.
A decreasing forcing sequence can require progressively more accurate KKT solves as the outer residual decreases.
boundary_notes: A small linear-system residual may not ensure a useful step when \(K_k\) is badly conditioned; error-based stopping is a nearby stronger variant.
Iterative solution of a nonlinear QP optimality mapping without forming successive linear KKT systems belongs more naturally to iterative full-QP solving.
No inspected locator supports this precise preconditioned residual definition.

knowledge_statements.ambient_context_latex: Let an SQP model at \(x_k\) produce a candidate step \(d_k\) for a smooth constrained nonlinear program. Let \(\mathcal V(x)\geq0\) measure constraint violation and let \(\mathcal M_k(d)\) denote the local objective-Lagrangian and constraint model used to predict progress.
knowledge_statements.scope_note: Finite-dimensional smooth constrained optimization. This is a class definition covering scalar-merit line searches, trust regions, filters, feasible methods, and nonmonotone acceptance rules.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex: An SQP globalization family augments the local SQP step computation with a control state \(\gamma_k\) and an acceptance predicate \[\mathsf{Accept}_k(x_k,d,\gamma_k)\in\{\mathrm{true},\mathrm{false}\}\] based on actual values of \(f\), \(\mathcal V\), or a scalar merit function and on model-predicted progress. If a trial step is rejected, the mechanism modifies a step length, trust-region radius, restoration state, penalty parameter, filter, or reference value and generates another trial. The accepted update has the form \(x_{k+1}=x_k+s_k\), where \(s_k\) is either a scaled SQP step or a recomputed restricted step.
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: An SQP globalization family is an SQP method equipped with an explicit trial-step acceptance rule and a state-update mechanism. Acceptance compares actual objective or feasibility behavior with predicted behavior; rejection changes a control such as step length, radius, penalty weight, filter, or reference value before another trial is considered.
knowledge_statements.conclusion_latex: A local SQP iteration is globalized in this sense exactly when trial acceptance and rejection are governed by an explicit nonlocal control state and measurable progress predicate.
special_cases_latex: Line-search SQP sets \(s_k=\alpha_kd_k\) and reduces \(\alpha_k\) after rejection.
Trust-region SQP recomputes or restricts \(d\) under \(\|d\|\leq\Delta_k\).
Filter SQP accepts using a partial order involving objective and constraint violation rather than a fixed scalar penalty.
immediate_consequences_latex: The local quadratic model and the globalization mechanism are logically distinct components of an SQP method.
Different families may use the same QP step while accepting different trial points.
boundary_notes: The word globalized does not itself guarantee convergence from every starting point; such a theorem requires regularity, boundedness, model-quality, and safeguard assumptions.
Restoration procedures and second-order corrections are compatible additions but are not required by this class definition.
No single inspected source locator was established for this full taxonomy-level definition.
review_flags: The taxonomy-wide definition and its exact acceptance abstraction need an authoritative source.

knowledge_statements.slot_contract: State the canonical mathematical definition of the source node, with its domain, quantifiers, notation, and a precise source locator.
knowledge_statements.ambient_context_latex: At \(x_k\), let \(d_k\) be an SQP direction and let \(\Phi_k:\mathbb R^n\to\mathbb R\) be a merit function or scalar acceptance function. Let \(D\Phi_k(x_k;d_k)\) denote its directional derivative, which may be nonsmooth.
knowledge_statements.scope_note: Finite-dimensional smooth constrained optimization with a scalar line-search acceptance function; nonsmooth exact-penalty merit functions are permitted through directional derivatives.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex: A line-search SQP method selects \(\alpha_k\) from a decreasing trial sequence, commonly \(\{1,\beta,\beta^2,\ldots\}\) with \(0<\beta<1\), and sets \(x_{k+1}=x_k+\alpha_kd_k\). A canonical sufficient-decrease acceptance test is \[\Phi_k(x_k+\alpha_kd_k)\leq\Phi_k(x_k)+\sigma\alpha_kD\Phi_k(x_k;d_k),\qquad 0<\sigma<1,\] with the direction required to satisfy \(D\Phi_k(x_k;d_k)<0\), unless a restoration or correction step is invoked.
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: Line-search SQP first computes an SQP direction and then chooses a scalar step length. Trial lengths are reduced until a scalar merit or acceptance function achieves sufficient decrease relative to its directional prediction; the accepted iterate is \(x_k+\alpha_kd_k\).
knowledge_statements.conclusion_latex: The defining globalization operation is selection of a scalar \(\alpha_k>0\) along the fixed SQP direction using the stated sufficient-decrease predicate.
equivalent_formulations_latex: The directional derivative may be replaced by a model decrement \(-\operatorname{Pred}_k(d_k)<0\), giving \(\Phi_k(x_k+\alpha d_k)\leq\Phi_k(x_k)-\sigma\alpha\operatorname{Pred}_k(d_k)\).
special_cases_latex: Backtracking begins with \(\alpha=1\) and repeatedly applies \(\alpha\leftarrow\beta\alpha\).
An exact line search chooses a minimizer of \(\alpha\mapsto\Phi_k(x_k+\alpha d_k)\) over a prescribed interval.
A nonmonotone line search replaces \(\Phi_k(x_k)\) on the right by a controlled reference value.

knowledge_statements.title: L1 Merit-Function SQP
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: The method applies Armijo backtracking to the objective plus an L1 measure of equality violations and positive-part inequality violations, after choosing the penalty parameter so that the SQP step is a descent direction.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex: Let \(f:\mathbb R^n\to\mathbb R\), \(h:\mathbb R^n\to\mathbb R^{m_e}\), and \(g:\mathbb R^n\to\mathbb R^{m_i}\) be continuously differentiable, with constraints \(h(x)=0\) and \(g(x)\le0\). For \(\rho>0\), define \[\Phi_\rho(x)=f(x)+\rho\left(\lVert h(x)\rVert_1+\lVert[g(x)]_+\rVert_1\right).\] At iterate \(x_k\), compute an SQP step \(p_k\) and choose \(\rho_k>0\) such that \(\Phi_{\rho_k}'(x_k;p_k)<0\). Given \(0<\beta<1\) and \(0<\sigma<1\), choose \(\alpha_k=\beta^j\), where \(j\) is the first nonnegative integer satisfying \[\Phi_{\rho_k}(x_k+\alpha_kp_k)\le\Phi_{\rho_k}(x_k)+\sigma\alpha_k\Phi_{\rho_k}'(x_k;p_k).\] Set \(x_{k+1}=x_k+\alpha_kp_k\). The derivative is directional because \(\Phi_\rho\) is generally nonsmooth.
assumptions_latex: \(f:\mathbb R^n\to\mathbb R\), \(h:\mathbb R^n\to\mathbb R^{m_e}\), and \(g:\mathbb R^n\to\mathbb R^{m_i}\) are continuously differentiable.
\(\rho_k>0\) is chosen so that \(\Phi_{\rho_k}'(x_k;p_k)<0\).

For an unconstrained problem, the violation term vanishes and the test reduces to an objective line search.

knowledge_statements.statement_plain: The method applies Armijo backtracking to the objective plus the largest equality or positive-part inequality violation, after choosing the penalty parameter so that the SQP step is a descent direction.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex: Let \(f:\mathbb R^n\to\mathbb R\), \(h:\mathbb R^n\to\mathbb R^{m_e}\), and \(g:\mathbb R^n\to\mathbb R^{m_i}\) be continuously differentiable, with constraints \(h(x)=0\) and \(g(x)\le0\). Define \[V_\infty(x)=\max\left\{\lVert h(x)\rVert_\infty,\lVert[g(x)]_+\rVert_\infty\right\},\qquad \Phi_\rho(x)=f(x)+\rho V_\infty(x),\quad \rho>0.\] At iterate \(x_k\), compute an SQP step \(p_k\) and choose \(\rho_k>0\) such that \(\Phi_{\rho_k}'(x_k;p_k)<0\). Given \(0<\beta<1\) and \(0<\sigma<1\), choose \(\alpha_k=\beta^j\), where \(j\) is the first nonnegative integer satisfying \[\Phi_{\rho_k}(x_k+\alpha_kp_k)\le\Phi_{\rho_k}(x_k)+\sigma\alpha_k\Phi_{\rho_k}'(x_k;p_k).\] Set \(x_{k+1}=x_k+\alpha_kp_k\). The maximum and positive-part operations make \(\Phi_\rho\) generally nonsmooth, so its directional derivative is used.

knowledge_statements.statement_plain: A differentiable locally exact penalty globalizes an SQP-based primal-auxiliary descent direction through an ordinary gradient Armijo line search.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex: Let \(P_\rho:\mathbb R^n\times\mathbb R^q\to\mathbb R\) be continuously differentiable in the primal variable \(x\in\mathbb R^n\) and auxiliary variable \(w\in\mathbb R^q\). Assume that there is \(\bar\rho>0\) such that, for every \(\rho\ge\bar\rho\), local minimizers of \(P_\rho\) in a specified neighborhood correspond to KKT points of the constrained problem. At iteration \(k\), compute an SQP-based direction \((p_k,d_k^w)\in\mathbb R^n\times\mathbb R^q\) and choose \(\rho_k\ge\bar\rho\) such that \[\nabla P_{\rho_k}(x_k,w_k)^\top(p_k,d_k^w)<0.\] Given \(0<\beta<1\) and \(0<\sigma<1\), choose \(\alpha_k=\beta^j\), where \(j\) is the first nonnegative integer satisfying \[P_{\rho_k}\bigl((x_k,w_k)+\alpha_k(p_k,d_k^w)\bigr)\le P_{\rho_k}(x_k,w_k)+\sigma\alpha_k\nabla P_{\rho_k}(x_k,w_k)^\top(p_k,d_k^w).\] Update \((x_{k+1},w_{k+1})=(x_k,w_k)+\alpha_k(p_k,d_k^w)\).

For every \(\rho\ge\bar\rho\), local minimizers of \(P_\rho\) in the specified neighborhood correspond to constrained KKT points.
The computed direction is a descent direction for \(P_{\rho_k}\).

knowledge_statements.statement_title: Differentiable Exact-Penalty Merit SQP with Multiplier Estimation
knowledge_statements.ambient_context_latex: Consider \(\min f(x)\) subject to \(c(x)=0\), with \(f,c\) twice continuously differentiable. Let \(A(x)=\nabla c(x)^T\) have full row rank on a neighborhood and define the smooth least-squares multiplier estimate \(y(x)=(A(x)A(x)^T)^{-1}A(x)\nabla f(x)\).
knowledge_statements.scope_note: Finite-dimensional equality-constrained line-search SQP using a differentiable exact-penalty construction based on a smooth multiplier estimate. General inequalities require a distinct extension.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex: A smooth exact-penalty SQP method uses a continuously differentiable function of the form \[\Phi_\rho^{\mathrm{SE}}(x)=f(x)-c(x)^Ty(x)+\frac\rho2\|c(x)\|_2^2\] and requires local exactness: for each regular constrained local solution \(x_*\), there is a finite \(\bar\rho\) such that \(x_*\) is a local minimizer of \(\Phi_\rho^{\mathrm{SE}}\) for every \(\rho>\bar\rho\). The SQP direction is globalized by a smooth sufficient-decrease line search in \(\Phi_{\rho_k}^{\mathrm{SE}}\), with \(\rho_k\) chosen to obtain descent.
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: The method replaces a nonsmooth absolute-value penalty by a differentiable merit function that incorporates a smooth multiplier estimate. It subtracts the estimated multiplier pairing with the constraint residual and adds a squared feasibility term. Above a finite local threshold, the constrained solution is required to remain a local minimizer, and a smooth line search globalizes the SQP direction.
knowledge_statements.conclusion_latex: The family is defined by a differentiable multiplier-estimate penalty possessing the stated finite-threshold local exactness property and used as the SQP line-search function.
equivalent_formulations_latex: The multiplier estimate is the unique minimizer of \(\min_y\|\nabla f(x)-A(x)^Ty\|_2^2\) when \(A(x)\) has full row rank.
Other smooth multiplier estimates may replace the displayed least-squares estimate if their defining source establishes differentiability and exactness of the resulting penalty.
special_cases_latex: At a feasible KKT point, \(c(x_*)=0\) and \(y(x_*)\) equals the least-squares KKT multiplier.
For an unconstrained problem, the correction and penalty terms vanish, leaving \(f\).
immediate_consequences_latex: Ordinary gradient-based Armijo tests apply wherever \(A(x)A(x)^T\) remains nonsingular.
The construction differs from a quadratic penalty because of the multiplier-correction term \(-c(x)^Ty(x)\).
boundary_notes: Full row rank is essential for the displayed multiplier formula; rank-deficient variants require a generalized inverse and additional smoothness analysis.
Smoothness alone does not establish exactness; the finite-threshold property is part of the definition and needs hypotheses.
No inspected source confirms this exact formula and threshold statement.

knowledge_statements.statement_title: Predicted-Reduction Management of an SQP Penalty Weight
knowledge_statements.ambient_context_latex: Let \(\Phi_\rho(x)=f(x)+\rho v(x)\), where \(v(x)\geq0\) measures constraint violation. For an SQP step \(d_k\), let \(q_k(d)=\nabla f(x_k)^Td+\tfrac12d^TB_kd\) and let \(v_k^{\mathrm{lin}}(d)\) be the violation of the linearized constraints.
knowledge_statements.scope_note: Finite-dimensional merit-function SQP with a nonnegative penalty weight chosen from predicted objective and feasibility changes. The rule is independent of whether \(v\) is an L1 or maximum-norm violation.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex: Define the predicted merit reduction \[\operatorname{Pred}_k(\rho;d_k)=-q_k(d_k)+\rho\bigl(v(x_k)-v_k^{\mathrm{lin}}(d_k)\bigr).\] A penalty-parameter management rule selects \(\rho_k\geq\rho_{k-1}\) so that \[\operatorname{Pred}_k(\rho_k;d_k)\geq\theta\rho_k\bigl(v(x_k)-v_k^{\mathrm{lin}}(d_k)\bigr)>0\] whenever the predicted violation decrease is positive, where \(0<\theta<1\). A safeguarded implementation chooses the smallest value satisfying this inequality and a lower bound, then optionally rounds upward by a factor \(\tau>1\).
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: Penalty management compares the SQP model's objective change with its predicted reduction in constraint violation. The weight is retained when the combined predicted merit decrease is adequate and increased only enough to meet a fixed sufficient-prediction condition. A safeguard or geometric enlargement prevents marginal updates.
knowledge_statements.conclusion_latex: The managed sequence \((\rho_k)\) is defined by nondecreasing, safeguarded selection satisfying the displayed predicted-merit reduction inequality at each applicable iteration.
equivalent_formulations_latex: If \(\Delta v_k=v(x_k)-v_k^{\mathrm{lin}}(d_k)>0\), the inequality is equivalent to \(\rho_k\geq q_k(d_k)/((1-\theta)\Delta v_k)\) when the right-hand side is positive.
The reciprocal convention \(\Phi_\mu=\mu f+v\) produces a nonincreasing objective weight \(\mu_k\) instead of a nondecreasing violation weight \(\rho_k\).
special_cases_latex: A monotone update sets \(\rho_k=\max\{\rho_{k-1},\rho_k^{\mathrm{trial}}\}\).
A geometric safeguard sets \(\rho_k=\rho_{k-1}\) when adequate and otherwise chooses at least \(\tau\rho_{k-1}\).
immediate_consequences_latex: The rule explicitly couples the global merit function to the local SQP model.
If the old weight already satisfies the prediction condition, no increase is required.
boundary_notes: When the model predicts no violation decrease, the displayed quotient rule is undefined and a restoration or alternative safeguard is required.
Nondecreasing penalty weights need not remain bounded without additional assumptions on multiplier estimates and steps.
The exact prediction formula varies across SQP conventions, and no authoritative source was inspected for this version.

knowledge_statements.title: Monotone Penalty Management
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: Maintain an exact-penalty weight that can increase but never decrease, raising it when multiplier estimates or predicted merit descent require stronger feasibility emphasis.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex: For the merit function \(\Phi_\rho(x)=f(x)+\rho v(x)\), initialize \(\rho_0>0\). At iteration \(k\), let \(d_k\) be the SQP step and \(\widehat\lambda_{k+1}\) the QP multiplier estimate. Choose a safeguard \(\delta>0\) and set \(\widehat\rho_k=\max\{\rho_k,\|\widehat\lambda_{k+1}\|_\infty+\delta\}\). If the predicted merit reduction computed with \(\widehat\rho_k\) satisfies the prescribed positive-fraction condition, take \(\rho_{k+1}=\widehat\rho_k\); otherwise increase it until that condition holds. Thus accepted updates obey \(\rho_{k+1}\geq\rho_k\).
assumptions_latex: \(f\) and the constraint functions are continuously differentiable near the iterates.
\(v(x)\geq0\) is an exact-penalty violation measure with \(v(x)=0\) exactly at feasible points.
knowledge_statements.conclusion_latex: \(\rho_{k+1}\geq\rho_k>0\), and each accepted step satisfies the chosen predicted merit-decrease test.
knowledge_statements.scope_note: One-directional updates for an exact-penalty merit function in line-search SQP.

knowledge_statements.statement_title: Monotone management of an SQP exact-penalty parameter
knowledge_statements.ambient_context_latex: Consider a smooth equality-constrained problem \(\min_{x\in\mathbb R^n} f(x)\) subject to \(c(x)=0\), an SQP trial step \(s_k\), and the exact merit function \(\phi(x,\sigma)=f(x)+\sigma\lVert c(x)\rVert\), where \(\sigma>0\). Let \(\delta m_k^{F}\) and \(\delta m_k^{N}>0\) denote, respectively, the objective-model and feasibility-model contributions to predicted reduction.
knowledge_statements.scope_note: Finite-dimensional smooth SQP with an exact-penalty merit function. The definition concerns the parameter rule, not convergence of the resulting method.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex: A penalty-management rule is monotone if it generates \(\{\sigma_k\}_{k\ge0}\subset(0,\infty)\) satisfying \(\sigma_k\ge\sigma_{k-1}\) at every iteration. A canonical sufficient-decrease realization fixes \(\nu\in(0,1)\), \(\tau_1\ge1\), and \(\tau_2\ge0\) with \((\tau_1-1)\tau_2>0\), computes a required threshold \[\sigma_k^C=\max\!\left\{\sigma_k^B,-\frac{\delta m_k^F}{(1-\nu)\delta m_k^N}\right\},\] and sets \[\sigma_k=\begin{cases}\max\{\sigma_k^C,\tau_1\sigma_{k-1},\sigma_{k-1}+\tau_2\},&\sigma_{k-1}<\sigma_k^C,\\ \sigma_{k-1},&\sigma_{k-1}\ge\sigma_k^C.\end{cases}\] Here \(\sigma_k^B\ge0\) is an auxiliary bounded lower target, often formed from a multiplier estimate. Thus the parameter is retained when already adequate and is otherwise increased by a nontrivial amount; it is never reduced.
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: Monotone penalty management generates a positive penalty sequence that can stay fixed or increase but can never decrease. A canonical SQP rule first computes the least parameter needed for sufficient predicted merit decrease, possibly also imposing a bounded multiplier-based target. If the old parameter meets that threshold, it is retained. Otherwise it is replaced by the maximum of the threshold, a multiplicative increase, and an additive increase. The constants are chosen so every actual change is nontrivial.
knowledge_statements.conclusion_latex: \(\sigma_k\ge\sigma_{k-1}>0\) for every \(k\), with equality when the preceding value meets the current adequacy threshold.
equivalent_formulations_latex: The defining property is equivalently that \(\{\sigma_k\}\) is a nondecreasing sequence in \((0,\infty)\).
special_cases_latex: With \(\tau_1>1\) and \(\tau_2=0\), an inadequate parameter is increased at least multiplicatively.
With \(\tau_1=1\) and \(\tau_2>0\), an inadequate parameter is increased at least additively.
immediate_consequences_latex: Every update satisfies \(\sigma_k\ge\max\{\sigma_{k-1},\sigma_k^C\}\).
If the adequacy test eventually remains satisfied, then \(\sigma_k\) is eventually constant.
boundary_notes: This definition excludes parameter rules that deliberately decrease an oversized penalty after substantial feasibility progress.
The convention uses a penalty weight multiplying constraint violation; reciprocal-parameter conventions reverse the apparent monotonic direction.

notation.meaning: positive predicted reduction in the constraint-violation model

knowledge_statements.title: Adaptive Penalty Management
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: Adapt the penalty weight to multiplier estimates and descent tests, allowing safeguarded increases or decreases while retaining a positive lower bound.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex: For \(\Phi_\rho(x)=f(x)+\rho v(x)\), fix \(0<\rho_{\min}\), \(\delta>0\), and factors \(0<\gamma_-<1<\gamma_+\). Given a multiplier estimate \(\widehat\lambda_{k+1}\), define the target \(\tau_k=\max\{\rho_{\min},\|\widehat\lambda_{k+1}\|_\infty+\delta\}\). Increase \(\rho_k\) toward or beyond \(\tau_k\) when the current value fails the predicted merit-descent test. When that test remains satisfied and \(\rho_k\) substantially exceeds \(\tau_k\), permit the safeguarded reduction \(\rho_{k+1}=\max\{\tau_k,\gamma_-\rho_k\}\); otherwise retain \(\rho_k\).
assumptions_latex: \(v\) is a nonnegative exact-penalty violation measure.
The SQP subproblem supplies a finite multiplier estimate \(\widehat\lambda_{k+1}\).
knowledge_statements.conclusion_latex: \(\rho_{k+1}\geq\rho_{\min}\), while \(\rho_{k+1}\) may be either larger or smaller than \(\rho_k\).
knowledge_statements.scope_note: Multiplier-responsive penalty updates permitting both increases and safeguarded decreases.

Terms such as “substantially exceeds” and “increase toward or beyond” do not determine an algorithm, and the introduced factor gamma-plus is never used. A source for a precise multiplier-responsive decrease rule is required.

knowledge_statements.ambient_context_latex: Let \(\phi(x,\sigma)=f(x)+\sigma v(x)\) be an exact-penalty merit function for a finite-dimensional constrained problem, where \(v(x)\ge0\) measures constraint violation. At iteration \(k\), let \(y_k\) be a multiplier estimate and let \(v_k=v(x_k)\).
knowledge_statements.scope_note: Smooth nonlinear programming with an exact-penalty merit function. Unlike monotone management, the rule may reduce an unnecessarily large penalty weight.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex: Penalty management is adaptive when the positive parameter \(\sigma_k\) is selected from current multiplier, model, and feasibility information without imposing \(\sigma_k\ge\sigma_{k-1}\). A canonical instance uses positive margins \(\epsilon_1,\epsilon_2\): if \(\sigma_{k-1}<\lVert y_k\rVert_D\), it increases the weight according to \[\sigma_k\ge\max\{\sigma_{k-1}+\epsilon_1,\lVert y_k\rVert_D+\epsilon_2\}.\] If a prescribed significant-feasibility event occurs, for example \(v_k\le v_{k-1}-\epsilon_v\) with \(\epsilon_v>0\), the rule may reset \(\sigma_k\) to any selected positive value, including a value below \(\sigma_{k-1}\). Otherwise it may retain the old value. The defining feature is therefore a bidirectional, state-responsive map \[\sigma_k=U(\sigma_{k-1},y_k,v_k,v_{k-1},\text{model data})>0\] whose increases enforce penalty adequacy and whose permitted decreases control excessive conditioning.
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: Adaptive penalty management chooses the positive exact-penalty weight from current multiplier estimates, constraint violation, and model information, without requiring a nondecreasing sequence. It raises an inadequate weight above a multiplier-based threshold. After a certified significant reduction in infeasibility, it may retain, increase, or reduce the weight. This distinguishes the family from monotone rules, which forbid every decrease.
knowledge_statements.conclusion_latex: The update always has \(\sigma_k>0\), but both \(\sigma_k>\sigma_{k-1}\) and \(\sigma_k<\sigma_{k-1}\) are permitted when triggered by the current state.
equivalent_formulations_latex: Adaptive management is equivalently a positive-valued feedback law for the penalty parameter whose admissible update set is not restricted to \([\sigma_{k-1},\infty)\).
special_cases_latex: Suppressing every decrease recovers monotone penalty management.
A multiplier-only rule increases \(\sigma_k\) whenever it lies below \(\lVert y_k\rVert_D\).
immediate_consequences_latex: A decrease can undo an excessively large penalty weight after sufficient feasibility progress.
The multiplier margin prevents an accepted downward reset from being treated as permanently adequate when later multiplier estimates exceed it.
boundary_notes: An arbitrary oscillating positive sequence is not adaptive management unless its changes are tied to specified algorithmic information.
Reciprocal penalty conventions must translate increase and decrease directions accordingly.

knowledge_statements.slot_contract: State the canonical mathematical definition of the source node, with its domain, quantifiers, notation, and a precise source locator.
knowledge_statements.ambient_context_latex: Consider \(\min_{x\in\mathbb R^n}f(x)\) subject to \(c_E(x)=0\) and \(c_I(x)\ge0\), with continuously differentiable constraints and objective. At \(x_k\), write \(g_k=\nabla f(x_k)\), \(A_k=\nabla c(x_k)\), and let \(H_k=H_k^T\) approximate the Lagrangian Hessian.
knowledge_statements.scope_note: Finite-dimensional smooth nonlinear programming. The definition covers coupled and composite-step trust-region SQP variants and does not prescribe a particular merit or filter acceptance device.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex: A trust-region SQP method constructs each trial displacement from a quadratic Lagrangian model subject to local constraint models and an explicit radius. In its coupled form it approximately solves \[\min_s\;q_k(s)=g_k^Ts+\tfrac12s^TH_ks\quad\text{subject to}\quad c_E(x_k)+A_{E,k}s=0,\;c_I(x_k)+A_{I,k}s\ge0,\;\lVert s\rVert_k\le\Delta_k.\] If the linearized constraints are incompatible with the ball, the method replaces this problem by a specified relaxation or decomposes \(s_k=n_k+t_k\), where \(n_k\) reduces linearized infeasibility and \(t_k\) reduces the quadratic model while preserving the normal-step feasibility gain. A trial point is assessed by agreement between an actual progress measure and its local prediction; rejection leaves \(x_{k+1}=x_k\), while acceptance sets \(x_{k+1}=x_k+s_k\). The radius \(\Delta_k>0\) is contracted after poor agreement and may be retained or enlarged after adequate agreement.
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: A trust-region SQP method forms a quadratic approximation to the Lagrangian, linearizes the constraints, and restricts the trial displacement to a norm ball of positive radius. It may solve one coupled constrained quadratic model or split the step into feasibility and tangential components when the coupled model is incompatible. Acceptance compares achieved progress with predicted progress, and the agreement controls both acceptance and the next radius.
knowledge_statements.conclusion_latex: Every trial step is generated under an explicit trust-region restriction \(\lVert s_k\rVert_k\le\Delta_k\), or under component restrictions guaranteeing a uniformly bounded composite step.
equivalent_formulations_latex: The radius constraint may use any fixed or uniformly equivalent norm; weighted Euclidean and polyhedral trust regions are standard.
A composite-step realization replaces the single constrained model by consecutive normal and tangential model problems.
special_cases_latex: With no constraints, the definition reduces to an ordinary trust-region method.
If the linearized constraints intersect the ball and a single quadratic program is solved, the method is coupled trust-region SQP.
immediate_consequences_latex: The method can reject an unreliable SQP step without changing the current iterate.
Incompatibility of the linearized constraints and the trust-region ball necessitates relaxation, decomposition, or restoration.
boundary_notes: A line-search SQP method that computes an unrestricted direction and controls only a scalar step length is outside this definition.
The definition alone supplies no convergence claim.

knowledge_statements.title: Coupled Trust-Region SQP
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: Compute the whole SQP step in one equality-constrained quadratic model under a single trust-region bound, then update the radius from model agreement.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex: At iterate \(x_k\), form \(g_k=\nabla f(x_k)\), \(c_k=c(x_k)\), \(A_k=\nabla c(x_k)\), and a symmetric Lagrangian-Hessian approximation \(B_k\). For radius \(\Delta_k>0\), compute one step \(d_k\) from \[\min_d\; g_k^\top d+\tfrac12 d^\top B_kd\quad\text{subject to}\quad c_k+A_kd=0,\qquad \|d\|\leq\Delta_k.\] Accept or reject \(d_k\) by comparing actual and predicted reduction in a globalization measure, then update \(\Delta_k\). The same norm bound controls feasibility correction and tangential objective improvement.
assumptions_latex: \(f:\mathbb R^n\to\mathbb R\) and \(c:\mathbb R^n\to\mathbb R^m\) are continuously differentiable.
The displayed trust-region subproblem is feasible.
knowledge_statements.conclusion_latex: The trial step satisfies \(c_k+A_kd_k=0\) and \(\|d_k\|\leq\Delta_k\).
knowledge_statements.scope_note: Equality-constrained SQP with one trust region imposed directly on the complete step.
