knowledge_statements.ambient_context_latex: For a smooth nonlinear program, let \(q_k(s)=g_k^Ts+\tfrac12s^TH_ks\) be the local quadratic objective model and let \(\mathcal L_k\) be the feasible set of the linearized equality and inequality constraints at \(x_k\).
knowledge_statements.scope_note: Finite-dimensional smooth SQP in which feasibility, optimality, and step size are handled in one subproblem.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex: A coupled trust-region SQP step is any prescribed approximate solution \(s_k\) of the single model problem \[\min_{s\in\mathbb R^n}q_k(s)\quad\text{subject to}\quad s\in\mathcal L_k,\qquad \lVert s\rVert_k\le\Delta_k,\] where \(\Delta_k>0\). Thus the same variable \(s\) simultaneously satisfies the linearized constraints, reduces the quadratic model, and obeys one trust-region bound. For equality constraints, \(\mathcal L_k=\{s:c(x_k)+A_ks=0\}\); with inequalities it additionally includes \(c_I(x_k)+A_{I,k}s\ge0\). The defining coupling is lost if separate normal and tangential subproblems with independent radii are used. The subproblem is well defined only when \(\mathcal L_k\cap\{s:\lVert s\rVert_k\le\Delta_k\}\ne\varnothing\); a method that encounters an empty intersection must invoke a declared relaxation or restoration mechanism before it again computes a coupled step.
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: Coupled trust-region SQP computes one step variable from one constrained quadratic model. The step must simultaneously satisfy all linearized constraints, reduce the quadratic objective model, and lie in a single trust-region ball. No separate feasibility and tangential steps are used. If the linearized feasible set does not intersect the ball, an additional relaxation or restoration mechanism is required.
knowledge_statements.conclusion_latex: \(s_k\in\mathcal L_k\cap\{s:\lVert s\rVert_k\le\Delta_k\}\) and \(s_k\) is selected by the quadratic model \(q_k\) in that same feasible region.
equivalent_formulations_latex: For equality constraints the coupled subproblem is the trust-region quadratic program with \(c_k+A_ks=0\) and \(\lVert s\rVert_k\le\Delta_k\).
special_cases_latex: When \(c(x_k)=0\), the equality restriction becomes \(A_ks=0\), so the step lies in the linearized tangent space.
When \(H_k\succeq0\) and the linearized feasible set is convex, the coupled subproblem is a convex trust-region quadratic program.
immediate_consequences_latex: A feasible coupled step is automatically a feasible point of the local linearized model.
The method may fail to produce a step when the trust-region ball and linearized constraints are incompatible.
boundary_notes: Composite-step methods are excluded because they allocate feasibility and optimality to separate component calculations.
This definition does not require exact global minimization of a nonconvex quadratic subproblem.

knowledge_statements.statement_title: Coupled trust-region SQP subproblem and compatibility failure
knowledge_statements.scope_note: Formulation and feasibility boundary for a single coupled trust-region restriction in SQP.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex:
At an SQP iterate \(x_k\), a coupled trust-region step may be defined by
\[
\min_p\ f_k+\nabla f_k^Tp+\tfrac12p^T\nabla_{xx}^2\mathcal L_kp
\]
subject to
\[
c_i(x_k)+\nabla c_i(x_k)^Tp=0\ (i\in\mathcal E),\qquad c_i(x_k)+\nabla c_i(x_k)^Tp\ge0\ (i\in\mathcal I),\qquad \|p\|\le\Delta_k.
\]
The Lagrangian Hessian need not be positive definite. Even when the linearized equality and inequality constraints are mutually consistent, their intersection with \(\{p:\|p\|\le\Delta_k\}\) can be empty. Enlarging \(\Delta_k\) merely to recover feasibility compromises the model-validity role of the trust region; trust-region SQP therefore permits controlled relaxation or improvement of linearized feasibility when exact satisfaction is excluded by the radius.
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: A coupled trust-region SQP step minimizes the quadratic Lagrangian model subject to all linearized constraints and one norm bound. The Hessian may be indefinite. Consistency of the linearized constraints alone does not guarantee feasibility after imposing the trust-region bound, so feasibility should be relaxed or improved rather than forcing the radius to expand until the constraints intersect the region.

f\text{ and each }c_i\text{ are differentiable at }x_k.
\nabla_{xx}^2\mathcal L_k\text{ is available or modeled; positive definiteness is not assumed.}
knowledge_statements.conclusion_latex: \operatorname{feas}\{\text{linearized constraints}\}\not\Rightarrow\operatorname{feas}\{\text{linearized constraints},\ \|p\|\le\Delta_k\};\text{ controlled feasibility relaxation may therefore be necessary.}

children.title: Composite-Step Trust-Region SQP
children.top_down_role: Trust-region SQP separating progress toward feasibility from progress along the local constraint manifold.

knowledge_statements.slot_contract: State the canonical mathematical definition of the source node, with its domain, quantifiers, notation, and a precise source locator.
knowledge_statements.ambient_context_latex: Consider \(\min f(x)\) subject to \(c(x)=0\), with \(A_k=\nabla c(x_k)\), \(g_k=\nabla f(x_k)\), symmetric \(H_k\), and radius \(\Delta_k>0\).
knowledge_statements.scope_note: Finite-dimensional smooth equality-constrained SQP; inequality extensions require an active-set or related local constraint representation.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex: A composite-step trust-region SQP method explicitly forms \[s_k=n_k+t_k.\] The normal component \(n_k\) is chosen inside a prescribed fraction of the trust region to reduce a linearized infeasibility model, such as \(\lVert c(x_k)+A_kn\rVert\). After \(n_k\) is fixed, the tangential component is chosen to reduce the quadratic model while preserving the achieved linearized residual, canonically by approximately solving \[\min_t\;\tfrac12t^TH_kt+(g_k+H_kn_k)^Tt\quad\text{subject to}\quad A_kt=0,\qquad \lVert n_k+t\rVert\le\Delta_k.\] The condition \(A_kt=0\) gives \(c(x_k)+A_k(n_k+t)=c(x_k)+A_kn_k\), so the tangential step does not undo the normal step's linearized feasibility gain. Centered component bounds may replace the off-centered final bound provided they guarantee \(\lVert n_k+t_k\rVert\le C\Delta_k\) for a fixed constant \(C\).
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: Composite-step trust-region SQP writes the trial displacement as a normal component plus a tangential component. The normal component reduces linearized constraint violation. The tangential component then reduces the quadratic objective model while remaining in the null space of the constraint Jacobian, so it preserves the normal component's linearized feasibility improvement. The combined step is controlled by a trust-region bound or by component bounds that uniformly control its size.
knowledge_statements.conclusion_latex: \(s_k=n_k+t_k\), with \(n_k\) assigned feasibility reduction and \(A_kt_k=0\) assigning model reduction without changing the attained linearized residual.
equivalent_formulations_latex: The tangential condition is equivalently \(A_ks_k=A_kn_k\).
For Euclidean norms, a centered tangential bound \(\lVert t_k\rVert_2\le\sqrt{\Delta_k^2-\lVert n_k\rVert_2^2}\) is a standard surrogate for the off-centered bound.
special_cases_latex: If \(c(x_k)=0\), one may take \(n_k=0\), leaving a tangential trust-region step.
If the minimum-norm normal step is used, it is orthogonal to every exact null-space tangential step.
immediate_consequences_latex: The linearized residual after the composite step equals that after the normal step.
The tangential subproblem is always feasible at \(t=0\) whenever the normal step obeys the overall radius.
boundary_notes: The words normal and tangential are descriptive; approximate components need not be exactly orthogonal.
A single coupled trust-region quadratic program is not a composite-step construction unless its step is explicitly formed through these two roles.

knowledge_statements.scope_note: Normal-step relaxation, relaxed SQP solve, and merit-based acceptance for equality-constrained optimization.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex:
For equality constraints \(c(x)=0\), compute
\[
v_k\in\arg\min_{\|v\|_2\le0.8\Delta_k}\|A_kv+c_k\|_2^2,
\qquad r_k=A_kv_k+c_k.
\]
Then compute an approximate solution of
\[
\min_{\|p\|_2\le\Delta_k} f_k+\nabla f_k^Tp+\tfrac12p^T\nabla_{xx}^2\mathcal L_kp
\quad\text{s.t.}\quad A_kp+c_k=r_k.
\]
This subproblem is consistent because \(p=v_k\) satisfies both the relaxed equality and the trust-region bound. The normal problem may be treated by a dogleg path; when \(A_kA_k^T\) is nonsingular, its minimum-norm unconstrained correction is \(-A_k^T(A_kA_k^T)^{-1}c_k\). The relaxed quadratic problem may be treated by projected conjugate gradients initialized at \(v_k\), with termination at the trust-region boundary or upon detection of negative curvature. Step acceptance can use
\[
\phi_2(x;\mu)=f(x)+\mu\|c(x)\|_2,
\quad q_\mu(p)=f_k+\nabla f_k^Tp+\tfrac12p^T\nabla_{xx}^2\mathcal L_kp+\mu\|c_k+A_kp\|_2,
\]
and \(\rho_k=[\phi_2(x_k;\mu)-\phi_2(x_k+p_k;\mu)]/[q_\mu(0)-q_\mu(p_k)]\).
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: For equality-constrained optimization, first minimize the norm of the linearized constraint residual inside a reduced trust region. Use the resulting residual as the relaxed right-hand side of the SQP constraint, then solve the relaxed trust-region quadratic model. The normal step is automatically a feasible starting point for the second subproblem. Dogleg and projected-CG procedures provide practical inexact solves, and actual versus predicted reduction in an l2 merit function can govern acceptance.
assumptions_latex: c:\mathbb R^n\to\mathbb R^m\text{ is differentiable at }x_k\text{ with }A_k=\nabla c(x_k)^T\text{ under the stated convention}.
\Delta_k>0.
A_kA_k^T\text{ is nonsingular only for the displayed minimum-norm correction formula; the relaxation construction itself does not require that formula.}
knowledge_statements.conclusion_latex: A_kv_k+c_k=r_k\ \land\ \|v_k\|_2\le0.8\Delta_k<\Delta_k\ \Longrightarrow\ v_k\text{ is feasible for the relaxed SQP subproblem.}

knowledge_statements.statement_title: Normal and tangential geometry of a composite SQP step
knowledge_statements.ambient_context_latex: Let \(c:\mathbb R^n\to\mathbb R^m\) be differentiable, let \(A=\nabla c(x)\), and assume \(A\) has full row rank when the explicit orthogonal projector formulas are used.
knowledge_statements.scope_note: Local Euclidean geometry for smooth equality constraints. Approximate decompositions may relax orthogonality while retaining the residual identities.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex: The canonical composite-step geometry at \(x\) is the decomposition of a displacement \(s\) into \(s=n+t\), where the normal space is \(\mathcal N_x=\operatorname{range}(A^T)\) and the linearized tangent space is \(\mathcal T_x=\ker A\). The minimum-norm correction of the full linearized equations is \[n^c=-A^T(AA^T)^{-1}c(x)\in\mathcal N_x,\qquad An^c+c(x)=0.\] Its trust-region truncation is \(n=\alpha n^c\), with \(0\le\alpha\le\min\{1,\Delta/\lVert n^c\rVert_2\}\). A tangential displacement satisfies \(t\in\mathcal T_x\), equivalently \(At=0\), and hence \[c(x)+A(n+t)=c(x)+An.\] Under full row rank, the orthogonal projectors are \(P_N=A^T(AA^T)^{-1}A\) and \(P_T=I-P_N\); consequently \(n^Tt=0\) whenever \(n\in\mathcal N_x\) and \(t\in\mathcal T_x\).
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: Composite-step geometry splits the ambient space into the range of the transposed constraint Jacobian and the null space of that Jacobian. A normal component lies in the former and corrects the linearized constraint residual. A tangential component lies in the latter and therefore leaves that residual unchanged. With a full-row-rank Jacobian, the two spaces are orthogonal, explicit projectors exist, and the minimum-norm full linearized correction is obtained with the Jacobian pseudoinverse.
knowledge_statements.conclusion_latex: \(\mathbb R^n=\operatorname{range}(A^T)\oplus\ker A\) and every exact normal-tangential pair satisfies \(At=0\) and \(c(x)+A(n+t)=c(x)+An\).
equivalent_formulations_latex: The minimum-norm correction is \(n^c=-A^{\dagger}c(x)\) when \(A\) has full row rank.
Tangential invariance is equivalently \(As=An\).
special_cases_latex: At a feasible point, \(c(x)=0\) and the minimum-norm normal correction is zero.
If \(m=n\) and \(A\) is nonsingular, then \(\ker A=\{0\}\), so there is no nonzero tangential component.
immediate_consequences_latex: For orthogonal components, \(\lVert n+t\rVert_2^2=\lVert n\rVert_2^2+\lVert t\rVert_2^2\).
Shortening the normal correction leaves trust-region capacity for tangential model reduction.
boundary_notes: When \(A\) is rank deficient, pseudoinverse projectors remain meaningful but the displayed inverse \((AA^T)^{-1}\) does not exist.
Practical composite-step methods may use quasi-normal components that are not exactly in \(\operatorname{range}(A^T)\).

notation.meaning: normal space, the range of the transposed Jacobian
linearized tangent space, the Jacobian null space

knowledge_statements.title: Normal-Step Geometry
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: The normal step lies in a prescribed ball and primarily reduces the residual of the linearized constraints, exactly solving them when attainable.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex: Given \(c_k\in\mathbb R^m\), \(A_k\in\mathbb R^{m\times n}\), and a normal radius \(\Delta_k^N>0\), a normal step is any approximate solution \(n_k\) of \[\min_n\;\tfrac12\|c_k+A_kn\|_2^2\quad\text{subject to}\quad\|n\|_2\leq\Delta_k^N.\] When the linearized equations are attainable inside the ball, one may require \(A_kn_k=-c_k\); otherwise the least-squares formulation produces a bounded step giving sufficient reduction of the linearized violation.

\(\Delta_k^N>0\).

knowledge_statements.title: Tangential-Step Geometry
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: The tangential step lies in the constraint Jacobian's null space, improves the quadratic objective, and preserves the normal step's linearized feasibility gain.

knowledge_statements.title: Composite-Step Coupling
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: Couple normal and tangential components so the normal step uses only part of the radius and their sum remains inside the full trust region.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex: Let \(d_k=n_k+t_k\), where \(n_k\) reduces linearized infeasibility and \(A_kt_k=0\). knowledge_statements.title: Vardi-Like SQP Methods
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: Scale the linearized feasibility correction, then add a null-space objective step and globalize the resulting composite step within a trust region.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex: At iteration \(k\), choose a relaxation scalar \(\alpha_k\in[0,1]\). Compute a normal component \(n_k\) satisfying, exactly or approximately, \(A_kn_k=-\alpha_kc_k\) under a norm bound. Then compute a tangential component \(t_k\) with \(A_kt_k=0\) to reduce the quadratic model \(g_k^\top d+\tfrac12d^\top B_kd\) for \(d=n_k+t_k\), subject to the trust-region coupling. Select \(\alpha_k\), the step, and the radius through a globalization test; \(\alpha_k=1\) recovers the full linearized-feasibility equation.
assumptions_latex: \(f\) and \(c\) are continuously differentiable near \(x_k\).
The normal and tangential subproblems admit the required approximate solutions.
knowledge_statements.conclusion_latex: \(A_k(n_k+t_k)=-\alpha_kc_k\), so the predicted residual is \((1-\alpha_k)c_k\).
knowledge_statements.scope_note: Composite equality-constrained SQP based on a relaxed linearized-feasibility equation.

enrichment_metadata.review_comment: The algorithm kind matches the Vardi-like methods container, but no citation is supplied for identifying this scaled feasibility equation as Vardi-like SQP. The selection of alpha_k and the globalization/coupling rules are variant-dependent, so the mathematical family cannot be reviewed reliably without an authoritative locator.

knowledge_statements.slot_contract: State the canonical mathematical definition of the source node, with its domain, quantifiers, notation, and a precise source locator.
knowledge_statements.ambient_context_latex: Consider smooth equality constraints \(c(x)=0\), Jacobian \(A=\nabla c(x)\), a norm trust region of radius \(\Delta>0\), and a local quadratic model \(q(s)=g^Ts+\tfrac12s^THs\).
knowledge_statements.scope_note: Finite-dimensional smooth equality-constrained SQP with relaxed linearized feasibility.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex: A Vardi-like trust-region SQP step replaces the full linearized equation \(As+c(x)=0\) by \[As+\alpha c(x)=0,\qquad \alpha\in(0,1],\qquad \lVert s\rVert\le\Delta,\] where \(\alpha\) is chosen so that the relaxed affine constraint intersects the trust-region ball. In the Euclidean norm, if \(A\) has full row rank and \[n^c=-A^T(AA^T)^{-1}c(x),\] then the largest feasible relaxation factor is \[\alpha_{\max}=\min\{1,\Delta/\lVert n^c\rVert_2\}.\] A value \(0<\alpha\le\alpha_{\max}\), often strictly below \(\alpha_{\max}\) when the latter is less than one, defines the normal component \(n=\alpha n^c\). The remaining freedom is used to reduce the quadratic model with a tangential component \(t\) satisfying \(At=0\) and the final trust-region restriction. The resulting residual is \(c(x)+A(n+t)=(1-\alpha)c(x)\).
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: A Vardi-like SQP method restores compatibility between a trust region and the linearized constraints by scaling the current constraint residual with a factor between zero and one. Under full row rank, the maximum admissible factor is determined by the norm of the minimum-norm linearized correction. The scaled correction supplies the normal step, and a null-space tangential step uses any remaining radius to reduce the quadratic model.
knowledge_statements.conclusion_latex: The step satisfies \(A(n+t)+\alpha c(x)=0\), so its linearized residual equals \((1-\alpha)c(x)\) while remaining trust-region feasible.
equivalent_formulations_latex: The relaxed equation is equivalently \(c(x)+As=(1-\alpha)c(x)\).
special_cases_latex: If \(\lVert n^c\rVert_2\le\Delta\), then \(\alpha=1\) is allowed and the complete linearized equations can be satisfied.
If \(\alpha<\alpha_{\max}\), the unused radius provides room for tangential model reduction.
immediate_consequences_latex: For every \(\Delta>0\), sufficiently small positive \(\alpha\) makes the relaxed equation compatible when \(A\) has full row rank.
The linearized infeasibility is reduced by the factor \(1-\alpha\).
boundary_notes: The value \(\alpha=0\) is a limiting compatibility case but supplies no feasibility improvement and is excluded from the canonical update.
This differs from Byrd-Omojokun methods, which compute the normal component from a constrained least-squares problem rather than a scalar relaxation of the full correction.

notation.meaning: relaxation factor for the current constraint residual
minimum-norm solution of the full linearized equations

knowledge_statements.statement_plain: A Byrd-Omojokun method computes two separately controlled components. First it minimizes linearized constraint violation inside a smaller normal trust region. knowledge_statements.ambient_context_latex: For a smooth equality-constrained problem, let \(c_k=c(x_k)\), \(A_k=\nabla c(x_k)\), \(H_k=H_k^T\), a Lagrangian-gradient estimate \(\nabla_x\ell(x_k,y_k)\), and radius \(\Delta_k>0\) be given.
knowledge_statements.scope_note: Finite-dimensional equality-constrained trust-region SQP using coupled feasibility and radius restrictions.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex:
A Celis-Dennis-Tapia SQP method first computes a feasibility-improving reference step \(n_k\) with \(\lVert n_k\rVert\le\Delta_k\) and defines \[\theta_k=\lVert A_kn_k+c_k\rVert\le\lVert c_k\rVert,\] with strict inequality unless \(c_k=0\). It then computes the whole step \(s_k\), rather than adding a separate tangential correction, as an approximate solution of \[\min_s\;\tfrac12s^TH_ks+\nabla_x\ell(x_k,y_k)^Ts\] \[\text{subject to}\quad\lVert A_ks+c_k\rVert\le\theta_k,
\qquad\lVert s\rVert\le\Delta_k.\] Thus one quadratic objective is restricted simultaneously by a feasibility-residual region and a trust-region ball. With Euclidean norms these are two quadratic constraints; with polyhedral norms the model can be represented as an inequality-constrained quadratic program.
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: A Celis-Dennis-Tapia method uses a preliminary feasibility step only to determine an allowable linearized residual. The actual SQP step is then selected from one quadratic model constrained both by that residual bound and by the trust-region radius. Unlike normal-plus-tangential methods, the preliminary step is not necessarily a component of the final step.
knowledge_statements.conclusion_latex: The final step satisfies both \(\lVert A_ks_k+c_k\rVert\le\theta_k\le\lVert c_k\rVert\) and \(\lVert s_k\rVert\le\Delta_k\).
equivalent_formulations_latex: With Euclidean norms the feasible set is described by the two quadratic inequalities \(\theta_k^2-\lVert A_ks+c_k\rVert_2^2\ge0\) and \(\Delta_k^2-\lVert s\rVert_2^2\ge0\).
special_cases_latex: If \(c_k=0\), then \(\theta_k=0\) and the final step satisfies \(A_ks_k=0\).
A Cauchy step for the feasibility residual is a standard choice of \(n_k\).
immediate_consequences_latex: The final step cannot have greater linearized infeasibility than the current point.
The preliminary feasibility step guarantees that the two-constraint feasible set contains at least one point.
boundary_notes: The reference step \(n_k\) determines \(\theta_k\) but need not appear additively in \(s_k\).
The Euclidean two-quadratic-constraint subproblem can be substantially harder than an ordinary trust-region subproblem.

notation.meaning: allowed norm of the linearized constraint residual
reference feasibility-reducing step used to set theta

knowledge_statements.title: Relaxation-Based Trust-Region SQP
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: Add a penalized residual variable to the trust-region SQP subproblem so a bounded trial step remains available even when exact linearized feasibility is unattainable.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex: For the equality-constrained problem, introduce a relaxation vector \(r\in\mathbb R^m\) and solve a local model of the form \[\min_{d,r}\;g_k^\top d+\tfrac12d^\top B_kd+\sigma_k\|r\|\quad\text{subject to}\quad c_k+A_kd=r,\qquad\|d\|\leq\Delta_k.\] Choose \(\sigma_k>0\) and update it when the relaxation is insufficiently discouraged. Accept or reject \(d_k\) using actual and predicted reduction in a compatible penalty or merit model, update \(\Delta_k\), and retain \(r_k\) as the modeled infeasibility.
assumptions_latex: \(f\) and \(c\) are continuously differentiable.
The norm penalty on \(r\) is finite and \(\sigma_k>0\).
knowledge_statements.conclusion_latex: The subproblem is feasible via \(d=0\), \(r=c_k\), and its solution satisfies \(c_k+A_kd_k=r_k\).
knowledge_statements.scope_note: Trust-region SQP with explicit relaxation preserving subproblem feasibility.

A precise authoritative source is required.

knowledge_statements.statement_title: Elastic relaxation of a trust-region SQP subproblem
knowledge_statements.ambient_context_latex: Consider smooth constraints \(c_E(x)=0\), \(c_I(x)\ge0\), a quadratic model \(q_k(s)=g_k^Ts+\tfrac12s^TH_ks\), and radius \(\Delta_k>0\).
knowledge_statements.scope_note: Finite-dimensional smooth SQP using explicit nonnegative relaxation variables to prevent failure from inconsistent linearizations.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex:
A relaxation-based trust-region SQP step is obtained from an elastic local model in which violations of the linearized constraints are represented by nonnegative variables and penalized. A canonical \(\ell_1\) realization solves \[\min_{s,u^+,u^-,v}\;q_k(s)+\sigma_k\bigl(\mathbf1^Tu^++\mathbf1^Tu^-+\mathbf1^Tv\bigr)\] subject to \[c_E(x_k)+A_{E,k}s=u^+-u^-,\qquad c_I(x_k)+A_{I,k}s+v\ge0,\] \[u^+,u^-,v\ge0,
\qquad\lVert s\rVert\le\Delta_k.\] Because \(s=0\), \(u^+=(c_E(x_k))_+\), \(u^-=(-c_E(x_k))_+\), and \(v=(-c_I(x_k))_+\) are feasible, the relaxed subproblem remains viable even when the unrelaxed linearized constraints do not intersect the trust-region ball. The parameter \(\sigma_k>0\) prices relaxation, so sufficiently expensive elastic variables favor the original linearized constraints whenever they are attainable.
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: Relaxation-based trust-region SQP adds nonnegative elastic variables to the local equality and inequality models and penalizes their sum in the quadratic objective. This makes the local subproblem feasible even when the original linearized constraints are incompatible with the trust-region ball. A positive penalty discourages elastic violation and favors the original local constraints when they can be satisfied.
knowledge_statements.conclusion_latex: The elastic subproblem has a feasible point for every \(x_k\) and \(\Delta_k>0\), and zero elastic variables recover the ordinary trust-region SQP model.
equivalent_formulations_latex: Eliminating the elastic variables gives the nonsmooth model \(q_k(s)+\sigma_k\lVert(c(x_k)+A_ks)^{I-}\rVert_1\) over \(\lVert s\rVert\le\Delta_k\).
special_cases_latex: For equality constraints only, the penalty term becomes \(\sigma_k\lVert c(x_k)+A_ks\rVert_1\).
If the unrelaxed linearized constraints are attainable and the selected solution has zero elastic variables, the step is an ordinary trust-region SQP step.
immediate_consequences_latex: Inconsistency of the linearized constraints does not by itself make the elastic subproblem infeasible.
Polyhedral norms yield a quadratic-programming representation.
boundary_notes: A relaxation parameter that is too small may favor constraint violation over feasibility.
This definition concerns elastic local constraints; feasibility restoration instead changes the iterate through a separate phase.

notation.meaning: nonnegative equality and inequality relaxation variables
positive price assigned to local constraint relaxation

knowledge_statements.title: Sequential L1 Quadratic Programming
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: Minimize a trust-region quadratic model plus the L1 norm of linearized constraint violation, then globalize using the corresponding exact-penalty merit function.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex: For equality constraints, choose \(\sigma_k>0\), \(\Delta_k>0\), and symmetric \(B_k\). Compute \(d_k\) from \[\min_{\|d\|\leq\Delta_k}\;g_k^\top d+\tfrac12d^\top B_kd+\sigma_k\|c_k+A_kd\|_1.\] Equivalently, introduce nonnegative slacks \(u,v\) with \(c_k+A_kd=u-v\) and penalize \(\mathbf1^\top(u+v)\). Accept the trial point using actual versus predicted reduction in \(f(x)+\sigma_k\|c(x)\|_1\), then update the radius and, when necessary, the penalty weight.
assumptions_latex: \(f\) and \(c\) are continuously differentiable.
\(B_k\) is symmetric, \(\sigma_k>0\), and \(\Delta_k>0\).
knowledge_statements.conclusion_latex: \(d_k\) minimizes the stated bounded L1-penalized quadratic model to the prescribed subproblem accuracy.
knowledge_statements.scope_note: Trust-region sequential quadratic modeling of an exact linearized L1 penalty.

notation.meaning: nonnegative positive and negative residual slacks

knowledge_statements.slot_contract: State the canonical mathematical definition of the source node, with its domain, quantifiers, notation, and a precise source locator.
knowledge_statements.ambient_context_latex: For a smooth nonlinear program, let \(q_k(s)=f(x_k)+g_k^Ts+\tfrac12s^TH_ks\), let \(c_k=c(x_k)\), and let \(A_k=\nabla c(x_k)\). For mixed constraints, \((c_k+A_ks)^{I-}\) collects absolute equality residuals and negative parts of inequality residuals.
knowledge_statements.scope_note: Finite-dimensional smooth nonlinear programming globalized by a nonsmooth exact \(\ell_1\)-penalty model and a trust region.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex: A sequential \(\ell_1\) quadratic programming method computes a trial step by approximately solving \[\min_{\lVert s\rVert\le\Delta_k}\;m_k(s),\qquad m_k(s)=q_k(s)+\sigma_k\bigl\lVert(c_k+A_ks)^{I-}\bigr\rVert_1,\] where \(\sigma_k>0\). For equality constraints this reduces to \[m_k(s)=f(x_k)+g_k^Ts+\tfrac12s^TH_ks+\sigma_k\lVert c_k+A_ks\rVert_1.\] The model is the second-order local model of the exact-penalty function \(f(x)+\sigma_k\lVert c(x)^{I-}\rVert_1\). With a polyhedral trust-region norm, conventionally \(\ell_\infty\), the absolute values and negative parts can be represented by linear auxiliary constraints, so the step subproblem is a quadratic program. Sequential repetition at updated iterates gives the \(S\ell_1QP\) method.
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: Sequential L1 quadratic programming minimizes, at each iterate, a quadratic objective model plus a positive weight times the L1 norm of the linearized constraint violation. A trust-region bound controls the step. Because both the violation norm and a conventional infinity-norm trust region are polyhedral, auxiliary variables turn the local nonsmooth model into a quadratic program. Rebuilding and solving this model sequentially defines the method.
knowledge_statements.conclusion_latex: Each trial step approximately minimizes the exact-penalty model \(q_k(s)+\sigma_k\lVert(c_k+A_ks)^{I-}\rVert_1\) within \(\lVert s\rVert\le\Delta_k\).
equivalent_formulations_latex: Introducing nonnegative positive and negative residual variables yields an elastic quadratic program with a linear \(\ell_1\) penalty.
For equality constraints, the violation term is simply \(\lVert c_k+A_ks\rVert_1\).
special_cases_latex: With \(H_k=0\), the model becomes a sequential \(\ell_1\) linear programming model.
If the selected step satisfies the linearized constraints, its penalty contribution is zero.
immediate_consequences_latex: The subproblem remains meaningful when the unrelaxed linearized constraints are inconsistent with the trust region.
For polyhedral norms the model admits a finite quadratic-programming formulation.
boundary_notes: The \(\ell_1\) term is nonsmooth at zero residual.
The penalty weight must be sufficiently large for the exact-penalty model's critical points to correspond reliably to constrained critical points.

notation.meaning: combined equality absolute residual and inequality negative-part mapping

knowledge_statements.slot_contract: State the canonical mathematical definition of the source node, with its domain, quantifiers, notation, and a precise source locator.
knowledge_statements.ambient_context_latex: Let \(f:\mathbb R^n\to\mathbb R\) be the objective and \(\vartheta:\mathbb R^n\to[0,\infty)\) a constraint-violation measure, such as the maximum equality and inequality violation. Associate each point \(x\) with \((\vartheta(x),f(x))\).
knowledge_statements.scope_note: Finite-dimensional constrained SQP using bicriteria acceptance rather than a fixed scalar penalty merit function.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex: A filter is a finite set \(\mathcal F\subset[0,\infty)\times\mathbb R\) of mutually nondominated pairs: for any distinct \((\vartheta_i,f_i),(\vartheta_j,f_j)\in\mathcal F\), \(\vartheta_i<\vartheta_j\) or \(f_i<f_j\). Given \(\gamma_\vartheta\in(0,1)\), a point \(x\) is acceptable for \(\mathcal F\) when, for every \((\vartheta_j,f_j)\in\mathcal F\), \[\vartheta(x)<(1-\gamma_\vartheta)\vartheta_j\quad\text{or}\quad f(x)<f_j-\gamma_\vartheta\vartheta(x).\] A filter-SQP method generates a local SQP step and accepts a trial point only when it is acceptable for both the stored filter and the current iterate, together with any model-decrease safeguard imposed for objective-dominated steps. When an accepted pair is inserted, pairs dominated by its margin are removed. Hence feasibility and objective progress are treated as separate acceptance dimensions rather than combined through a fixed penalty parameter.
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: A filter stores mutually nondominated pairs of constraint violation and objective value. A trial point is acceptable only if, relative to every stored pair, it sufficiently reduces violation or sufficiently improves the objective. A filter-SQP method applies this test to SQP trial points, inserts selected accepted pairs, and removes pairs they dominate. It therefore globalizes SQP without fixing a scalar tradeoff between feasibility and objective reduction.
knowledge_statements.conclusion_latex: Every filter-accepted trial point achieves a margin-qualified improvement in at least one of \(\vartheta\) or \(f\) relative to every relevant stored pair.
equivalent_formulations_latex: Without margins, filter acceptability is precisely nondominance in the bicriteria order minimizing \((\vartheta,f)\).
special_cases_latex: At a feasible point \(\vartheta=0\), further feasibility reduction is impossible, so objective safeguards govern acceptance.
An initially empty filter imposes no historical dominance restriction.
immediate_consequences_latex: A trial point may be accepted even when its objective increases, provided feasibility improves sufficiently.
No single penalty weight is needed to scalarize \(\vartheta\) and \(f\).
boundary_notes: Practical filter methods add safeguards against arbitrarily small improvements and may use a restoration phase.
The filter definition alone does not specify whether step control uses a trust region or a line search.

notation.meaning: set of mutually nondominated violation-objective pairs

knowledge_statements.title: Trust-Region Filter-SQP
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: Accept a trust-region SQP trial point when it sufficiently improves infeasibility or objective relative to every stored filter entry, subject to model safeguards.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex: Maintain a filter \(\mathcal F_k\) of pairs \((\theta_i,f_i)\), where \(\theta(x)\geq0\) measures infeasibility. Compute an SQP trial step \(d_k\) with \(\|d_k\|\leq\Delta_k\). For fixed \(\gamma_\theta,\gamma_f\in(0,1)\), declare \(x_k+d_k\) acceptable to the filter if, for every \((\theta_i,f_i)\in\mathcal F_k\), either \(\theta(x_k+d_k)\leq(1-\gamma_\theta)\theta_i\) or \(f(x_k+d_k)\leq f_i-\gamma_f\theta_i\). Apply the method's model-reduction safeguard, update the filter after acceptance, and shrink \(\Delta_k\) after rejection.
assumptions_latex: \(f\) and the constraints are continuously differentiable near the iterates.
\(\theta(x)=0\) exactly at feasible points and \(\theta(x)\geq0\).
knowledge_statements.conclusion_latex: Every filter-accepted pair is sufficiently nondominated relative to all entries in \(\mathcal F_k\), and every trial step satisfies \(\|d_k\|\leq\Delta_k\).
knowledge_statements.scope_note: Trust-region SQP globalized by nondominance in objective and constraint violation.

enrichment_metadata.review_comment: The algorithm kind and filter nondominance test match the trust-region Filter-SQP leaf. An authoritative Filter-SQP locator is required.

knowledge_statements.slot_contract: State the canonical mathematical definition of the source node, with its domain, quantifiers, notation, and a precise source locator.
knowledge_statements.ambient_context_latex: Let \(q_k\) be an SQP quadratic model, \(\Delta_k>0\) a trust-region radius, \(\vartheta\) a constraint-violation measure, and \(\mathcal F_k\) a filter of violation-objective pairs.
knowledge_statements.scope_note: Finite-dimensional smooth constrained optimization combining trust-region step control with filter globalization.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex: A trust-region filter-SQP method computes a trial step \(s_k\) from an SQP model subject to \(\lVert s_k\rVert\le\Delta_k\), possibly using normal and tangential components. The trial point \(x_k^+=x_k+s_k\) must satisfy the filter condition \[\vartheta(x_k^+)<(1-\gamma_\vartheta)\vartheta_j\quad\text{or}\quad f(x_k^+)<f_j-\gamma_\vartheta\vartheta(x_k^+)\] for every relevant \((\vartheta_j,f_j)\in\mathcal F_k\), including the current pair when required. For steps classified as objective-improving, the method additionally compares actual objective decrease with predicted quadratic-model decrease. An unacceptable or poorly predicted trial is rejected and the radius is reduced; an acceptable, sufficiently reliable trial is accepted, and the radius may be retained or enlarged. Selected accepted iterates are inserted into the filter, with dominated entries removed.
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: Trust-region filter-SQP computes an SQP step inside a radius and judges the resulting point using separate feasibility and objective criteria stored in a filter. Objective-type steps also satisfy a model-agreement safeguard. Rejected or unreliable trials cause radius contraction; accepted reliable trials may preserve or enlarge the radius. Filter entries are updated only according to the specified acceptance logic.
knowledge_statements.conclusion_latex: Every accepted trial is trust-region feasible and filter acceptable, while rejection preserves \(x_{k+1}=x_k\) and leads to a nonincreased radius.
equivalent_formulations_latex: The method is the intersection of trust-region step generation and bicriteria filter acceptance, supplemented by model agreement where required.
special_cases_latex: If the filter is empty, initial acceptance is governed by the current-pair and model safeguards.
If \(\vartheta(x_k)=0\), the step behaves locally like an objective trust-region step restricted by the linearized constraints.
immediate_consequences_latex: Penalty-parameter selection is not required for ordinary filter acceptance.
Trust-region contraction supplies a mechanism for recovering from an unacceptable full trial step.
boundary_notes: A restoration procedure is still required if the local trust-region quadratic program is incompatible.
This differs from line-search filter-SQP, where a fixed direction is shortened by a scalar step length.

knowledge_statements.title: Line-Search Filter-SQP
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: Backtrack along an SQP direction until the trial point sufficiently improves either infeasibility or objective relative to every filter entry, then update the filter.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex:
For the problem \(\min f(x)\) subject to \(c(x)=0\), set \(\theta(x)=\lVert c(x)\rVert\) and maintain a filter \(\mathcal F_k\subset\mathbb R_+\times\mathbb R\). Compute an SQP direction \(d_k\) from a quadratic model with linearized constraints. Starting with \(\alpha=1\), reduce \(\alpha\leftarrow\tau\alpha\), where \(0<\tau<1\), until for every \((\theta_i,f_i)\in\mathcal F_k\),
\[
\theta(x_k+\alpha d_k)\le \beta\theta_i
\quad\text{or}\quad
f(x_k+\alpha d_k)\le f_i-\gamma\theta(x_k+\alpha d_k),
\]
with \(0<\beta<1\) and \(\gamma>0\). Accept \(x_{k+1}=x_k+\alpha d_k\), delete filter entries dominated by the accepted pair, insert that pair, and stop when prescribed feasibility and stationarity tolerances hold.
assumptions_latex: \(f:\mathbb R^n\to\mathbb R\) and \(c:\mathbb R^n\to\mathbb R^m\) are continuously differentiable.
The SQP subproblem supplies a direction \(d_k\).
knowledge_statements.conclusion_latex: The accepted pair \((\theta(x_{k+1}),f(x_{k+1}))\) is not dominated under the stated filter margins.
knowledge_statements.scope_note: Equality-constrained filter-SQP with backtracking along an SQP direction.

knowledge_statements.slot_contract: State the canonical mathematical definition of the source node, with its domain, quantifiers, notation, and a precise source locator.
knowledge_statements.ambient_context_latex: Let \(d_k\) be an SQP search direction, \(\alpha\in(0,1]\) a step length, \(\vartheta\) a constraint-violation measure, and \(\mathcal F_k\) a filter of violation-objective pairs.
knowledge_statements.scope_note: Finite-dimensional smooth constrained optimization using filter acceptance and backtracking step-length control.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex: A line-search filter-SQP method first computes an SQP direction \(d_k\) independently of the final step length. From a sequence \(\alpha_{k,j}=\beta^j\alpha_{k,0}\), where \(\beta\in(0,1)\), it selects the first trial point \(x_k+\alpha_{k,j}d_k\) satisfying, for every \((\vartheta_i,f_i)\in\mathcal F_k\), \[\vartheta(x_k+\alpha_{k,j}d_k)<(1-\gamma_\vartheta)\vartheta_i\quad\text{or}\quad f(x_k+\alpha_{k,j}d_k)<f_i-\gamma_\vartheta\vartheta(x_k+\alpha_{k,j}d_k),\] together with a current-iterate margin and any switching sufficient-decrease condition imposed when the trial is primarily an objective step. It then sets \(x_{k+1}=x_k+\alpha_kd_k\). If no tested step length is acceptable, the method invokes its declared fallback or restoration mechanism rather than accepting a dominated trial.
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: Line-search filter-SQP computes an SQP direction and then backtracks along that direction. It accepts the first step length whose trial point sufficiently improves either constraint violation or objective value relative to every filter entry, while also satisfying current-iterate and objective-decrease safeguards when applicable. If backtracking finds no acceptable point, a fallback or restoration phase is required.
knowledge_statements.conclusion_latex: The accepted displacement has the form \(s_k=\alpha_kd_k\) with \(\alpha_k\in(0,1]\), and its trial point satisfies the filter and switching acceptance tests.
equivalent_formulations_latex: The defining step-control operation is scalar contraction along a fixed SQP direction rather than contraction of a trust-region radius followed by recomputation.
special_cases_latex: If the full step \(\alpha=1\) is acceptable, no backtracking is performed.
At a feasible iterate, objective sufficient-decrease conditions normally govern the line search.
immediate_consequences_latex: A filter-acceptable shorter step may be selected even when the full SQP step is rejected.
The direction and step-length calculations are logically distinct.

children.title: Filter-Restoration Architecture
children.top_down_role: The interaction between filter acceptance and dedicated feasibility recovery.

knowledge_statements.slot_contract: State the canonical mathematical definition of the source node, with its domain, quantifiers, notation, and a precise source locator.
knowledge_statements.ambient_context_latex: Let \(\vartheta(x)\ge0\) measure constraint violation, let \(\mathcal F_k\) be a filter, and let \(\operatorname{TRQP}(x,\Delta)\) denote the local trust-region SQP model at \(x\).
knowledge_statements.scope_note: Trust-region filter-SQP with an explicit mode switch between optimization and feasibility recovery.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex: A filter-restoration architecture has two modes. In normal mode it attempts to compute a compatible SQP model step and tests the resulting point by the filter and model-adequacy rules. The local model is called compatible when its linearized feasible set is nonempty and leaves prescribed trust-region freedom for objective reduction. If compatibility fails, the current pair is inserted into the filter and the method enters restoration mode. Restoration approximately minimizes \[\min_{x\in\mathbb R^n}\vartheta(x)\] from the current iterate until it finds \(x_k^R=x_k+r_k\) such that: (i) \(x_k^R\) is acceptable for the updated filter, and (ii) \(\operatorname{TRQP}(x_k^R,\Delta_{k+1})\) is compatible for some \(\Delta_{k+1}>0\). The method then returns to normal SQP mode. If restoration converges to an infeasible stationary point of \(\vartheta\) or cannot produce an acceptable compatible point, it reports restoration failure.
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: A filter-restoration architecture alternates between ordinary SQP optimization and a dedicated feasibility-recovery mode. It enters restoration when the local SQP model is incompatible or leaves too little room for objective progress. Restoration reduces a constraint-violation measure until it finds a point that is both acceptable to the filter and suitable for restarting the SQP model. Failure may occur at an infeasible stationary point of the violation measure.
knowledge_statements.conclusion_latex: A successful restoration step returns a point \(x_k^R\) that is simultaneously filter acceptable and compatible with a subsequent SQP trust-region subproblem.
equivalent_formulations_latex: The architecture is a two-state mechanism with transitions normal-to-restoration on incompatibility and restoration-to-normal on acceptable compatibility.
special_cases_latex: If every local SQP model remains compatible, restoration mode is never entered.
The violation measure may use \(\ell_1\), \(\ell_2\), or \(\ell_\infty\) residual norms, provided the acceptance and compatibility tests are defined consistently.
immediate_consequences_latex: Restoration is not merely enlargement of the radius: the restored point must differ sufficiently to pass the updated filter.
A successful restored point provides a valid starting point for the next normal SQP iteration.
boundary_notes: Restoration can terminate unsuccessfully at a locally least-infeasible point.
The restoration objective is feasibility, not decrease of the original objective function.

children.title: Restoration-Phase SQP
children.top_down_role: SQP architectures invoking a distinct feasibility-restoration phase.

knowledge_statements.title: Restoration-Phase SQP
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: When the SQP model or acceptance test fails, approximately minimize constraint violation, accept a sufficiently more feasible point, and restart the SQP model.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex:
For \(\min f(x)\) subject to \(c(x)=0\), let \(\theta(x)=\lVert c(x)\rVert\). At \(x_k\), attempt to compute and globally accept an SQP trial step. If the quadratic subproblem is infeasible, no acceptable step length is found, or the trial does not provide the required feasibility progress, enter restoration. The restoration phase approximately solves
\[
\min_x\ \tfrac12\lVert c(x)\rVert^2
\]
from \(x_k\) until it produces \(x_k^R\) satisfying \(\theta(x_k^R)\le\kappa_R\theta(x_k)\) for a fixed \(0<\kappa_R<1\) and acceptable to the filter. Set \(x_{k+1}=x_k^R\), rebuild the SQP model there, and terminate only at the prescribed feasibility and stationarity tolerances.
assumptions_latex: \(c:\mathbb R^n\to\mathbb R^m\) is continuously differentiable.
The restoration solver either returns the stated reduction or reports failure.
knowledge_statements.conclusion_latex: A successful restoration replaces the failed SQP trial by an accepted iterate with \(\theta(x_{k+1})\le\kappa_R\theta(x_k)\).
knowledge_statements.scope_note: Filter-SQP architecture with a separately invoked feasibility-restoration phase.

knowledge_statements.slot_contract: State the canonical mathematical definition of the source node, with its domain, quantifiers, notation, and a precise source locator.
knowledge_statements.ambient_context_latex: For constraints \(c_E(x)=0\), \(c_I(x)\ge0\), define \[\vartheta(x)=\max\{0,\max_{i\in E}|c_i(x)|,\max_{i\in I}(-c_i(x))\}.\] Let \(x_k\) be an SQP iterate at which the ordinary local subproblem is unsuitable.
knowledge_statements.scope_note: Finite-dimensional smooth constrained optimization. The restoration subproblem is generally nonsmooth because the displayed violation measure is a maximum.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex: A restoration-phase SQP method is an SQP architecture that, upon a declared trigger such as an inconsistent linearized subproblem or insufficient trust-region freedom, suspends objective-model optimization and generates restoration iterates \(z_j\) aimed at approximately solving \[\min_{z\in\mathbb R^n}\vartheta(z),\qquad z_0=x_k.\] A successful restoration phase terminates at \(z_J=x_k+r_k\) only when \(\vartheta(z_J)\) is sufficiently reduced and the ordinary SQP model at \(z_J\) is again admissible or compatible; in a filter method, \(z_J\) must additionally be acceptable for the current filter. The next SQP iteration starts from \(x_{k+1}=z_J\). An unsuccessful phase may terminate at an infeasible first-order stationary point or local minimizer of \(\vartheta\), which is interpreted as a locally least-infeasible point rather than as a solution of the original constrained problem.
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: Restoration-phase SQP invokes a separate feasibility procedure when the normal SQP subproblem cannot be used reliably. During restoration, the original objective is suspended and a nonnegative constraint-violation measure is reduced. Restoration succeeds only when it returns a sufficiently less-infeasible point from which the ordinary SQP model can restart, and, in filter methods, when that point also passes the filter. It may fail at a locally least-infeasible point.
knowledge_statements.conclusion_latex: A successful phase returns \(x_k+r_k\) with reduced \(\vartheta\) and a valid subsequent SQP subproblem; otherwise it reports an infeasible stationary restoration outcome.
equivalent_formulations_latex: Other norms of the equality residuals and inequality negative parts may replace the maximum norm in \(\vartheta\).
special_cases_latex: If a feasible point is reached, then \(\vartheta=0\) and feasibility restoration has achieved its minimum possible value.
When the original constraints are infeasible, a restoration phase can at best return a locally least-infeasible point.
immediate_consequences_latex: The original objective need not decrease during restoration.
A successful restoration supplies a new base point rather than merely a trial step for the failed local model.
boundary_notes: First-order stationarity for \(\vartheta\) does not imply feasibility.
Restoration is a distinct algorithmic phase, not an elastic relaxation solved inside every SQP subproblem.

children.top_down_role: Filter-SQP variants changing the balance among composite and restoration steps.

knowledge_statements.title: Alternative Filter Step Strategies
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: Construct normal and tangential components, test composite or feasibility-oriented alternatives against one filter, and invoke restoration only if all permitted candidates fail.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex: For \(\min f(x)\) subject to \(c(x)=0\), first compute a normal step \(n_k\) satisfying \(\lVert c(x_k)+J_k n_k\rVert\le\kappa_n\lVert c(x_k)\rVert\). When the remaining radius permits, compute a tangential step \(t_k\) with \(J_k t_k=0\) that decreases the quadratic objective model, and test the composite step \(d_k=n_k+t_k\) against the filter. If that step is rejected, the strategy may test a shortened normal step before invoking restoration. Accept the first candidate satisfying the fixed filter margins; otherwise call restoration. Output the accepted iterate, or report restoration failure, and stop when feasibility and stationarity tolerances are met.
assumptions_latex: \(f\) and \(c\) are continuously differentiable.
A normal step satisfying the stated contraction is available unless restoration is invoked.
knowledge_statements.conclusion_latex: Every ordinary accepted step is one of the prescribed candidates and satisfies the same filter acceptance predicate.
knowledge_statements.scope_note: Composite filter-SQP using selectable normal, tangential, and restoration steps.

knowledge_statements.slot_contract: State the canonical mathematical definition of the source node, with its domain, quantifiers, notation, and a precise source locator.
knowledge_statements.ambient_context_latex: Consider minimizing \(f:\mathbb R^n\to\mathbb R\) subject to \(c(x)=0\), with constraint violation \(\vartheta(x)=\|c(x)\|\), quadratic model \(m_k\), trust-region radius \(\Delta_k>0\), and a filter containing nondominated pairs \((\vartheta,f)\).
knowledge_statements.scope_note: Finite-dimensional smooth equality-constrained filter-SQP; this slot defines the single-step alternative to the normal-plus-tangential composite strategy.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex: \[\text{Choose }s_k'\text{ feasible for }\operatorname{TRQP}(x_k,\Delta_k)\text{ such that }m_k(x_k)-m_k(x_k+s_k')\ge \epsilon_1\min\{\pi(x_k),\Delta_k\},\quad \epsilon_1>0.\] If the trust-region QP has an empty feasible set, a restoration step \(r_k\) is instead required to produce a filter-acceptable point \(x_k+r_k\) at which a compatible trust-region QP exists. This rule defines an alternative filter step strategy because one directly computed step replaces the separate normal step, generalized Cauchy point, and tangential step of composite filter-SQP.
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: An alternative single-step filter-SQP strategy directly computes a trust-region QP-feasible step whose quadratic-model decrease is at least a fixed positive multiple of the smaller of a continuous criticality measure and the trust-region radius. If the local QP is infeasible, the method invokes restoration to reach a filter-acceptable point with a compatible subsequent QP.
assumptions_latex: \(f\) and \(c\) are continuously differentiable on a neighborhood of the iterates.
\(\pi:\mathbb R^n\to[0,\infty)\) is continuous and vanishes at the relevant first-order critical points.
The trial point must satisfy the current filter acceptability test.
knowledge_statements.conclusion_latex: \(s_k'\in\operatorname{feas}(\operatorname{TRQP}(x_k,\Delta_k))\) and \(m_k(x_k)-m_k(x_k+s_k')\ge\epsilon_1\min\{\pi_k,\Delta_k\}\), or restoration is invoked when this feasible set is empty.
equivalent_formulations_latex: The strategy is the single-step specialization of filter-SQP in which the composite decomposition \(s_k=n_k+t_k\) is not explicitly required.
special_cases_latex: When \(\operatorname{TRQP}(x_k,\Delta_k)\) is compatible, no restoration step is needed.
When \(x_k\) is feasible, filter acceptance reduces locally to objective improvement without adding a feasible point to the filter.
immediate_consequences_latex: A valid \(s_k'\) supplies both linearized feasibility and quantified model progress.
Failure of the QP feasibility test is handled by restoration rather than by solving an empty subproblem.
boundary_notes: The definition does not assert that the required single step exists for every model and radius.
The filter acceptance rule and restoration stopping test remain separate parts of the globalization architecture.

notation.meaning: The quadratic SQP model with linearized constraints and trust-region bound at iteration k.
A continuous first-order criticality measure evaluated at the current iterate.

knowledge_statements.slot_contract: State the canonical mathematical definition of the source node, with its domain, quantifiers, notation, and a precise source locator.
knowledge_statements.ambient_context_latex: Let \(f:\mathbb R^n\to\mathbb R\), \(c_E:\mathbb R^n\to\mathbb R^{m_E}\), and \(c_I:\mathbb R^n\to\mathbb R^{m_I}\) define \(\min f(x)\) subject to \(c_E(x)=0\) and \(c_I(x)\ge0\). Write \(\mathcal F=\{x:c_E(x)=0,\ c_I(x)\ge0\}\).
knowledge_statements.scope_note: Finite-dimensional smooth nonlinear programming; feasibility may be maintained exactly by projection or nonlinear correction, rather than merely for the linearized constraints.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex: \[x_0\in\mathcal F,\qquad d_k\text{ solves an SQP or reduced-SQP model},\qquad x_{k+1}=P_k(x_k+\alpha_k d_k)\in\mathcal F\quad(k\ge0),\] where \(P_k\) is a locally defined nonlinear correction or feasible-arc map satisfying \(P_k(x_k)=x_k\). An SQP method is feasible when every accepted iterate satisfies the original nonlinear constraints, not only their first-order linearizations.
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: A feasible SQP method starts from a feasible point, computes an SQP or reduced-SQP trial direction, and applies a feasible-arc or nonlinear correction map so that every accepted iterate remains feasible for the original nonlinear equalities and inequalities.
assumptions_latex: \(x_0\in\mathcal F\).
The active constraint Jacobian has sufficient local rank for the feasible correction or elimination map to be defined.
Each accepted step length \(\alpha_k\) lies in the domain on which the corrected arc remains feasible.
knowledge_statements.conclusion_latex: \(x_k\in\mathcal F\) for every accepted iterate \(k\), with SQP curvature information used to select the tangent or reduced-space motion.
equivalent_formulations_latex: For equality constraints, feasibility preservation is \(c_E(x_k)=0\) for all \(k\).
A feasible-arc representation is \(x_{k+1}=x_k+\delta_k(\alpha_k)\) with \(c_E(x_k+\delta_k(\alpha))=0\) throughout the accepted arc.
special_cases_latex: Reduced-gradient and nonlinear-elimination methods are equality-feasible instances.
An active-set feasible method additionally maintains inactive inequalities on their feasible side.
immediate_consequences_latex: No feasibility merit term is needed merely to repair accepted iterates, although globalization is still required for objective progress.
The inner nonlinear correction may restrict the admissible step length.
boundary_notes: Linearized feasibility alone does not make an SQP method feasible in this sense.
The definition excludes infeasible-start SQP until an exactly feasible iterate has been obtained.

notation.meaning: The feasible set of the original nonlinear program.
A nonlinear projection, elimination, or feasible-arc correction map.

source_refs.locator: Section 12.5, nonlinear elimination and feasible-direction methods, especially equations (12.5.1)–(12.5.11), pp. 317–323

children.title: Equality-Feasible SQP
children.top_down_role: SQP preserving nonlinear equality feasibility.

knowledge_statements.title: Equality-Feasible SQP
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: Move in a tangent SQP direction and retract or correct the trial point back onto the equality manifold before accepting it.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex:
For \(\min f(x)\) subject to \(c(x)=0\), initialize with \(c(x_0)=0\). At \(x_k\), compute a tangential SQP direction \(d_k\) satisfying \(J_kd_k=0\) and decreasing the quadratic Lagrangian model on \(\ker J_k\). Choose a step length \(\alpha_k>0\), then compute a correction \(r_k\) such that
\[
c(x_k+\alpha_kd_k+r_k)=0,
\qquad
\lVert r_k\rVert=O(\alpha_k^2\lVert d_k\rVert^2).
\]
Accept \(x_{k+1}=x_k+\alpha_kd_k+r_k\) when the chosen objective globalization test holds. If no correction or acceptable step is obtained, report failure; stop at the prescribed tangential-stationarity tolerance.
assumptions_latex: \(f\) and \(c\) are twice continuously differentiable near the iterates.
\(J_k\) has full row rank.
The initial point satisfies \(c(x_0)=0\).
knowledge_statements.conclusion_latex: Every successfully accepted iterate satisfies \(c(x_k)=0\).
knowledge_statements.scope_note: SQP whose accepted iterates remain feasible for nonlinear equalities.

knowledge_statements.slot_contract: State the canonical mathematical definition of the source node, with its domain, quantifiers, notation, and a precise source locator.
knowledge_statements.ambient_context_latex: Consider \(\min_{x\in\mathbb R^n} f(x)\) subject to \(c(x)=0\), where \(c:\mathbb R^n\to\mathbb R^m\) is smooth, \(m<n\), and \(A(x)=\nabla c(x)^T\) has full row rank near the iterates.
knowledge_statements.scope_note: Smooth equality-constrained nonlinear programming with feasible initialization and exact nonlinear feasibility restoration after each tangent SQP motion.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex: Choose \(x_0\) with \(c(x_0)=0\). At iteration \(k\), let \(Z_k\) span \(\ker A(x_k)\), compute a reduced SQP displacement \(Z_kp_k\), and define \(\delta_k(\alpha)\) by \[c(x_k+\delta_k(\alpha))=0,\qquad \delta_k(\alpha)=\alpha Z_kp_k+O(\alpha^2).\] An equality-feasible SQP iteration is \(x_{k+1}=x_k+\delta_k(\alpha_k)\), so that \(c(x_{k+1})=0\) for every accepted \(k\).
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: Equality-feasible SQP starts from a point satisfying all nonlinear equalities, computes an SQP direction tangent to the equality manifold, and corrects that tangent displacement along a locally defined feasible arc. Consequently every accepted iterate satisfies the original nonlinear equalities exactly.
assumptions_latex: \(A(x_k)\) has full row rank, so a null-space basis \(Z_k\) and local feasible correction exist.
The selected \(\alpha_k\) is small enough that the nonlinear correction iteration is defined and converges.
knowledge_statements.conclusion_latex: \(c(x_k)=0\) for all accepted \(k\), while \(\delta_k'(0)=Z_kp_k\) is the SQP tangent direction.
equivalent_formulations_latex: Using local coordinates \((y_1,y_2)\), the equality manifold is represented by \(y_1=0\), and the SQP step changes only the free coordinates \(y_2\) before nonlinear elimination.
A projection iteration may correct \(x_k+\alpha Z_kp_k\) in a complementary range-space direction until \(c=0\).
special_cases_latex: Choosing \(p_k=-Z_k^T\nabla f(x_k)\) gives a feasible reduced-gradient method.
Choosing \(p_k\) from a reduced Lagrangian-Hessian system gives a second-order feasible SQP method.
immediate_consequences_latex: The accepted sequence lies on the nonlinear equality manifold.
The first-order tangent displacement is unchanged by an \(O(\alpha_k^2)\) correction.
boundary_notes: A merely linearized equality \(c(x_k)+A(x_k)d_k=0\) does not guarantee equality feasibility at \(x_k+d_k\).
Rank loss can destroy the local feasible-coordinate construction.

notation.meaning: A matrix whose columns span the null space of the equality Jacobian.
The nonlinear feasible-arc displacement generated from the tangent SQP motion.

source_refs.locator: Section 12.5, equations (12.5.1)–(12.5.9) and the feasible-arc construction, pp. 317–321

children.title: Strictly Feasible Inequality SQP
children.top_down_role: SQP retaining iterates in the strict interior of inequality constraints.

knowledge_statements.title: Strictly Feasible Inequality SQP
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: Start strictly inside all inequalities and backtrack each SQP trial until it satisfies both the globalization test and every strict nonlinear inequality.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex:
For \(\min f(x)\) subject to \(g_i(x)\le0\), initialize with \(g_i(x_0)<0\) for every \(i\). At \(x_k\), compute an SQP direction \(d_k\) from a quadratic model whose linearized inequalities satisfy \(g_i(x_k)+\nabla g_i(x_k)^\top d_k\le0\). Starting from a prescribed trial length, backtrack \(\alpha\leftarrow\tau\alpha\), where \(0<\tau<1\), until both the globalization test and
\[
g_i(x_k+\alpha d_k)<0\quad\text{for every }i
\]
hold. Set \(x_{k+1}=x_k+\alpha d_k\). Terminate at the prescribed KKT tolerance, or report failure if the direction or step length cannot be obtained.
assumptions_latex: Each \(g_i:\mathbb R^n\to\mathbb R\) is continuously differentiable.
The initial iterate is strictly feasible.
The accepted step length is required to be positive.
knowledge_statements.conclusion_latex: All successfully generated iterates obey \(g_i(x_k)<0\) for every \(i\).
knowledge_statements.scope_note: Feasible SQP maintaining strict interiority for smooth inequalities.

knowledge_statements.slot_contract: State the canonical mathematical definition of the source node, with its domain, quantifiers, notation, and a precise source locator.
knowledge_statements.ambient_context_latex: Consider \(\min f(x)\) subject to \(c_i(x)\ge0\) for \(i\in\mathcal I\), with strict interior \(\mathcal F^\circ=\{x:c_i(x)>0\ \forall i\}\). Slack variables satisfy \(c_i(x)-z_i=0\), \(z_i>0\).
knowledge_statements.scope_note: Smooth finite-dimensional inequality-constrained SQP or barrier-SQP; equality constraints, if present, require a separate feasibility mechanism.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex: A strictly feasible inequality SQP method chooses \(x_0\in\mathcal F^\circ\) and accepts \(x_{k+1}=x_k+\alpha_kd_k\) only when \[c_i(x_k+\alpha_kd_k)>0\quad\text{for every }i\in\mathcal I.\] Equivalently, in slack form it maintains \(z_{k,i}=c_i(x_k)>0\) and selects \(\alpha_k\) so that \(z_k+\alpha_kd_k^z>0\), commonly with the fraction-to-the-boundary safeguard \(z_k+\alpha_kd_k^z\ge(1-\tau)z_k\) for some \(\tau\in(0,1)\).
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: A strictly feasible inequality SQP method begins in the strict interior and restricts every accepted step so that each nonlinear inequality remains strict. In slack-variable form, all slacks stay positive, usually by a fraction-to-the-boundary condition.
assumptions_latex: \(c_i(x_0)>0\) for every inequality index \(i\).
The step length is chosen within an interval on which the original nonlinear inequalities remain strict.
For the slack formulation, \(z_{k,i}=c_i(x_k)>0\).
knowledge_statements.conclusion_latex: \(x_k\in\mathcal F^\circ\) and \(z_k>0\) componentwise for every accepted iteration.
equivalent_formulations_latex: Strict primal feasibility is equivalent to positive nonlinear slacks \(z_i=c_i(x)>0\).
A fraction-to-the-boundary condition provides a quantitative interiority margin rather than positivity alone.
special_cases_latex: For affine inequalities, the maximum admissible step can be computed directly from the linear slack change.
Barrier-SQP methods preserve positive slacks while solving perturbed primal-dual SQP systems.
immediate_consequences_latex: No accepted iterate lies on or outside an inequality boundary.
Logarithmic barrier terms remain finite at every accepted iterate.
boundary_notes: The definition requires an interior starting point and therefore does not cover general infeasible starts.
Linearized slack positivity is insufficient unless it also guarantees positivity of the nonlinear constraints at the accepted point.

notation.meaning: The strict interior of the nonlinear inequality-feasible set.
A fraction-to-the-boundary parameter in the open interval from zero to one.

source_refs.locator: Section 15.4.4, inequality constraints and slack variables explicitly bounded away from zero, pp. 717–720

children.title: Feasibility-Preserving Correction SQP
children.top_down_role: Feasible SQP combining primary and corrective directions.

knowledge_statements.title: Feasibility-Preserving Correction SQP
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: Add a corrective direction to each primary tangent SQP step, then accept only a corrected trial that preserves feasibility and passes globalization.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex:
For \(\min f(x)\) subject to \(c(x)=0\), assume \(c(x_k)=0\). Compute a primary SQP direction \(d_k\) satisfying \(J_kd_k=0\). For a trial length \(\alpha\), compute a correction \(r_k(\alpha)\) from
\[
J_k r_k(\alpha)=-c(x_k+\alpha d_k),
\]
or solve the corresponding nonlinear correction equation to the prescribed feasibility tolerance. Backtrack \(\alpha\) until the corrected point \(x_k+\alpha d_k+r_k(\alpha)\) is feasible and satisfies the objective globalization test. Accept it as \(x_{k+1}\); otherwise report correction failure. Stop when the tangent-model stationarity residual is below tolerance.
assumptions_latex: \(f\) and \(c\) are twice continuously differentiable.
\(J_k\) has full row rank near the iterates.
The current iterate satisfies \(c(x_k)=0\).
knowledge_statements.conclusion_latex: Each successfully corrected and accepted point satisfies the prescribed equality-feasibility tolerance.
knowledge_statements.scope_note: Feasible SQP combining a primary direction with a nonlinear corrective direction.

knowledge_statements.slot_contract: State the canonical mathematical definition of the source node, with its domain, quantifiers, notation, and a precise source locator.
knowledge_statements.ambient_context_latex: Let \(c:\mathbb R^n\to\mathbb R^m\) define smooth equality constraints, let \(x_k\) satisfy \(c(x_k)=0\), and let \(d_k\) be a primary SQP step satisfying \(A_kd_k=0\), where \(A_k=\nabla c(x_k)^T\).
knowledge_statements.scope_note: Equality-feasible SQP with an explicit nonlinear corrective displacement; analogous inequality corrections require active-set and interiority safeguards.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex: A feasibility-preserving correction SQP step has the decomposition \[s_k=d_k+q_k,\qquad c(x_k+s_k)=0,\qquad q_k=O(\|d_k\|^2),\] where \(d_k\) is the primary tangent or reduced-SQP direction and \(q_k\) is computed by a nonlinear projection or Newton correction, for example from successive systems \(A(x_k+d_k+q_k^{(r)})\Delta q_k^{(r)}=-c(x_k+d_k+q_k^{(r)})\). The accepted iterate is \(x_{k+1}=x_k+s_k\).
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: This SQP variant combines a primary tangent SQP direction with a smaller nonlinear correction. The correction removes the constraint residual created by curvature, so the accepted point is feasible for the original equality constraints while retaining the primary direction to first order.
assumptions_latex: The constraint Jacobian has full row rank near the correction path.
The nonlinear correction is solved to the feasibility tolerance defining acceptance.
equivalent_formulations_latex: The correction may be viewed as projection of the tangent trial point back onto the nonlinear constraint manifold.
In local free coordinates, the same construction eliminates the dependent variables after the primary reduced-space move.
special_cases_latex: A single Newton correction is an inexact feasibility-preserving variant when its residual meets the prescribed tolerance.
Repeated Newton corrections give an exact-feasibility implementation in exact arithmetic.
immediate_consequences_latex: The corrected displacement and primary direction have the same first-order tangent.
Constraint curvature is handled in the correction rather than in the linearized SQP constraint.
boundary_notes: If the correction is terminated with a nonzero residual, feasibility is only approximate.
The correction can fail when the Jacobian loses rank or the primary step leaves the correction's local convergence region.

notation.meaning: The primary tangent or reduced-space SQP displacement.

source_refs.locator: Section 12.5, projection iteration (12.5.3) and nonlinear correction systems (12.5.10)–(12.5.11), pp. 318–323

children.title: Nonmonotone SQP Globalization
children.top_down_role: Globalization families permitting controlled temporary deterioration in acceptance measures.

top_down_textbook_witnesses.source_query: Sun and Yuan, Optimization Theory and Methods

locator_traceability.matched_excerpt: - 12.5 Global Convergence of Block Relaxation p. 302

knowledge_statements.slot_contract: State the canonical mathematical definition of the source node, with its domain, quantifiers, notation, and a precise source locator.
knowledge_statements.ambient_context_latex: Let \(\Phi:\mathbb R^n\to\mathbb R\) be an SQP merit or acceptance function, \(m_k\) its local model, and \(d_k\) an SQP trial step. Let \(R_k\) be a reference value constructed from current or historical accepted iterates.
knowledge_statements.scope_note: Deterministic smooth SQP globalization by line search or trust region; controlled increases in the acceptance function are permitted.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex: An SQP globalization is nonmonotone if acceptance is tested against a historical reference \(R_k\ge\Phi(x_k)\), rather than requiring decrease from \(\Phi(x_k)\) itself. A canonical line-search condition is \[\Phi(x_k+\alpha_kd_k)\le R_k+\sigma\alpha_kD\Phi(x_k;d_k),\qquad \sigma\in(0,1),\quad D\Phi(x_k;d_k)<0,\] with \(R_k\) chosen so that a controlled reference subsequence decreases. Temporary values \(\Phi(x_{k+1})>\Phi(x_k)\) are therefore admissible.
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: Nonmonotone SQP globalizes an SQP step by comparing the trial merit value with a historical or aggregated reference that may exceed the current value. The method permits temporary deterioration but requires sufficient progress relative to that controlled reference.
assumptions_latex: The SQP step is a descent direction for the modeled acceptance function or supplies positive predicted reduction.
The reference sequence is updated by a rule that prevents unbounded accumulation of accepted deterioration.
The sufficient-decrease parameter lies strictly between zero and one.
knowledge_statements.conclusion_latex: A trial point may be accepted with \(\Phi(x_{k+1})>\Phi(x_k)\) provided it satisfies the reference-based sufficient-progress test.
equivalent_formulations_latex: In a trust-region form, actual reduction from a reference iterate is divided by cumulative predicted reduction and compared with an acceptance threshold.
A finite-window rule may take \(R_k=\max_{0\le j\le M_k}\Phi(x_{k-j})\).
special_cases_latex: The monotone rule is recovered when \(R_k=\Phi(x_k)\).
Watchdog and finite-window reference-value strategies are distinct nonmonotone specializations.
immediate_consequences_latex: Accepted merit values need not form a decreasing sequence.
The reference mechanism, rather than each individual iteration, carries the monotonic progress requirement.
boundary_notes: Arbitrary increases without a controlled reference update do not define a globalization method.
This definition does not select a unique merit function, window length, or reference aggregation.

notation.meaning: The historical or aggregated acceptance reference at iteration k.
The directional derivative of the acceptance function along the SQP step.

children.title: Watchdog SQP
children.top_down_role: SQP using monitored nonmonotone trial sequences.

knowledge_statements.title: Watchdog SQP
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: Allow a bounded run of nonmonotone SQP trials, accepting it upon sufficient checkpoint-relative progress; otherwise roll back and resume monotone line search.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex:
Let \(\Phi(x;\rho)\) be an exact-penalty merit function. At a checkpoint \(z\), compute the reference value \(\Phi_z=\Phi(z;\rho)\). Permit at most \(M\) successive full or otherwise relaxed SQP steps, producing monitored points \(y_1,\ldots,y_j\), without requiring monotone decrease at every point. Accept the monitored sequence and establish a new checkpoint when some \(y_j\) satisfies
\[
\Phi(y_j;\rho)\le \Phi_z-\sigma\Delta_z,
\]
where \(\sigma\in(0,1)\) and \(\Delta_z>0\) is the checkpoint model’s predicted merit decrease. If no such point occurs by \(j=M\), return to \(z\) and perform an ordinary monotone merit-function line search. Stop at the prescribed KKT tolerance.
assumptions_latex: The merit function \(\Phi(\cdot;\rho)\) and predicted decrease \(\Delta_z\) are defined at each checkpoint.
The watchdog horizon satisfies \(M\in\mathbb N\).
knowledge_statements.conclusion_latex: Every watchdog episode either reaches the checkpoint decrease test within \(M\) trials or returns to the checkpoint for monotone globalization.
knowledge_statements.scope_note: SQP permitting monitored nonmonotone trial sequences before rollback.

knowledge_statements.slot_contract: State the canonical mathematical definition of the source node, with its domain, quantifiers, notation, and a precise source locator.
knowledge_statements.ambient_context_latex: Let \(\Phi(x)\) be an exact-penalty merit function and let \(t\ge2\) be a fixed monitoring horizon. A satisfactory point satisfies the method's prescribed sufficient reduction in \(\Phi\).
knowledge_statements.scope_note: Nonmonotone SQP designed to avoid repeated rejection of locally fast full SQP steps, including rejection caused by the Maratos effect.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex: At a satisfactory reference iterate \(x_r\), a watchdog SQP method attempts successive full SQP steps without requiring merit decrease at each intermediate point. Within at most \(t\) attempted iterations it must obtain a new satisfactory point \(x_j\) satisfying the designated reduction relative to \(x_r\); otherwise it restores \(x_r\) and resumes a safeguarded search. Thus \[1\le j-r\le t\quad\Longrightarrow\quad x_j\text{ satisfactory relative to }x_r,\] or the monitored sequence is discarded and the reference iterate is reinstated.
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: Watchdog SQP stores the last satisfactory iterate, lets full SQP steps run for a bounded number of iterations without enforcing merit decrease at every step, and then evaluates the accumulated result. If satisfactory reduction has not occurred within the monitoring horizon, it backtracks to the stored reference and applies a safeguarded step.
assumptions_latex: \(t>1\) is a fixed finite watchdog horizon.
A full SQP step is attempted during the monitored phase whenever it is defined.
The reference iterate and sufficient-reduction test are retained until the monitored phase succeeds or is abandoned.
knowledge_statements.conclusion_latex: Merit reduction is required at least once per completed watchdog cycle, while intermediate accepted trial points may increase \(\Phi\).
equivalent_formulations_latex: The watchdog is a bounded nonmonotone excursion from a stored satisfactory reference point.
Failure of the monitored excursion triggers rollback to the reference rather than continuation from the last trial point.
special_cases_latex: For \(t=1\), the mechanism reduces to a monotone satisfactory-step requirement.
Near a regular solution, the monitored full-step sequence can accept steps rejected by a pointwise merit test.
immediate_consequences_latex: The stored reference provides a recovery point for erratic trial behavior.
Temporary merit deterioration is bounded by the finite monitoring horizon.
boundary_notes: A sequence with no rollback and no finite monitoring horizon is not the watchdog mechanism defined here.
The definition does not prescribe the particular penalty function or safeguarded recovery search.

notation.meaning: The most recent satisfactory reference iterate retained by the watchdog.
The maximum number of monitored iterations before satisfactory reduction or rollback.
