children.title: Reference-Value Nonmonotone SQP
children.top_down_role: SQP using historical or aggregated acceptance references.

knowledge_statements.title: Reference-Value Nonmonotone SQP
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: Accept an SQP trial relative to the largest recent merit value rather than the current value, thereby allowing controlled nonmonotonicity over a fixed window.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex:
Let \(\Phi_k=\Phi(x_k;\rho_k)\) be a merit value and fix a memory length \(M\ge1\). Define
\[
R_k=\max_{0\le j\le\min\{k,M-1\}}\Phi_{k-j}.
\]
Given an SQP direction \(d_k\) with predicted merit reduction \(\Delta_k>0\), backtrack from \(\alpha=1\) using \(\alpha\leftarrow\tau\alpha\), where \(0<\tau<1\), until
\[
\Phi(x_k+\alpha d_k;\rho_k)\le R_k-\sigma\alpha\Delta_k
\]
for \(0<\sigma<1\). Set \(x_{k+1}=x_k+\alpha d_k\), update the reference window, and stop when the prescribed KKT residual is below tolerance.
assumptions_latex: The merit function is finite at all stored and trial points.
The SQP model supplies \(\Delta_k>0\).
knowledge_statements.conclusion_latex: An accepted step satisfies the stated sufficient-decrease inequality relative to \(R_k\), though it need not decrease \(\Phi_k\).
knowledge_statements.scope_note: Windowed-reference nonmonotone merit-function globalization for SQP.

knowledge_statements.slot_contract: State the canonical mathematical definition of the source node, with its domain, quantifiers, notation, and a precise source locator.
knowledge_statements.ambient_context_latex: Let \(\Phi_k=\Phi(x_k)\) be an SQP merit value, \(d_k\) a trial step, and \(r(k)\le k\) a reference index. Let \(\delta m_i>0\) denote predicted model reduction on successful iteration \(i\).
knowledge_statements.scope_note: Reference-value nonmonotonicity with a historical acceptance ratio; the construction applies to merit-function SQP and analogous trust-region acceptance measures.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex: Define the cumulative predicted reduction \(\Sigma_k^h=\sum_{i=r(k)}^{k-1}\delta m_i\) over successful iterations and the historical ratio \[\rho_k^h=\frac{\Phi(x_{r(k)})-\Phi(x_k+d_k)}{\Sigma_k^h+\delta m_k}.\] With the current ratio \(\rho_k^c=[\Phi(x_k)-\Phi(x_k+d_k)]/\delta m_k\), a reference-value nonmonotone SQP rule accepts when \(\rho_k=\max\{\rho_k^h,\rho_k^c\}\ge\eta_1\), while reference indices are chosen so that the reference subsequence decreases.
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: This nonmonotone SQP rule compares a trial point both with the current iterate and with a selected historical reference. The historical comparison uses the cumulative predicted reduction since that reference. Acceptance occurs when either comparison passes the usual ratio threshold, while the reference subsequence remains decreasing.
assumptions_latex: \(\delta m_k>0\) for each nonstationary trial step.
\(r(k)\le k\), with reference indices updated so that \(\Phi(x_{r(k)})\) decreases along the reference subsequence.
The acceptance threshold satisfies \(\eta_1\in(0,1)\).
knowledge_statements.conclusion_latex: \(x_{k+1}=x_k+d_k\) whenever \(\max\{\rho_k^h,\rho_k^c\}\ge\eta_1\), even if \(\Phi(x_k+d_k)>\Phi(x_k)\).
equivalent_formulations_latex: A finite-window maximum reference is obtained by selecting a recent iterate attaining \(R_k=\max_{0\le j\le M_k}\Phi(x_{k-j})\).
An aggregated reference may replace a single historical value when its update retains the required controlled decrease.
special_cases_latex: Choosing \(r(k)=k\) gives the ordinary monotone current-iteration ratio.
If \(\rho_k^h\ge\eta_1>\rho_k^c\), the step is accepted solely because of its historical progress.
immediate_consequences_latex: The nonmonotone ratio is never smaller than the current ratio.
A locally unfavorable step may be accepted when it remains favorable over the stored history.
boundary_notes: The cumulative denominator must include only model reductions associated with the represented history.
An unconstrained choice of reference values can invalidate the progress mechanism.

notation.meaning: Cumulative predicted model decrease since the reference iteration.

knowledge_statements.slot_contract: State the canonical mathematical definition of the source node, with its domain, quantifiers, notation, and a precise source locator.
knowledge_statements.statement_title: Mathematical Partition of SQP Failure Events and Safeguards
knowledge_statements.ambient_context_latex: At SQP iteration \(k\), let \(Q_k\) be the quadratic subproblem, \(d_k\) its candidate step, \(B_k\) the Lagrangian-Hessian model, \(A_k\) the active constraint Jacobian, and \(\mathcal A_k\) the acceptance test.
knowledge_statements.scope_note: A formal iteration-level taxonomy rather than a convergence theorem; categories may overlap when one numerical event has several causes.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex: Define the SQP failure-event set \(\mathfrak F_k=\mathfrak F_k^{\mathrm{con}}\cup\mathfrak F_k^{\mathrm{mod}}\cup\mathfrak F_k^{\mathrm{acc}}\cup\mathfrak F_k^{\mathrm{curv}}\cup\mathfrak F_k^{\mathrm{reg}}\), where \[\mathfrak F_k^{\mathrm{con}}=\{\operatorname{feas}(Q_k)=\varnothing\},\quad \mathfrak F_k^{\mathrm{mod}}=\{\operatorname{pred}_k(d_k)\le0\},\quad \mathfrak F_k^{\mathrm{acc}}=\{\mathcal A_k(d_k)=\mathrm{reject}\},\] \[\mathfrak F_k^{\mathrm{curv}}=\{B_k\text{ has unsuitable reduced curvature or the KKT system is unstable}\},\quad \mathfrak F_k^{\mathrm{reg}}=\{A_k\text{ is rank deficient or ill-conditioned}\}.\] A safeguard taxonomy assigns restoration or relaxation to constraint inconsistency, model regularization to curvature failure, nonmonotone or second-order correction to acceptance failure, and rank-revealing or stabilized systems to regularity failure.
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: The SQP failure-safeguard taxonomy partitions iteration failures into inconsistent constraints, inadequate predicted model progress, globalization rejection, unsuitable curvature or unstable KKT systems, and deficient constraint regularity. Each class is paired with its principal safeguard family, while overlaps are permitted.
assumptions_latex: An SQP iteration supplies a quadratic model, linearized constraints, an acceptance mechanism, and a linear-algebra realization of its KKT system.
Failure predicates are evaluated relative to explicit numerical tolerances where exact equalities or ranks cannot be tested.
knowledge_statements.conclusion_latex: \(\mathfrak F_k\) is classified by constraint, model, acceptance, curvature, and regularity predicates, with a corresponding safeguard map into relaxation/restoration, model regularization, acceptance correction, and stabilized linear algebra.
special_cases_latex: An empty linearized feasible set belongs to \(\mathfrak F_k^{\mathrm{con}}\).
Maratos rejection belongs to \(\mathfrak F_k^{\mathrm{acc}}\) even when the SQP step is locally accurate.
Rank-deficient active constraints belong to \(\mathfrak F_k^{\mathrm{reg}}\).
immediate_consequences_latex: A single iteration may carry multiple labels, such as simultaneous rank deficiency and subproblem inconsistency.
Safeguard selection can be expressed as a map \(S:\mathfrak F_k\rightrightarrows\mathfrak S\) into a set of correction families.
boundary_notes: No inspected source supplied this exact five-way taxonomy as a canonical definition.
The categories classify observable SQP failure mechanisms and do not claim mutual exclusivity or exhaustive coverage of implementation failures.

notation.meaning: The set of failure events diagnosed at iteration k.
The predicted reduction of the current SQP model at the candidate step.

review_flags: A precise authoritative source for the complete taxonomy and its category boundaries was not located.
The mathematical partition is a candidate synthesis and requires independent sourcing.

children.title: Inconsistent Linearizations
children.top_down_role: Failure of the linearized constraints to admit a viable SQP subproblem step.

knowledge_statements.slot_contract: State the canonical mathematical definition of the source node, with its domain, quantifiers, notation, and a precise source locator.
knowledge_statements.ambient_context_latex: For \(c_E(x)=0\) and \(c_I(x)\ge0\), the SQP linearized feasible set at \(x_k\) is \(\mathcal L_k=\{d:c_E(x_k)+A_{E,k}d=0,\ c_I(x_k)+A_{I,k}d\ge0\}\), optionally intersected with \(\|d\|\le\Delta_k\).
knowledge_statements.scope_note: Finite-dimensional smooth nonlinear programming; distinguishes intrinsic inconsistency of the affine constraints from incompatibility caused only by a trust-region bound.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex: The constraint linearization is inconsistent at \(x_k\) when \[\mathcal L_k=\varnothing.\] The trust-region linearization is incompatible at radius \(\Delta_k\) when \[\mathcal L_k\cap\{d:\|d\|\le\Delta_k\}=\varnothing,\] or, in composite-step frameworks, when the remaining freedom after a normal step is too small to meet the prescribed model-decrease compatibility condition. In either case the standard SQP QP has no viable step under the current local restrictions.
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: An SQP linearization is inconsistent when no displacement satisfies all affine equality and inequality models. A trust-region version is incompatible when no such displacement lies in the current trust region, or when the feasible freedom is too small to provide the required model progress.
assumptions_latex: Constraint values and Jacobians are defined at \(x_k\).
The sign convention is \(c_I(x)\ge0\).
When compatibility includes model freedom, its quantitative decrease threshold is fixed by the SQP framework.
knowledge_statements.conclusion_latex: \(\operatorname{feas}(Q_k)=\varnothing\) for an inconsistent linearization, while trust-region incompatibility may occur even when \(\mathcal L_k\ne\varnothing\).
equivalent_formulations_latex: For equality constraints alone, inconsistency means that \(A_{E,k}d=-c_E(x_k)\) has no solution.
For mixed affine constraints, inconsistency is infeasibility of the corresponding phase-I linear program.
special_cases_latex: If \(A_{E,k}\) has full row rank, equality linearizations alone are consistent for every right-hand side.
A too-small radius can make the trust-region subproblem incompatible without making the unrestricted affine system inconsistent.
immediate_consequences_latex: A standard SQP step cannot be computed without relaxation, radius modification, or restoration.
The diagnostic should distinguish an empty affine set from an overly restrictive trust region.
boundary_notes: Inconsistency of a local linearization does not by itself prove infeasibility of the original nonlinear problem.
Conversely, a feasible affine linearization does not guarantee feasibility of its nonlinear trial point.

notation.meaning: The feasible set of the affine constraint model at iteration k.

knowledge_statements.statement_title: Elastic ell-one reformulation of inconsistent SQP linearizations
knowledge_statements.scope_note: SQP-specific elastic treatment of incompatible linearized equality and inequality constraints, including its exactness and infeasibility boundaries.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex:
Linearized nonlinear constraints can be inconsistent; for example, linearizing $x\leq 1$ and $x^2\geq4$ at $x_k=1$ yields $-p\geq0$ and $2p-3\geq0$. Introduce $v_i,w_i,t_i\geq0$ and solve
\[
\min_{x,v,w,t} f(x)+\mu\sum_{i\in\mathcal E}(v_i+w_i)+\mu\sum_{i\in\mathcal I}t_i
\]
subject to $c_i(x)=v_i-w_i$ for $i\in\mathcal E$ and $c_i(x)\geq-t_i$ for $i\in\mathcal I$. For every $\mu>0$, the associated SQP quadratic subproblem is feasible. If the original problem has a solution $x^*$ satisfying the regularity assumptions required for exact $\ell_1$ penalization, then for all sufficiently large $\mu$, $(x^*,0,0,0)$ solves the elastic problem. If the original problem is infeasible, exact recovery is unavailable; for sufficiently large $\mu$ the elastic formulation instead generally targets a stationary point of its constraint-violation measure.
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: Nonlinear constraints may have mutually inconsistent linearizations even when the nonlinear problem is feasible. Nonnegative elastic variables with an ell-one penalty make every resulting SQP quadratic subproblem feasible. Under the regularity conditions for exact penalization, a feasible solution of the original problem with zero elastic variables also solves the reformulation for a sufficiently large penalty. When the original problem is infeasible, the reformulation instead generally seeks stationarity of a violation measure.
assumptions_latex: \mu>0
c_i(x)=0\ (i\in\mathcal E),\qquad c_i(x)\geq0\ (i\in\mathcal I)
\text{For exact recovery: }x^*\text{ solves the original problem and satisfies the regularity assumptions for exact }\ell_1\text{ penalization.}
knowledge_statements.conclusion_latex: \text{The elastic SQP subproblem is always feasible; for sufficiently large }\mu\text{ it is exact at regular feasible solutions, while infeasible problems retain only a violation-stationarity interpretation.}

children.title: Elastic-Mode SQP
children.top_down_role: SQP subproblem families introducing controlled constraint relaxation.

knowledge_statements.title: Elastic-Mode SQP
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: Add nonnegative elastic variables to inconsistent linearized equalities and penalize them, making the SQP subproblem feasible while measuring unresolved linearized violation.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex:
For \(\min f(x)\) subject to \(c(x)=0\), define \(g_k=\nabla f(x_k)\), \(A_k=\nabla c(x_k)^\top\), and a symmetric model matrix \(B_k\). Given \(\rho_k>0\), solve
\[
\min_{d,v,w}\ g_k^\top d+\tfrac12d^\top B_kd+\rho_k\mathbf1^\top(v+w)
\quad\text{subject to}\quad
c(x_k)+A_kd=v-w,\quad v\ge0,\quad w\ge0.
\]
Use \(d_k=d\) in the chosen SQP globalization procedure. Increase \(\rho_k\) when the elastic variables fail to contract sufficiently, and terminate when the KKT residual and \(\lVert v+w\rVert\) are below their tolerances.
assumptions_latex: \(f\) and \(c\) are continuously differentiable.
The elastic quadratic program has a finite minimizer.
knowledge_statements.conclusion_latex: The elastic constraints are always feasible, and \(v=w=0\) recovers the unrelaxed linearized equalities.
knowledge_statements.scope_note: Equality-constrained SQP with linearly penalized elastic variables.

notation.meaning: nonnegative positive and negative elastic variables

knowledge_statements.slot_contract: State the canonical mathematical definition of the source node, with its domain, quantifiers, notation, and a precise source locator.
knowledge_statements.ambient_context_latex: At \(x_k\), let \(g_k=\nabla f(x_k)\), let \(B_k\) be a symmetric Lagrangian-Hessian model, and partition constraints into equality indices \(\mathcal E\) and inequality indices \(\mathcal I\), using \(c_i(x)\ge0\) for inequalities.
knowledge_statements.scope_note: Smooth finite-dimensional SQP with componentwise nonnegative elastic variables and an \(\ell_1\) penalty; a trust-region bound may be included.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex: For \(\mu_k>0\), the elastic-mode SQP subproblem is \[\min_{d,v,w,t}\ g_k^Td+\tfrac12d^TB_kd+\mu_k\sum_{i\in\mathcal E}(v_i+w_i)+\mu_k\sum_{i\in\mathcal I}t_i\] subject to \[c_i(x_k)+\nabla c_i(x_k)^Td=v_i-w_i\ (i\in\mathcal E),\qquad c_i(x_k)+\nabla c_i(x_k)^Td\ge-t_i\ (i\in\mathcal I),\] \[v,w,t\ge0,\qquad \|d\|\le\Delta_k\ \text{when a trust region is used}.\] The nonnegative elastic variables quantify and penalize violations, making the constraint system feasible.
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: Elastic-mode SQP adds nonnegative positive and negative violation variables to equality linearizations and nonnegative violation variables to inequality linearizations. Their sum is penalized in the quadratic objective, so the subproblem remains feasible even when the unrelaxed linearized constraints are inconsistent.
assumptions_latex: \(B_k\) is symmetric; positive definiteness is not required for the definition when a bounded trust region is present.
Elastic variables are componentwise nonnegative.
knowledge_statements.conclusion_latex: The elastic constraint system is feasible, since sufficiently large \(v,w,t\) accommodate any displacement \(d\), including \(d=0\).
equivalent_formulations_latex: Eliminating \(v,w,t\) yields a quadratic model plus an \(\ell_1\) penalty on linearized constraint violations.
For equalities, \(v_i-w_i\) represents a signed residual with cost \(v_i+w_i=|r_i|\) at an optimal elastic decomposition.
special_cases_latex: With no inequalities, only the paired equality elastic variables \(v,w\) are needed.
With \(\|d\|_\infty\le\Delta_k\), the formulation remains a smooth quadratic program with linear constraints.
immediate_consequences_latex: Inconsistent unrelaxed linearizations do not make the elastic subproblem infeasible.
Zero elastic variables recover the ordinary SQP linearized constraints.
boundary_notes: A small penalty parameter may favor violation reduction inadequately; penalty selection is outside the definition.
Elastic feasibility does not ensure that the original nonlinear constraints are feasible.

notation.meaning: Componentwise nonnegative elastic variables for equality and inequality residuals.

children.title: Relaxed-Linearization SQP
children.top_down_role: SQP variants regularizing or relaxing incompatible local constraints.

knowledge_statements.title: Relaxed-Linearization SQP
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: Replace incompatible linearized equalities by a weighted squared residual in the SQP model, then strengthen the weight when feasibility progress is inadequate.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex:
For \(\min f(x)\) subject to \(c(x)=0\), choose \(\rho_k>0\) and compute \(d_k\) as a minimizer of
\[
g_k^\top d+\tfrac12d^\top B_kd+\tfrac{\rho_k}{2}\lVert c(x_k)+A_kd\rVert^2.
\]
This soft-constrained subproblem is used when \(c(x_k)+A_kd=0\) is inconsistent or undesirable to impose exactly. Globalize \(d_k\) with the selected merit, filter, or trust-region mechanism. Increase \(\rho_k\) when the linearized residual is not sufficiently reduced, and stop when nonlinear feasibility and stationarity tolerances hold. If the penalized subproblem is unbounded or has no acceptable trial, invoke the designated safeguard.
assumptions_latex: \(f\) and \(c\) are continuously differentiable.
\(B_k+\rho_kA_k^\top A_k\) is positive semidefinite on the modeled step space.
knowledge_statements.conclusion_latex: The step subproblem remains defined without requiring solvability of \(c(x_k)+A_kd=0\).
knowledge_statements.scope_note: SQP replacing incompatible linearized equalities by a quadratic residual penalty.

knowledge_statements.slot_contract: State the canonical mathematical definition of the source node, with its domain, quantifiers, notation, and a precise source locator.
knowledge_statements.ambient_context_latex: For the equality-constrained problem \(\min f(x)\) subject to \(c(x)=0\), define \(A_k=\nabla c(x_k)^T\), a trust-region radius \(\Delta_k\), and a constraint-violation model \(\tfrac12\|c(x_k)+A_kd\|^2\).
knowledge_statements.scope_note: Smooth equality-constrained trust-region SQP; relaxation is introduced through a normal step before tangential objective reduction.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex: A relaxed-linearization SQP step is decomposed as \(s_k=n_k+t_k\). The normal step satisfies \[\|n_k\|\le\xi^N\Delta_k\] and achieves a prescribed fraction of the reduction in \(\tfrac12\|c(x_k)+A_kn\|^2\) obtainable by a normal Cauchy step. The tangential step satisfies \[A_kt_k=0,\qquad \|t_k\|\le\xi^T\Delta_k,\] and sufficiently reduces the quadratic Lagrangian model from the normal-step point. Thus the possibly incompatible exact condition \(c(x_k)+A_ks_k=0\) is replaced by quantified reduction of its residual.
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: Relaxed-linearization SQP first computes a bounded normal step that sufficiently decreases the norm of the linearized constraint residual, without requiring that residual to become zero. It then computes a tangential step in the Jacobian null space to decrease the quadratic objective model.
assumptions_latex: The normal step meets the method's Cauchy-type constraint-reduction condition.
The tangential step meets a Cauchy-type quadratic-model reduction condition and remains in \(\ker A_k\).
knowledge_statements.conclusion_latex: \(s_k=n_k+t_k\) balances quantified feasibility improvement with tangential objective progress even when \(c(x_k)+A_ks=0\) cannot be imposed within the trust region.
equivalent_formulations_latex: The normal subproblem is a trust-region least-squares problem for the linearized constraint residual.
The tangential subproblem is a reduced-space trust-region quadratic program on \(\ker A_k\).
special_cases_latex: If a normal step attains \(c(x_k)+A_kn_k=0\), the construction reduces locally to the standard composite SQP step.
If \(c(x_k)=0\), the normal step may be zero and only tangential objective reduction remains.
immediate_consequences_latex: The normal subproblem is meaningful even when the exact affine constraints are incompatible with the current trust region.
Separate radius fractions reserve room for both feasibility and optimality components.
boundary_notes: Relaxed linearization does not introduce the componentwise elastic variables characteristic of elastic-mode SQP.
The definition does not require exact nonlinear feasibility of the accepted trial point.

notation.meaning: The normal step reducing linearized constraint violation.
The tangential step reducing the quadratic objective model.

children.title: Restoration for Inconsistent Models
children.top_down_role: Feasibility-recovery architectures invoked after local model inconsistency.

knowledge_statements.title: Restoration for Inconsistent Models
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: Detect an inconsistent local constraint model, suspend the objective step, reduce nonlinear infeasibility in a separate restoration problem, and rebuild the SQP model.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex:
For \(\min f(x)\) subject to \(c(x)=0\), test whether the linearized constraint system \(c(x_k)+A_kd=0\), together with any step restrictions, is feasible. If it is infeasible or its minimum attainable residual exceeds a prescribed model tolerance, suspend the objective SQP step and solve a restoration problem
\[
\min_d\ \tfrac12\lVert c(x_k+d)\rVert^2
\quad\text{subject to the restoration step restrictions.}
\]
Accept \(x_k^R=x_k+d_R\) only if \(\lVert c(x_k^R)\rVert\le\kappa_R\lVert c(x_k)\rVert\) for \(0<\kappa_R<1\). Rebuild the SQP model at \(x_k^R\); otherwise report restoration failure.
assumptions_latex: \(c:\mathbb R^n\to\mathbb R^m\) is continuously differentiable.
Model consistency can be tested to the prescribed tolerance.
knowledge_statements.conclusion_latex: Successful restoration returns a new model center whose constraint violation is reduced by at least the factor \(\kappa_R\).
knowledge_statements.scope_note: Feasibility recovery triggered by an infeasible SQP linearization.

knowledge_statements.statement_title: Feasibility Restoration after SQP Model Incompatibility
knowledge_statements.ambient_context_latex: Let \(\vartheta(x)\ge0\) measure nonlinear constraint violation, for example \(\vartheta(x)=\|c(x)\|_\infty\). Let \(\operatorname{TRQP}(x,\Delta)\) denote the local trust-region SQP subproblem.
knowledge_statements.scope_note: Filter or trust-region SQP with a distinct feasibility-recovery phase invoked when the local linearized model is empty or incompatible.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex: When \(\operatorname{TRQP}(x_k,\Delta_k)\) is incompatible, a restoration phase approximately solves \[\min_{x\in\mathbb R^n}\vartheta(x)\] from \(x_k\) and returns a displacement \(r_k\) such that \(x_k+r_k\) is acceptable to the globalization mechanism and \(\operatorname{TRQP}(x_k+r_k,\Delta_{k+1})\) is compatible for some \(\Delta_{k+1}>0\). If restoration instead converges to an infeasible first-order critical point of \(\vartheta\), it terminates unsuccessfully and identifies a locally least-infeasible outcome.
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: After detecting an incompatible SQP model, restoration temporarily minimizes a nonlinear constraint-violation measure rather than the original objective. A successful restoration returns a globalization-acceptable point from which a compatible SQP subproblem can be formed; an unsuccessful one may terminate at an infeasible stationary point of the violation measure.
assumptions_latex: \(\vartheta(x)\ge0\), with \(\vartheta(x)=0\) exactly at feasible points for the represented constraints.
The restoration procedure begins at the incompatible-model iterate \(x_k\).
Success requires both globalization acceptability and compatibility of a subsequent trust-region SQP model.
knowledge_statements.conclusion_latex: Either a restored point \(x_k+r_k\) with a compatible subsequent SQP model is obtained, or restoration reports failure at an infeasible first-order critical point of \(\vartheta\).
equivalent_formulations_latex: Norms \(\ell_1\), \(\ell_2\), or \(\ell_\infty\) may define \(\vartheta\).
Restoration is a phase-I nonlinear optimization problem embedded in the SQP architecture.
special_cases_latex: For equality constraints, \(\vartheta(x)=\|c(x)\|_\infty\) is a canonical choice.
A feasible restored point automatically has \(\vartheta=0\), but compatibility may be achieved before exact feasibility.
immediate_consequences_latex: The algorithm does not attempt to solve an empty or unusable SQP subproblem.
Restoration can return meaningful least-infeasibility information even when feasibility is not recovered.
boundary_notes: Stationarity of \(\vartheta\) at a positive value does not establish global infeasibility.
Restoration is distinct from an elastic QP because it changes the current nonlinear point through a separate phase.

notation.meaning: The displacement produced by the restoration phase.

children.top_down_role: The classical local acceptance pathology and the main families used to prevent loss of fast convergence.

knowledge_statements.slot_contract: State the canonical mathematical definition of the source node, with its domain, quantifiers, notation, and a precise source locator.
knowledge_statements.ambient_context_latex: For \(\min f(x)\) subject to \(c(x)=0\), let \(s\) be a full SQP step satisfying \(c(x)+A(x)s=0\), and let \(\Phi\) be an exact-penalty merit function used for step acceptance.
knowledge_statements.scope_note: Local smooth equality-constrained SQP near a regular solution; the definition identifies both the acceptance pathology and the asymptotic correction requirements.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex: The Maratos effect is the rejection or shortening of a locally fast full SQP step because constraint curvature gives \[c(x+s)=c(x)+A(x)s+O(\|s\|^2)=O(\|s\|^2),\] and this second-order violation prevents the merit-function sufficient-decrease test from accepting \(s\). A Maratos correction is an additional step \(s^{\mathrm{soc}}\) satisfying \[s^{\mathrm{soc}}=o(\|s\|),\qquad c(x+s+s^{\mathrm{soc}})=o(\|s\|^2).\] The corrected trial point retains the full SQP step to first order while removing the leading constraint-curvature residual.
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: The Maratos effect occurs when an otherwise fast full SQP step is rejected by the merit test because nonlinear constraint curvature creates a second-order feasibility residual absent from the linearized constraints. A valid correction is smaller than the primary step and reduces the corrected residual below second order.
assumptions_latex: \(f\) and \(c\) are twice continuously differentiable near the reference solution.
The primary step satisfies the equality linearization \(c(x)+A(x)s=0\).
The active constraint Jacobian is regular enough for a local correction to be computed.
knowledge_statements.conclusion_latex: The correction calculus requires \(s^{\mathrm{soc}}=o(\|s\|)\) and \(c(x+s+s^{\mathrm{soc}})=o(\|s\|^2)\), thereby preserving the primary step's first-order asymptotics.
equivalent_formulations_latex: Under stronger regularity, the standard construction gives \(s^{\mathrm{soc}}=O(\|s\|^2)\) and often \(c(x+s+s^{\mathrm{soc}})=O(\|s\|^3)\).
Nonmonotone acceptance can serve as an alternative safeguard when it accepts the full step despite temporary merit deterioration.
special_cases_latex: A minimum-norm solution of \(c(x+s)+A(x)s^{\mathrm{soc}}=0\) is a standard correction.
Reevaluating the Jacobian at \(x+s\) gives the alternative equation \(c(x+s)+A(x+s)s^{\mathrm{soc}}=0\).
immediate_consequences_latex: The corrected displacement is asymptotically equivalent to the primary SQP step.
The correction targets nonlinear constraint curvature rather than the tangential objective model.
boundary_notes: Ordinary globalization rejection far from a solution is not necessarily the Maratos effect.
The stated calculus assumes a smooth regular constraint manifold and does not cover degenerate active sets.

notation.meaning: A second-order correction added to the primary SQP step.
The equality-constraint Jacobian in row-oriented form.

children.title: SQP Second-Order Corrections
children.top_down_role: Correction families addressing nonlinear constraint-model mismatch.

knowledge_statements.slot_contract: State the canonical mathematical definition of the source node, with its domain, quantifiers, notation, and a precise source locator.
knowledge_statements.ambient_context_latex: Let \(c:\mathbb R^n\to\mathbb R^m\) be twice continuously differentiable, let \(A(x)=\nabla c(x)^T\), and let \(s\) satisfy the SQP linearized equality constraints \(c(x)+A(x)s=0\).
knowledge_statements.scope_note: Local equality-constrained SQP with a full-row-rank Jacobian; the correction is defined independently of a particular merit or trust-region update.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex: An SQP second-order correction is a vector \(s^{\mathrm{soc}}\) satisfying \[s^{\mathrm{soc}}=o(\|s\|),\qquad c(x+s+s^{\mathrm{soc}})=o(\|s\|^2).\] A canonical realization is the minimum-norm solution of \[c(x+s)+A(x)s^{\mathrm{soc}}=0,\] equivalently the saddle system \[\begin{pmatrix}I&A(x)^T\\A(x)&0\end{pmatrix}\begin{pmatrix}s^{\mathrm{soc}}\\-y^{\mathrm{soc}}\end{pmatrix}=-\begin{pmatrix}0\\c(x+s)\end{pmatrix}.\] Under regularity, \(s^{\mathrm{soc}}=O(\|s\|^2)\).
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: A second-order SQP correction is an asymptotically smaller displacement added after the primary SQP step so that the remaining nonlinear equality residual becomes smaller than second order. The canonical correction solves the linear system that cancels the residual at the trial point using the current constraint Jacobian.
assumptions_latex: \(c\) is twice continuously differentiable near \(x\).
\(A(x)\) has full row rank.
The primary step satisfies \(c(x)+A(x)s=0\).
knowledge_statements.conclusion_latex: The corrected step \(s+s^{\mathrm{soc}}\) satisfies \(c(x+s+s^{\mathrm{soc}})=o(\|s\|^2)\) without changing the primary step to first order.
equivalent_formulations_latex: Using \(A(x+s)\) instead gives \(c(x+s)+A(x+s)s^{\mathrm{soc}}=0\).
Replacing \(I\) by a suitable symmetric matrix \(H\) gives a minimum-\(H\)-norm correction when the associated saddle system is nonsingular.
special_cases_latex: The current-Jacobian construction commonly yields a corrected residual \(O(\|s\|^3)\).
Two consecutive local SQP solves can realize a second-order correction when evaluated at the trial point.
immediate_consequences_latex: The correction compensates for the constraint curvature omitted by the affine SQP constraints.
Its quadratic size preserves the local convergence order of an accepted full SQP step.
boundary_notes: If the Jacobian is rank deficient, the canonical saddle system may be singular or inconsistent.
A large feasibility restoration step is not a second-order correction because it need not be asymptotically smaller than \(s\).

notation.meaning: The multiplier associated with the minimum-norm correction system.

knowledge_statements.title: Canonical SQP Second-Order Correction

knowledge_statements.statement_title: SQP second-order correction and local superlinear convergence
knowledge_statements.scope_note: A method-specific Maratos correction formed using constraint values at the uncorrected SQP trial point.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex:
After an SQP step \(p_k\) has been computed, evaluate \(c_i(x_k+p_k)\) and set
\[
d_i=c_i(x_k+p_k)-\nabla c_i(x_k)^Tp_k,
\qquad i\in\mathcal E\cup\mathcal I.
\]
Compute a correction \(\hat p_k\) from
\[
\min_p\ \nabla f_k^Tp+\tfrac12p^T\nabla_{xx}^2\mathcal L_kp
\]
subject to
\[
\nabla c_i(x_k)^Tp+d_i=0\quad(i\in\mathcal E),\qquad
\nabla c_i(x_k)^Tp+d_i\ge0\quad(i\in\mathcal I).
\]
The quantities \(d_i\) replace the unavailable quadratic constraint terms by using
\(c_i(x_k+p_k)\approx c_i(x_k)+\nabla c_i(x_k)^Tp_k+\tfrac12p_k^T\nabla^2c_i(x_k)p_k\)
and the approximation \(p^T\nabla^2c_i(x_k)p\approx p_k^T\nabla^2c_i(x_k)p_k\). A possible safeguard invokes the correction only when an increase in \(\phi_1\) is accompanied by an increase in the constraint norm. Near a solution satisfying second-order sufficient conditions, the resulting SQP algorithm accepts either \(p_k\) or \(p_k+\hat p_k\); merit-function interference is avoided and superlinear convergence is attained.
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: When an SQP step suffers from nonlinear constraint-model error, constraint values at the trial point can be used to define shifted linearized constraints for a second quadratic subproblem. The resulting correction may be attempted only when both the merit value and constraint norm increase. Near a solution satisfying second-order sufficient conditions, either the original or corrected step is accepted, preventing merit-function interference and preserving superlinear convergence.
assumptions_latex: p_k\text{ is generated by the stated SQP subproblem}
c_i(x_k+p_k)\text{ is evaluated for every }i\in\mathcal E\cup\mathcal I
\text{the local solution satisfies second-order sufficient conditions}
\text{the iterates are sufficiently near that solution for the local guarantee}
knowledge_statements.conclusion_latex: \text{The algorithm takes }p_k\text{ or }p_k+\hat p_k\text{ and converges superlinearly without local merit-function interference.}

children.title: Constraint-Curvature Corrections
children.top_down_role: Corrections directed at curved-constraint effects omitted by the linearized model.

knowledge_statements.title: Constraint-Curvature Corrections
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: Cancel the quadratic constraint residual omitted by tangent linearization; under regularity, the correction is quadratic in the step and leaves cubic residual.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex:
Let \(c(x_k)=0\), \(J_k=\nabla c(x_k)^\top\), and let \(d_k\) satisfy \(J_kd_k=0\). Compute the constraint-curvature defect
\[
q_k=c(x_k+d_k)-c(x_k)-J_kd_k
\]
and choose a correction \(r_k\) solving \(J_kr_k=-q_k\), for example the minimum-norm solution. Use \(x_k+d_k+r_k\) as the corrected SQP trial. If \(c\) is three times continuously differentiable, \(J_k\) has a uniformly bounded right inverse, and \(\lVert d_k\rVert\to0\), then \(\lVert r_k\rVert=O(\lVert d_k\rVert^2)\) and
\[
\lVert c(x_k+d_k+r_k)\rVert=O(\lVert d_k\rVert^3).
\]
assumptions_latex: \(c\) is three times continuously differentiable near \(x_k\).
\(J_k\) has full row rank with a uniformly bounded right inverse.
knowledge_statements.conclusion_latex: The correction satisfies \(\lVert r_k\rVert=O(\lVert d_k\rVert^2)\) and the corrected constraint residual is \(O(\lVert d_k\rVert^3)\).
knowledge_statements.scope_note: Second-order correction for curvature omitted by equality linearization.

knowledge_statements.slot_contract: State the canonical mathematical definition of the source node, with its domain, quantifiers, notation, and a precise source locator.
knowledge_statements.ambient_context_latex: For smooth equalities \(c(x)=0\), let \(s\) satisfy \(c(x)+A(x)s=0\). Define the curvature residual \(r_c(x,s)=c(x+s)-c(x)-A(x)s\), which is \(O(\|s\|^2)\).
knowledge_statements.scope_note: Local smooth equality-constrained SQP; this slot isolates corrections aimed specifically at the curved-constraint residual rather than general feasibility restoration.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex: A constraint-curvature correction is a vector \(q\) chosen to cancel the second-order residual omitted by the affine constraint model: \[A(x)q=-c(x+s)=-r_c(x,s),\] where the second equality uses \(c(x)+A(x)s=0\). A canonical choice minimizes \(\tfrac12q^THq\) subject to this equation, with saddle system \[\begin{pmatrix}H&A(x)^T\\A(x)&0\end{pmatrix}\begin{pmatrix}q\\-\nu\end{pmatrix}=-\begin{pmatrix}0\\c(x+s)\end{pmatrix}.\] For a regular Jacobian and bounded inverse system, \(q=O(\|s\|^2)\) and \(c(x+s+q)=O(\|s\|^3)\).
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: A constraint-curvature correction computes the second-order residual left after an SQP step satisfies the affine constraints and solves a minimum-norm linear system to cancel that residual. The correction is quadratic in the primary step and reduces the corrected nonlinear residual to third order under regularity.
assumptions_latex: \(c\) has locally Lipschitz continuous second derivatives or sufficient smoothness for the stated residual orders.
\(A(x)\) has full row rank.
\(H\) is symmetric and positive definite on the relevant correction space so the saddle system is nonsingular.
knowledge_statements.conclusion_latex: \(A(x)q=-r_c(x,s)\), with \(q=O(\|s\|^2)\) and \(c(x+s+q)=O(\|s\|^3)\) under the stated regularity.
equivalent_formulations_latex: Using the trial-point Jacobian gives \(A(x+s)q=-c(x+s)\).
Taking \(H=I\) yields the Euclidean minimum-norm curvature correction.
special_cases_latex: For affine constraints, \(r_c(x,s)=0\), so the correction is \(q=0\).
For one equality with nonzero gradient, the Euclidean correction is normal to the linearized constraint surface.
immediate_consequences_latex: The correction vanishes when no constraint curvature is present.
The primary tangential SQP displacement is unchanged to first order.
boundary_notes: This correction addresses constraint curvature only; it does not repair an inconsistent primary linearization.
The stated third-order residual can fail without the required smoothness or Jacobian regularity.

notation.meaning: The nonlinear constraint residual omitted by the affine SQP model.

children.title: Feasibility-Restoring Corrections
children.top_down_role: Corrective directions emphasizing recovery of nonlinear feasibility.

knowledge_statements.title: Feasibility-Restoring Corrections
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: Solve a minimum-norm linear correction at the trial point, producing third-order constraint residual while requiring the correction to remain quadratic in the SQP step.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex: Given an SQP step \(d_k\) satisfying \(A_kd_k+c(x_k)=0\), compute a correction \(s_k\) from \[s_k\in\operatorname*{argmin}_{s\in\mathbb R^n}\tfrac12\lVert s\rVert^2\quad\text{subject to}\quad A(x_k+d_k)s=-c(x_k+d_k).\] Set \(p_k=d_k+s_k\). If the correction system is consistent and \(A(x)\) has uniformly full row rank near a feasible limit point, then \(c(x_k+p_k)=O(\lVert d_k\rVert^3)\) whenever \(c\) has locally Lipschitz second derivatives. Reject or regularize the correction if \(\lVert s_k\rVert>\kappa\lVert d_k\rVert^2\).
assumptions_latex: \(c:\mathbb R^n\to\mathbb R^m\) is twice continuously differentiable with locally Lipschitz second derivatives.
\(A(x)=\nabla c(x)^\top\) has full row rank locally.
\(d_k\to0\) and satisfies the linearized equality constraints.
knowledge_statements.conclusion_latex: \(p_k=d_k+s_k\) satisfies \(c(x_k+p_k)=O(\lVert d_k\rVert^3)\) when \(\lVert s_k\rVert=O(\lVert d_k\rVert^2)\).
knowledge_statements.scope_note: Minimum-norm second-order correction for equality-constrained SQP.

enrichment_metadata.review_comment: The algorithm and local residual estimate are mathematically plausible, but the cited general SQP locator does not inspectably support this particular trial-point minimum-norm correction, its quadratic-size safeguard, or the stated third-order residual guarantee.

knowledge_statements.slot_contract: State the canonical mathematical definition of the source node, with its domain, quantifiers, notation, and a precise source locator.
knowledge_statements.ambient_context_latex: Let \(f,c_i\in C^2\) define \(\min f(x)\) subject to \(c_i(x)=0\) for \(i\in\mathcal E\) and \(c_i(x)\geq0\) for \(i\in\mathcal I\). Define \(\theta(x)=\|c_{\mathcal E}(x)\|+\|[-c_{\mathcal I}(x)]_+\|\). At iterate \(x_k\), let \(p_k\) satisfy the SQP linearized constraints for an active-set estimate \(\mathcal A_k\subseteq\mathcal I\).
knowledge_statements.scope_note: Finite-dimensional smooth SQP; the definition concerns a local correction appended to an already computed SQP step.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex: A vector \(r_k\in\mathbb R^n\) is a feasibility-restoring correction for \(p_k\) if the corrected trial step \(s_k=p_k+r_k\) satisfies \(\theta(x_k+s_k)\leq\kappa_f\theta(x_k+p_k)\) for some fixed \(0\leq\kappa_f<1\), while \(\|r_k\|\leq\kappa_r\|p_k\|^2\). In the equation-based second-order form, \(r_k\) satisfies \(J_k r_k=-c_{ar{\mathcal A}_k}(x_k+p_k)\), exactly or to residual \(o(\|p_k\|^2)\), where \(\bar{\mathcal A}_k=\mathcal E\cup\mathcal A_k\) and \(J_k=\nabla c_{ar{\mathcal A}_k}(x_k)\).
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: A feasibility-restoring correction is a vector \(r_k\) added to the SQP step \(p_k\) that contracts nonlinear constraint violation by a fixed factor and remains second-order small, \(\|r_k\|=O(\|p_k\|^2)\). In its equation-based form it cancels, exactly or asymptotically, the nonlinear residual left after the linearized SQP step.
knowledge_statements.conclusion_latex: \(s_k=p_k+r_k\), \(\theta(x_k+s_k)\leq\kappa_f\theta(x_k+p_k)\), and \(\|r_k\|\leq\kappa_r\|p_k\|^2\).
equivalent_formulations_latex: When \(J_k\) has full row rank, a minimum-norm correction is \(r_k=-J_k^T(J_kJ_k^T)^{-1}c_{\bar{\mathcal A}_k}(x_k+p_k)\).
special_cases_latex: For equality constraints only, \(\theta(x)=\|c(x)\|\) and the correction equation reduces to \(J_k r_k=-c(x_k+p_k)\).
immediate_consequences_latex: The bound \(\|r_k\|=O(\|p_k\|^2)\) preserves the first-order SQP direction while modifying its nonlinear feasibility at second order.
boundary_notes: A restoration-phase step of first-order size is not covered by this local second-order-correction definition.
For inequalities, the active-set estimate must be specified; imposing correction equations for every inactive constraint may be inappropriate.

children.title: Nonmonotone Maratos Safeguards
children.top_down_role: Acceptance mechanisms that avoid overly restrictive monotone merit behavior.

knowledge_statements.title: Nonmonotone Maratos Safeguards
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: Accept a trial point relative to the largest recent merit value, permitting a controlled one-step increase that a monotone test would reject.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex: Let \(\phi\) be a merit function and let \(M\ge1\). Define \(R_k=\max_{0\le j\le\min\{k,M-1\}}\phi(x_{k-j})\). A trial step \(p_k\) passes the finite-memory nonmonotone safeguard when \[\phi(x_k+\alpha_kp_k)\le R_k-\sigma\alpha_k\Delta_k,\] where \(\alpha_k\in(0,1]\), \(\sigma\in(0,1)\), and \(\Delta_k>0\) is the model-predicted merit decrease. Thus a full step may be accepted despite \(\phi(x_k+p_k)>\phi(x_k)\), provided its merit value decreases sufficiently relative to the recent reference maximum.
assumptions_latex: \(\phi:\mathbb R^n\to\mathbb R\) is bounded below on the generated level region.
\(M\) is a fixed positive integer.
\(\Delta_k>0\) is computed consistently from the SQP model.
knowledge_statements.conclusion_latex: \(\phi(x_k+\alpha_kp_k)\le R_k-\sigma\alpha_k\Delta_k\) is sufficient for nonmonotone acceptance.
knowledge_statements.scope_note: Finite-memory merit acceptance allowing controlled increases at an SQP trial point.

notation.meaning: Maximum merit value in the finite reference window.

enrichment_metadata.review_comment: The finite-memory condition is a valid generic nonmonotone acceptance test and the content kind fits, but the supplied SQP locator does not establish this exact reference-maximum variant or its use specifically as a Maratos safeguard.

knowledge_statements.slot_contract: State the canonical mathematical definition of the source node, with its domain, quantifiers, notation, and a precise source locator.
knowledge_statements.ambient_context_latex: Let \(\Phi_\rho:\mathbb R^n\to\mathbb R\) be an exact-penalty merit function, let \(s_k=p_k+r_k\) be an SQP trial step with an optional second-order correction, and let \(\Delta m_k>0\) denote its predicted merit reduction. Fix \(M\geq1\) and \(\sigma\in(0,1)\).
knowledge_statements.scope_note: Smooth finite-dimensional line-search SQP with a finite-memory nonmonotone acceptance reference.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex: A finite-window nonmonotone Maratos safeguard accepts \(x_k+\alpha_k s_k\), with \(\alpha_k\in(0,1]\), whenever \(\Phi_\rho(x_k+\alpha_k s_k)\leq R_k-\sigma\alpha_k\Delta m_k\), where \(R_k=\max_{0\leq j\leq\min\{k,M-1\}}\Phi_\rho(x_{k-j})\). It is a Maratos safeguard when the same test is applied to the corrected step after the uncorrected full SQP step fails the chosen acceptance test, and the correction obeys \(\|r_k\|=O(\|p_k\|^2)\).
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: The safeguard compares the corrected SQP trial point with the largest merit value in a finite recent window, rather than requiring decrease from the current merit value. Acceptance requires the actual merit value to lie below that reference by a fixed fraction \(\sigma\) of the predicted reduction. The correction remains second-order small so that the local SQP direction is retained.
knowledge_statements.conclusion_latex: \(x_{k+1}=x_k+\alpha_k(p_k+r_k)\) is accepted if \(\Phi_\rho(x_{k+1})\leq R_k-\sigma\alpha_k\Delta m_k\).
equivalent_formulations_latex: A weighted reference \(R_k\geq\Phi_\rho(x_k)\) may replace the window maximum provided its update has bounded memory and enforces eventual descent.
special_cases_latex: For \(M=1\), \(R_k=\Phi_\rho(x_k)\), so the rule becomes the usual monotone sufficient-decrease test.
immediate_consequences_latex: For \(M>1\), an accepted iteration may satisfy \(\Phi_\rho(x_{k+1})>\Phi_\rho(x_k)\) while still meeting the windowed decrease condition.
boundary_notes: This definition does not by itself establish convergence; a complete method also needs conditions on penalty updates, predicted reduction, and failed-trial handling.
A filter method is distinct unless its acceptance reference is explicitly representable by the stated scalar merit rule.
review_flags: The supplied hints do not identify an inspected source locator for this precise windowed Maratos acceptance rule.
knowledge_statements.title: Windowed nonmonotone Maratos safeguard
Maratos Acceptance Pathology
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: Constraint curvature creates a second-order merit penalty that can cause repeated rejection of otherwise accurate full SQP steps and destroy superlinear convergence.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex: Consider equality-constrained SQP approaching a regular solution and producing steps \(d_k\) with \(A_kd_k+c(x_k)=0\). Although \(d_k\) may be a superlinearly accurate primal step, nonlinear curvature generally gives \(c(x_k+d_k)=O(\lVert d_k\rVert^2)\). For an exact-penalty merit function, this positive second-order feasibility term can dominate the Armijo allowance based on the predicted decrease. Consequently the monotone line search may reject \(\alpha_k=1\) for infinitely many \(k\), forcing shortened steps and preventing the underlying SQP iteration from attaining its local superlinear rate.

knowledge_statements.title: Correction Applicability Boundaries
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: Second-order corrections are unsafe under Jacobian rank loss, active-set changes, or corrections too large relative to the primary SQP step.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex: A second-order feasibility correction based on \(A(x_k+d_k)s_k=-c(x_k+d_k)\) is locally reliable only while the relevant constraint Jacobian has stable full row rank, the active set used by the correction remains valid, and a solution satisfies \(\lVert s_k\rVert=O(\lVert d_k\rVert^2)\). If rank is lost, the system may be inconsistent or ill-conditioned; if the active set changes, it corrects the wrong manifold; and if \(\lVert s_k\rVert\) is not quadratic in \(\lVert d_k\rVert\), the correction can destroy the SQP model step. In any such case it must be rejected, regularized, or replaced by restoration.
assumptions_latex: The correction is formed from constraints predicted active by the SQP subproblem.
The primary step \(d_k\) is nonzero and sufficiently small.
knowledge_statements.conclusion_latex: Failure of rank stability, active-set stability, or \(\lVert s_k\rVert=O(\lVert d_k\rVert^2)\) invalidates the standard local correction guarantee.
knowledge_statements.scope_note: Regularity and scale conditions delimiting reliable second-order corrections.

children.top_down_role: Curvature and linear-algebra failures affecting subproblem stability or boundedness.

knowledge_statements.slot_contract: State the canonical mathematical definition of the source node, with its domain, quantifiers, notation, and a precise source locator.
knowledge_statements.ambient_context_latex: At \(x_k\), consider the equality-form SQP subproblem \(\min_p q_k(p)=g_k^Tp+\tfrac12p^TB_kp\) subject to \(A_kp=b_k\), or its active-set reduction for inequalities. knowledge_statements.scope_note: Finite-dimensional SQP model diagnostics; pathology is defined for the local quadratic model, not necessarily for the original nonlinear program.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex: The SQP model is in a pathology regime if at least one of the following holds: \(\{p:A_kp=b_k\}=\varnothing\); there exist a feasible \(p_0\) and \(d\in\ker A_k\) for which \(q_k(p_0+td)\to-\infty\) as \(t\to\infty\); \(K_k\) is singular; or the reduced Hessian \(Z_k^TB_kZ_k\) has a nonpositive eigenvalue when a uniquely solvable strictly convex tangent-space model is required.
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: An SQP quadratic model is pathological when its linearized constraints are incompatible, its objective is unbounded below along a feasible recession direction, its KKT system is singular, or its reduced curvature fails the positivity required for a unique stable minimizer. These alternatives distinguish feasibility, boundedness, rank, and curvature failures.
knowledge_statements.conclusion_latex: The pathology indicator is true exactly when at least one stated feasibility, recession, singularity, or reduced-curvature condition holds.

special_cases_latex: For unconstrained SQP, \(A_k\) is absent and the curvature pathology reduces to \(B_k\not\succ0\) or singularity of \(B_k\).
immediate_consequences_latex: Different pathology classes call for different responses: elastic variables address incompatibility, whereas regularization addresses curvature or KKT singularity.
boundary_notes: Indefiniteness is not automatically a failure when the algorithm intentionally searches for negative curvature.
Ill-conditioning without exact singularity is a numerical warning but is not included in the exact pathology predicate.

children.title: SQP Hessian Regularization
children.top_down_role: Curvature modifications intended to stabilize the quadratic model.

knowledge_statements.slot_contract: State the canonical mathematical definition of the source node, with its domain, quantifiers, notation, and a precise source locator.
knowledge_statements.ambient_context_latex: Let \(B_k=B_k^T\in\mathbb R^{n\times n}\) approximate the Lagrangian Hessian, let \(A_k\in\mathbb R^{m\times n}\) be the active constraint Jacobian, and let \(Z_k\) have columns spanning \(\ker A_k\). Fix a desired curvature floor \(\gamma_k>0\).
knowledge_statements.scope_note: Smooth finite-dimensional SQP; regularization is measured on the tangent space of the current active linearization.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex: An SQP Hessian regularization is a symmetric modification \(E_k=E_k^T\) producing \(\widehat B_k=B_k+E_k\) such that \(Z_k^T\widehat B_kZ_k\succeq\gamma_k I\). The regularized QP replaces \(\tfrac12p^TB_kp\) by \(\tfrac12p^T\widehat B_kp\) while retaining the same linearized constraints. A minimal-norm version selects \(E_k\) from an admissible class by minimizing \(\|E\|\) subject to the reduced-curvature inequality.
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: SQP Hessian regularization replaces the symmetric curvature approximation \(B_k\) by \(B_k+E_k\) so that the resulting quadratic model has a prescribed positive curvature floor on all feasible tangent directions. The linearized constraint model is unchanged. The modification may be diagonal, spectral, modified-Cholesky based, or otherwise structured.
knowledge_statements.conclusion_latex: For every \(d\in\ker A_k\), \(d^T\widehat B_kd\geq\gamma_k\|d\|^2\).
equivalent_formulations_latex: The condition is equivalent to \(\lambda_{\min}(Z_k^T\widehat B_kZ_k)\geq\gamma_k\) when \(Z_k\) has orthonormal columns.
special_cases_latex: If \(B_k\) already satisfies the curvature floor, \(E_k=0\) is admissible.
A scalar shift uses \(E_k=\delta_k I\) with sufficiently large \(\delta_k\geq0\).
immediate_consequences_latex: If \(A_k\) has full row rank, the regularized equality-constrained QP has a unique primal minimizer whenever its affine constraint set is nonempty.
boundary_notes: Positive definiteness on all of \(\mathbb R^n\) is stronger than required; only tangent-space curvature is intrinsic to the equality-constrained QP.
This definition does not prescribe how \(E_k\) is reduced near a solution.

children.title: Primal Hessian Regularization
children.top_down_role: Regularization applied to the primal curvature representation.

knowledge_statements.title: Primal Hessian Regularization
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: Add a diagonal shift until the Hessian is uniformly positive definite on feasible directions, then solve the stabilized quadratic subproblem, which has a unique minimizer whenever its affine constraints are consistent.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex: Let \(g_k,d\in\mathbb R^n\), \(B_k\in\mathbb R^{n\times n}\) with \(B_k=B_k^\top\), \(A_k\in\mathbb R^{m\times n}\), and \(b_k\in\mathbb R^m\). For the SQP subproblem \[\min_{d\in\mathbb R^n}\; g_k^\top d+\tfrac12d^\top B_kd\quad\text{subject to}\quad A_kd=b_k,\] choose \(\tau_k\ge0\) and set \(\widehat B_k=B_k+\tau_kI_n\). Increase \(\tau_k\) until a factorization or reduced-space test verifies \[z^\top\widehat B_kz\ge\epsilon\lVert z\rVert^2\qquad\text{for every }z\in\ker A_k,\] where \(\epsilon>0\) is prescribed. Solve the regularized QP and return its primal step. If \(A_kd=b_k\) is consistent, the regularized objective is strongly convex on the feasible affine space and therefore has a unique minimizer.
assumptions_latex: \(B_k=B_k^\top\).
\(A_k\in\mathbb R^{m\times n}\) has full row rank.
The affine system \(A_kd=b_k\) is consistent.
\(\epsilon>0\).
knowledge_statements.conclusion_latex: \(z^\top(B_k+\tau_kI_n)z\ge\epsilon\lVert z\rVert^2\) for every \(z\in\ker A_k\), and the regularized QP has a unique minimizer.
knowledge_statements.scope_note: Diagonal stabilization of the primal quadratic model in equality-constrained SQP.

knowledge_statements.slot_contract: State the canonical mathematical definition of the source node, with its domain, quantifiers, notation, and a precise source locator.
knowledge_statements.ambient_context_latex: Let \(B_k=B_k^T\) be an SQP Hessian approximation and \(A_k\) the active constraint Jacobian. Let \(Z_k\) be orthonormal with \(\operatorname{range}(Z_k)=\ker A_k\), and fix \(\gamma_k>0\).
knowledge_statements.scope_note: Primal-only regularization of a smooth finite-dimensional SQP quadratic model.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex: Primal Hessian regularization by a scalar shift chooses \(\delta_k\geq0\) and replaces \(B_k\) by \(B_k^{\mathrm{reg}}=B_k+\delta_k I\), where \(\delta_k\geq\max\{0,\gamma_k-\lambda_{\min}(Z_k^TB_kZ_k)\}\). The regularized step solves the original linearized constraints with quadratic objective \(g_k^Tp+\tfrac12p^TB_k^{\mathrm{reg}}p\); no dual-block perturbation is introduced.
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: Primal Hessian regularization adds a nonnegative multiple of the identity to the primal quadratic term. The shift is large enough to raise the smallest reduced-Hessian eigenvalue to at least \(\gamma_k\), while leaving the constraint equations and multiplier block unchanged.
knowledge_statements.conclusion_latex: \(Z_k^TB_k^{\mathrm{reg}}Z_k\succeq\gamma_k I\) with \(B_k^{\mathrm{reg}}=B_k+\delta_kI\).
equivalent_formulations_latex: The smallest admissible scalar shift is \(\delta_k^*=\max\{0,\gamma_k-\lambda_{\min}(Z_k^TB_kZ_k)\}\).
special_cases_latex: For an unconstrained model, \(Z_k=I\) and \(\delta_k^*=\max\{0,\gamma_k-\lambda_{\min}(B_k)\}\).
immediate_consequences_latex: The shifted quadratic model is strongly convex along every feasible tangent direction.
boundary_notes: A general matrix modification \(E_k\) is Hessian regularization but is not necessarily scalar primal regularization.
The definition excludes simultaneous perturbation of the multiplier block.

children.title: Primal-Dual Regularization

knowledge_statements.title: Primal-Dual Regularization
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: Regularize both primal and multiplier blocks, adjust the shifts using factorization diagnostics, and solve the resulting nonsingular saddle-point system.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex: Given the primal-dual Newton equations, choose \(\delta_k>0\) and \(\gamma_k>0\), then solve \[\begin{pmatrix}B_k+\delta_kI&A_k^\top\\A_k&-\gamma_kI\end{pmatrix}\begin{pmatrix}d_k\\\Delta\lambda_k\end{pmatrix}=-\begin{pmatrix}r_k^d\\r_k^p\end{pmatrix}.\] Increase the shifts when factorization detects singularity or unacceptable inertia, and decrease them as the residuals approach zero. If \(B_k+\delta_kI\) is positive definite, the displayed matrix is nonsingular for every \(A_k\), because its dual Schur complement is negative definite. Output \((d_k,\lambda_k+\Delta\lambda_k)\).
assumptions_latex: \(B_k=B_k^\top\).
\(B_k+\delta_kI\) is positive definite.
\(\delta_k>0\) and \(\gamma_k>0\).
knowledge_statements.conclusion_latex: The regularized primal-dual matrix is nonsingular and defines a unique pair \((d_k,\Delta\lambda_k)\).
knowledge_statements.scope_note: Coupled diagonal stabilization of the saddle-point SQP equations.

children.title: SQP Inertia Control
children.top_down_role: Factorization-based safeguards aligning linear-system inertia with the desired step geometry.

knowledge_statements.title: SQP Inertia Control
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: Factor the equality-constrained KKT matrix and regularize until its positive, negative, and zero eigenvalue counts are n, m, and zero, which certifies positive curvature on all nonzero feasible directions.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex: Let \(B_k\in\mathbb R^{n\times n}\) satisfy \(B_k=B_k^\top\), and let \(A_k\in\mathbb R^{m\times n}\) have full row rank. Form the symmetric KKT matrix \[K_k=\begin{pmatrix}B_k&A_k^\top\\A_k&0_{m\times m}\end{pmatrix}\in\mathbb R^{(n+m)\times(n+m)}.\] Compute a symmetric-indefinite factorization and the inertia \(\operatorname{In}(K_k)=(n_+,n_-,n_0)\), ordered as the numbers of positive, negative, and zero eigenvalues. If the inertia is not \((n,m,0)\), modify the primal Hessian or both diagonal blocks and refactor. Under the full-row-rank assumption, \(\operatorname{In}(K_k)=(n,m,0)\) is equivalent to \(z^\top B_kz>0\) for every nonzero \(z\in\ker A_k\). Accept the linear-system step only after the target inertia is obtained.
assumptions_latex: \(B_k\in\mathbb R^{n\times n}\) and \(B_k=B_k^\top\).
\(A_k\in\mathbb R^{m\times n}\) has full row rank.
knowledge_statements.conclusion_latex: \(\operatorname{In}(K_k)=(n,m,0)\) if and only if \(z^\top B_kz>0\) for every nonzero \(z\in\ker A_k\).
knowledge_statements.scope_note: Symmetric-factorization test for curvature adequacy of equality-constrained SQP systems.

notation.meaning: Ordered counts of positive, negative, and zero eigenvalues.

knowledge_statements.scope_note: Equality-constrained or fixed-active-set SQP using a symmetric-indefinite factorization.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex: SQP inertia control is the rule of selecting a symmetric modification \(E_k\) and factoring \(K_k(E_k)\) until \(\operatorname{In}(K_k(E_k))=(n,m,0)\). The target inertia certifies positive definiteness of \(B_k+E_k\) on \(\ker A_k\). A factorization-based implementation obtains the inertia from the signed pivots of a stable symmetric-indefinite factorization and increases or revises \(E_k\) whenever the observed counts differ from \((n,m,0)\).
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: SQP inertia control modifies the KKT matrix until a symmetric factorization reports exactly \(n\) positive, \(m\) negative, and no zero eigenvalues. Under full row rank of the active Jacobian, this is the saddle-point signature associated with positive curvature on feasible tangent directions and a nonsingular SQP system.
knowledge_statements.conclusion_latex: The accepted regularized KKT matrix satisfies \(\operatorname{In}(K_k(E_k))=(n,m,0)\).
equivalent_formulations_latex: With full-row-rank \(A_k\), the target inertia is equivalent to \(Z_k^T(B_k+E_k)Z_k\succ0\).
special_cases_latex: If the unmodified matrix already has inertia \((n,m,0)\), the controller may take \(E_k=0\).
immediate_consequences_latex: The zero count vanishes, so the controlled KKT equations have a unique primal-dual solution.
boundary_notes: The target \((n,m,0)\) assumes \(m\) independent equality or active constraints.
Numerical pivot tolerances produce an estimated inertia; near-zero pivots require an explicit threshold policy.

knowledge_statements.title: Negative-Curvature SQP
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: Detect negative curvature in the linearized feasible space and follow it to the trust-region boundary when doing so improves the SQP model.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex: At iterate \(x_k\), compute a normal or SQP step \(d_k\) and seek \(z_k\in\ker A_k\) with \(\lVert z_k\rVert=1\) and \(z_k^\top B_kz_k<0\). Choose its sign so that \((g_k+B_kd_k)^\top z_k\le0\), and select the largest \(t_k\ge0\) satisfying \(\lVert d_k+t_kz_k\rVert\le\Delta_k\). Compare the model values of the base and curvature-augmented candidates, returning the lower one. The trust-region bound makes the step finite while the curvature component decreases the quadratic model whenever \(t_k>0\).

\(A_kz_k=0\) and \(z_k^\top B_kz_k<0\).
\(\Delta_k>0\) bounds the trial step.
knowledge_statements.conclusion_latex: The selected curvature-augmented step is bounded and has quadratic-model value no greater than that of the base candidate.

Indefinite Curvature Regimes
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: The SQP model has indefinite feasible curvature exactly when its reduced Hessian has both a positive and a negative eigenvalue; the negative direction makes the feasible quadratic model nonconvex.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex: Let \(B_k\in\mathbb R^{n\times n}\) satisfy \(B_k=B_k^\top\), let \(A_k\in\mathbb R^{m\times n}\) have full row rank with \(m<n\), and let \(Z_k\in\mathbb R^{n\times(n-m)}\) have columns forming a basis of \(\ker A_k\). Define the reduced Hessian by \(H_k^R=Z_k^\top B_kZ_k\). The SQP quadratic model is in an indefinite-curvature regime precisely when \(H_k^R\) has at least one positive and at least one negative eigenvalue. Equivalently, there exist nonzero \(u_k,v_k\in\ker A_k\) such that \(u_k^\top B_ku_k<0\) and \(v_k^\top B_kv_k>0\). In particular, the negative feasible curvature precludes convexity of the quadratic objective on the linearized feasible affine space.

\(A_k\in\mathbb R^{m\times n}\) has full row rank and \(m<n\).

knowledge_statements.title: Singular KKT Systems
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: The equality-constrained KKT matrix is singular through constraint-rank loss or, when the constraint matrix has full row rank, through singularity of the reduced Hessian.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex: Let \(B\in\mathbb R^{n\times n}\) satisfy \(B=B^\top\), let \(A\in\mathbb R^{m\times n}\), and define \[K=\begin{pmatrix}B&A^\top\\A&0_{m\times m}\end{pmatrix}.\] The matrix \(K\) is singular exactly when there is a nonzero pair \((d,y)\in\mathbb R^n\times\mathbb R^m\) satisfying \(Bd+A^\top y=0\) and \(Ad=0\). If \(A\) has full row rank and \(Z\in\mathbb R^{n\times(n-m)}\) has columns forming a basis of \(\ker A\), then \(K\) is nonsingular if and only if \(Z^\top BZ\) is nonsingular. If \(A\) lacks full row rank, then \(K\) is singular because there exists a nonzero \(y\in\mathbb R^m\) with \(A^\top y=0\).
assumptions_latex: \(B\in\mathbb R^{n\times n}\) and \(B=B^\top\).
\(A\in\mathbb R^{m\times n}\).
When \(A\) has full row rank, the columns of \(Z\in\mathbb R^{n\times(n-m)}\) form a basis of \(\ker A\).
knowledge_statements.conclusion_latex: If \(A\) has full row rank, then \(K\) is nonsingular if and only if \(Z^\top BZ\) is nonsingular; if \(A\) lacks full row rank, then \(K\) is singular.
knowledge_statements.scope_note: Null-space criterion for singular equality-constrained SQP saddle-point matrices.

notation.meaning: Null-space basis matrix for the constraint matrix.

knowledge_statements.title: Unbounded QP Subproblems
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: A feasible point together with a feasible negative-curvature recession direction certifies that the quadratic model tends to minus infinity and has no finite minimizer.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex: Let \(B\in\mathbb R^{n\times n}\) satisfy \(B=B^\top\), let \(g,d\in\mathbb R^n\), let \(A\in\mathbb R^{m\times n}\), and let \(b\in\mathbb R^m\). Consider \[q(d)=g^\top d+\tfrac12d^\top Bd\quad\text{subject to}\quad Ad=b.\] Suppose there is a feasible point \(d_0\in\mathbb R^n\) and a nonzero vector \(z\in\mathbb R^n\) satisfying \(Az=0\) and \(z^\top Bz<0\). Then \(d_0+tz\) is feasible for every \(t\ge0\), and \[q(d_0+tz)=q(d_0)+t(g+Bd_0)^\top z+\tfrac12t^2z^\top Bz\longrightarrow-\infty\quad\text{as }t\to\infty.\] Thus \((d_0,z)\) certifies that the unrestricted-radius SQP quadratic subproblem is unbounded below and has no finite minimizer.
assumptions_latex: \(B\in\mathbb R^{n\times n}\) and \(B=B^\top\).
There exists \(d_0\in\mathbb R^n\) with \(Ad_0=b\).
There exists nonzero \(z\in\mathbb R^n\) with \(Az=0\) and \(z^\top Bz<0\).
knowledge_statements.conclusion_latex: \(\inf\{q(d):d\in\mathbb R^n,\ Ad=b\}=-\infty\).
knowledge_statements.scope_note: Negative-curvature recession certificate for an equality-constrained SQP subproblem.

notation.meaning: A feasible point of the affine constraint system.

children.title: SQP Subproblem Failure Diagnostics
children.top_down_role: Subproblem outcomes used to distinguish incompatible constraints, uncontrolled curvature, and rank loss.

knowledge_statements.slot_contract: State the canonical mathematical definition of the source node, with its domain, quantifiers, notation, and a precise source locator.
knowledge_statements.ambient_context_latex: Let \(Q_k\) be the SQP quadratic program with objective \(q_k(p)=g_k^Tp+\tfrac12p^TB_kp\) and polyhedral linearized feasible set \(F_k\). Let \(K_k\) denote the KKT matrix associated with a candidate active set.
knowledge_statements.scope_note: Exact finite-dimensional diagnostics for a local SQP QP; numerical implementations may replace equalities by tolerance tests.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex: An SQP subproblem failure diagnostic is a map \(\mathcal D(Q_k)\in\{\mathrm{INFEASIBLE},\mathrm{UNBOUNDED},\mathrm{SINGULAR},\mathrm{SOLVABLE}\}\) whose non-solvable outputs require certificates: \(F_k=\varnothing\) or a Farkas certificate for \(\mathrm{INFEASIBLE}\); a feasible base point and recession direction along which \(q_k\to-\infty\) for \(\mathrm{UNBOUNDED}\); and a nonzero null vector of the relevant KKT matrix for \(\mathrm{SINGULAR}\). The output \(\mathrm{SOLVABLE}\) requires a finite KKT point with no applicable failure certificate.
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: The diagnostic classifies an SQP quadratic subproblem by mathematically distinct certificates. Incompatibility concerns the linearized feasible set, unboundedness concerns objective behavior on its recession cone, and singularity concerns rank loss in the active-set KKT equations. A solver status without a corresponding certificate is only an implementation warning, not an exact diagnostic under this definition.
knowledge_statements.conclusion_latex: Each failure label is attached only when its defining feasibility, recession, or null-space certificate is present.
special_cases_latex: For a strictly convex QP with a nonempty feasible polyhedron, the unbounded and singular-primal-solution labels are excluded.
immediate_consequences_latex: The labels separate remedies: elastic constraints target infeasibility, curvature control targets unboundedness, and rank-revealing regularization targets singularity.
boundary_notes: The three failures need not be mutually exclusive for every malformed active-set representation; a priority convention may be needed.
Iteration limits and floating-point breakdown are computational failures, not exact mathematical certificates.

notation.meaning: linearized feasible set of the SQP subproblem

children.title: SQP QP Infeasibility Diagnostics
children.top_down_role: Diagnostic families for incompatible local constraint models.

knowledge_statements.title: SQP QP Infeasibility Diagnostics
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: A free equality multiplier and a nonnegative inequality multiplier satisfying the displayed Farkas relations certify, and are equivalent to, infeasibility of the SQP subproblem's linear constraints.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex: Let \(A\in\mathbb R^{m_e\times n}\), \(b\in\mathbb R^{m_e}\), \(C\in\mathbb R^{m_i\times n}\), and \(h\in\mathbb R^{m_i}\). For the linear QP constraints \(Ad=b\) and \(Cd\le h\), interpreted componentwise, a primal infeasibility certificate is a pair \((y,z)\in\mathbb R^{m_e}\times\mathbb R^{m_i}\) satisfying \[z\ge0,\qquad A^\top y+C^\top z=0,\qquad b^\top y+h^\top z<0.\] These relations are directly checkable from the QP data. By the finite-dimensional theorem of alternatives, such a pair exists if and only if there is no \(d\in\mathbb R^n\) satisfying both \(Ad=b\) and \(Cd\le h\). Thus an SQP implementation can diagnose incompatible local linearized constraints independently of the quadratic objective.
assumptions_latex: \(A\in\mathbb R^{m_e\times n}\), \(b\in\mathbb R^{m_e}\), \(C\in\mathbb R^{m_i\times n}\), and \(h\in\mathbb R^{m_i}\).
The inequality \(Cd\le h\) and the condition \(z\ge0\) are interpreted componentwise.
knowledge_statements.conclusion_latex: There is no \(d\in\mathbb R^n\) satisfying \(Ad=b\) and \(Cd\le h\) if and only if there exist \(y\in\mathbb R^{m_e}\) and \(z\in\mathbb R^{m_i}\) with \(z\ge0\), \(A^\top y+C^\top z=0\), and \(b^\top y+h^\top z<0\).
knowledge_statements.scope_note: Farkas certificate for incompatibility of an SQP linearized constraint system.

notation.meaning: Numbers of equality and inequality constraints.

knowledge_statements.statement_title: Farkas diagnostic for an infeasible SQP linearization
knowledge_statements.ambient_context_latex: Let the SQP QP constraints be \(A_Ep=b_E\) and \(A_Ip\geq b_I\). The quadratic objective is irrelevant to feasibility. Multipliers \(y_E\) are unrestricted and \(y_I\geq0\).
knowledge_statements.scope_note: Exact finite-dimensional infeasibility of affine equality and inequality constraints.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex: The SQP QP is diagnosed as infeasible if its affine constraint set \(F=\{p:A_Ep=b_E,\ A_Ip\geq b_I\}\) is empty. Equivalently, a normalized Farkas diagnostic is a pair \((y_E,y_I)\) satisfying \(A_E^Ty_E-A_I^Ty_I=0\), \(y_I\geq0\), \(b_E^Ty_E-b_I^Ty_I=-1\). Any pair satisfying the same first two conditions and \(b_E^Ty_E-b_I^Ty_I<0\) is an unnormalized certificate.
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: An SQP QP infeasibility diagnostic certifies that no step satisfies the linearized equality and inequality constraints. The certificate consists of unrestricted equality multipliers and nonnegative inequality multipliers whose weighted constraint normals cancel while their weighted right-hand sides have a strict contradictory sign. Scaling gives the normalized value \(-1\).
knowledge_statements.conclusion_latex: \(F=\varnothing\) if and only if such a Farkas multiplier pair exists.
equivalent_formulations_latex: Introducing nonnegative elastic variables and minimizing their weighted sum yields a strictly positive optimal violation whenever the original affine system is infeasible, under an exact elastic formulation.
special_cases_latex: With equalities only, infeasibility is certified by \(A_E^Ty_E=0\) and \(b_E^Ty_E\neq0\), after choosing the sign and scaling appropriately.
immediate_consequences_latex: Changing \(B_k\) cannot repair this failure because feasibility depends only on the affine constraint system.
boundary_notes: A nearly inconsistent system is not exactly infeasible; numerical classification requires tolerances.
This certificate diagnoses the QP linearization and does not imply that the original nonlinear constraints are globally infeasible.

children.title: SQP QP Unboundedness Diagnostics
children.top_down_role: Diagnostic families for uncontrolled descent in the quadratic model.

knowledge_statements.title: SQP QP Unboundedness Diagnostics
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: A feasible recession direction with negative quadratic curvature, or zero curvature and negative linear slope, certifies that the SQP quadratic subproblem is unbounded below.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex:
Consider the SQP subproblem
\[\inf_d\; q(d):=g^{\mathsf T}d+\tfrac12 d^{\mathsf T}Bd\quad\text{subject to}\quad Ad=b,\; Cd\le r,\]
where \(B=B^{\mathsf T}\). If the subproblem has a feasible point and there is a nonzero vector \(v\) satisfying \(Av=0\), \(Cv\le0\), and either \(v^{\mathsf T}Bv<0\), or \(Bv=0\) and \(g^{\mathsf T}v<0\), then the QP is unbounded below. Thus negative curvature or negative linear slope along a feasible recession direction is a certificate of uncontrolled model descent.
assumptions_latex: \(B=B^{\mathsf T}\) and the QP feasible set is nonempty.
knowledge_statements.conclusion_latex: \(\inf\{q(d):Ad=b,\;Cd\le r\}=-\infty\).
knowledge_statements.scope_note: Recession-direction certificate for an SQP quadratic subproblem with linearized constraints.

source_witnesses.locator: Chapter 10 Quadratic Programming p. 229

knowledge_statements.slot_contract: State the canonical mathematical definition of the source node, with its domain, quantifiers, notation, and a precise source locator.
knowledge_statements.ambient_context_latex: Let \(q(p)=g^Tp+\tfrac12p^TBp\), with \(B=B^T\), be minimized over a nonempty polyhedron \(F=\{p:A_Ep=b_E,\ A_Ip\geq b_I\}\). Its recession cone is \(F^\infty=\{d:A_Ed=0,\ A_Id\geq0\}\).
knowledge_statements.scope_note: Exact unboundedness of a finite-dimensional SQP quadratic subproblem with a nonempty polyhedral feasible set.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex: An SQP QP unboundedness diagnostic is a feasible base point \(p_0\in F\) and a nonzero recession direction \(d\in F^\infty\) such that either \(d^TBd<0\), or \(d^TBd=0\) and \((g+Bp_0)^Td<0\). In either case, \(p_0+td\in F\) for every \(t\geq0\) and \(q(p_0+td)\to-\infty\) as \(t\to\infty\).
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: The diagnostic consists of a feasible QP point and a feasible recession ray. Strictly negative quadratic curvature along the ray makes the model diverge downward quadratically. If the ray has zero quadratic curvature, a strictly negative directional linear term makes it diverge downward linearly.
knowledge_statements.conclusion_latex: The certified ray satisfies \(\inf_{p\in F}q(p)=-\infty\).
equivalent_formulations_latex: For a convex QP with \(B\succeq0\), only the zero-curvature linear-descent alternative can certify unboundedness.
special_cases_latex: For an unconstrained QP, \(F^\infty=\mathbb R^n\).
If \(B=0\), the condition reduces to a linear-programming recession direction with \(g^Td<0\).
immediate_consequences_latex: A trust-region bound makes the safeguarded subproblem bounded even when the unrestricted QP has this certificate.
boundary_notes: A negative-curvature direction that is not in the recession cone does not certify unboundedness.
Solver divergence without an explicit feasible ray is not an exact mathematical certificate.

children.title: SQP QP Singularity Diagnostics
children.top_down_role: Diagnostic families for rank loss and nonunique subproblem solutions.

knowledge_statements.title: SQP QP Singularity Diagnostics
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: A null vector of the active-set KKT matrix diagnoses singularity; its primal or dual component identifies flat feasible curvature or dependent active gradients.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex:
For an active set with constraint matrix \(A\), the equality-constrained SQP QP has KKT matrix
\[K=\begin{pmatrix}B&A^{\mathsf T}\\A&0\end{pmatrix}.\]
A nonzero pair \((v,w)\) satisfying \(Bv+A^{\mathsf T}w=0\) and \(Av=0\) certifies that \(K\) is singular. In particular, a nonzero \(v\in\ker A\) with \(Bv=0\) yields a primal flat direction; if one QP solution exists, addition of suitable multiples of such a feasible null direction can produce nonunique primal solutions. A nonzero \(w\in\ker A^{\mathsf T}\) certifies rank loss in the active gradients and possible nonuniqueness of QP multipliers.
assumptions_latex: \(B=B^{\mathsf T}\).
\(A\) is the Jacobian matrix of the constraints treated as active.
knowledge_statements.conclusion_latex: \(\ker K\ne\{0\}\), so the active-set KKT system is singular and its solution, when consistent, need not be unique.
knowledge_statements.scope_note: Nullspace tests for singularity and nonuniqueness in equality-constrained active-set QP systems.

source_witnesses.locator: 10.3 Active Set Methods p. 236
