knowledge_statements.statement_title: Null-vector diagnostic for an SQP KKT system
knowledge_statements.ambient_context_latex: For a candidate active set, let \(K=\begin{bmatrix}B&A^T\\A&0\end{bmatrix}\) be the symmetric KKT matrix of the equality-form QP. A primal-dual solution satisfies \(K\begin{bmatrix}p\\y\end{bmatrix}=r\).
knowledge_statements.scope_note: Exact algebraic singularity for a finite-dimensional active-set SQP KKT system.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex: An SQP QP singularity diagnostic is a nonzero pair \((u,v)\) satisfying \(Bu+A^Tv=0\) and \(Au=0\), equivalently \(K\begin{bmatrix}u\\v\end{bmatrix}=0\). If \(u\neq0\), the diagnostic exposes a primal tangent null direction and permits nonuniqueness of primal KKT solutions when the affine system is consistent. If \(u=0\) and \(v\neq0\), it exposes dependence among active constraint gradients and nonuniqueness of multipliers.
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: The KKT system is singular exactly when it has a nonzero null vector. A null vector with a nonzero primal part identifies a tangent direction invisible to the KKT curvature equations. A purely dual null vector identifies linear dependence among active constraint normals and hence multiplier ambiguity.
knowledge_statements.conclusion_latex: \(K\) is singular if and only if there exists \((u,v)\neq(0,0)\) with \(Bu+A^Tv=0\) and \(Au=0\).
equivalent_formulations_latex: If \(A\) has full row rank, singularity is equivalent to singularity of the reduced Hessian \(Z^TBZ\).
special_cases_latex: For an unconstrained QP, the diagnostic reduces to a nonzero \(u\) satisfying \(Bu=0\).
immediate_consequences_latex: A consistent singular KKT system has either no unique primal-dual solution or an affine family of solutions.
boundary_notes: A large condition number is not exact singularity, although it may trigger a numerical safeguard.
KKT singularity does not alone distinguish an infeasible right-hand side from a consistent nonunique system.

knowledge_statements.ambient_context_latex: Consider \(\min f(x)\) subject to \(c_i(x)=0\) for \(i\in\mathcal E\) and \(c_i(x)\geq0\) for \(i\in\mathcal I\). At a feasible point \(x\), let \(\mathcal A(x)=\{i\in\mathcal I:c_i(x)=0\}\), and let \(\Lambda(x)\) be the set of KKT multipliers.
knowledge_statements.scope_note: Smooth finite-dimensional nonlinear programming at a feasible point, emphasizing geometry relevant to local SQP models.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex: The point \(x\) lies in a degenerate constraint regime if at least one of the following holds: the gradients \(\{\nabla c_i(x):i\in\mathcal E\cup\mathcal A(x)\}\) are linearly dependent; \(\Lambda(x)\) is empty or is not a singleton; or some KKT multiplier \(\lambda\in\Lambda(x)\) has \(\lambda_i=0\) for an active inequality \(i\in\mathcal A(x)\). These alternatives represent failure of active-gradient independence, multiplier existence or uniqueness, and strict complementarity, respectively.
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: A degenerate constraint regime occurs when active constraint normals lose independence, KKT multipliers fail to exist or are nonunique, or an active inequality has zero multiplier at a KKT point. The definition collects distinct primal and dual irregularities that can destabilize SQP active-set identification, multiplier estimates, and KKT solves.
knowledge_statements.conclusion_latex: Degeneracy is the disjunction of active-gradient dependence, abnormal multiplier-set behavior, or failure of strict complementarity.
equivalent_formulations_latex: Active-gradient dependence is failure of LICQ at \(x\).
For a specified KKT pair \((x,\lambda)\), failure of strict complementarity means \(c_i(x)=0\) and \(\lambda_i=0\) for at least one inequality index \(i\).
special_cases_latex: With equality constraints only, the strict-complementarity alternative is absent.
immediate_consequences_latex: The active-set KKT matrix may be singular when active gradients are dependent, even if the primal point is isolated.
boundary_notes: Failure of LICQ does not necessarily imply failure of weaker qualifications such as MFCQ.
Nonuniqueness of multipliers and weak activity are related but not identical phenomena.

children.title: Constraint-Qualification Failure
children.top_down_role: Irregular feasible geometry affecting SQP steps and multiplier estimates.

knowledge_statements.title: Constraint-Qualification Failure
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: MFCQ fails when equality gradients are dependent or no equality-tangent direction strictly decreases every active inequality, removing standard regularity guarantees for SQP steps and multipliers.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex:
Consider constraints \(h(x)=0\) and \(c(x)\le0\), and let \(I(x)=\{i:c_i(x)=0\}\). The Mangasarian--Fromovitz constraint qualification fails at a feasible point \(x\) precisely when either the rows of \(
abla h(x)\) are linearly dependent, or no direction \(d\) satisfies
\[
abla h(x)d=0,\qquad 
abla c_i(x)^{\mathsf T}d<0\quad(i\in I(x)).\]
At this boundary, linearized feasible directions need not represent the local feasible geometry, KKT multipliers may be absent or unbounded, and the standard SQP step and multiplier estimates lose the regularity guaranteed under MFCQ.
assumptions_latex: \(h:\mathbb R^n\to\mathbb R^m\) and \(c:\mathbb R^n\to\mathbb R^p\) are continuously differentiable.
\(x\) is feasible.
knowledge_statements.conclusion_latex: \(\operatorname{rank}\nabla h(x)<m\) or no MFCQ direction exists; standard MFCQ-based SQP regularity is unavailable.
knowledge_statements.scope_note: Failure of MFCQ as a concrete boundary for regular local SQP analysis.

knowledge_statements.statement_latex:
MFCQ fails at \(x\) if either the equality gradients \(\{
abla c_i(x):i\in\mathcal E\}\) are linearly dependent, or there exists no direction \(d\in\mathbb R^n\) satisfying \(

knowledge_statements.statement_plain: Constraint-qualification failure here means failure of MFCQ. It occurs when equality gradients are dependent or when no direction remains tangent to every equality while moving strictly into the feasible side of every active inequality. This describes irregular local feasible geometry that can invalidate standard SQP multiplier and linearization arguments.
knowledge_statements.conclusion_latex: MFCQ fails exactly under the stated dependence-or-no-direction disjunction.
equivalent_formulations_latex: Under independent equality gradients, MFCQ failure is equivalent to existence of a nonzero abnormal multiplier satisfying the homogeneous first-order stationarity relations with the appropriate inequality signs.
special_cases_latex: With equality constraints only, MFCQ reduces to linear independence of the equality gradients.
With inequalities only, MFCQ requires a direction strictly increasing every active constraint.
immediate_consequences_latex: Failure of MFCQ permits unbounded or nonexistent multiplier sets and may make the SQP linearized geometry unstable.
boundary_notes: This slot uses MFCQ; failure of LICQ alone is a different, stronger notion of qualification failure.
MFCQ failure at one feasible point does not imply global infeasibility of the nonlinear program.

children.title: Nonunique-Multiplier Regimes
children.top_down_role: SQP behavior when local multiplier estimates are not unique.

knowledge_statements.title: Nonunique-Multiplier Regimes
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: A feasible point has nonunique multipliers when its KKT multiplier set contains at least two distinct elements, so SQP multiplier estimates can vary despite an unchanged primal point.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex:
For a feasible point \(x\), define the multiplier set
\[\Lambda(x)=\{(\lambda,\mu):
abla f(x)+
abla h(x)^{\mathsf T}\lambda+
abla c(x)^{\mathsf T}\mu=0,\;\mu\ge0,\;\mu_i c_i(x)=0\}.\]
The point lies in a nonunique-multiplier regime exactly when \(\Lambda(x)\) contains two distinct elements. Equivalently, for some \((\lambda,\mu)\in\Lambda(x)\), there is a nonzero perturbation \((\delta\lambda,\delta\mu)\) preserving stationarity, complementarity, and dual feasibility for a nontrivial interval of perturbation sizes. An SQP primal step may then be well determined while its QP multiplier estimate is not.
assumptions_latex: \(f,h,c\) are continuously differentiable near the feasible point \(x\).
Inequalities use the convention \(c(x)\le0\).
knowledge_statements.scope_note: Local predicate for multiplicity of KKT multipliers at a feasible point.

children.title: Weakly Active Constraints
children.top_down_role: Activity regimes associated with absent strict complementarity and unstable working sets.

knowledge_statements.title: Weakly Active Constraints
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: A constraint is weakly active when it is binding but has zero KKT multiplier; any such constraint violates strict complementarity and may destabilize working-set identification.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex:
Let \(x^*\) be a KKT point for constraints \(c_i(x)\le0\), with inequality multiplier vector \(\mu^*\). An inequality index \(i\) is weakly active relative to \((x^*,\mu^*)\) when
\[c_i(x^*)=0\qquad\text{and}\qquad \mu_i^*=0.\]
The weakly active set is \(I_0(x^*,\mu^*)=\{i:c_i(x^*)=0,\;\mu_i^*=0\}\). Strict complementarity holds exactly when this set is empty. Because a weakly active constraint is geometrically active but exerts no positive multiplier force, small perturbations can move it into or out of an SQP working set.
assumptions_latex: \(x^*\) satisfies the KKT conditions for inequalities \(c_i(x)\le0\).
\(\mu^*\ge0\) is a selected KKT multiplier vector.
knowledge_statements.conclusion_latex: \(i\in I_0(x^*,\mu^*)\) if and only if \(c_i(x^*)=0\) and \(\mu_i^*=0\).
knowledge_statements.scope_note: Active inequalities with zero multiplier at a KKT point.

knowledge_statements.slot_contract: State the canonical mathematical definition of the source node, with its domain, quantifiers, notation, and a precise source locator.
knowledge_statements.ambient_context_latex: At \(x_k\), let \(g_k\) be the objective gradient, \(B_k=B_k^T\) a curvature approximation, and \(c_k+J_kp=0\) the equality-form local constraint model. Let \(e_k\) be an elastic residual and let \(\delta_k,\rho_k>0\).
knowledge_statements.scope_note: A concrete family of smooth finite-dimensional SQP variants responding to rank loss or multiplier instability through elastic feasibility and primal regularization.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex: A degeneracy-responsive SQP family computes \((p_k,e_k)\) from \(\min_{p,e}\ g_k^Tp+\tfrac12p^T(B_k+\delta_kI)p+\rho_k\|e\|_1\) subject to \(c_k+J_kp=e\), with the analogous signed elastic formulation for inequalities. It is degeneracy-responsive when a diagnostic such as \(\sigma_{\min}(J_k)\leq\tau_J\), an excessive multiplier norm, or an incorrect KKT inertia triggers \(\delta_k>0\), permits \(e_k\neq0\), or increases \(\rho_k\); outside the trigger region, the parameters are allowed to return to the ordinary SQP regime \(e_k=0\) and vanishing regularization.
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: This family replaces a potentially inconsistent or singular SQP subproblem by an elastic, regularized quadratic model. Constraint residuals are represented explicitly by \(e_k\) and penalized in the objective, while \(\delta_k\) stabilizes primal curvature. Rank, multiplier, or inertia diagnostics govern when these mechanisms are activated and when ordinary SQP is recovered.
knowledge_statements.conclusion_latex: Each step is a solution of the stated elastic-regularized QP, with safeguard parameters coupled to an explicit degeneracy diagnostic.
equivalent_formulations_latex: Splitting \(e=e^+-e^-\) with \(e^+,e^-\geq0\) converts the \(\ell_1\) elastic term to a standard QP objective \(\rho_k\mathbf1^T(e^++e^-)\).
special_cases_latex: With \(e_k=0\) and \(\delta_k=0\), the subproblem is ordinary equality-constrained SQP.
With \(\delta_k=0\), the family specializes to an elastic-mode feasibility safeguard.
immediate_consequences_latex: The elastic subproblem remains feasible because \(e\) can absorb any equality-model residual.
boundary_notes: This definition specifies a family, not a convergence theorem; parameter-update conditions require separate analysis.
Merely using regularization without a degeneracy-dependent trigger does not satisfy the responsive-family definition.
review_flags: The node denotes a broad method family, and no inspected source supports this exact elastic-regularized instantiation.

Stabilized SQP Methods
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: Stabilized SQP adds a positive dual proximal block to the primal-dual Newton system, then globalizes the resulting step and updates the stabilization parameter.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex:
For \(\min f(x)\) subject to \(h(x)=0\), initialize \((x_0,\lambda_0)\), symmetric matrices \(B_k\), and \(\sigma_k>0\). At iteration \(k\), compute \((d_k,\delta\lambda_k)\) from
\[\begin{pmatrix}B_k&J_k^{\mathsf T}\\J_k&-\sigma_k I\end{pmatrix}\begin{pmatrix}d_k\\\delta\lambda_k\end{pmatrix}=-\begin{pmatrix}\nabla_xL(x_k,\lambda_k)\\h(x_k)\end{pmatrix},\qquad J_k=\nabla h(x_k).\]
Choose an accepted step length \(\alpha_k\in(0,1]\), set \(x_{k+1}=x_k+\alpha_kd_k\) and \(\lambda_{k+1}=\lambda_k+\alpha_k\delta\lambda_k\), and update \(B_k\) and \(\sigma_k\). Stop when primal and stationarity residuals meet prescribed tolerances.
assumptions_latex: \(f\) and \(h\) are twice continuously differentiable.
\(B_k=B_k^{\mathsf T}\) and \(\sigma_k>0\).
knowledge_statements.conclusion_latex: The iteration outputs an approximate primal-dual KKT point when \(\|h(x_k)\|\) and \(\|\nabla_xL(x_k,\lambda_k)\|\) satisfy their tolerances.
knowledge_statements.scope_note: Representative equality-constrained primal-dual SQP stabilization by a dual proximal term.

An authoritative locator for this stabilized SQP variant is required.

knowledge_statements.title: Regularized SQP Methods
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: Regularized SQP shifts the model Hessian until it is uniformly positive definite, adapting the shift according to factorization and step-acceptance diagnostics.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex:
At iterate \(x_k\), form an SQP QP with linearized constraints and replace the symmetric Hessian approximation \(B_k\) by
\[\widehat B_k=B_k+\rho_k I,\qquad \rho_k\ge\max\{0,\varepsilon-\lambda_{\min}(B_k)\},\]
where \(\varepsilon>0\). Compute a QP step \(d_k\) using \(\widehat B_k\), accept a step length or trust-region trial according to the globalization test, and update \(x_{k+1}=x_k+\alpha_kd_k\). Increase \(\rho_k\) after factorization failure, unacceptable negative curvature, or rejected model steps; decrease it after reliable accepted steps. Stop at prescribed feasibility and stationarity tolerances.
assumptions_latex: \(B_k=B_k^{\mathsf T}\).
\(\varepsilon>0\) is a prescribed curvature floor.
knowledge_statements.conclusion_latex: \(\widehat B_k\succeq\varepsilon I\), so the regularized quadratic objective is strongly convex on every linear subspace.
knowledge_statements.scope_note: Primal Hessian regularization for a convexified SQP quadratic subproblem.

enrichment_metadata.review_comment: The Hessian-shift formula and its positive-definiteness conclusion are correct, and algorithm is the right kind. However, the stated triggers for increasing or decreasing the regularization and the resulting complete method are a specific representative policy not supported by the supplied generic SQP locator.

knowledge_statements.title: Degeneracy-Responsive Hybrid SQP
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: A hybrid SQP method monitors Jacobian rank and reduced curvature, activating dual stabilization, primal regularization, or both only when the corresponding degeneracy diagnostic fails.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex: At iteration \(k\), estimate the smallest singular value \(s_k\) of the active constraint Jacobian and the smallest reduced-Hessian eigenvalue \(r_k\). Given thresholds \(\tau_J,	au_B>0\), use the ordinary SQP step if \(s_k\ge\tau_J\) and \(r_k\ge\tau_B\); use dual stabilization when \(s_k<\tau_J\); use primal regularization when \(r_k<\tau_B\); and use both when both tests fail. Globalize the selected step with one common merit, filter, or trust-region acceptance test. After acceptance update the primal-dual iterate; otherwise strengthen stabilization or regularization and resolve. Terminate when feasibility and stationarity residuals meet their tolerances.
assumptions_latex: The active Jacobian and a reduced Hessian approximation are available at each iteration.
\(\tau_J>0\) and \(\tau_B>0\) are fixed diagnostic thresholds.
knowledge_statements.conclusion_latex: The chosen subproblem responds separately to detected rank loss \(s_k<\tau_J\) and deficient reduced curvature \(r_k<\tau_B\).
knowledge_statements.scope_note: Representative diagnostic switch between ordinary, stabilized, and regularized SQP systems.

enrichment_metadata.review_comment: The algorithm kind fits the hybrid-method leaf, but the threshold-based four-way switching architecture is presented without any citation. Its exact diagnostics, switching rule, and common globalization mechanism require an authoritative source.

knowledge_statements.slot_contract: State the canonical mathematical definition of the source node, with its domain, quantifiers, notation, and a precise source locator.
knowledge_statements.statement_title: Accuracy and curvature safeguards for inexact SQP derivatives
knowledge_statements.ambient_context_latex: Let \(\widetilde g_k\), \(\widetilde J_k\), and \(B_k=B_k^T\) be approximate objective-gradient, constraint-Jacobian, and Lagrangian-Hessian data used in an SQP model. Let \(s_k=x_{k+1}-x_k\), \(y_k\) be a computed Lagrangian-gradient difference, and \(\Delta_k>0\) a local step scale.
knowledge_statements.scope_note: Finite-dimensional smooth SQP with inexact derivatives or quasi-Newton curvature information.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex: A derivative-error safeguard is a rule that accepts derivative data for the SQP model only when prescribed accuracy tests \(\|\widetilde g_k-\nabla f(x_k)\|\leq\eta_g\Delta_k\) and \(\|\widetilde J_k-J(x_k)\|\leq\eta_J\Delta_k\) hold, using computable estimators in place of unavailable exact errors, and accepts a quasi-Newton update only when \(s_k^Ty_k\geq\epsilon_c\|s_k\|^2\). Upon failure, it recomputes derivatives at higher accuracy, shrinks \(\Delta_k\), skips the update, or replaces \(y_k\) by a damped vector \(\bar y_k\) satisfying \(s_k^T\bar y_k\geq\epsilon_c\|s_k\|^2\).
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: Derivative-error safeguards require approximate first derivatives to be accurate relative to the current local step scale and require positive, sufficiently separated secant curvature before updating a quasi-Newton matrix. Failed tests trigger more accurate evaluation, a smaller step scale, a skipped update, or damping that restores the curvature inequality.
knowledge_statements.conclusion_latex: Only derivative models satisfying the stated scale-dependent accuracy conditions and only quasi-Newton pairs satisfying the safeguarded curvature condition are used without modification.
equivalent_formulations_latex: A relative error test may replace the absolute bounds when it has the form \(\|E_k\|\leq\eta\max\{\Delta_k,\|\text{model residual}\|\}\).
special_cases_latex: For exact analytic derivatives, the first-derivative error bounds hold with zero left-hand side.
Skipping the update when \(s_k^Ty_k<\epsilon_c\|s_k\|^2\) is the simplest curvature safeguard.
immediate_consequences_latex: A damped BFGS update using a safeguarded pair can preserve positive definiteness when the previous approximation is positive definite.
boundary_notes: The exact-error inequalities are mathematical acceptance conditions; practical estimators require separate specification.
Random derivative noise requires probabilistic accuracy conditions and is outside this deterministic definition.
review_flags: No inspected source locator supports this combined derivative-accuracy and damped-curvature safeguard definition.

children.title: SQP Update Restarts
children.top_down_role: Restart families for unreliable curvature approximations.

knowledge_statements.title: SQP Update Restarts
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: When a quasi-Newton curvature or conditioning test fails, SQP discards the unreliable Hessian approximation and restarts from a bounded positive scalar multiple of the identity.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex:
Maintain a symmetric SQP Hessian approximation \(B_k\). After an accepted step, form \(s_k=x_{k+1}-x_k\) and a Lagrangian-gradient difference \(y_krowncolon=\nabla_xL(x_{k+1},\lambda_{k+1})-\nabla_xL(x_k,\lambda_{k+1})\). Apply the chosen quasi-Newton update only if its curvature and conditioning tests hold. Otherwise restart with
\[B_{k+1}=\gamma_k I,\qquad \gamma_k=\min\{\gamma_{\max},\max\{\gamma_{\min},(s_k^{\mathsf T}y_k)/(s_k^{\mathsf T}s_k)\}\},\]
using a prescribed fallback value if \(s_k^{\mathsf T}y_k\le0\). Re-solve the next SQP subproblem with the restarted model and stop at the usual KKT tolerances.
assumptions_latex: \(0<\gamma_{\min}\le\gamma_{\max}<\infty\).
The accepted step satisfies \(s_k\ne0\).
knowledge_statements.conclusion_latex: After a restart, \(\gamma_{\min}I\preceq B_{k+1}\preceq\gamma_{\max}I\).
knowledge_statements.scope_note: Restart safeguard for unreliable quasi-Newton Lagrangian Hessian approximations.

enrichment_metadata.review_comment: The algorithm kind fits the restart leaf, but statement_latex contains the invalid command \y_krowncolon, and the clipped spectral-scaling restart rule is not supported by the supplied generic SQP locator. A source for this exact restart policy is needed before a mathematical replacement can be certified.

knowledge_statements.slot_contract: State the canonical mathematical definition of the source node, with its domain, quantifiers, notation, and a precise source locator.
knowledge_statements.ambient_context_latex: Consider an SQP iteration for a smooth nonlinear program, with primal-dual iterate \(z_k=(x_k,\lambda_k)\), Lagrangian-Hessian approximation \(B_k\in\mathbb S^n\), step \(s_k=x_{k+1}-x_k\), and curvature displacement \(y_k=\nabla_x\mathcal L(x_{k+1},\lambda_{k+1})-\nabla_x\mathcal L(x_k,\lambda_{k+1})\).
knowledge_statements.scope_note: Finite-dimensional deterministic SQP with a full or reduced quasi-Newton curvature model; the definition concerns a safeguard, not a convergence theorem.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex: An SQP update restart is an iteration index \(k\) at which the ordinary secant update \(B_{k+1}=U(B_k,s_k,y_k)\) is deliberately discarded because a reliability test \(R_k\) fails, and the next curvature model is reinitialized as \[B_{k+1}=B_k^{\mathrm{reset}},\qquad B_k^{\mathrm{reset}}\in\mathbb S^n,\qquad d^TB_k^{\mathrm{reset}}d\ge \gamma_k\|d\|^2\quad\text{for every relevant tangent direction }d,\] with \(\gamma_k>0\). Typical tests include failed or numerically insignificant curvature, such as \(s_k^Ty_k<\eta\|s_k\|\|y_k\|\), excessive conditioning, or repeated model-step rejection. A restart family is specified by the trigger \(R_k\), the reset map \(B_k^{\mathrm{reset}}=\mathcal R(z_k,B_k)\), and whether accumulated update history is wholly or partially erased.
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: An SQP update restart occurs when the method rejects its normal quasi-Newton secant update after a curvature-reliability test fails and replaces the Hessian or reduced-Hessian approximation by a newly initialized symmetric model that has prescribed positive curvature on the relevant tangent space. The restart policy consists of its trigger, reset map, and rule for discarding update history.
knowledge_statements.conclusion_latex: \(\neg R_k\Longrightarrow B_{k+1}=\mathcal R(z_k,B_k)\) instead of \(B_{k+1}=U(B_k,s_k,y_k)\), with \(d^TB_{k+1}d\ge\gamma_k\|d\|^2\) on the designated tangent space.
equivalent_formulations_latex: For a reduced-Hessian method, the same definition applies to \(M_k=Z_k^TB_kZ_k\), with \(M_{k+1}=M_k^{\mathrm{reset}}\succ0\).
special_cases_latex: A scalar reset has \(B_k^{\mathrm{reset}}=\tau_k I\) with \(\tau_k>0\); a derivative-based reset may use a safeguarded finite-difference approximation to \(\nabla_{xx}^2\mathcal L\).
immediate_consequences_latex: The post-restart QP has controlled curvature on feasible directions whenever the reset matrix satisfies the stated lower bound.
boundary_notes: The inspected source discusses quasi-Newton restarts generally, but does not establish this precise safeguard as a canonical SQP-specific definition.
Damping or skipping one update while retaining the previous matrix is not necessarily a restart unless the declared policy classifies it as such.
review_flags: A general quasi-Newton restart is supported by Practical Optimization, §8.3.2.1, but an exact source for the SQP-specific trigger-and-reset definition was not located.
The derivative-error interpretation and tangent-space reset requirement require direct scholarly support.

children.title: Successive Error Restoration
children.top_down_role: Robust SQP architectures that recover from derivative-induced step failures.

knowledge_statements.title: Successive Error Restoration
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: When derivative-based predictions fail, the method rejects the step, refreshes derivatives, shrinks its radius, and uses a least-squares feasibility restoration step before resuming SQP.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex:
Given \(x_k\), derivative approximations, and a radius \(\Delta_k>0\), compute a trial SQP step \(d_k\). Compare actual changes in the objective and constraint residual with their model predictions. If the discrepancy exceeds a prescribed relative tolerance, reject the trial, reduce \(\Delta_k\), and refresh or improve the derivative approximations. If the refreshed SQP subproblem remains inconsistent or repeatedly fails, compute a restoration step
\[d_k^R\in\mathop{\arg\min}_{\|d\|\le\Delta_k}\tfrac12\|h(x_k)+J_kd\|^2+\tfrac12\|[c(x_k)+C_kd]_+\|^2.\]
Resume SQP after sufficient feasibility decrease; terminate only at KKT tolerances or a declared restoration failure.
assumptions_latex: The problem functions can be reevaluated independently of their derivative approximations.
\(\Delta_k>0\), and the restoration subproblem is solved to a specified accuracy.
knowledge_statements.conclusion_latex: An accepted iteration either passes the model-consistency test or achieves the prescribed restoration decrease in constraint violation.
knowledge_statements.scope_note: Derivative-error safeguard alternating model validation, derivative refresh, and feasibility restoration.

enrichment_metadata.review_comment: The algorithm kind is suitable, but neither the term “successive error restoration” nor the specified sequence of model validation, derivative refresh, radius reduction, and least-squares restoration is sourced. An authoritative source is required for this exact architecture.

knowledge_statements.slot_contract: State the canonical mathematical definition of the source node, with its domain, quantifiers, notation, and a precise source locator.
knowledge_statements.statement_title: Successive restoration after unreliable SQP steps
knowledge_statements.ambient_context_latex: Let \(h:\mathbb R^n\to\mathbb R_+\) measure nonlinear constraint violation, for example \(h(x)=\|c_E(x)\|+\|[c_I(x)]_-\|\), and let an SQP globalization mechanism either accept a trial step or declare a step-generation failure.
knowledge_statements.scope_note: Finite-dimensional filter or trust-region SQP. This candidate formalizes the node title as a repeated restoration architecture; the exact phrase is not standard in the inspected source.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex: A successive error-restoration mechanism is a state machine with an optimization state \(O\) and a restoration state \(R\). If the SQP step at \(x_k\) fails a declared reliability test—such as infeasibility of the linearized subproblem, repeated rejection, or a step length below \(\alpha_{\min}\)—the method enters \(R\) and generates restoration iterates \(x_k^{(0)}=x_k,x_k^{(1)},\ldots\) satisfying \[h(x_k^{(j+1)})\le h(x_k^{(j)})-\delta_j,\qquad \delta_j>0,\] until a finite index \(J_k\) meets a restoration-exit test \(h(x_k^{(J_k)})\le\tau_k\) together with the globalization acceptance test. It then sets \(x_{k+1}=x_k^{(J_k)}\), refreshes derivative or model data, and returns to \(O\). “Successive” permits multiple restoration iterations and later re-entry into \(R\).
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: Successive error restoration is a two-state SQP architecture. A failed or unreliable optimization step starts a sequence devoted to decreasing constraint violation. Restoration continues until a specified violation and acceptance test is met, after which the restored point becomes the next optimization iterate and model or derivative data are refreshed. The method may invoke such phases repeatedly.
knowledge_statements.conclusion_latex: \(\text{failure at }x_k\Longrightarrow O\to R\), and exit from \(R\) occurs only at a finite \(J_k\) satisfying \(h(x_k^{(J_k)})\le\tau_k\) and the declared acceptance test.
equivalent_formulations_latex: The restoration phase may be written as approximate solution of \(\min_x h(x)\), subject to any bounds or trust region used by the implementation.
special_cases_latex: For filter SQP, restoration can be invoked after an excessively small line-search step or after rejected trust-region trials render the step subproblem incompatible.
immediate_consequences_latex: During restoration, objective reduction is not required unless it is part of the restoration acceptance rule.
boundary_notes: Ordinary feasibility restoration is source-supported, but the stronger derivative-error semantics and the name “successive error restoration” were not located verbatim.
The definition does not guarantee that a finite restoration-exit index exists.
review_flags: Nocedal and Wright §15.4 supports feasibility restoration after small accepted step lengths, rejected trials, or incompatible subproblems, but not the exact derivative-error taxonomy represented by this node.
A direct source for the named mechanism and its derivative-refresh semantics is required.

top_down_textbook_witnesses.source_query: Sun and Yuan, Optimization Theory and Methods

knowledge_statements.slot_contract: State the canonical mathematical definition of the source node, with its domain, quantifiers, notation, and a precise source locator.
knowledge_statements.ambient_context_latex: For a smooth nonlinear program, let \(z_k=(x_k,\lambda_k)\) be SQP primal-dual iterates and let \(F(z)\) denote the KKT residual map, including stationarity, feasibility, and complementarity residuals as appropriate.
knowledge_statements.scope_note: Finite-dimensional deterministic smooth SQP; this definition organizes global accumulation, local convergence, and rate statements without asserting them for every SQP algorithm.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex: An SQP convergence specification is a tuple \((\mathcal H,\mathcal A,\mathcal L,\mathcal R)\), where \(\mathcal H\) lists problem and algorithm hypotheses, \(\mathcal A\) states the global accumulation conclusion, \(\mathcal L\) gives a neighborhood in which \(z_k\to z_*\), and \(\mathcal R\) states a rate in a fixed norm. Canonical rate predicates are \[\|z_{k+1}-z_*\|\le q\|z_k-z_*\|\quad(0<q<1),\] for Q-linear convergence, \[\frac{\|z_{k+1}-z_*\|}{\|z_k-z_*\|}\to0\] for Q-superlinear convergence, and \[\|z_{k+1}-z_*\|\le C\|z_k-z_*\|^2\] for Q-quadratic convergence. A global statement instead requires every accumulation point, or at least one accumulation point, to satisfy \(F(z_*)=0\), under its stated globalization hypotheses.
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: SQP convergence theory is the collection of precisely scoped statements that connect assumptions on the nonlinear program and algorithm to KKT accumulation, local convergence, and a specified rate. Linear, superlinear, and quadratic rates are defined by explicit error inequalities for the primal-dual sequence; global convergence is expressed through KKT residuals at accumulation points.
knowledge_statements.conclusion_latex: A claim belongs to the specified convergence class only when its hypotheses \(\mathcal H\), limiting object \(z_*\), residual conclusion, neighborhood, and rate predicate are all stated.
equivalent_formulations_latex: When the KKT Jacobian is locally nonsingular, convergence of \(z_k\) and convergence of \(F(z_k)\) have locally comparable error scales, although their Q-rate labels should still identify the measured quantity.
special_cases_latex: Exact-Hessian equality SQP is Newton's method for its KKT equations; quasi-Newton SQP replaces the exact Jacobian block by an approximation.
immediate_consequences_latex: A global KKT accumulation result alone does not imply convergence of the whole sequence or a fast local rate.
boundary_notes: Stochastic, nonsmooth, infinite-dimensional, and derivative-free SQP variants require different residuals and hypotheses.

knowledge_statements.slot_contract: State the canonical mathematical definition of the source node, with its domain, quantifiers, notation, and a precise source locator.
knowledge_statements.statement_title: Local regularity regime for Newton-like SQP
knowledge_statements.ambient_context_latex: Consider \(\min f(x)\) subject to \(c(x)=0\), with \(f:\mathbb R^n\to\mathbb R\), \(c:\mathbb R^n\to\mathbb R^m\), Lagrangian \(\mathcal L(x,\lambda)=f(x)-\lambda^Tc(x)\), and KKT point \(z_*=(x_*,\lambda_*)\).
knowledge_statements.scope_note: Smooth finite-dimensional equality SQP; after stable active-set identification the same definition applies to inequalities using the active constraints.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex:
The point \(z_*\) is in the local regular SQP regime when: \(f\) and \(c\) are twice differentiable near \(x_*\) with locally Lipschitz second derivatives; the active constraint Jacobian \(A_*\) has full row rank; and the Lagrangian Hessian is positive definite on the tangent space, \[d^T
abla_{xx}^2\mathcal L(x_*,\lambda_*)d>0\quad	ext{for every }d
e0	ext{ with }A_*d=0.\] Equivalently, the saddle-point KKT Jacobian \[F'(z_*)= egin{bmatrix}
abla_{xx}^2\mathcal L(x_*,\lambda_*)&-A_*^T\A_*&0\end{bmatrix}\] is nonsingular under these rank and reduced-curvature conditions. A local SQP run is in this regime once all its iterates remain in a neighborhood where the corresponding rank and tangent-curvature bounds persist uniformly.
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: A solution lies in the local regular SQP regime when the data have sufficiently regular second derivatives, the active constraint Jacobian has full row rank, and the Lagrangian Hessian is positive definite along nonzero tangent directions. These conditions make the local KKT linearization nonsingular and remain uniformly valid in a sufficiently small neighborhood.
knowledge_statements.conclusion_latex: \(\operatorname{rank}A_*=m\) and \(d^T\nabla_{xx}^2\mathcal L_*d>0\) for all \(0\ne d\in\ker A_*\), with locally Lipschitz second derivatives.
equivalent_formulations_latex: If \(Z_*\) has columns spanning \(\ker A_*\), tangent-space positivity is equivalent to \(Z_*^T\nabla_{xx}^2\mathcal L_*Z_*\succ0\).
special_cases_latex: For an unconstrained problem, \(A_*\) is absent and the condition reduces to \(\nabla^2f(x_*)\succ0\).
immediate_consequences_latex: The local SQP quadratic subproblem and Newton-KKT system are uniquely solvable near \(z_*\).
boundary_notes: For inequalities without identified activity, critical-cone curvature is the appropriate formulation.
Full row rank excludes redundant active constraints.

knowledge_statements.slot_contract: State the canonical mathematical definition of the source node, with its domain, quantifiers, notation, and a precise source locator.
knowledge_statements.statement_title: Constraint-qualification regime at an SQP limit point
knowledge_statements.ambient_context_latex: Let \(\Omega=\{x:c_i(x)=0\ (i\in E),\ c_i(x)\ge0\ (i\in I)\}\), let \(x\in\Omega\), and let \(A(x)=E\cup\{i\in I:c_i(x)=0\}\).
knowledge_statements.scope_note: Smooth finite-dimensional nonlinear programming; the regime determines whether the linearized constraints used by SQP correctly represent local feasible geometry.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex:
An SQP constraint-qualification regime at \(x\) is a declared condition \(Q(x)\) on the active gradients for which the linearized cone \[\mathcal F(x)=\{d:
abla c_i(x)^Td=0\ (i\in E),\ 
abla c_i(x)^Td\ge0\ (i\in A(x)\cap I)\}\] has the local geometric and multiplier properties required by the associated SQP analysis. The classical LICQ regime requires linear independence of all active gradients. The MFCQ regime requires linear independence of the equality gradients and existence of \(w\) satisfying \(
abla c_i(x)^Tw=0\) for \(i\in E\) and \(
abla c_i(x)^Tw>0\) for \(i\in A(x)\cap I\). The selected qualification must be stated explicitly because it controls multiplier uniqueness or boundedness and the validity of tangent-space linearization.
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: An SQP constraint-qualification regime specifies a condition on active constraint gradients ensuring that the linearized feasible cone used in the SQP subproblem adequately represents local feasible geometry. LICQ requires independence of every active gradient; MFCQ requires independent equality gradients and a direction that preserves equalities while moving strictly into all active inequalities.
knowledge_statements.conclusion_latex: The regime is identified by an explicit predicate \(Q(x)\), such as LICQ or MFCQ, together with the corresponding linearized cone \(\mathcal F(x)\).
equivalent_formulations_latex: Under LICQ, the active-gradient matrix has full row rank.

knowledge_statements.title: LICQ SQP Regime
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: The LICQ SQP regime occurs when equality and active-inequality gradients are linearly independent, implying uniqueness of any KKT multiplier vector at the point.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex:
For constraints \(h(x)=0\) and \(c(x)\le0\), let \(I(x)=\{i:c_i(x)=0\}\). The linear independence constraint qualification holds at a feasible point \(x\) when
\[\operatorname{rank}\begin{pmatrix}\nabla h(x)\\ \nabla c_{I(x)}(x)^{\mathsf T}\end{pmatrix}=m+|I(x)|.\]
Equivalently, the equality-constraint gradients together with all active inequality gradients are linearly independent. In this SQP regime, any KKT multiplier vector at \(x\), if it exists, is unique; nearby active-set KKT systems retain full constraint rank under sufficiently small perturbations that preserve the active set.
assumptions_latex: \(h:\mathbb R^n\to\mathbb R^m\) and \(c:\mathbb R^n\to\mathbb R^p\) are continuously differentiable.
\(x\) is feasible.
knowledge_statements.conclusion_latex: \(\operatorname{rank}\begin{pmatrix}\nabla h(x)\\ \nabla c_{I(x)}(x)^{\mathsf T}\end{pmatrix}=m+|I(x)|\), and any KKT multiplier vector at \(x\) is unique when it exists.
knowledge_statements.scope_note: Classical local SQP regime defined by independent active constraint gradients.

knowledge_statements.ambient_context_latex: For the smooth nonlinear program \(c_i(x)=0\) for \(i\in E\) and \(c_i(x)\ge0\) for \(i\in I\), define \(A(x)=E\cup\{i\in I:c_i(x)=0\}\).
knowledge_statements.scope_note: Finite-dimensional smooth SQP at a feasible point or candidate limit point.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex: The linear independence constraint qualification holds at \(x\) precisely when \[\sum_{i\in A(x)}\alpha_i\nabla c_i(x)=0\quad\Longrightarrow\quad \alpha_i=0\ \text{for every }i\in A(x).\] Equivalently, the matrix whose rows are \(\nabla c_i(x)^T\), \(i\in A(x)\), has full row rank. An SQP sequence is in a uniform local LICQ regime near \(x_*\) when there are a neighborhood \(U\) and \(\sigma>0\) such that the smallest singular value of the relevant active Jacobian is at least \(\sigma\) at every iterate in \(U\) for which that active set is used.
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: LICQ holds when the gradients of the equality constraints and active inequalities are linearly independent. In a uniform local LICQ regime, the active Jacobians used by nearby SQP subproblems retain a singular-value bound away from zero.
knowledge_statements.conclusion_latex: \(\operatorname{rank}[\nabla c_i(x)^T]_{i\in A(x)}=|A(x)|\).
equivalent_formulations_latex: No nonzero vector of coefficients gives a zero linear combination of the active gradients.
special_cases_latex: For equality-only SQP, LICQ is \(\operatorname{rank}A(x)=m\).
immediate_consequences_latex: At a KKT point satisfying LICQ, the multiplier vector is unique.
The KKT tangent cone equals the linearized feasible cone under the regularity described in the source.
boundary_notes: LICQ can fail solely because of redundant active constraints even when weaker qualifications hold.
LICQ does not imply strict complementarity or second-order sufficiency.

knowledge_statements.title: Weaker Constraint-Qualification SQP Regimes
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: MFCQ requires full-rank equality gradients and an equality-tangent direction strictly decreasing all active inequalities; it is weaker than LICQ and permits nonunique but bounded multiplier sets.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex:
For constraints \(h(x)=0\) and \(c(x)\le0\), MFCQ holds at a feasible point \(x\) when \(\nabla h(x)\) has full row rank and there exists \(d\in\mathbb R^n\) such that
\[\nabla h(x)d=0,
\qquad \nabla c_i(x)^{\mathsf T}d<0\quad\text{for every }i\in I(x).\]
LICQ implies MFCQ, but the converse can fail because active inequality gradients may be dependent. Under MFCQ, the linearized constraints admit a strict feasible direction and the KKT multiplier set, when nonempty, is bounded, although multipliers need not be unique; SQP analysis must therefore accommodate multiplier-set behavior.
assumptions_latex: \(h:\mathbb R^n\to\mathbb R^m\) and \(c:\mathbb R^n\to\mathbb R^p\) are continuously differentiable.
\(x\) is feasible.
knowledge_statements.conclusion_latex: MFCQ holds at \(x\); the linearized cone has a strict inequality-feasible direction, and any nonempty KKT multiplier set is bounded.
knowledge_statements.scope_note: MFCQ as the canonical local SQP regime weaker than LICQ.

knowledge_statements.statement_title: MFCQ as a weaker SQP regularity regime
knowledge_statements.ambient_context_latex: Let \(x\) be feasible for smooth equalities \(c_i(x)=0\), \(i\in E\), and inequalities \(c_i(x)\ge0\), \(i\in I\), with active set \(A(x)\).
knowledge_statements.scope_note: Finite-dimensional smooth nonlinear programming; MFCQ is used as the canonical representative of qualifications strictly weaker than LICQ.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex:
The Mangasarian–Fromovitz constraint qualification holds at \(x\) when the equality gradients \(\{
abla c_i(x):i\in E\}\) are linearly independent and there exists \(w\in\mathbb R^n\) such that \[
abla c_i(x)^Tw=0\quad(i\in E),\qquad 
abla c_i(x)^Tw>0\quad(i\in A(x)\cap I).\] The weaker-CQ SQP regime consists of local analyses that assume MFCQ, or another explicitly identified qualification not implying full independence of all active gradients, and therefore do not rely on uniqueness of the multiplier. For MFCQ, the KKT multiplier set at a local solution is nonempty under the usual first-order assumptions and is bounded, but it may contain more than one multiplier.
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: MFCQ holds when equality gradients are independent and one direction is tangent to every equality while pointing strictly into every active inequality. It is weaker than LICQ because active inequality gradients may be dependent. SQP analysis in this regime must accommodate a bounded but potentially nonunique multiplier set.
knowledge_statements.conclusion_latex: \(\operatorname{rank}[\nabla c_i(x)^T]_{i\in E}=|E|\) and \(\exists w\) satisfying the displayed strict linearized inequalities.
equivalent_formulations_latex: At a local solution in the stated smooth setting, MFCQ is equivalent to boundedness of the KKT multiplier set.
special_cases_latex: If \(E=\varnothing\), MFCQ requires a direction strictly increasing every active inequality to first order.
immediate_consequences_latex: LICQ implies MFCQ.
MFCQ permits linearly dependent active inequality gradients and hence nonunique multipliers.
boundary_notes: The source does not establish that every classical fast local SQP theorem remains valid under MFCQ alone.
Other weaker qualifications must be named and stated separately rather than silently identified with MFCQ.

knowledge_statements.slot_contract: State the canonical mathematical definition of the source node, with its domain, quantifiers, notation, and a precise source locator.
knowledge_statements.statement_title: Second-order sufficient condition used in SQP
knowledge_statements.ambient_context_latex: Let \(x_*\) be feasible for a twice continuously differentiable nonlinear program, let \(\lambda_*\) satisfy its KKT conditions, let \(\mathcal L\) be the Lagrangian, and let \(\mathcal C(x_*,\lambda_*)\) be the critical cone.
knowledge_statements.scope_note: Finite-dimensional smooth nonlinear programming with equality and inequality constraints.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex:
The SQP second-order sufficient condition holds at \((x_*,\lambda_*)\) when \[d^T
abla_{xx}^2\mathcal L(x_*,\lambda_*)d>0\qquad	ext{for every }0
e d\in\mathcal C(x_*,\lambda_*).\] Because the unit slice of the critical cone is compact, this is equivalently the existence of \(\sigma>0\) such that \[d^T
abla_{xx}^2\mathcal L(x_*,\lambda_*)d\ge\sigma\|d\|^2\qquad(d\in\mathcal C(x_*,\lambda_*)).\] The condition is attached to a particular KKT multiplier whenever multipliers are nonunique. It supplies the positive critical-direction curvature used in local SQP subproblem and stability analysis.
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: The SQP second-order sufficient condition requires the Hessian of the Lagrangian to have strictly positive curvature along every nonzero critical direction. Equivalently, its quadratic form has a positive uniform lower bound on the critical cone. With nonunique multipliers, the condition must identify the multiplier used to form the Lagrangian and critical cone.
knowledge_statements.conclusion_latex: \(d^T\nabla_{xx}^2\mathcal L(x_*,\lambda_*)d>0\) for all \(0\ne d\in\mathcal C(x_*,\lambda_*)\).
equivalent_formulations_latex: \(\exists\sigma>0\) such that \(d^T\nabla_{xx}^2\mathcal L_*d\ge\sigma\|d\|^2\) on the critical cone.
special_cases_latex: Under LICQ and strict complementarity, the critical cone is the null space of the active Jacobian, so the condition is positive definiteness of the reduced Hessian.
immediate_consequences_latex: Together with the KKT conditions, the condition makes \(x_*\) a strict local solution.
It yields quadratic local growth in the source's finite-dimensional smooth setting.
boundary_notes: Positive definiteness on all of \(\mathbb R^n\) is stronger than required.
Second-order necessity uses nonnegative rather than strictly positive curvature.

knowledge_statements.statement_title: Active-Set Agreement for a Nearby SQP Subproblem
knowledge_statements.scope_note: Applies to the inequality-constrained nonlinear program (18.10) and its local SQP subproblem (18.11); the equation numbers are source-local identifiers.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex: Suppose that x^* is a local solution of (18.10), that the KKT conditions hold at (x^*,\lambda^*), and that LICQ, strict complementarity, and the second-order sufficient conditions hold at (x^*,\lambda^*). Then there exists a neighborhood U of (x^*,\lambda^*) such that, for every (x_k,\lambda_k)\in U, the SQP subproblem (18.11) has a local solution whose active set \mathcal A_k satisfies \mathcal A_k=\mathcal A(x^*).
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: Let x* be a local solution of the nonlinear program with KKT multiplier lambda*. If LICQ, strict complementarity, and the second-order sufficient conditions hold at this primal-dual point, then every sufficiently nearby SQP iterate-multiplier pair has an associated local solution of the SQP subproblem whose active set is exactly the active set of the nonlinear program at x*.

(x^*,\lambda^*)\text{ satisfies the KKT conditions}

\text{the second-order sufficient conditions hold at }(x^*,\lambda^*)
(x_k,\lambda_k)\text{ is sufficiently close to }(x^*,\lambda^*)
knowledge_statements.conclusion_latex: \exists\text{ a local solution of (18.11) such that }\mathcal A_k=\mathcal A(x^*).

knowledge_statements.title: Critical-Cone Curvature Regime
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: The Lagrangian Hessian is positive definite on all nonzero first-order feasible directions that are critical for the objective at the selected KKT multiplier.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex:
Let \(f:\mathbb{R}^n	o\mathbb{R}\), \(h:\mathbb{R}^n	o\mathbb{R}^m\), and \(g:\mathbb{R}^n	o\mathbb{R}^p\), and consider minimizing \(f(x)\) subject to \(h(x)=0\) and \(g(x)\le 0\). Define \(L(x,\lambda,\mu)=f(x)+\lambda^	op h(x)+\mu^	op g(x)\). At a KKT point \((x^*,\lambda^*,\mu^*)\), let \(I_+=\{i:g_i(x^*)=0,\ \mu_i^*>0\}\), \(I_0=\{i:g_i(x^*)=0,\ \mu_i^*=0\}\), and
\[C=\{d\in\mathbb{R}^n:
abla h(x^*)d=0,\ 
abla g_i(x^*)^	op d=0\ (i\in I_+),\ 
abla g_i(x^*)^	op d\le0\ (i\in I_0),\ 
abla f(x^*)^	op d=0\}.\]
The critical-cone curvature condition is
\[d^	op
abla_{xx}^2L(x^*,\lambda^*,\mu^*)d>0\quad	ext{for every }d\in C\setminus\{0\}.\]
assumptions_latex: \(f\), \(h\), and \(g\) are twice continuously differentiable near \(x^*\).
\((x^*,\lambda^*,\mu^*)\) satisfies the KKT conditions and \(\mu^*\ge0\).
knowledge_statements.conclusion_latex: \(d^\top\nabla_{xx}^2L(x^*,\lambda^*,\mu^*)d>0\) for every \(d\in C\setminus\{0\}\).
knowledge_statements.scope_note: Second-order sufficient condition for a finite-dimensional smooth NLP at a KKT point with active inequalities.

knowledge_statements.title: Tangent-Space Curvature Regime
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: The reduced Lagrangian Hessian is positive definite on the tangent space of the equality constraints or permanently identified active constraints, independently of the tangent-space basis.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex:
Let \(f:\mathbb{R}^n\to\mathbb{R}\) and \(c:\mathbb{R}^n\to\mathbb{R}^m\), where \(c(x)=0\) collects the equality constraints and any inequalities treated as permanently active. Define \(L(x,y)=f(x)+y^\top c(x)\), and let \((x^*,y^*)\) be a KKT point. If \(A=\nabla c(x^*)\in\mathbb{R}^{m\times n}\) has full row rank and the columns of \(Z\in\mathbb{R}^{n\times(n-m)}\) form a basis of \(\ker A\), the tangent-space curvature condition is
\[Z^\top\nabla_{xx}^2L(x^*,y^*)Z\succ0.\]
Equivalently,
\[d^\top\nabla_{xx}^2L(x^*,y^*)d>0\quad\text{for every }d\in\ker A\setminus\{0\}.\]
This condition is independent of the chosen basis \(Z\).
assumptions_latex: \(f\) and \(c\) are twice continuously differentiable near \(x^*\).
\((x^*,y^*)\) is a KKT point and \(\nabla c(x^*)\) has full row rank.
knowledge_statements.conclusion_latex: \(Z^\top\nabla_{xx}^2L(x^*,y^*)Z\succ0\), equivalently \(d^\top\nabla_{xx}^2L(x^*,y^*)d>0\) for every \(d\in\ker A\setminus\{0\}\).
knowledge_statements.scope_note: Reduced-Hessian sufficient condition for finite-dimensional equality-constrained or fixed-active-set SQP.

notation.meaning: Jacobian of the locally active constraints at the solution
basis matrix for the tangent space \(\ker A\)
Lagrangian of the locally equality-constrained problem

knowledge_statements.statement_latex:

abla_{xx}^2\mathcal L(x_*,\lambda_*)Z_*\] is positive definite. Equivalently, \[d^T

e d\in\ker A_*.\] A uniform regime has a constant \(\gamma>0\) satisfying \(u^TH_{\mathrm{red}}u\ge\gamma\|u\|^2\) for all \(u\), after choosing an orthonormal null-space basis. The property is invariant under replacement of \(Z_*\) by another basis of the same null space.
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: Tangent-space curvature means that the Hessian of the Lagrangian is positive definite on directions satisfying the linearized active constraints. It is equivalently positive definiteness of the reduced Hessian formed with any basis of the active Jacobian's null space.

With no constraints, \(Z_*=I\) and the reduced Hessian is the ordinary Hessian.
immediate_consequences_latex: Together with full row rank of \(A_*\), the KKT saddle-point matrix is nonsingular.

children.title: SQP Activity-Multiplier Stability Regimes
children.top_down_role: Local activity and multiplier regimes affecting identification and convergence rates.

knowledge_statements.slot_contract: State the canonical mathematical definition of the source node, with its domain, quantifiers, notation, and a precise source locator.
knowledge_statements.ambient_context_latex: Let \((x_*,\lambda_*)\) satisfy the KKT conditions for inequalities \(c_i(x)\ge0\), and let \(\Lambda(x_*)\) be the set of all KKT multipliers.
knowledge_statements.scope_note: Local finite-dimensional inequality-constrained SQP.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex: Define \[A_+=\{i\in A(x_*):\exists\lambda\in\Lambda(x_*)\text{ with }\lambda_i>0\},\qquad A_0=\{i\in A(x_*):\lambda_i=0\text{ for every }\lambda\in\Lambda(x_*)\}.\] An SQP activity-multiplier regime is the triple \((A_+,A_0,\Lambda(x_*))\) together with declared stability properties of these objects under nearby SQP subproblems. It is strictly complementary when \(A_0=\varnothing\); weakly active when \(A_0\ne\varnothing\); multiplier-unique when \(\Lambda(x_*)\) is a singleton; and multiplier-bounded when \(\sup_{\lambda\in\Lambda(x_*)}\|\lambda\|<\infty\). These attributes are logically distinct and must not be conflated.
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: The activity-multiplier regime records which active inequalities can have positive multipliers, which are weakly active with zero multiplier for every KKT multiplier, and whether the multiplier set is unique or merely bounded. Strict complementarity, weak activity, and multiplier uniqueness are separate properties.
knowledge_statements.conclusion_latex: The local regime is classified by \((A_+,A_0,\Lambda(x_*))\) and the stated uniqueness, boundedness, or complementarity properties.
equivalent_formulations_latex: Under LICQ, \(\Lambda(x_*)=\{\lambda_*\}\), so \(A_+=\{i\in A(x_*):\lambda_{*,i}>0\}\) and \(A_0=\{i\in A(x_*):\lambda_{*,i}=0\}\).
special_cases_latex: LICQ plus strict complementarity gives a unique multiplier and \(A_+=A(x_*)\).
immediate_consequences_latex: Weakly active constraints may be difficult for an active-set method to identify stably.
A positive active multiplier gives first-order sensitivity of the optimal value to displacement of that constraint.
boundary_notes: An active constraint may be strongly active for some multiplier without every multiplier assigning it a positive component when multipliers are nonunique.

notation.meaning: strongly and weakly active index sets

children.title: Strict-Complementarity SQP Regime
children.top_down_role: The classical stable-activity regime for inequality-constrained SQP.

knowledge_statements.title: Strict-Complementarity SQP Regime
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: Strict complementarity means that every active inequality has a positive multiplier. Along convergent primal-dual iterates this separates positive active multipliers from strictly inactive constraints, but it does not alone prove finite active-set identification by an SQP algorithm.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex:
Let \(f:\mathbb{R}^n\to\mathbb{R}\), \(h:\mathbb{R}^n\to\mathbb{R}^m\), and \(g:\mathbb{R}^n\to\mathbb{R}^p\), and consider minimizing \(f(x)\) subject to \(h(x)=0\) and \(g(x)\le0\). A KKT point \((x^*,\lambda^*,\mu^*)\) satisfies strict complementarity when
\[g_i(x^*)=0\quad\Longrightarrow\quad\mu_i^*>0\qquad(i=1,\ldots,p).\]
Complementarity also gives \(g_i(x^*)<0\Rightarrow\mu_i^*=0\). Consequently, for any primal-dual sequence \((x_k,\lambda_k,\mu_k)\to(x^*,\lambda^*,\mu^*)\), every active index has \(\mu_{k,i}>0\) eventually, and every inactive index has \(g_i(x_k)<0\) eventually. Finite identification by a particular SQP method requires additional algorithmic assumptions.
assumptions_latex: \((x^*,\lambda^*,\mu^*)\) satisfies the KKT conditions for the stated nonlinear program.
The active inequality gradients together with the equality gradients are linearly independent.
knowledge_statements.conclusion_latex: \(g_i(x^*)=0\Rightarrow\mu_i^*>0\), with eventual sign separation along every primal-dual sequence converging to \((x^*,\lambda^*,\mu^*)\).
knowledge_statements.scope_note: Classical local inequality regime in which every active constraint has a positive KKT multiplier.

knowledge_statements.slot_contract: State the canonical mathematical definition of the source node, with its domain, quantifiers, notation, and a precise source locator.
knowledge_statements.ambient_context_latex: Let \((x_*,\lambda_*)\) satisfy the KKT conditions for \(c_i(x)\ge0\), \(i\in I\), using multipliers \(\lambda_{*,i}\ge0\).
knowledge_statements.scope_note: Smooth finite-dimensional inequality-constrained SQP at a KKT pair.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex: Strict complementarity holds at \((x_*,\lambda_*)\) when, for every inequality index \(i\in I\), exactly one of \(c_i(x_*)\) and \(\lambda_{*,i}\) is zero. Equivalently, \[i\in A(x_*)\cap I\Longrightarrow\lambda_{*,i}>0,\qquad i\notin A(x_*)\Longrightarrow c_i(x_*)>0\text{ and }\lambda_{*,i}=0.\] A uniform strict-complementarity SQP regime additionally has a margin \(\delta>0\) such that \(\lambda_{*,i}\ge\delta\) on active inequalities and \(c_i(x_*)\ge\delta\) on inactive inequalities, after fixing the problem's scaling.
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: Strict complementarity means that every active inequality has a positive multiplier and every inactive inequality has positive slack and zero multiplier. A uniform regime separates positive multipliers and inactive slacks from zero by a fixed margin.
knowledge_statements.conclusion_latex: \(\lambda_{*,i}>0\) for every \(i\in A(x_*)\cap I\).
equivalent_formulations_latex: There is no inequality index satisfying both \(c_i(x_*)=0\) and \(\lambda_{*,i}=0\).
special_cases_latex: For equality-only SQP, strict complementarity imposes no condition.

With a unique multiplier, the critical cone reduces to the null space of the active Jacobian.

knowledge_statements.title: Weak-Activity SQP Regime
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: A weakly active inequality is active with zero multiplier. Complementarity alone cannot separate it from inactivity, so strict-complementarity-based arguments cannot guarantee identification of the complete active set, although fast convergence may still occur.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex:
Let \(f:\mathbb{R}^n\to\mathbb{R}\), \(h:\mathbb{R}^n\to\mathbb{R}^m\), and \(g:\mathbb{R}^n\to\mathbb{R}^p\), and let \((x^*,\lambda^*,\mu^*)\) be a KKT point for minimizing \(f(x)\) subject to \(h(x)=0\) and \(g(x)\le0\). Define
\[I_0=\{i\in\{1,\ldots,p\}:g_i(x^*)=0,\ \mu_i^*=0\}.\]
The weak-activity regime occurs when \(I_0\ne\varnothing\). For \(i\in I_0\), complementarity alone does not separate the active state \(g_i=0\) from an inactive state \(g_i<0\), because both can occur with \(\mu_i=0\). Therefore strict-complementarity arguments cannot establish finite identification of the complete active set. This boundary alone does not rule out fast local convergence under other assumptions.
assumptions_latex: \((x^*,\lambda^*,\mu^*)\) satisfies the KKT conditions and \(\mu^*\ge0\).
At least one active inequality has zero multiplier.
knowledge_statements.conclusion_latex: \(I_0\ne\varnothing\), so strict-complementarity-based finite identification of the complete active set is not available.
knowledge_statements.scope_note: Local inequality regime in which at least one active constraint has a zero KKT multiplier.

source_witnesses.locator: 3.4.1 Active set of constraints p. 91

knowledge_statements.slot_contract: State the canonical mathematical definition of the source node, with its domain, quantifiers, notation, and a precise source locator.
knowledge_statements.ambient_context_latex: Let \(x_*\) solve a smooth inequality-constrained nonlinear program and let \(\Lambda(x_*)\) be its KKT multiplier set.
knowledge_statements.scope_note: Local inequality-SQP behavior without strict complementarity.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex: An active inequality \(i\in A(x_*)\cap I\) is weakly active when \[\lambda_i=0\qquad\text{for every }\lambda\in\Lambda(x_*).\] The weak-activity SQP regime holds when the set \[A_0(x_*)=\{i\in A(x_*)\cap I:\lambda_i=0\ \text{for every }\lambda\in\Lambda(x_*)\}\] is nonempty. Under a unique multiplier this reduces to the existence of an active index with \(\lambda_{*,i}=0\), exactly the failure of strict complementarity. Such an index enters the critical cone through the one-sided condition \(\nabla c_i(x_*)^Td\ge0\), rather than the equality imposed for a positive-multiplier active constraint.
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: A constraint is weakly active when it is active at the solution but receives zero multiplier from every KKT multiplier vector. The weak-activity regime occurs when at least one such constraint exists. With a unique multiplier, this is precisely failure of strict complementarity at an active inequality.
knowledge_statements.conclusion_latex: \(A_0(x_*)\ne\varnothing\).
equivalent_formulations_latex: If the KKT multiplier is unique, weak activity means \(c_i(x_*)=0\) and \(\lambda_{*,i}=0\) for some inequality \(i\).
special_cases_latex: A problem can satisfy LICQ and second-order sufficiency while still having weakly active constraints.
immediate_consequences_latex: An SQP active-set estimate may move repeatedly on and off a weakly active constraint.
The critical cone generally remains a cone rather than collapsing to the active-constraint tangent subspace.
boundary_notes: A constraint that has zero multiplier for one KKT multiplier but positive multiplier for another is strongly active under the source's definition, not weakly active.
Weak activity is not the same as linear dependence of active gradients.

knowledge_statements.title: Stable Multiplier Regimes
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: Small KKT perturbations produce a unique nearby primal-dual solution whose multipliers vary at most Lipschitz-continuously with the perturbation.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex:
Write the KKT system near a reference solution as the generalized equation
\[0\in F(z,p)+N_K(z),\]
where \(z=(x,\lambda,\mu)\), \(p\) is a perturbation, and \(K\) encodes multiplier sign restrictions. A stable multiplier regime holds when there exist neighborhoods \(U\) of \(z^*\) and \(V\) of \(0\), and a constant \(\kappa>0\), such that every \(p\in V\) has a unique solution \(z(p)\in U\) and
\[\|z(p)-z(q)\|\le\kappa\|p-q\|\quad(p,q\in V).\]
This strong local regularity makes the nearby multiplier selection unique and Lipschitz continuous.
assumptions_latex: The perturbed KKT system admits a generalized-equation formulation near \((z^*,0)\).
The generalized equation is strongly regular at \((z^*,0)\).
knowledge_statements.conclusion_latex: \(z(p)\) is locally single-valued and \(\|z(p)-z(q)\|\le\kappa\|p-q\|\).
knowledge_statements.scope_note: Local stability expressed through a single-valued Lipschitz primal-dual solution mapping.

notation.meaning: local perturbation of the KKT system
normal-cone mapping encoding sign or complementarity structure

enrichment_metadata.review_comment: The property kind is plausible, but the record equates the leaf with strong regularity of a particular generalized-equation representation without defining the perturbation model or cone precisely. An authoritative source with a theorem or definition locator is required before selecting this exact stability notion.

knowledge_statements.title: Nonunique-Multiplier Stability Boundaries
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: Multiple KKT multipliers rule out stability of the entire primal-dual solution as a single-valued mapping, though the primal point or a branch may remain stable.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex:
Let \(x^*\) be a KKT point and let
\[\Lambda(x^*)=\{(\lambda,\mu):\nabla_xL(x^*,\lambda,\mu)=0,\ h(x^*)=0,\ 0\le\mu\perp-g(x^*)\ge0\}.\]
If \(\Lambda(x^*)\) contains distinct multipliers, then no neighborhood of the unperturbed KKT data can possess a single-valued primal-dual solution mapping whose value at zero includes every nearby KKT triple. Indeed, the same primal point and zero perturbation already correspond to at least two multiplier vectors. Primal stability may nevertheless remain possible, and a chosen multiplier branch may be stable under additional structure.
assumptions_latex: \(x^*\) is feasible and satisfies the KKT conditions.
There exist \((\lambda^1,\mu^1)\ne(\lambda^2,\mu^2)\) in \(\Lambda(x^*)\).
knowledge_statements.conclusion_latex: The full local primal-dual KKT solution mapping cannot be single-valued at zero perturbation.
knowledge_statements.scope_note: Boundary at which multiplier uniqueness and single-valued primal-dual stability fail.

notation.meaning: set of KKT multiplier pairs associated with \(x^*\)

enrichment_metadata.review_comment: The elementary obstruction to a single-valued full primal-dual mapping is plausible and the failure-boundary kind fits. However, the scope of the mapping, the perturbation parameterization, and the branchwise-stability qualification require an authoritative theorem or definition locator.

children.title: SQP Local Rate Families
children.top_down_role: Rate classifications for exact-curvature, quasi-Newton, and inexact SQP methods.

knowledge_statements.slot_contract: State the canonical mathematical definition of the source node, with its domain, quantifiers, notation, and a precise source locator.
knowledge_statements.ambient_context_latex: Let \(z_k=(x_k,\lambda_k)\to z_*\) be a local SQP sequence and define \(e_k=\|z_k-z_*\|\) in a fixed norm.
knowledge_statements.scope_note: Finite-dimensional deterministic local SQP, distinguishing exact-Hessian, quasi-Newton, and degraded or inexact regimes.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex: The local Q-rate family of \(\{z_k\}\) is defined by its error recursion. It is Q-linear if \(e_{k+1}\le q e_k\) eventually for some \(q\in(0,1)\); Q-superlinear if \(e_{k+1}/e_k\to0\); and Q-quadratic if \(e_{k+1}\le C e_k^2\) eventually for some \(C>0\). It is stagnant relative to this error measure if \(e_k\not\to0\), or if a nonzero limiting error floor persists. In regular local SQP, exact Lagrangian curvature corresponds to the Newton or quadratic family; quasi-Newton models satisfying the projected Dennis–Moré condition correspond to the superlinear family; and fixed relative model or subproblem errors generally belong to a linear or possibly stagnant family unless their forcing terms vanish.
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: SQP local rates are classified through explicit recursions for the primal-dual error. Linear convergence contracts by a fixed factor, superlinear convergence has an error ratio tending to zero, and quadratic convergence bounds the next error by a constant times the squared current error. Exact Hessians, asymptotically accurate quasi-Newton models, and persistent inaccuracies occupy different rate families.
knowledge_statements.conclusion_latex: The rate label is determined by the corresponding quantified predicate for \(e_k=\|z_k-z_*\|\).
equivalent_formulations_latex: For superlinear convergence, \(e_{k+1}=o(e_k)\); for quadratic convergence, \(e_{k+1}=O(e_k^2)\).
special_cases_latex: For equality SQP with exact curvature under Assumptions 18.2, the primal-dual sequence is locally Q-quadratic.
BFGS SQP under the source's local hypotheses is Q-superlinear in the primal iterates.
immediate_consequences_latex: Q-quadratic convergence implies Q-superlinear convergence when \(e_k\to0\).
A convergence-rate assertion must specify whether it measures primal, dual, primal-dual, step, or residual error.
boundary_notes: R-linear and R-superlinear rates are different classifications and are not silently identified with the Q-rates above.
Finite termination is stronger than any asymptotic Q-rate.

children.title: SQP Local Quadratic Convergence
children.top_down_role: The exact-curvature Newton rate family for regular local solutions.

knowledge_statements.slot_contract: State the canonical mathematical definition of the source node, with its domain, quantifiers, notation, and a precise source locator.
knowledge_statements.ambient_context_latex: Let \(z_k=(x_k,\lambda_k)\) be the primal-dual iterates of an SQP method and let \(z_*=(x_*,\lambda_*)\) be a regular KKT pair.
knowledge_statements.scope_note: Local exact-curvature Newton-SQP; this slot defines the rate property rather than asserting that every SQP implementation has it.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex: The SQP sequence converges locally Q-quadratically to \(z_*\) if there exist a neighborhood \(U\) of \(z_*\), constants \(C>0\) and \(\varepsilon>0\), and an index \(K\) such that every run initialized with \(z_0\in U\) is well defined, remains in \(U\), converges to \(z_*\), and satisfies \[\|z_{k+1}-z_*\|\le C\|z_k-z_*\|^2\qquad(k\ge K),\] whenever \(\|z_k-z_*\|\le\varepsilon\). In exact-Hessian equality SQP, \(z_{k+1}\) is the Newton iterate for the KKT residual map, so the definition applies jointly to primal and multiplier errors.
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: Local quadratic convergence means that sufficiently close SQP primal-dual iterates remain close, converge to the regular KKT pair, and eventually have next-iterate error bounded by a constant times the square of the current error. For exact-Hessian equality SQP, this is the Newton rate for the KKT equations.
knowledge_statements.conclusion_latex: \(\exists C>0,K\) such that \(\|z_{k+1}-z_*\|\le C\|z_k-z_*\|^2\) for every \(k\ge K\).
equivalent_formulations_latex: With \(e_k=\|z_k-z_*\|\), Q-quadratic convergence is \(e_{k+1}=O(e_k^2)\).
special_cases_latex: If an inequality SQP method has identified and retained the correct active set, the local iteration reduces to equality SQP on those active constraints.
immediate_consequences_latex: Provided \(e_k\to0\), Q-quadratic convergence implies \(e_{k+1}/e_k\to0\).
boundary_notes: Quadratic convergence of primal iterates alone does not automatically state a quadratic multiplier rate.
A second-order correction or other globalization safeguard may be needed before full local steps are consistently accepted.

children.title: Equality-SQP Quadratic Rate
children.top_down_role: Quadratic local behavior in equality-constrained geometry.

knowledge_statements.title: Equality-SQP Quadratic Rate
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: At a regular equality-constrained KKT point with positive-definite reduced Lagrangian Hessian and a locally Lipschitz KKT Jacobian, exact-Hessian full-step SQP is Newton's method for the KKT equations and converges quadratically from sufficiently close initial points.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex:
Let \(f:\mathbb{R}^n\to\mathbb{R}\) and \(c:\mathbb{R}^n\to\mathbb{R}^m\), define \(L(x,\lambda)=f(x)+\lambda^\top c(x)\), and set \(z=(x,\lambda)\in\mathbb{R}^{n+m}\) and
\[F(z)=\begin{pmatrix}\nabla_xL(x,\lambda)\\c(x)\end{pmatrix}.\]
Suppose \(F(z^*)=0\), \(\nabla c(x^*)\) has full row rank, and \(d^\top\nabla_{xx}^2L(x^*,\lambda^*)d>0\) for every \(d\in\ker\nabla c(x^*)\setminus\{0\}\). Suppose also that \(F'\) is locally Lipschitz near \(z^*\). If exact-Hessian, full-step SQP is written as
\[F'(z_k)s_k=-F(z_k),\qquad z_{k+1}=z_k+s_k,\]
then there are a neighborhood of \(z^*\) and a constant \(C>0\) such that every \(z_0\) in that neighborhood generates well-defined iterates satisfying
\[\|z_{k+1}-z^*\|\le C\|z_k-z^*\|^2.\]
assumptions_latex: \(f\) and \(c\) are twice continuously differentiable near \(x^*\), and the KKT Jacobian \(F'\) is locally Lipschitz near \(z^*\).
\(\nabla c(x^*)\) has full row rank and the reduced Lagrangian Hessian is positive definite.
Every SQP iteration takes the full Newton step using the exact Lagrangian Hessian.
knowledge_statements.conclusion_latex: For \(z_0\) sufficiently close to \(z^*\), \(\|z_{k+1}-z^*\|\le C\|z_k-z^*\|^2\).
knowledge_statements.scope_note: Local quadratic convergence of finite-dimensional full-step equality SQP with the exact Lagrangian Hessian.

source_witnesses.locator: 3.5.3 Sequential quadratic programming (SQP) p. 107

knowledge_statements.slot_contract: State the canonical mathematical definition of the source node, with its domain, quantifiers, notation, and a precise source locator.
knowledge_statements.ambient_context_latex: Consider \(\min f(x)\) subject to \(c(x)=0\), where \(f:\mathbb R^n\to\mathbb R\), \(c:\mathbb R^n\to\mathbb R^m\), \(A(x)=c'(x)\), and \(\mathcal L(x,\lambda)=f(x)-\lambda^Tc(x)\).
knowledge_statements.scope_note: Finite-dimensional equality-constrained SQP with exact Lagrangian Hessians and full local steps.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex:
The equality-SQP quadratic-rate regime at \(z_*=(x_*,\lambda_*)\) consists of the following conditions: \(f\) and \(c\) are twice differentiable near \(x_*\) with Lipschitz continuous second derivatives; \(A(x_*)\) has full row rank; \(d^T
abla_{xx}^2\mathcal L(x_*,\lambda_*)d>0\) for all \(0
e d\in\ker A(x_*)\); the SQP model uses \(B_k=
abla_{xx}^2\mathcal L(x_k,\lambda_k)\); and \(z_0\) is sufficiently close to \(z_*\). The step and new multiplier solve \[ egin{bmatrix}B_k&-A_k^T\A_k&0\end{bmatrix} egin{bmatrix}p_k\\lambda_{k+1}\end{bmatrix}= egin{bmatrix}-
abla f(x_k)\-c(x_k)\end{bmatrix},\qquad x_{k+1}=x_k+p_k.\] In this regime the associated rate property is \(\|z_{k+1}-z_*\|\le C\|z_k-z_*\|^2\) eventually.
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: The equality-SQP quadratic-rate regime uses exact Lagrangian Hessians, a full-rank equality Jacobian, positive reduced-Hessian curvature, Lipschitz second derivatives, full local steps, and a sufficiently close initial primal-dual point. Its KKT system is exactly the Newton system for the equality-constrained KKT equations, and the resulting primal-dual error is locally quadratic.
knowledge_statements.conclusion_latex: Under the defining regime, \(\exists C>0,K\) such that \(\|(x_{k+1},\lambda_{k+1})-(x_*,\lambda_*)\|\le C\|(x_k,\lambda_k)-(x_*,\lambda_*)\|^2\) for \(k\ge K\).
equivalent_formulations_latex: The displayed SQP iteration is Newton's method applied to \(F(x,\lambda)=(\nabla f(x)-A(x)^T\lambda,c(x))=0\).
special_cases_latex: When \(m=0\), the system and rate reduce to ordinary exact-Hessian Newton optimization.
immediate_consequences_latex: The primal and multiplier components converge together at the stated quadratic rate in any fixed product norm.
The KKT matrix is nonsingular in a sufficiently small neighborhood.
boundary_notes: Replacing the exact Hessian by BFGS generally changes the canonical rate to superlinear rather than quadratic.
The definition does not cover inexact KKT solves unless their residual forcing is sufficiently strong and separately specified.

knowledge_statements.title: Identified-Active-Set Quadratic Rate
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: After the correct active inequalities are permanently fixed, exact-Hessian full-step SQP becomes equality-constrained Newton SQP and converges quadratically from a sufficiently close primal-dual iterate.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex:
Let \(f:\mathbb{R}^n\to\mathbb{R}\), \(h:\mathbb{R}^n\to\mathbb{R}^m\), and \(g:\mathbb{R}^n\to\mathbb{R}^p\), and consider minimizing \(f(x)\) subject to \(h(x)=0\) and \(g(x)\le0\). Let \(z^*=(x^*,\lambda^*,\mu^*)\) be a KKT point and let \(I^*=\{i:g_i(x^*)=0\}\). Form the fixed-active-set equality system from \(h(x)=0\) and \(g_i(x)=0\) for \(i\in I^*\), and let \(F_{I^*}\) be its primal-dual KKT residual. Suppose LICQ and strict complementarity hold at \(z^*\), the Lagrangian Hessian is positive definite on the tangent space of this equality system, and \(F_{I^*}'\) is locally Lipschitz. If, from an index \(K\), SQP permanently uses exactly \(I^*\), takes full steps, and uses the exact Lagrangian Hessian, then its subsequent iteration is Newton's method for \(F_{I^*}=0\). If \(z_K\) is sufficiently close to \(z^*\), there is a constant \(C>0\) such that
\[\|z_{k+1}-z^*\|\le C\|z_k-z^*\|^2\qquad(k\ge K).\]
assumptions_latex: The fixed-active-set KKT residual \(F_{I^*}\) is continuously differentiable and \(F_{I^*}'\) is locally Lipschitz near \(z^*\).
LICQ, strict complementarity, and positive definiteness of the Lagrangian Hessian on the fixed-active-set tangent space hold at \(z^*\).
From iteration \(K\), the exact active set is permanently identified and full exact-Hessian SQP steps are taken.
knowledge_statements.conclusion_latex: If \(z_K\) is sufficiently close to \(z^*\), then \(\|z_{k+1}-z^*\|\le C\|z_k-z^*\|^2\) for every \(k\ge K\).
knowledge_statements.scope_note: Local quadratic convergence of exact-Hessian full-step SQP after permanent identification of the solution's active inequalities.

notation.meaning: active inequality set at the solution
KKT residual for the equality system formed from the equalities and fixed active inequalities
first iteration after permanent correct active-set identification
