knowledge_statements.slot_contract: State the canonical mathematical definition of the source node, with its domain, quantifiers, notation, and a precise source locator.
knowledge_statements.ambient_context_latex: Consider a twice-smooth nonlinear program \(\min f(x)\) subject to \(c_i(x)=0\), \(i\in\mathcal E\), and \(c_i(x)\ge 0\), \(i\in\mathcal I\). Let \((x^*,\lambda^*)\) be a KKT pair, let \(\mathcal A^*=\mathcal E\cup\{i\in\mathcal I:c_i(x^*)=0\}\), and let \((x_k,\lambda_k)\) be SQP iterates whose QP active sets are \(\mathcal A_k\).
knowledge_statements.scope_note: Finite-dimensional, deterministic, local exact-Hessian SQP after the optimal inequality active set has stabilized; this is a rate definition, not an identification theorem.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex: The sequence is in the identified-active-set quadratic regime at \((x^*,\lambda^*)\) if there exists \(K<\infty\) such that \(\mathcal A_k=\mathcal A^*\) for every \(k\ge K\), \((x_k,\lambda_k)\to(x^*,\lambda^*)\), and there are \(C>0\) and \(K_1\ge K\) satisfying \[\|(x_{k+1}-x^*,\lambda_{k+1}-\lambda^*)\|\le C\|(x_k-x^*,\lambda_k-\lambda^*)\|^2\quad(k\ge K_1).\] The post-identification SQP step must be the full Newton-SQP step for the equality-constrained system indexed by \(\mathcal A^*\), using the exact Lagrangian Hessian.
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: An SQP sequence has an identified-active-set quadratic rate when, after some finite iteration, every QP uses exactly the constraints active at the limiting KKT point and the resulting full exact-Hessian SQP iteration reduces the primal-dual error by at most a constant times its square. Both primal and multiplier errors are included in the rate.
knowledge_statements.conclusion_latex: \[\exists K_1,C>0\ \forall k\ge K_1:\quad \mathcal A_k=\mathcal A^*,\qquad \|z_{k+1}-z^*\|\le C\|z_k-z^*\|^2,\quad z_k=(x_k,\lambda_k).\]
equivalent_formulations_latex: Provided \(z_k\ne z^*\) eventually, quadratic convergence is equivalently expressed by \(\limsup_{k\to\infty}\|z_{k+1}-z^*\|/\|z_k-z^*\|^2<\infty\), together with finite stabilization \(\mathcal A_k=\mathcal A^*\).
special_cases_latex: For equality-constrained SQP, \(\mathcal A_k=\mathcal A^*=\mathcal E\) automatically, so the definition reduces to local quadratic convergence of exact Newton applied to the KKT equations.
immediate_consequences_latex: Once \(\mathcal A^*\) is identified, inactive inequalities no longer enter the local KKT system, and the local rate is governed by the equality-constrained Newton-SQP iteration.
boundary_notes: Correct active-set identification alone does not imply quadratic convergence; exact second derivatives, full local steps, and regularity of the reduced KKT system remain necessary.
Without strict complementarity, finite stabilization of the QP active set is not supplied by the cited identification result.

knowledge_statements.statement_title: Local Q-superlinear convergence of SQP iterates
knowledge_statements.ambient_context_latex: Let \((x_k,\lambda_k)\) be primal-dual iterates of an SQP method for a finite-dimensional smooth nonlinear program, and suppose they converge to a KKT pair \((x^*,\lambda^*)\). Write \(z_k=(x_k,\lambda_k)\) and measure errors in any fixed norm on the product space.
knowledge_statements.scope_note: Local Q-superlinear convergence of the complete SQP primal-dual sequence; reduced-Hessian two-step superlinear behavior is treated separately.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex: The SQP sequence converges locally Q-superlinearly to \(z^*=(x^*,\lambda^*)\) if \(z_k\to z^*\) and \[\lim_{k\to\infty}\frac{\|z_{k+1}-z^*\|}{\|z_k-z^*\|}=0,\] with the quotient required only for indices for which \(z_k\ne z^*\). In a full quasi-Newton equality-SQP method, a canonical superlinear regime additionally has eventual full steps and tangential curvature errors that vanish along the SQP displacements.
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: Local Q-superlinear SQP convergence means that the next primal-dual error divided by the current primal-dual error tends to zero. Thus no fixed positive linear contraction factor describes the asymptotic behavior. For full quasi-Newton SQP, the defining rate is associated with unit steps and increasingly accurate projected Lagrangian-Hessian action along the computed displacements.
equivalent_formulations_latex: For every \(\varepsilon>0\), there exists \(K_\varepsilon\) such that \(\|z_{k+1}-z^*\|\le\varepsilon\|z_k-z^*\|\) for all \(k\ge K_\varepsilon\).

For equality-SQP under the regularity assumptions of the cited characterization, primal Q-superlinear convergence is equivalent to \[\frac{\|P_k(B_k-\nabla_{xx}^2\mathcal L_*)s_k\|}{\|s_k\|}\to0,\qquad s_k=x_{k+1}-x_k.\]
special_cases_latex: Quadratic convergence, \(\|z_{k+1}-z^*\|\le C\|z_k-z^*\|^2\), implies Q-superlinear convergence whenever \(z_k\to z^*\).
immediate_consequences_latex: For every prescribed \(q\in(0,1)\), the errors eventually satisfy \(\|z_{k+1}-z^*\|\le q\|z_k-z^*\|\).
boundary_notes: R-superlinear convergence and two-step superlinear convergence are weaker notions and are not identified with the displayed Q-superlinear definition.
The definition does not itself guarantee convergence from a remote starting point or eventual acceptance of unit steps.

knowledge_statements.title: Dennis-More SQP Regime
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: The Hessian approximation need only reproduce the true Lagrangian-Hessian action asymptotically along SQP steps to support superlinear convergence.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex:
Let \(z_k=(x_k,y_k)\to z^*\) be primal-dual SQP iterates, let \(p_k=x_{k+1}-x_k\), and let \(B_k\) approximate \(H^*=\nabla_{xx}^2L(x^*,y^*)\). The Dennis–Moré SQP condition along the step sequence is
\[\frac{\|(B_k-H^*)p_k\|}{\|p_k\|}\longrightarrow0\]
for all sufficiently large \(k\) with \(p_k\ne0\). Under local KKT regularity, a nonsingular KKT linearization, bounded curvature approximations, and eventual full-step acceptance, this asymptotic condition makes the quasi-Newton SQP correction differ from the exact Newton correction by \(o(\|z_k-z^*\|)\), yielding
\[\|z_{k+1}-z^*\|=o(\|z_k-z^*\|).\]
assumptions_latex: The KKT solution is locally regular and its linearization is nonsingular.
\(B_k\) and the relevant KKT-system inverses remain uniformly bounded.
Full SQP steps are accepted eventually.
knowledge_statements.conclusion_latex: The Dennis–Moré condition implies \(\|z_{k+1}-z^*\|=o(\|z_k-z^*\|)\).
knowledge_statements.scope_note: Full-space Dennis–Moré curvature accuracy along the accepted SQP steps.

knowledge_statements.statement_title: Projected Dennis–Moré condition for full quasi-Newton SQP
knowledge_statements.ambient_context_latex: For equality-constrained SQP, let \(A_k\) be the constraint Jacobian, \(P_k=I-A_k^T(A_kA_k^T)^{-1}A_k\) the orthogonal projector onto \(\ker A_k\), \(B_k\) a full quasi-Newton Hessian approximation, \(H_*=\nabla_{xx}^2\mathcal L(x^*,\lambda^*)\), and \(s_k=x_{k+1}-x_k\).
knowledge_statements.scope_note: Finite-dimensional local equality-SQP with full quasi-Newton matrices and a regular constraint Jacobian; the condition concerns Hessian action along realized steps, not matrix-norm convergence.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex: The SQP sequence is in the projected Dennis–Moré regime at \((x^*,\lambda^*)\) when \(x_k\to x^*\), \(s_k\ne0\) eventually, and \[\lim_{k\to\infty}\frac{\|P_k(B_k-H_*)s_k\|}{\|s_k\|}=0.\] Thus the tangential component of the curvature-model error is of smaller order than the SQP displacement along the directions actually taken.
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: The Dennis–Moré SQP regime requires the projected error in applying the quasi-Newton matrix instead of the limiting Lagrangian Hessian to the current SQP displacement to be negligible relative to that displacement. Only the component tangent to the constraints is relevant. The whole matrix need not converge to the exact Hessian.
equivalent_formulations_latex: For every \(\varepsilon>0\), there exists \(K\) such that \(\|P_k(B_k-H_*)s_k\|\le\varepsilon\|s_k\|\) for every \(k\ge K\).
Under Assumptions 18.2 and convergence of equality-SQP iterates, the cited characterization makes this condition equivalent to primal Q-superlinear convergence.
special_cases_latex: If \(\|P_k(B_k-H_*)\|\to0\), then the projected Dennis–Moré condition holds, although operator-norm convergence is stronger than required.
For unconstrained optimization, \(P_k=I\), recovering the usual Dennis–Moré condition \(\|(B_k-H_*)s_k\|/\|s_k\|\to0\).
immediate_consequences_latex: Persistent curvature errors on directions orthogonal to the realized steps do not by themselves violate the condition.
The condition separates superlinear directional accuracy from full Hessian consistency.
boundary_notes: For reduced-Hessian SQP, the applicable condition is two-sided projected and generally yields two-step rather than one-step Q-superlinear convergence.
The condition alone does not encode globalization or full-step acceptance.

knowledge_statements.title: Reduced-Hessian Superlinear SQP
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: Superlinear convergence follows when the Hessian model becomes sufficiently accurate only in tangent directions, provided normal-step errors are higher order.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex:
Let \(z_k=(x_k,y_k)\to z^*\), let \(p_k=x_{k+1}-x_k\), and let the columns of \(Z_k\) span the tangent space of the equality constraints or permanently identified active set at \(x_k\). Suppose full steps are eventually taken and the reduced Hessian approximations satisfy
\[\frac{\|Z_k^\top(B_k-\nabla_{xx}^2L(x^*,y^*))p_k\|}{\|p_k\|}\longrightarrow0.\]
If LICQ holds, the exact reduced Hessian is positive definite, the normal-step linearization error is of higher order, and the primal-dual iterates remain on a locally unique KKT branch, then
\[\|z_{k+1}-z^*\|=o(\|z_k-z^*\|).\]
assumptions_latex: LICQ and positive definiteness of the exact reduced Lagrangian Hessian hold at \(z^*\).
The active structure or equality manifold is locally stable, with higher-order normal-step error.
Full steps are accepted eventually and relevant reduced systems remain uniformly nonsingular.
knowledge_statements.scope_note: Superlinear SQP from tangent-space accuracy of a reduced curvature model.

notation.meaning: basis matrix for the current tangent space

knowledge_statements.statement_latex: A reduced-Hessian SQP sequence is in the two-step superlinear regime at \(x^*\) if \(x_k\to x^*\) and \[\lim_{k\to\infty}\frac{\|x_{k+2}-x^*\|}{\|x_k-x^*\|}=0.\] A canonical reduced-curvature accuracy condition associated with this regime is \[\lim_{k\to\infty}\frac{\|P_k(B_k-H_*)P_ks_k\|}{\|s_k\|}=0,\] with \(\{B_k\}\) bounded.
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: Reduced-Hessian SQP is two-step superlinear when the error two iterations later is negligible relative to the current error. The associated curvature requirement controls the reduced Hessian only on the tangential component of the realized displacement. Because a reduced model does not represent the one-sided range-space cross term of the full Hessian, the supported conclusion is generally two-step rather than ordinary one-step superlinear convergence.
equivalent_formulations_latex: For every \(\varepsilon>0\), there is \(K\) such that \(\|x_{k+2}-x^*\|\le\varepsilon\|x_k-x^*\|\) for all \(k\ge K\).
special_cases_latex: For smoothly varying null-space bases and reduced BFGS updates with a symmetric positive-definite initial reduced matrix, the cited source states that the two-sided projected condition yields two-step superlinear convergence.
immediate_consequences_latex: Each parity subsequence \(\{x_{2j}\}\) and \(\{x_{2j+1}\}\), when infinite and nonstationary, has an asymptotic contraction factor tending to zero over its own successive terms.
boundary_notes: Two-step superlinear convergence does not imply that \(\|x_{k+1}-x^*\|/\|x_k-x^*\|\to0\).
A full Dennis–Moré condition on \(P_k(B_k-H_*)s_k\) is stronger than the reduced-space condition displayed here.

children.title: Inexact SQP Superlinear Regime
children.top_down_role: Superlinear behavior under progressively improving inner accuracy.

knowledge_statements.title: Inexact SQP Superlinear Regime
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: Inner KKT solves become superlinearly adequate when their relative residual tolerance tends to zero; a first-order forcing tolerance yields quadratic convergence.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex:
Let \(F(z)=0\) denote the smooth local KKT system after equality reduction or stable active-set identification, with \(F'(z^*)\) nonsingular. Suppose an inexact SQP step \(s_k\) satisfies
\[F'(z_k)s_k=-F(z_k)+r_k,\qquad \|r_k\|\le\eta_k\|F(z_k)\|,\]
where \(z_{k+1}=z_k+s_k\), full steps are eventually accepted, and \(\eta_k\to0\). If \(F'\) is continuous near \(z^*\) and \(z_k\to z^*\), then
\[\|z_{k+1}-z^*\|=o(\|z_k-z^*\|).\]
If additionally \(F'\) is locally Lipschitz and \(\eta_k=O(\|F(z_k)\|)\), the rate is quadratic.
assumptions_latex: The reduced local KKT mapping \(F\) is continuously differentiable and \(F'(z^*)\) is nonsingular.
The iterates converge to \(z^*\) and full steps are eventually accepted.
The inner residual satisfies \(\|r_k\|\le\eta_k\|F(z_k)\|\) with \(\eta_k\to0\).
knowledge_statements.conclusion_latex: \(\|z_{k+1}-z^*\|=o(\|z_k-z^*\|)\); under the stronger forcing rule, the rate is quadratic.
knowledge_statements.scope_note: Superlinear local convergence with a forcing sequence tending to zero.

notation.meaning: residual of the inexact KKT linear solve

knowledge_statements.statement_latex: The iteration is in the vanishing-forcing inexact SQP superlinear regime if \(z_k\to z^*\), \(F(z^*)=0\), \(J(z^*)\) is nonsingular, and there are forcing terms \(\eta_k\ge0\) such that \[\|r_k\|\le\eta_k\|F(z_k)\|,\qquad \eta_k\to0,\] while full local steps are taken. The defining rate is \[\frac{\|z_{k+1}-z^*\|}{\|z_k-z^*\|}\to0.\]
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: Inexact SQP is in a superlinear regime when the residual left in the primal-dual KKT linear system is bounded by a forcing factor times the current KKT residual, the forcing factors tend to zero, and the resulting full primal-dual iteration converges with a vanishing ratio of successive errors.
knowledge_statements.conclusion_latex: \[\eta_k\to0,\quad \|r_k\|\le\eta_k\|F(z_k)\|,\quad \frac{\|z_{k+1}-z^*\|}{\|z_k-z^*\|}\to0.\]
equivalent_formulations_latex: The residual condition can be written \(\|J_kd_k+F(z_k)\|=o(\|F(z_k)\|)\).
special_cases_latex: Exact SQP corresponds to \(r_k=0\) and \(\eta_k=0\).
A fixed bound \(\eta_k\le\bar\eta<1\) generally describes a linear inexact-Newton regime, not the superlinear regime defined here.
immediate_consequences_latex: Inner linear or quadratic subproblem solves must become relatively more accurate as the outer KKT residual decreases.
boundary_notes: The definition does not specify a unique inexact QP solver or residual norm.
For inequality SQP without finite activity stabilization, a semismooth or generalized-equation formulation may be required instead of the smooth KKT system used here.

knowledge_statements.title: Eventual Full-Step Acceptance
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: When actual and predicted merit reductions agree to relative higher order, the acceptance ratio tends to one and the globalization accepts all later full steps.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex:
Let \(s_k\) be the SQP step, let \(\Phi\) be the globalization merit function, and define the agreement ratio
\[\rho_k=\frac{\Phi(z_k)-\Phi(z_k+s_k)}{m_k(0)-m_k(s_k)},\]
whenever \(m_k(0)-m_k(s_k)>0\). Suppose the globalization rule accepts the full step whenever \(\rho_k\ge\eta\), where \(0<\eta<1\). If, along a convergent local SQP sequence, the model has positive predicted reduction and
\[\Phi(z_k+s_k)-\Phi(z_k)=m_k(s_k)-m_k(0)+o\bigl(m_k(0)-m_k(s_k)\bigr),\]
then \(\rho_k\to1\). Hence there exists \(K\) such that every full step is accepted for \(k\ge K\).
assumptions_latex: The predicted merit reduction \(m_k(0)-m_k(s_k)\) is positive for all sufficiently large \(k\).
The actual-minus-predicted reduction is little-o of the predicted reduction.
The acceptance threshold satisfies \(0<\eta<1\).
knowledge_statements.conclusion_latex: \(\rho_k\to1\), so \(s_k\) is accepted with step length one for all sufficiently large \(k\).
knowledge_statements.scope_note: Acceptance-ratio criterion linking globalization to the local SQP model.

source_witnesses.locator: 3.5.3 Sequential quadratic programming (SQP) p. 107

knowledge_statements.statement_title: Eventual acceptance of unit SQP steps
knowledge_statements.ambient_context_latex: Let \(p_k\) be the SQP primal step, let \(\alpha_k\in(0,1]\) be the step length selected by a line search, and set \(x_{k+1}=x_k+\alpha_kp_k\). A corrected method may instead accept \(x_k+p_k+\widehat p_k\), where \(\widehat p_k\) is a second-order correction.
knowledge_statements.scope_note: Local acceptance regime connecting a globally safeguarded SQP method to its fast full-step local model.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex: An SQP globalization mechanism has eventual full-step acceptance along a convergent run if there exists \(K<\infty\) such that, for every \(k\ge K\), the first unit trial is accepted: \[\alpha_k=1,\qquad x_{k+1}=x_k+p_k.\] For a method explicitly allowing second-order correction, the corrected variant means that for every sufficiently large \(k\), the accepted point is either \(x_k+p_k\) or \(x_k+p_k+\widehat p_k\), with \(\|\widehat p_k\|=O(\|p_k\|^2)\), and no backtracking scales the principal SQP step.
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: Eventual full-step acceptance means that after a finite iteration the globalization device no longer shortens the main SQP direction: every initial unit trial is accepted. If second-order correction is part of the method, accepting a unit SQP step plus a correction of second order also belongs to the corrected full-step regime.
knowledge_statements.conclusion_latex: \[\exists K\ \forall k\ge K:\quad \alpha_k=1.\]
equivalent_formulations_latex: For a backtracking search initialized at one, eventual full-step acceptance is equivalent to eventual termination of the acceptance loop without any reduction of the initial trial step.
special_cases_latex: In a pure local SQP method with no globalization, \(\alpha_k\equiv1\) by construction.
A second-order correction can restore eventual acceptance when a nonsmooth merit function would otherwise exhibit the Maratos effect.
immediate_consequences_latex: Once unit steps are accepted, local Newton or quasi-Newton rate results are no longer diluted by persistent step-length contraction.
boundary_notes: The definition is an observed tail property of an iteration; it is not a global-convergence guarantee.
Accepting \(\alpha_k\to1\) is weaker than finite eventual equality \(\alpha_k=1\).

source_refs.locator: Section 18.3, Second-Order Correction, statement immediately before Section 18.4 that near a regular solution either the full or corrected step is taken and superlinear convergence is attained, pp. 542–543

knowledge_statements.statement_title: Linear, sublinear, and stagnant SQP error regimes
knowledge_statements.ambient_context_latex: Let \(z_k=(x_k,\lambda_k)\) be an SQP primal-dual sequence and let \(S\) be the target KKT solution set. Define \(e_k=\operatorname{dist}(z_k,S)\ge0\). When a particular isolated solution \(z^*\) is fixed, one may take \(e_k=\|z_k-z^*\|\).
knowledge_statements.scope_note: Rate taxonomy for deterministic finite-dimensional SQP sequences; it classifies an observed error sequence without asserting which mechanism causes the rate.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex: Assume \(e_k>0\) eventually. The sequence is Q-linearly convergent if there are \(q\in(0,1)\) and \(K\) such that \(e_{k+1}\le qe_k\) for all \(k\ge K\). It is Q-sublinear when \(e_k\to0\) and \(e_{k+1}/e_k\to1\). It is stagnant at positive error when \(e_k\to\bar e>0\); it is ratio-stagnant at the solution when \(e_k\to0\) but \(e_{k+1}/e_k\to1\) and progress \(e_k-e_{k+1}\) becomes asymptotically negligible relative to \(e_k\).
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: The linear-to-stagnant taxonomy uses the primal-dual distance to the KKT solution set. Linear convergence has a uniform contraction factor below one. Sublinear convergence reaches the solution while the ratio of consecutive errors approaches one. Positive-error stagnation means the iterates stop improving before reaching the solution set. Ratio stagnation at zero is the limiting slow case in which relative progress vanishes despite convergence.
knowledge_statements.conclusion_latex: \[\text{linear: }e_{k+1}\le qe_k;\qquad \text{sublinear: }e_k\to0,\ e_{k+1}/e_k\to1;\qquad \text{positive stagnation: }e_k\to\bar e>0.\]
equivalent_formulations_latex: Positive-error stagnation is equivalently \(\operatorname{dist}(z_k,S)\to\bar e>0\).
When \(e_k\) is eventually nonincreasing, ratio-stagnation at zero is equivalent to \((e_k-e_{k+1})/e_k\to0\).
special_cases_latex: A persistent inexact-Newton forcing factor bounded away from zero can be compatible with a linear regime.
Termination at a non-KKT fixed point is a special case of positive-error stagnation.
immediate_consequences_latex: Neither sublinear convergence nor stagnation satisfies the Q-superlinear condition \(e_{k+1}/e_k\to0\).
boundary_notes: Oscillatory or nonconvergent error sequences may fit none of these three regimes.
Function-value rates need not equal primal-dual iterate rates.

notation.meaning: Primal-dual distance to the target set.

review_flags: No inspected authoritative source was located that presents this combined SQP-specific linear-to-stagnant taxonomy with the exact stated distinctions.
knowledge_statements.title: Linear, sublinear, and stagnant SQP error regimes
SQP Linear Local Rates
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: The primal-dual SQP iterates converge locally Q-linearly when their error contracts eventually by a uniform factor below one, and locally R-linearly when their error is eventually bounded by a geometrically decreasing envelope.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex:
Let \(n,m\in\mathbb{N}\), let \(x_k\in\mathbb{R}^n\) and \(\lambda_k\in\mathbb{R}^m\), and set \(z_k=(x_k,\lambda_k)\in\mathbb{R}^{n+m}\). Suppose \(z_k\to z_*=(x_*,\lambda_*)\), where \(z_*\) is a KKT point. The convergence is locally Q-linear if there exist \(q\in(0,1)\) and \(k_0\in\mathbb{N}\) such that
\[
\lVert z_{k+1}-z_*\rVert\le q\lVert z_k-z_*\rVert\qquad\text{for every }k\ge k_0.
\]
It is locally R-linear if there exist \(C>0\), \(q\in(0,1)\), and \(k_0\in\mathbb{N}\) such that
\[
\lVert z_k-z_*\rVert\le Cq^{k-k_0}\qquad\text{for every }k\ge k_0.
\]
assumptions_latex: \(n,m\in\mathbb{N}\), \(x_k\in\mathbb{R}^n\), and \(\lambda_k\in\mathbb{R}^m\).
\(z_k=(x_k,\lambda_k)\to z_*=(x_*,\lambda_*)\), where \(z_*\) satisfies the KKT conditions.
The norm \(\lVert\cdot\rVert\) is a fixed norm on \(\mathbb{R}^{n+m}\).
knowledge_statements.conclusion_latex: For Q-linear convergence, \(\lVert z_{k+1}-z_*\rVert\le q\lVert z_k-z_*\rVert\) eventually for some \(q\in(0,1)\); for R-linear convergence, \(\lVert z_k-z_*\rVert\le Cq^{k-k_0}\) eventually for some \(C>0\), \(q\in(0,1)\), and \(k_0\in\mathbb{N}\).
knowledge_statements.scope_note: Q-linear and R-linear convergence of finite-dimensional primal-dual SQP iterates near a KKT point.

notation.meaning: geometric factor strictly between zero and one
positive constant in the R-linear error envelope

source_witnesses.locator: 3.5.3 Sequential quadratic programming (SQP) p. 107

knowledge_statements.title: SQP Sublinear Local Rates
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: A convergent primal-dual SQP sequence is locally Q-sublinear in the ratio-one sense when the ratio of successive positive errors tends to one; hence no fixed eventual Q-linear contraction factor below one applies.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex:
Let \(n,m\in\mathbb{N}\), let \(z_k=(x_k,\lambda_k)\in\mathbb{R}^{n+m}\) converge to a KKT point \(z_*\), and define \(e_k=\lVert z_k-z_*\rVert\). Assume \(e_k>0\) for all sufficiently large \(k\). The SQP sequence converges locally Q-sublinearly in the ratio-one sense if
\[
\lim_{k\to\infty}\frac{e_{k+1}}{e_k}=1.
\]
Consequently, no \(q\in(0,1)\) can satisfy \(e_{k+1}\le q e_k\) for every sufficiently large \(k\).
assumptions_latex: \(n,m\in\mathbb{N}\) and \(z_k=(x_k,\lambda_k)\in\mathbb{R}^{n+m}\).
\(z_k\to z_*\), where \(z_*\) is a KKT point.
\(e_k=\lVert z_k-z_*\rVert>0\) for all sufficiently large \(k\).
knowledge_statements.conclusion_latex: \(e_{k+1}/e_k\to1\), so there is no \(q\in(0,1)\) for which \(e_{k+1}\le q e_k\) holds eventually.
knowledge_statements.scope_note: Q-sublinear convergence of finite-dimensional primal-dual SQP errors, distinguished from an eventual uniform linear contraction.

notation.meaning: primal-dual error norm at iteration k

source_witnesses.locator: 3.5.3 Sequential quadratic programming (SQP) p. 107

knowledge_statements.title: SQP Local Stagnation Regimes
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: SQP stagnates when accepted steps vanish while the iterates repeatedly remain a positive distance from the intended KKT point.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex:
Let \(z_k=(x_k,\lambda_k)\) be SQP iterates and let \(z_*\) be a target KKT point. A local stagnation regime occurs if the iterates remain in a neighborhood of \(z_*\) but there exist \(\varepsilon>0\) and an infinite index set \(K\subseteq\mathbb{N}\) such that
\[
\|z_k-z_*\|\ge\varepsilon\qquad(k\in K),
\]
while the accepted steps satisfy \(\|z_{k+1}-z_k\|\to0\). Thus vanishing steps do not certify convergence to the target; rejected steps, degenerating step lengths, inconsistent models, or convergence to a non-KKT point may produce stagnation.
assumptions_latex: The SQP iterates remain in a fixed neighborhood of a target KKT point \(z_*\).
Accepted primal-dual steps satisfy \(\|z_{k+1}-z_k\|\to0\).
knowledge_statements.conclusion_latex: There may exist \(\varepsilon>0\) and infinitely many \(k\) with \(\|z_k-z_*\|\ge\varepsilon\); vanishing steps alone therefore do not imply local convergence.
knowledge_statements.scope_note: Failure of local SQP errors to decrease despite bounded or vanishing computed steps.

notation.meaning: positive separation from the target KKT point

enrichment_metadata.review_comment: The failure-boundary kind fits the terminal container, and the separation-plus-vanishing-step condition is internally intelligible. However, no source establishes this as an SQP stagnation regime, and the listed mechanisms depend on particular globalization, acceptance, and model-update rules. A specific SQP stagnation reference is required before the mathematical scope can be fixed reliably.

children.top_down_role: Finite and asymptotic stabilization of inequality activity in SQP.

knowledge_statements.statement_title: Active-set identification by SQP working sets
knowledge_statements.ambient_context_latex: For \(\min f(x)\) subject to \(c_i(x)=0\), \(i\in\mathcal E\), and \(c_i(x)\ge0\), \(i\in\mathcal I\), let \(x^*\) be a feasible limit point and \(\mathcal A^*=\mathcal E\cup\{i\in\mathcal I:c_i(x^*)=0\}\). Let \(\mathcal W_k\) denote the SQP working set, or the active set of the QP solution in an IQP method.
knowledge_statements.scope_note: Combinatorial stabilization of inequality activity in active-set or inequality-QP SQP methods; finite and asymptotic identification are distinguished.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex: The sequence \(\{\mathcal W_k\}\) identifies \(\mathcal A^*\) finitely if \(\exists K\ \forall k\ge K:\mathcal W_k=\mathcal A^*\). It identifies \(\mathcal A^*\) asymptotically if, for every \(i\in\mathcal A^*\), the activity residual associated with \(i\) tends to zero and, for every \(i\notin\mathcal A^*\), the index is eventually excluded, without requiring exact equality \(\mathcal W_k=\mathcal A^*\) after a finite index.
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: SQP active-set identification means that the working-set decisions recover the constraints active at the limiting solution. Finite identification requires exact equality of the estimated and true active sets after some iteration. Asymptotic identification requires correct limiting activity and eventual exclusion of truly inactive constraints but allows weakly active constraints to enter and leave indefinitely.
knowledge_statements.conclusion_latex: \[\text{finite identification}\iff \exists K\ \forall k\ge K:\ \mathcal W_k=\mathcal A^*.\]
equivalent_formulations_latex: For a finite index set, finite identification is equivalent to eventual inclusion of every index in \(\mathcal A^*\) and eventual exclusion of every index outside \(\mathcal A^*\).
special_cases_latex: In an IQP-SQP method, \(\mathcal W_k\) can be taken as the set of inequalities active at the solution of the current quadratic subproblem.
For equality-only problems, identification is immediate because \(\mathcal A^*=\mathcal E\) is fixed.
immediate_consequences_latex: After finite identification, the local SQP iteration can be represented as equality-constrained SQP on \(\mathcal A^*\).
boundary_notes: Convergence of constraint values alone does not imply finite identification of the discrete working sets.
Strict complementarity is central to the cited finite local identification result.

notation.meaning: True active set at the limiting solution.
SQP estimate of the active set at iteration \(k\).

source_refs.locator: Section 18.1, Inequality Constraints, definition of the QP active-set estimate and Theorem 18.1, p. 531

review_flags: The source directly supports the finite local notion; the asymptotic contrast is included as a scoped taxonomy and is not attributed to Theorem 18.1.

children.title: Finite Active-Set Identification
children.top_down_role: Identification families establishing the correct working set after finitely many iterations.

knowledge_statements.title: Finite Active-Set Identification
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: Under local regularity and strict complementarity, a consistent active-set SQP method eventually selects exactly the constraints active at the limiting solution.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex:
Consider \(\min f(x)\) subject to \(c_i(x)\ge0\) for \(i=1,\ldots,m\), and let \((x_*,\lambda_*)\) be a KKT point. Define \(\mathcal A_*:=\{i:c_i(x_*)=0\}\). An SQP working-set sequence \(W_k\subseteq\{1,ldots,m\}\) finitely identifies the active set if there exists \(k_0\) such that
\[
W_k=\mathcal A_*\qquad(k\ge k_0).
\]
For standard local active-set SQP methods, this property is obtained when the iterates converge to \((x_*,\lambda_*)\), LICQ and strict complementarity hold there, and the QP working-set rule consistently includes constraints with positive limiting multipliers.
assumptions_latex: \((x_k,\lambda_k)\to(x_*,\lambda_*)\), and \((x_*,\lambda_*)\) satisfies the KKT conditions.
LICQ holds at \(x_*\), and \(\lambda_{*,i}>0\) for every \(i\in\mathcal A_*\).
The QP working-set rule is locally consistent with positive limiting multipliers.
knowledge_statements.conclusion_latex: There exists \(k_0\) such that \(W_k=\mathcal A_*\) for all \(k\ge k_0\).
knowledge_statements.scope_note: Eventual exact recovery of the active inequalities by an SQP working set.

notation.meaning: active inequality set at the limiting KKT point
working set selected by the kth SQP subproblem

enrichment_metadata.review_comment: The property kind is plausible for this leaf, but the asserted finite-identification result depends on the exact SQP subproblem and working-set update rule. The phrase 'locally consistent with positive limiting multipliers' is not a formal sufficient hypothesis, and the displayed index universe contains the malformed text \(\{1,ldots,m\}\). An algorithm-specific identification theorem and formal working-set assumptions are needed.

knowledge_statements.statement_title: Finite identification of the optimal SQP active set
knowledge_statements.ambient_context_latex: Let \((x^*,\lambda^*)\) be a KKT pair for a smooth nonlinear program with active set \(\mathcal A^*\), and let \(\mathcal A_k\) be the active set at the solution of the \(k\)-th SQP quadratic subproblem.
knowledge_statements.scope_note: Local IQP-SQP identification under LICQ, strict complementarity, and second-order sufficiency.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex: Finite active-set identification occurs when there exists a finite index \(K\) such that \[\mathcal A_k=\mathcal A^*\qquad\text{for every }k\ge K.\] In the canonical local IQP-SQP setting, \(\mathcal A_k\) consists of the equality indices and those QP inequalities satisfied as equalities by the selected local QP solution.
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: Finite active-set identification means that after some finite SQP iteration, the active set of every subsequent quadratic subproblem is exactly the active set of the limiting nonlinear-program solution. No later constraint is added or removed from that set.
knowledge_statements.conclusion_latex: \[\exists K<\infty\ \forall k\ge K:\quad \mathcal A_k=\mathcal A(x^*).\]
equivalent_formulations_latex: Because the constraint index set is finite, the definition is equivalent to eventual membership stabilization \(\mathbf 1_{\{i\in\mathcal A_k\}}=\mathbf 1_{\{i\in\mathcal A^*\}}\) for every constraint index \(i\).
special_cases_latex: Under LICQ, strict complementarity, and second-order sufficient conditions, the cited local result states that a sufficiently near SQP subproblem has a local solution whose active set equals \(\mathcal A^*\).
immediate_consequences_latex: After identification, the inequality SQP system has the same local active equations as an equality-constrained SQP system.
Warm-starting the QP working set from the previous iteration becomes locally exact at the level of index membership.
boundary_notes: The cited theorem guarantees a local QP solution with the correct active set; an implementation must select the relevant local solution.
Finite identification is stronger than convergence of slacks or multipliers.
Strict complementarity excludes weakly active indices with both zero slack and zero multiplier.

notation.meaning: Active constraints at the selected QP solution.
Active constraints at the nonlinear-program solution.

children.title: Asymptotic Active-Set Identification
children.top_down_role: Weaker activity-stabilization regimes without finite identification.

knowledge_statements.title: Asymptotic Active-Set Identification
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: Approximate activity indicators converge to the true active set as tolerances vanish, although the SQP working set need not become permanently constant.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex:
For inequalities \(c_i(x)\ge0\), let \(x_k\to x_*\) and \(\mathcal A_*:=\{i:c_i(x_*)=0\}\). Given tolerances \(\tau_k\downarrow0\), define the approximate active set
\[
\mathcal A_k(\tau_k):=\{i:c_i(x_k)\le\tau_k\}.
\]
The sequence asymptotically identifies \(\mathcal A_*\) if every inactive constraint is eventually excluded and every active constraint is eventually approximately active; equivalently,
\[
\mathbf 1_{\mathcal A_k(\tau_k)}\to\mathbf 1_{\mathcal A_*}.
\]
This permits the algorithmic working sets \(W_k\) themselves to keep changing, so it is weaker than finite working-set identification.
assumptions_latex: The activity tolerances satisfy \(\tau_k>0\) and \(\tau_k\to0\).
knowledge_statements.conclusion_latex: \(\mathbf 1_{\mathcal A_k(\tau_k)}\to\mathbf 1_{\mathcal A_*}\), without requiring eventual equality of the algorithmic working sets \(W_k\).
knowledge_statements.scope_note: Convergence of activity indicators without eventual equality of working sets.

notation.meaning: incidence vector of an index set

enrichment_metadata.review_comment: No source supports this proposed meaning of asymptotic SQP identification. From \(x_k\to x_*\) and \(\tau_k\downarrow0\) alone, an active constraint need not satisfy \(c_i(x_k)\le\tau_k\); a relation between activity residuals and tolerances is required. Moreover, convergence of finite-dimensional incidence vectors to a binary incidence vector implies eventual equality of the approximate sets, so the claimed distinction from finite identification rests entirely on separating \(\mathcal A_k(\tau_k)\) from the algorithmic working sets \(W_k\). A source must fix the intended SQP-specific concept.

knowledge_statements.statement_title: Asymptotic identification without finite working-set stabilization
knowledge_statements.ambient_context_latex: Let \(x_k\to x^*\) in a smooth inequality-constrained problem. Let \(s_{i,k}\ge0\) denote the QP or nonlinear slack estimate and \(\lambda_{i,k}\ge0\) its multiplier estimate. Define \(\mathcal A^*=\{i:s_i^*=0\}\).
knowledge_statements.scope_note: Weak activity recovery when exact discrete stabilization cannot be required, especially in degenerate problems.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex: The sequence asymptotically identifies \(\mathcal A^*\) if \[i\in\mathcal A^*\Rightarrow s_{i,k}\to0,\qquad i\notin\mathcal A^*\Rightarrow \exists K_i\ \forall k\ge K_i:\ i\notin\mathcal W_k,\] and every accumulation point of the activity indicators is compatible with zero limiting slack. Finite equality \(\mathcal W_k=\mathcal A^*\) is not required; weakly active indices may switch membership infinitely often.
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: Asymptotic identification recovers the limiting activity pattern through vanishing slacks and eventual rejection of truly inactive constraints, but it permits the discrete working set to keep changing among constraints whose limiting slack is zero. It is therefore weaker than finite identification.
knowledge_statements.conclusion_latex: \[s_{i,k}\to0\ (i\in\mathcal A^*),\qquad i\notin\mathcal W_k\text{ eventually }(i\notin\mathcal A^*).\]
equivalent_formulations_latex: For every \(\varepsilon>0\), all sufficiently large \(k\) satisfy \(s_{i,k}<\varepsilon\) for \(i\in\mathcal A^*\), while every strictly inactive index is absent from \(\mathcal W_k\).
special_cases_latex: Finite identification implies asymptotic identification when the iterates and slack estimates converge consistently.
If \(c_i(x^*)>0\), continuity gives a positive limiting slack and supports eventual exclusion of index \(i\).
immediate_consequences_latex: The active manifold may be approached geometrically even though no single working set is selected permanently.
boundary_notes: This definition does not treat an index as identified merely because its multiplier tends to zero.
The precise activity estimator depends on the SQP formulation; slack, multiplier, and working-set definitions must not be interchanged without additional assumptions.
review_flags: No inspected authoritative source was located that formalizes this exact asymptotic-identification notion for SQP while expressly allowing infinite switching.

children.title: Identification Failure Under Degeneracy
children.top_down_role: Activity instability under weak complementarity or nonunique multipliers.

knowledge_statements.title: Identification Failure Under Degeneracy
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: Redundant active constraints with zero multipliers can yield identical SQP steps for different working sets, so the full active set need not stabilize.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex: Consider \(\min x^2\) subject to \(c_1(x)=x\ge0\) and \(c_2(x)=2x\ge0\). At \(x_*=0\), both inequalities are active, their gradients are linearly dependent, and the KKT multipliers satisfy \(\lambda_1+2\lambda_2=0\) with \(\lambda_1,\lambda_2\ge0\), hence \(\lambda_1=\lambda_2=0\). Because neither active constraint has a positive multiplier and either constraint locally represents the same feasible boundary, an SQP subproblem may use \(W_k=\{1\}\), \(W_k=\{2\}\), or both without changing the primal step. Thus exact finite identification of the full active set is not guaranteed under degeneracy.
assumptions_latex: The working-set rule may choose any constraint representation producing the same QP feasible boundary.
No deterministic tie-breaking rule forces inclusion of every redundant active inequality.
knowledge_statements.conclusion_latex: Finite equality \(W_k=\{1,2\}\) cannot be guaranteed, even when the primal iterates converge to \(x_*=0\).
knowledge_statements.scope_note: Nonunique or weakly complementary multipliers can prevent stable working-set recovery.

notation.meaning: working set in the kth SQP subproblem

enrichment_metadata.review_comment: The example correctly exhibits redundant active constraints, LICQ failure, and zero multipliers, and the failure-boundary kind fits the leaf. It does not by itself establish behavior of an SQP sequence: whether different working sets are admissible and whether they fail to stabilize depends on the QP formulation and deterministic tie-breaking rule. A cited algorithm-specific counterexample or identification-failure result is required.

knowledge_statements.slot_contract: State the canonical mathematical definition of the source node, with its domain, quantifiers, notation, and a precise source locator.
knowledge_statements.statement_title: Failure of finite activity identification at a degenerate KKT point
knowledge_statements.ambient_context_latex: Let \(x_k\to x^*\), let \(\mathcal A^*=\{i:c_i(x^*)=0\}\), and let \(\mathcal W_k\) be SQP working sets. Call an active index weakly active when \(c_i(x^*)=0\) and some relevant KKT multiplier has \(\lambda_i^*=0\). Multiplier nonuniqueness is also treated as degeneracy.
knowledge_statements.scope_note: Descriptive failure regime for weak complementarity or nonunique multipliers; it does not assert that every degenerate problem must fail identification.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex: Finite identification fails at the convergent run if \[\forall K\ \exists k\ge K:\quad \mathcal W_k\ne\mathcal A^*.\] Activity instability is present when some index \(i\in\mathcal A^*\) changes membership infinitely often, namely both sets \(\{k:i\in\mathcal W_k\}\) and \(\{k:i\notin\mathcal W_k\}\) are infinite. Degeneracy is implicated when such an index is weakly active or when the limiting multiplier vector is nonunique, so that slack and multiplier signs do not uniquely separate active and inactive decisions.
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: Identification failure means there is no finite iteration after which every working set equals the true active set. A particularly clear failure mode is infinite switching of a weakly active constraint. Degeneracy describes the lack of a strict multiplier or unique multiplier signal that would force a stable decision; it is a possible mechanism, not a universal implication.
knowledge_statements.conclusion_latex: \[\neg\exists K\ \forall k\ge K:\mathcal W_k=\mathcal A^*.\]
equivalent_formulations_latex: Finite-identification failure is equivalent to the set \(\{k:\mathcal W_k\ne\mathcal A^*\}\) being infinite.
special_cases_latex: Infinite inclusion-exclusion switching of one weakly active inequality is sufficient for failure.
Permanent omission of an active index also constitutes failure even without switching.
immediate_consequences_latex: An equality-SQP local model based on one fixed optimal active set cannot be invoked on the entire tail of such a run.
boundary_notes: Failure of strict complementarity does not logically force identification failure for every algorithm.
Nonunique multipliers do not necessarily imply nonunique primal solutions.

knowledge_statements.statement_title: Globalized SQP family and its stationarity target
knowledge_statements.ambient_context_latex: Let \(\{x_k\}\subset\mathbb R^n\) be generated by SQP from an arbitrary admissible initial point. Let \(R(x,\lambda)\) be a KKT residual, and let the acceptance architecture be a line search, trust region, filter, restoration mechanism, or feasible-iterate rule.
knowledge_statements.scope_note: Family-level definition organized by acceptance and feasibility mechanisms; global convergence means attraction to stationarity, not global optimality.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex: An SQP scheme belongs to a globally convergent family on a stated problem class \(\mathcal P\) if, for every problem in \(\mathcal P\) and every admissible initialization, the iteration is well defined and its generated sequence satisfies a specified stationarity conclusion, such as \[\liminf_{k\to\infty}\inf_{\lambda}\|R(x_k,\lambda)\|=0,\] or the stronger property that every accumulation point is a KKT point. The family is identified by the mechanism that enforces sufficient progress: merit-function line search, trust-region agreement, filter acceptance with restoration, or maintained feasibility.
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: An SQP global-convergence family consists of SQP methods whose globalization architecture ensures an explicit stationarity outcome from every admissible start in a stated problem class. The conclusion is normally convergence of residuals or KKT character of accumulation points, not convergence to a globally optimal solution. Different families are distinguished by how they accept steps and restore feasibility.
knowledge_statements.conclusion_latex: \[\text{global stationarity target:}\quad \liminf_k\inf_\lambda\|R(x_k,\lambda)\|=0\quad\text{or}\quad \operatorname{acc}(x_k)\subseteq\operatorname{KKT}.\]
special_cases_latex: For the classical line-search SQP result in the cited source, every limit point is a KKT point under boundedness, feasible bounded QP steps, bounded multipliers, and a sufficiently large fixed exact-penalty parameter.
Trust-region SQP controls model validity by restricting the step and comparing actual with predicted merit reduction.
immediate_consequences_latex: A globalized family can transition to a fast local SQP regime if its acceptance mechanism eventually becomes inactive.
boundary_notes: Global convergence does not mean convergence to a global minimizer.
A theorem stated for one acceptance architecture cannot be transferred automatically to another.

knowledge_statements.ambient_context_latex: At iteration \(k\), let \(p_k\) solve the SQP quadratic subproblem, let \(\phi(\cdot;\mu_k)\) be a merit function, and choose \(\alpha_k\in\{1,\tau,\tau^2,\ldots\}\), \(0<\tau<1\). Let \(\Delta q_k=q_k(0)-q_k(p_k)\) be predicted merit-model reduction.
knowledge_statements.scope_note: Deterministic line-search SQP using a scalar merit function and backtracking; the classical cited theorem uses a fixed sufficiently large nonsmooth exact penalty.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex: A line-search SQP globalization accepts the first backtracking value \(\alpha_k\) satisfying a sufficient-decrease test of the form \[\phi(x_k+\alpha_kp_k;\mu_k)\le\phi(x_k;\mu_k)-\eta\alpha_k\Delta q_k,\qquad \eta\in(0,1).\] It is globally convergent on a stated class when the resulting sequence is well defined from every admissible start and all its accumulation points satisfy the KKT conditions, or an explicitly stated weaker stationarity conclusion.
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: Line-search SQP globalizes the quadratic-program direction by shortening it until a scalar merit function decreases sufficiently relative to predicted model improvement. A global-convergence statement must specify the problem class and the resulting stationarity conclusion. In the classical exact-penalty setting, boundedness and a sufficiently large penalty parameter yield KKT accumulation points.
knowledge_statements.conclusion_latex: \[\alpha_k=\max\{\tau^j:j\ge0,\ \phi(x_k+\tau^jp_k;\mu_k)\le\phi(x_k;\mu_k)-\eta\tau^j\Delta q_k\}.\]
equivalent_formulations_latex: When \(p_k\) is a descent direction for a directionally differentiable merit function, the test may be written in Armijo form using \(D\phi(x_k;p_k)\).
special_cases_latex: The cited classical method uses the \(\ell_1\) exact-penalty merit function, symmetric positive-definite \(B_k\), and backtracking initialized at \(\alpha=1\).
immediate_consequences_latex: The accepted step balances objective reduction and feasibility progress through one scalar acceptance measure.
If unit steps are eventually accepted, the method reduces locally to its unglobalized SQP iteration.
boundary_notes: Penalty-parameter update rules are part of the method and cannot be omitted from a complete global theorem.
Merit decrease alone does not exclude convergence to nonminimizing KKT points.

knowledge_statements.title: Exact-Penalty SQP Global Convergence
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: With sufficient exact-penalty decrease, stable QP curvature, an adequate penalty parameter, and constraint qualification, every SQP accumulation point is a KKT point.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex:
Consider continuously differentiable equality and inequality constraints and an SQP line search applied on a compact level set. Let
\[
\phi_\rho(x)=f(x)+\rho\bigl(\|h(x)\|_1+\|\min\{0,g(x)\}\|_1\bigr).
\]
Suppose the QP Hessian approximations are uniformly bounded and uniformly positive definite on linearized feasible directions, every accepted step gives sufficient decrease in \(\phi_\rho\), the penalty parameter is eventually large enough to dominate bounded multiplier estimates, and a constraint qualification holds at every accumulation point. Then either the method terminates at a KKT point or every accumulation point of \(\{x_k\}\) satisfies the KKT conditions.
assumptions_latex: The relevant merit-function level set is compact, and problem derivatives are continuous there.
The QP models have uniformly controlled positive curvature and generate sufficient merit decrease.
The penalty parameter eventually dominates bounded multiplier estimates, and a constraint qualification holds at accumulation points.
knowledge_statements.conclusion_latex: The method terminates at a KKT point or every accumulation point \(x_*\) of \(\{x_k\}\) admits multipliers satisfying the KKT conditions.
knowledge_statements.scope_note: Accumulation-point convergence for line-search SQP using an exact nonsmooth merit function.

notation.meaning: equality and componentwise nonnegative inequality constraint mappings

enrichment_metadata.review_comment: The theorem kind and exact-penalty scope fit the leaf, and the cited sections are specific enough to inspect. Nevertheless, the statement combines a broad SQP family with informal conditions such as sufficient decrease, controlled curvature, and an eventually adequate penalty parameter without defining the line search, step acceptance, multiplier estimates, or safeguards needed for the conclusion about every accumulation point. Full-text theorem matching is required to determine a reliable hypothesis set.

knowledge_statements.ambient_context_latex: For constraints \(c_i(x)=0\), \(i\in\mathcal E\), and \(c_i(x)\ge0\), \(i\in\mathcal I\), define \([t]^- =\max\{0,-t\}\) and \[\phi_1(x;\mu)=f(x)+\mu\sum_{i\in\mathcal E}|c_i(x)|+\mu\sum_{i\in\mathcal I}[c_i(x)]^-.\]
knowledge_statements.scope_note: Finite-dimensional nonsmooth exact-penalty line-search SQP; exactness is local and requires a penalty threshold.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex: An exact-penalty SQP globalization computes an SQP step \(p_k\), chooses \(\mu_k>0\), and accepts a step length \(\alpha_k\) only if \(\phi_1\) satisfies a directional Armijo or equivalent model-reduction condition. The penalty is exact at a KKT solution \((x^*,\lambda^*)\) when there is \(\mu^*>0\) such that every \(\mu>\mu^*\) makes \(x^*\) a local minimizer of \(\phi_1(\cdot;\mu)\); under the standard normalization one may take the threshold from the limiting multiplier norm. A classical global regime fixes \(\mu\ge\|\lambda_k\|_\infty+\rho\), \(\rho>0\), along the run.
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: Exact-penalty SQP uses a nonsmooth merit function that adds weighted absolute equality violations and negative parts of inequality constraints to the objective. Above a multiplier-dependent threshold, constrained local solutions are also local minimizers of the penalty. A line search accepts only steps with sufficient penalty decrease, and classical global results impose boundedness and a uniformly adequate penalty weight.
knowledge_statements.conclusion_latex: \[\phi_1(x_k+\alpha_kp_k;\mu)\le\phi_1(x_k;\mu)-\eta\alpha_k\bigl(q_\mu(0)-q_\mu(p_k)\bigr).\]
equivalent_formulations_latex: For equality-SQP, \(D\phi_1(x_k;p_k)=\nabla f_k^Tp_k-\mu\|c_k\|_1\), so sufficient descent follows under positive reduced curvature and \(\mu>\|\lambda_{k+1}\|_\infty\).
special_cases_latex: With only equality constraints, \(\phi_1(x;\mu)=f(x)+\mu\|c(x)\|_1\).
immediate_consequences_latex: A finite penalty can enforce local exactness, unlike a quadratic exterior penalty that generally requires an unbounded penalty sequence.
The merit function simultaneously measures objective improvement and feasibility.
boundary_notes: Nonsmooth exact penalties can exhibit the Maratos effect; second-order correction may be needed for fast local convergence.
Exactness is a local solution property and does not make every minimizer of \(\phi_1\) feasible.

knowledge_statements.statement_title: KKT Accumulation Points of Classical Exact-Penalty Line-Search SQP
knowledge_statements.scope_note: Global convergence to KKT points in the accumulation-point sense; it does not assert convergence of the full iterate sequence.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex:
Consider the described exact-penalty line-search SQP algorithm. Suppose that \(\{x_k\}\) and \(\{x_k+p_k\}\) lie in a closed, bounded, convex set \(D\subset\mathbb{R}^n\) on which \(f\) and every \(c_i\) are continuously differentiable. Suppose that \(\{B_k\}\) and the multiplier sequence \(\{\lambda_k\}\) are bounded and that, for some \(\rho>0\),
\[
\mu\geq \|\lambda_k\|_\infty+\rho\qquad\text{for all }k.
\]
Then every limit point of \(\{x_k\}\) is a KKT point of the nonlinear program.
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: For the described exact-penalty line-search SQP method, assume the iterates and full trial points remain in one closed, bounded, convex region where the objective and constraints are continuously differentiable. If the curvature approximations and multipliers are bounded and the fixed penalty parameter exceeds every multiplier infinity norm by a uniform positive margin, then every accumulation point of the iterates satisfies the KKT conditions.
assumptions_latex: \{x_k\}\cup\{x_k+p_k\}\subset D,\quad D\subset\mathbb{R}^n\text{ closed, bounded, and convex}.
f,c_i\in C^1(D)\quad\text{for every constraint }i.
\{B_k\}\text{ and }\{\lambda_k\}\text{ are bounded}.
\exists\rho>0\ \forall k,\quad \mu\geq\|\lambda_k\|_\infty+\rho.
\text{The iterates are generated by the described feasible-subproblem, positive-definite-model, exact-penalty backtracking SQP algorithm}.
knowledge_statements.conclusion_latex: \forall \bar x\in\operatorname{Limsup}_{k\to\infty}\{x_k\},\quad \bar x\text{ is a KKT point of the nonlinear program}.

knowledge_statements.statement_latex:
For every iteration \(k\), let \(p_k\) solve the SQP quadratic subproblem with its Lagrangian Hessian replaced by a symmetric positive-definite matrix \(B_k\), and set \(x_{k+1}=x_k+\alpha_kp_k\). Starting with \(\alpha=1\), backtrack until

\phi_1(x_k+\alpha_kp_k;\mu)\leq \phi_1(x_k;\mu)-\eta\alpha_k\bigl(q_\mu(0)-q_\mu(p_k)\bigr),\qquad \eta\in(0,1).
\]

The iterate uses a backtracking step starting from one and accepted by the stated l1-penalty sufficient-decrease test. Every subproblem must have a bounded solution, and the penalty parameter must remain fixed and sufficiently large.

\forall k,\quad \text{the SQP quadratic subproblem is feasible and has a bounded solution }p_k.
\eta\in(0,1),\qquad \mu\text{ is fixed for all }k\text{ and sufficiently large}.

knowledge_statements.title: Augmented-Lagrangian SQP Global Convergence
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: If feasibility is driven to zero and augmented-Lagrangian line searches yield vanishing stationarity residuals, every regular primal-dual accumulation point is KKT.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex:
For the equality-constrained problem \(\min f(x)\) subject to \(h(x)=0\), let an SQP line search use
\[
\mathcal L_\rho(x,\lambda)=f(x)-\lambda^{\mathsf T}h(x)+\frac{\rho}{2}\|h(x)\|^2
\]
and update both \(x_k\) and \(\lambda_k\). Suppose the primal-dual iterates remain in a compact set, derivatives and model Hessians are uniformly bounded, accepted steps provide sufficient decrease in a multiplier-consistent augmented-Lagrangian model, and LICQ holds at every feasible accumulation point. If infeasibility tends to zero and the stationarity residual has limit inferior zero, then every primal-dual accumulation point satisfies the KKT conditions.
assumptions_latex: The primal-dual iterates remain in a compact set, with bounded derivatives and model Hessians.
Accepted steps satisfy sufficient decrease for a multiplier-consistent augmented-Lagrangian model.
\(\|h(x_k)\|\to0\), the stationarity residual has limit inferior zero, and LICQ holds at feasible accumulation points.
knowledge_statements.conclusion_latex: Every accumulation point \((x_*,\lambda_*)\) satisfies \(h(x_*)=0\) and \(\nabla f(x_*)-\nabla h(x_*)^{\mathsf T}\lambda_*=0\).
knowledge_statements.scope_note: Accumulation-point convergence for multiplier-aware SQP line searches using an augmented Lagrangian.

enrichment_metadata.review_comment: The theorem kind fits the leaf, but feasibility convergence together with only a limit inferior of the stationarity residual equal to zero yields at most a stationary subsequence; it does not imply that every primal-dual accumulation point is stationary. The multiplier update and augmented-Lagrangian decrease condition are also unspecified. The cited global-convergence section must be inspected for a theorem with hypotheses strong enough to justify the stated universal conclusion.

knowledge_statements.slot_contract: State the canonical mathematical definition of the source node, with its domain, quantifiers, notation, and a precise source locator.
knowledge_statements.ambient_context_latex: For an equality-constrained problem \(c(x)=0\), define \[\mathcal L_A(x,\lambda;\mu)=f(x)-\lambda^Tc(x)+\frac{\mu}{2}\|c(x)\|_2^2,\qquad \mu>0.\] Let \((p_k,p_k^\lambda)\) be the SQP primal-multiplier trial direction.
knowledge_statements.scope_note: Equality-constrained multiplier-aware SQP globalization using an augmented Lagrangian as the acceptance function; a complete global theorem requires additional update and boundedness hypotheses.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex: An augmented-Lagrangian SQP line-search regime assesses a trial pair \[(x_k^+,\lambda_k^+)=(x_k,\lambda_k)+\alpha_k(p_k,p_k^\lambda)\] by comparing \(\mathcal L_A(x_k^+,\lambda_k^+;\mu_k)\) with its current value and accepts \(\alpha_k\) only when a prescribed sufficient-decrease condition holds. The penalty \(\mu_k\) and multiplier estimate \(\lambda_k\) are algorithmic state variables and are updated so that the primal-dual SQP direction is productive for the acceptance function.
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: Augmented-Lagrangian SQP uses a smooth function of both the primal variables and multiplier estimates to judge trial steps. It combines the objective, a linear multiplier term, and a squared feasibility penalty. Unlike a nonsmooth exact penalty in the primal variable alone, the standard augmented Lagrangian is generally stationary rather than minimized in the joint primal-multiplier space at a KKT pair, so its multiplier and penalty updates are essential parts of the globalization regime.
knowledge_statements.conclusion_latex: \[\mathcal L_A(x_k+\alpha_kp_k,\lambda_k+\alpha_kp_k^\lambda;\mu_k)\le \mathcal L_A(x_k,\lambda_k;\mu_k)+\text{prescribed negative model change}.\]
special_cases_latex: If the multiplier is held fixed during a primal trial, the acceptance function reduces to the usual augmented Lagrangian in \(x\).
immediate_consequences_latex: The acceptance measure directly incorporates current multiplier information as well as squared constraint violation.
A line search can compare complete primal-dual trial pairs rather than primal points alone.
boundary_notes: The standard augmented Lagrangian is not an exact merit function in the same sense as the nonsmooth \(\ell_1\) penalty.
The displayed definition does not by itself supply a global-convergence theorem or a unique update rule for \(\mu_k\) and \(\lambda_k\).

knowledge_statements.statement_title: Trust-region SQP globalization by actual-to-predicted reduction
knowledge_statements.ambient_context_latex: Let \(m_k(p)\) be an SQP quadratic model with linearized constraints, let \(\Delta_k>0\) be a trust-region radius, and let \(\phi\) be a merit function or an equivalent filter acceptance device. A composite-step method writes \(p_k=v_k+u_k\), where \(v_k\) targets feasibility and \(u_k\) targets tangential optimality.
knowledge_statements.scope_note: Deterministic trust-region SQP, including coupled and normal-tangential composite-step architectures.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex: A trust-region SQP globalization computes a trial step satisfying a bound such as \(\|p_k\|\le\Delta_k\), or separate bounds on normal and tangential components, and forms an agreement ratio \[\rho_k=\frac{\phi(x_k)-\phi(x_k+p_k)}{q_k(0)-q_k(p_k)}.\] The step is accepted only when \(\rho_k\) exceeds a prescribed threshold, and \(\Delta_k\) is reduced after poor agreement and may be enlarged after good agreement. The family is globally convergent on a stated class when these rules, together with feasibility safeguards and sufficient model decrease, imply an explicit first-order stationarity conclusion from every admissible start.
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: Trust-region SQP restricts each quadratic-model step to a region where the model is expected to be reliable. It accepts or rejects the trial point by comparing actual merit improvement with predicted improvement and adjusts the radius accordingly. Composite-step variants first compute a normal step for feasibility and then a tangential step for optimality. A global result additionally requires sufficient model reduction and safeguards for inconsistent linearized constraints.
knowledge_statements.conclusion_latex:
\[\|p_k\|\le\Delta_k,
\qquad \rho_k=\frac{\operatorname{ared}_k}{\operatorname{pred}_k},\qquad p_k\text{ accepted only if }\rho_k\ge\eta.\]
equivalent_formulations_latex: In a normal-tangential method, the trust-region constraint may be imposed separately as \(\|v_k\|\le\zeta\Delta_k\) and \(\|v_k+u_k\|\le\Delta_k\).
special_cases_latex: The Byrd–Omojokun architecture computes a normal step for linearized feasibility followed by a tangential correction.
Sequential \(\ell_1\)-QP and sequential linear-quadratic programming use composite or staged subproblems with trust-region control.
immediate_consequences_latex: Indefinite Lagrangian Hessian models can be handled without globally forcing positive definiteness.
Shrinking \(\Delta_k\) limits steps when the quadratic and constraint-linearization models are unreliable.
boundary_notes: A trust-region bound can make the linearized constrained subproblem infeasible; relaxation or composite-step devices are therefore part of the global architecture.
The ratio is undefined when predicted reduction is nonpositive, so a complete method must impose sufficient predicted decrease.

knowledge_statements.title: Coupled Trust-Region Global Convergence
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: A single-region SQP method with sufficient model decrease and standard radius updates drives a constrained criticality measure to zero and has KKT feasible accumulation points.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex:
Consider a smooth nonlinear program and an SQP method whose full step \(d_k\) solves or sufficiently reduces a quadratic model subject to the linearized constraints and \(\|d_k\|\le\Delta_k\). Suppose the iterates remain in a compact set, first derivatives are Lipschitz continuous, model Hessians are uniformly bounded, the step achieves a fixed fraction of generalized Cauchy decrease, and the trust-region radius is updated from the ratio of actual to predicted merit reduction. If restoration or feasibility safeguards prevent convergence to a nonstationary infeasible point, then
\[
\liminf_{k\to\infty}\chi(x_k)=0,
\]
where \(\chi\) is a continuous constrained first-order criticality measure; every feasible accumulation point with a constraint qualification is KKT.
assumptions_latex: Iterates lie in a compact set; first derivatives are Lipschitz continuous and model Hessians are uniformly bounded.
Each trust-region QP step achieves a uniform fraction of generalized Cauchy decrease.
Radius updates use actual-to-predicted reduction, and safeguards exclude nonstationary infeasible limits.
knowledge_statements.conclusion_latex: \(\liminf_{k\to\infty}\chi(x_k)=0\), and each feasible regular accumulation point satisfies the KKT conditions.
knowledge_statements.scope_note: First-order global convergence for SQP steps constrained by one shared trust region.

enrichment_metadata.review_comment: The theorem kind and single-region trust-region scope fit the leaf, but no source is supplied. The criticality measure, generalized Cauchy decrease, merit model, feasibility safeguards, and radius updates are method-specific and not defined sufficiently to support the claimed limit-inferior and KKT conclusions.

knowledge_statements.slot_contract: State the canonical mathematical definition of the source node, with its domain, quantifiers, notation, and a precise source locator.
knowledge_statements.ambient_context_latex: Consider the equality-constrained problem \(\min_{x\in\mathbb R^n} f(x)\) subject to \(c(x)=0\), where \(f:\mathbb R^n\to\mathbb R\) and \(c:\mathbb R^n\to\mathbb R^m\) are continuously differentiable. Write \(g_k=\nabla f(x_k)\), \(A_k=\nabla c(x_k)\), and let \(H_k=H_k^T\) model the Lagrangian Hessian.
knowledge_statements.scope_note: Finite-dimensional, smooth, equality-constrained SQP using one trust region for the complete primal step. The definition describes the architecture and its global-convergence property, not sufficient hypotheses for a particular implementation.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex:
A coupled trust-region SQP iteration computes one step \(s_k\) from the joint subproblem
\[\min_s\ q_k(s):=g_k^Ts+\tfrac12s^TH_ks\quad\text{subject to}\quad A_ks+c(x_k)=0,\quad \|s\|\leq\Delta_k.\]
When this feasible set is nonempty, define the predicted reduction \(\operatorname{pred}_k=M_k(0)-M_k(s_k)>0\) for a model \(M_k\) of a globalization function \(\Phi\), and
\[\rho_k=\frac{\Phi(x_k)-\Phi(x_k+s_k)}{\operatorname{pred}_k}.\]
The architecture is globally convergent to first-order constrained criticality on a problem class \(\mathcal P\) if, for every problem in \(\mathcal P\) and every admissible initialization, every infinite generated sequence satisfies
\[\liminf_{k\to\infty}\bigl(\|c(x_k)\|+\inf_y\|\nabla f(x_k)+A_k^Ty\|\bigr)=0,\]
or terminates at a pair \((x_k,y_k)\) for which both residuals vanish. The radius and acceptance rules are coupled because the same \(\Delta_k\) simultaneously restricts feasibility correction and tangential objective progress.
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: A coupled trust-region SQP method places the complete SQP step in one trust region and enforces the linearized constraints in the same quadratic subproblem. Trial points are accepted by comparing actual and predicted decrease, and the single radius is updated from that comparison. The architecture has the stated global-convergence property when every admissible infinite run has a subsequence whose feasibility and Lagrangian-stationarity residuals tend to zero, or terminates with both residuals equal to zero.
knowledge_statements.conclusion_latex: \[\text{global convergence}\iff \forall\text{ admissible runs},\quad \liminf_{k\to\infty}\left(\|c(x_k)\|+\inf_y\|\nabla f(x_k)+A_k^Ty\|\right)=0,\] unless exact first-order criticality is reached finitely.
equivalent_formulations_latex: If the iterates and multiplier estimates are bounded and every accumulation point is regular, the residual formulation is equivalent to requiring at least one accumulation point \((x_*,y_*)\) with \(c(x_*)=0\) and \(\nabla f(x_*)+\nabla c(x_*)^Ty_*=0\).
special_cases_latex: With \(c\equiv0\), the subproblem reduces to the ordinary unconstrained trust-region model.
If \(A_ks+c(x_k)=0\) has a solution of norm at most \(\Delta_k\), the coupled subproblem is the trust-region restriction of the standard equality-constrained SQP quadratic program.
immediate_consequences_latex: The coupled subproblem can be infeasible whenever the minimum-norm solution of \(A_ks+c(x_k)=0\) has norm larger than \(\Delta_k\).
Shrinking \(\Delta_k\) does not by itself guarantee subproblem feasibility; an additional relaxation, decomposition, or restoration mechanism may therefore be required.
boundary_notes: The definition excludes composite-step methods that allocate separate normal and tangential regions.
The residual conclusion is subsequential unless stronger assumptions establish convergence of the entire sequence.

notation.meaning: Radius of the single trust region imposed on the full SQP step.
Ratio of actual to predicted globalization-function decrease.
Merit or other scalar globalization function used by this coupled formulation.

children.title: Composite-Step Global Convergence
children.top_down_role: Global theory separating feasibility and tangential progress.

knowledge_statements.title: Composite-Step Global Convergence
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: When normal steps reduce infeasibility and tangential steps reduce the objective with reliable models, feasible regular accumulation points of composite-step SQP are KKT.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex: Let an SQP trust-region step be decomposed as \(d_k=n_k+t_k\), where the normal step \(n_k\) sufficiently reduces linearized constraint violation and the tangential step \(t_k\) sufficiently reduces the quadratic objective model while approximately preserving the feasibility improvement. Suppose iterates remain in a compact set, relevant derivatives are Lipschitz continuous, model Hessians are bounded, normal and tangential trust-region bounds are compatible, and accepted steps achieve uniform fractions of their predicted reductions. If the radius-update and restoration rules exclude nonstationary infeasible accumulation, then either a first-order stationary point is reached finitely or every feasible accumulation point satisfying a constraint qualification is a KKT point.
assumptions_latex: Iterates are bounded; relevant derivatives are Lipschitz continuous and model Hessians are bounded.
Normal and tangential steps attain uniform fractions of their respective predicted reductions.
Trust-region and restoration rules exclude nonstationary infeasible accumulation points.
knowledge_statements.conclusion_latex: The method terminates at first-order stationarity or every feasible accumulation point satisfying a constraint qualification satisfies the KKT conditions.
knowledge_statements.scope_note: Global convergence for normal-tangential SQP trust-region decompositions.

notation.meaning: normal step for reducing linearized infeasibility
tangential step for reducing the objective model

enrichment_metadata.review_comment: The theorem kind matches the composite-step convergence leaf, but the normal-step reduction, tangential-step reduction, compatibility bounds, acceptance test, and restoration rule are only qualitative. Different composite-step SQP methods require materially different hypotheses, so a specific theorem and locator are necessary before this conclusion can be reviewed reliably.

knowledge_statements.slot_contract: State the canonical mathematical definition of the source node, with its domain, quantifiers, notation, and a precise source locator.
knowledge_statements.ambient_context_latex: For \(\min f(x)\) subject to \(c(x)=0\), let \(g_k=\nabla f(x_k)\), \(A_k=\nabla c(x_k)\), and \(H_k=H_k^T\). Let \(\Delta_k>0\) be a trust-region radius and let \(m_k^N(n)=\|c(x_k)+A_kn\|\) measure linearized infeasibility.
knowledge_statements.scope_note: Finite-dimensional smooth equality-constrained SQP. The defining distinction is the explicit normal–tangential decomposition; inequality extensions require corresponding linearized feasible cones.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex:
A composite-step trust-region SQP method forms
\[s_k=n_k+t_k,\]
where the normal step satisfies \(\|n_k\|\leq\xi_N\Delta_k\), with \(0<\xi_N<1\), and achieves prescribed decrease in \(m_k^N\), while the tangential step satisfies
\[A_kt_k=0,\qquad \|n_k+t_k\|\leq\Delta_k,\]
and achieves prescribed decrease in
\[m_k^T(t)=(g_k+H_kn_k)^Tt+\tfrac12t^TH_kt.\]
Thus \(n_k\) targets feasibility and \(t_k\) preserves the attained linearized feasibility while reducing the quadratic objective model. Given a globalization model
\[M_k(s)=f(x_k)+g_k^Ts+\tfrac12s^TH_ks+\sigma_k\|c(x_k)+A_ks\|,\]
the family has the composite-step global-convergence property when every admissible infinite run satisfies
\[\liminf_{k\to\infty}\left(\|c(x_k)\|+\inf_y\|g_k+A_k^Ty\|\right)=0,\]
or terminates at exact first-order criticality. Sufficient normal and tangential model decreases are part of the admissibility conditions defining the family.
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: A composite-step SQP method explicitly writes each trial step as a normal component plus a tangential component. The normal component reduces linearized constraint violation inside a reserved portion of the trust region. The tangential component lies in the null space of the constraint Jacobian, preserves that feasibility improvement, and reduces the quadratic objective model. Global convergence means that every admissible infinite run approaches feasibility and first-order stationarity along a subsequence, unless exact criticality is reached finitely.
knowledge_statements.conclusion_latex: \[s_k=n_k+t_k,\quad n_k:\text{ feasibility decrease},\quad A_kt_k=0,\quad t_k:\text{ tangential model decrease},\] together with the residual convergence condition defining global convergence.
equivalent_formulations_latex: For the Euclidean norm, an off-centred tangential constraint \(\|n_k+t\|_2\leq\Delta_k\) may be replaced by a centred bound \(\|t\|_2\leq\sqrt{\Delta_k^2-\|n_k\|_2^2}\) when the additional geometry used by the method guarantees admissibility.
special_cases_latex: A Vardi-type normal step scales an approximate solution of \(A_kn+c(x_k)=0\).
A Byrd–Omojokun-type normal step approximately minimizes \(\|A_kn+c(x_k)\|\) in a smaller trust region before the tangential problem is solved.
immediate_consequences_latex: Because \(t_k\) is tangent to the linearized constraints, \(c(x_k)+A_ks_k=c(x_k)+A_kn_k\).
Reserving radius for \(t_k\) prevents the feasibility step from consuming all freedom for objective reduction.
boundary_notes: Normal and tangential components need not be orthogonal.
This definition does not prescribe one penalty update or one particular approximate subproblem solver.

notation.meaning: Normal component used to reduce linearized infeasibility.
Tangential component used to reduce the quadratic model.
Fraction of the trust-region radius reserved for the normal step.

knowledge_statements.slot_contract: State the canonical mathematical definition of the source node, with its domain, quantifiers, notation, and a precise source locator.
knowledge_statements.ambient_context_latex:
Consider \(\min f(x)\) subject to equality constraints \(c_i(x)=0\), \(i\in\mathcal E\), and inequalities \(c_i(x)\geq0\), \(i\in\mathcal I\). Define
\[\vartheta(x)=\max\{0,\max_{i\in\mathcal E}|c_i(x)|,\max_{i\in\mathcal I}[-c_i(x)]\}.\]
knowledge_statements.scope_note: Smooth finite-dimensional nonlinear programming with filter acceptance, trust-region SQP steps, and an optional restoration phase.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex:
A filter is a set \(\mathcal F\subset\mathbb R_+\times\mathbb R\) of mutually nondominated pairs \((\vartheta_j,f_j)\): for distinct pairs, \(\vartheta_i<\vartheta_j\) or \(f_i<f_j\). Given \(\gamma_\vartheta\in(0,1)\), a trial point \(x\) is acceptable when, for every \((\vartheta_j,f_j)\in\mathcal F\),
\[\vartheta(x)<(1-\gamma_\vartheta)\vartheta_j\quad\text{or}\quad f(x)<f_j-\gamma_\vartheta\vartheta(x).\]
A filter-SQP method computes an SQP trial step satisfying its trust-region and model-decrease conditions, accepts only points acceptable to the filter and the current iterate, and invokes restoration when the SQP model is incompatible. It has the filter-SQP global-convergence property if every admissible run either terminates at a restoration point stationary for the infeasibility problem, or possesses a subsequence \(x_{k_j}\to x_*\) such that
\[\vartheta(x_*)=0,\qquad \exists y_*:\ \nabla_xL(x_*,y_*)=0\]
with the appropriate sign and complementarity conditions for inequality multipliers.
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: A filter-SQP method treats objective reduction and constraint-violation reduction as separate criteria. Its filter stores mutually nondominated violation–objective pairs. A new point is acceptable only if it improves constraint violation by a fixed margin or improves the objective by a margin depending on its violation, relative to every stored pair. Global convergence is the stated alternative between an identified stationary failure of restoration and a subsequence converging to a feasible KKT point.
knowledge_statements.conclusion_latex: \[\text{acceptable}(x;\mathcal F)\iff\forall(\vartheta_j,f_j)\in\mathcal F:\ \vartheta(x)<(1-\gamma_\vartheta)\vartheta_j\ \lor\ f(x)<f_j-\gamma_\vartheta\vartheta(x),\] with the stated global-convergence alternative.
equivalent_formulations_latex: The filter represents an approximation to the efficient frontier of the bicriteria problem \(\min (\vartheta(x),f(x))\).
Nondominance without a margin is recovered formally by taking \(\gamma_\vartheta=0\), but the sourced convergence architecture requires a positive margin.
special_cases_latex: If all accepted steps are feasible, then \(\vartheta(x_k)=0\) and acceptance reduces to objective improvement.
An empty initial filter makes the first trial point subject only to acceptance relative to the current iterate and any model-agreement test.
immediate_consequences_latex: No scalar penalty parameter is needed to combine \(f\) and \(\vartheta\).
Insertion of a new filter pair removes pairs that it dominates under the filter margin.
boundary_notes: Filter acceptability alone is not a convergence theorem; model decrease, boundedness, smoothness, and restoration assumptions remain necessary.
The definition permits equality and inequality constraints but excludes nonsmooth constraint mappings.

notation.meaning: Set of stored nondominated violation–objective pairs.
