children.title: Filter Criticality Convergence
children.top_down_role: Convergence to constrained criticality under filter acceptance.

knowledge_statements.title: Filter Criticality Convergence
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: Under standard filter decrease and model-quality assumptions, infeasibility and constrained criticality cannot both remain bounded away from zero; regular feasible critical limits are KKT.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex:
Let \(\theta(x)\ge0\) measure constraint violation, and let a filter-SQP method accept an iterate only if it provides sufficient decrease in either \(\theta\) or the objective relative to every stored filter pair. Suppose iterates remain in a compact set, derivatives are Lipschitz continuous, QP models and steps satisfy uniform sufficient-decrease conditions, the filter margins are strictly positive, and restoration prevents permanent failure of the linearized constraints. Then
\[
\liminf_{k\to\infty}\max\{\theta(x_k),\chi(x_k)\}=0.
\]
If every accumulation point is feasible and satisfies a constraint qualification, every accumulation point with vanishing criticality measure is a KKT point.
assumptions_latex: Iterates are bounded, derivatives are Lipschitz continuous, and SQP models give uniform sufficient decrease.
Filter acceptance uses positive margins and requires objective or infeasibility improvement.
Restoration prevents permanent linearized-infeasibility failure, and regularity holds at feasible accumulation points.
knowledge_statements.conclusion_latex: \(\liminf_{k\to\infty}\max\{\theta(x_k),\chi(x_k)\}=0\); feasible accumulation points with \(\chi=0\) satisfy the KKT conditions.
knowledge_statements.scope_note: First-order convergence of filter-SQP without combining objective and infeasibility into one merit function.

notation.meaning: filter entry pairing infeasibility and objective value

enrichment_metadata.review_comment: The theorem kind fits filter criticality convergence, but no source is provided and the filter dominance margins, switching conditions, criticality measure, restoration behavior, and sufficient-decrease requirements are method-specific. The displayed limit-inferior claim therefore cannot be validated from the stated qualitative assumptions.

knowledge_statements.slot_contract: State the canonical mathematical definition of the source node, with its domain, quantifiers, notation, and a precise source locator.
knowledge_statements.ambient_context_latex:
Let \(\{x_k\}\) be generated by a smooth filter-SQP method. Let \(\vartheta(x)\geq0\) be a continuous feasibility measure and \(\chi(x)\geq0\) a continuous constrained first-order criticality measure satisfying, at feasible points,
\[\chi(x)=0\iff x\text{ satisfies first-order constrained criticality}.\]
knowledge_statements.scope_note: Subsequential first-order convergence for filter-accepted SQP iterates when restoration succeeds. This is not a full-sequence or rate statement.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex:
The sequence has filter criticality convergence if either it terminates at a reported restoration failure, or there exists an infinite index set \(K\) and a point \(x_*\) such that
\[x_k\to x_*,\qquad \vartheta(x_k)\to0,\qquad \chi(x_k)\to0\qquad(k\in K).\]
Equivalently, by continuity,
\[\vartheta(x_*)=0,\qquad \chi(x_*)=0.\]
For a normal–tangential filter-SQP method, one admissible measure is the optimal value
\[\chi_k=\left|\min_d\ \nabla f(x_k^N)^Td\right|,\]
where the minimization is over \(\|d\|\leq1\) and directions satisfying the linearized equality and inequality constraints at \(x_k\). Filter criticality convergence means that filter acceptance cannot support an infinite admissible run whose feasibility or constrained descent measure remains uniformly bounded away from zero along every subsequence.
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: Filter criticality convergence is a subsequential property. Unless restoration terminates with a declared failure, the sequence contains a subsequence converging to a point whose constraint violation and continuous constrained criticality measure both vanish. At feasible points, vanishing of that measure is required to characterize first-order constrained stationarity.
knowledge_statements.conclusion_latex: \[\exists K\subseteq\mathbb N,\ |K|=\infty:\quad \lim_{k\in K}\vartheta(x_k)=0,\qquad \lim_{k\in K}\chi(x_k)=0,\] unless restoration terminates unsuccessfully.
equivalent_formulations_latex: If \(\{x_k\}_{k\in K}\) is bounded and \(\vartheta\) and \(\chi\) are continuous, the residual formulation is equivalent to the existence of a feasible first-order critical accumulation point.
For equality constraints under a regularity condition, one may use \(\chi(x)=\inf_y\|\nabla f(x)+\nabla c(x)^Ty\|\).
special_cases_latex: For an unconstrained problem, \(\vartheta\equiv0\) and \(\chi(x)=\|\nabla f(x)\|\).
For feasible iterates, only \(\chi(x_k)\to0\) remains to be established.
immediate_consequences_latex: Any accumulation point of the convergent subsequence is feasible and first-order critical.
The definition rules out a successful infinite run with both residuals uniformly positive.
boundary_notes: The property allows other subsequences or limit points to behave differently.
An infeasible stationary point of the restoration objective is a distinct termination outcome, not a constrained critical point of the original problem.

notation.meaning: Infinite index set selecting a convergent critical subsequence.
Point obtained after the normal feasibility step.

children.title: Filter-Restoration Convergence
children.top_down_role: Global theory incorporating restoration outcomes.

knowledge_statements.title: Filter-Restoration Convergence
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: Filter restoration either exposes stationary infeasibility or produces asymptotic feasibility; feasible regular limits with vanishing SQP criticality are KKT points.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex: Consider a filter-SQP method with an optimization phase and a restoration phase that seeks to reduce a continuous violation measure \(\theta(x)\). Suppose iterates stay in a compact set, derivatives are Lipschitz continuous, accepted optimization steps satisfy filter decrease, and every restoration call either returns an acceptable point with a fixed fraction of predicted feasibility improvement or converges to a stationary point of the feasibility problem \(\min\theta(x)\). Then either restoration identifies an infeasible stationary point with \(\theta>0\), or \(\theta(x_k)\to0\) along a subsequence and every feasible regular accumulation point at which the SQP criticality measure vanishes satisfies the KKT conditions.
assumptions_latex: Iterates are bounded, derivatives are Lipschitz continuous, and optimization steps satisfy filter decrease.
Each restoration phase achieves uniform predicted feasibility progress or approaches stationarity for \(\min\theta\).
A constraint qualification holds at feasible accumulation points considered for KKT convergence.
knowledge_statements.conclusion_latex: Either an infeasible stationary point of \(\min\theta\) is obtained, or a subsequence becomes feasible and each feasible regular zero-criticality accumulation point is KKT.
knowledge_statements.scope_note: Global alternatives for filter-SQP with an explicit feasibility-restoration phase.

enrichment_metadata.review_comment: The theorem kind and restoration-focused scope fit the leaf, but the restoration acceptance rule, predicted feasibility reduction, stationarity notion for the generally nonsmooth violation function, and optimization-phase criticality mechanism are not defined. A specific filter-restoration SQP theorem is required to justify the proposed infeasible-stationary versus feasible-subsequence alternative.

knowledge_statements.slot_contract: State the canonical mathematical definition of the source node, with its domain, quantifiers, notation, and a precise source locator.
knowledge_statements.ambient_context_latex: Let \(\vartheta:\mathbb R^n\to\mathbb R_+\) measure nonlinear constraint violation. At an iterate \(x_k\), suppose the trust-region SQP subproblem is declared incompatible when its linearized constraints are infeasible or when its normal step leaves insufficient radius for model reduction.
knowledge_statements.scope_note: Smooth finite-dimensional filter-SQP with a restoration phase that approximately minimizes constraint violation.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex:
A restoration phase starting from \(x_k\) generates points for the auxiliary problem
\[\min_{x\in\mathbb R^n}\vartheta(x).\]
It succeeds if it returns \(x_k^R=x_k+r_k\) and a radius \(\Delta_{k+1}>0\) such that: (i) the SQP subproblem at \(x_k^R\) is compatible; and (ii) \(x_k^R\) is acceptable for the current filter. It fails stationarily if it generates a limiting point \(\bar x\) satisfying
\[\vartheta(\bar x)>0,\qquad 0\in\partial\vartheta(\bar x),\]
with the derivative notion appropriate to the chosen violation norm. A filter-SQP run has filter-restoration convergence if every restoration invocation has one of these two outcomes and, if all invocations succeed, the outer iterates possess a subsequence converging to a feasible first-order critical point of the original nonlinear program. Thus the terminal alternatives are
\[\text{feasible constrained criticality}\quad\text{or}\quad\text{certified stationary failure of feasibility restoration}.\]
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: Restoration approximately minimizes a constraint-violation function whenever the normal SQP model is incompatible. Restoration succeeds only when it produces a filter-acceptable point from which a compatible SQP step can again be computed. It fails stationarily when it converges to an infeasible stationary point of the violation problem. Filter-restoration convergence is the resulting alternative: successful restoration supports a subsequence converging to a feasible critical point, while unsuccessful restoration identifies stationary failure of the feasibility search.
knowledge_statements.conclusion_latex: \[\text{restoration outcome}\in\{\text{acceptable compatible point},\ \bar x:\vartheta(\bar x)>0,\ 0\in\partial\vartheta(\bar x)\},\] and perpetual successful restoration implies subsequential constrained criticality.
equivalent_formulations_latex: For differentiable \(\vartheta\), stationary restoration failure is \(\vartheta(\bar x)>0\) and \(\nabla\vartheta(\bar x)=0\).
For the maximum violation measure, \(0\in\partial\vartheta(\bar x)\) expresses nonsmooth first-order criticality of the feasibility problem.
special_cases_latex: If the current SQP subproblem is compatible, restoration is not invoked.
If restoration reaches \(\vartheta(x)=0\), feasibility is attained, although compatibility must still be checked.
immediate_consequences_latex: An infeasible restoration limit is distinguished from a KKT point of the original problem.
A restoration point must improve enough to pass the filter; merely enlarging the trust-region radius is not a successful restoration step.
boundary_notes: Stationarity of the violation measure does not prove that the original constraints are globally infeasible.
The definition does not prescribe the internal restoration algorithm or violation norm.

notation.meaning: Subdifferential of the selected violation measure.

children.title: Feasible-SQP Global Convergence
children.top_down_role: Global convergence families constrained to feasible iterate sequences.

knowledge_statements.title: Feasible-SQP Global Convergence
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: Sufficient merit decrease along bounded feasible iterates forces the stationarity residual to zero, so every accumulation point satisfying a constraint qualification is KKT-stationary.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex: Consider minimizing \(f(x)\) subject to \(h(x)=0\) and \(g(x)\le 0\). Let every SQP iterate \(x_k\) be feasible, remain in a compact set, and satisfy \(M(x_k)-M(x_{k+1})\ge \kappa\chi(x_k)^2\), where \(M\) is bounded below, \(\kappa>0\), and \(\chi\) is a continuous KKT-stationarity measure on the feasible set. Then \(\sum_{k=0}^{\infty}\chi(x_k)^2<\infty\), hence \(\chi(x_k)\to0\). If a constraint qualification holds at every accumulation point, each such point admits multipliers satisfying the KKT conditions.
assumptions_latex: \(f,h,g\) are continuously differentiable with Lipschitz derivatives on a neighborhood of the iterates.
\(M\) is bounded below on the feasible level set and \(\kappa>0\).
A constraint qualification holds at every accumulation point.
knowledge_statements.conclusion_latex: \(\chi(x_k)\to0\), and every accumulation point of \((x_k)\) is a KKT point.
knowledge_statements.scope_note: Abstract accumulation-point theorem for feasible-iterate SQP with sufficient merit decrease.

notation.meaning: globalization merit function evaluated on feasible iterates

enrichment_metadata.review_comment: The telescoping decrease argument is mathematically plausible, but the cited locators do not inspectably establish this feasible-iterate SQP theorem. In particular, the properties connecting the abstract measure chi to KKT stationarity under the stated constraint qualification must be specified and sourced.

knowledge_statements.slot_contract: State the canonical mathematical definition of the source node, with its domain, quantifiers, notation, and a precise source locator.
knowledge_statements.ambient_context_latex:
Let \(\mathcal X=\{x\in\mathbb R^n:c(x)=0,\ h(x)\geq0\}\) and consider \(\min_{x\in\mathcal X}f(x)\), with continuously differentiable data. Let \(T_{\mathcal X}(x)\) denote the tangent cone and define
\[\chi(x)=\max_{d\in T_{\mathcal X}(x),\ \|d\|\leq1}-\nabla f(x)^Td.\]
knowledge_statements.scope_note: Smooth finite-dimensional SQP variants whose accepted iterates remain feasible for the nonlinear constraints, not merely for their linearizations.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex:
A feasible-SQP method is an SQP iteration producing accepted iterates \(x_k\) such that
\[x_0\in\mathcal X\quad\Longrightarrow\quad x_k\in\mathcal X\quad\text{for every }k.\]
A trial displacement may combine an SQP direction with a retraction or correction \(r_k\), but acceptance must satisfy
\[x_{k+1}=x_k+s_k+r_k\in\mathcal X.\]
The method has feasible-SQP global convergence on a problem class \(\mathcal P\) if every admissible infinite sequence generated from a feasible initial point satisfies
\[\liminf_{k\to\infty}\chi(x_k)=0,\]
or terminates at an iterate with \(\chi(x_k)=0\). Under a constraint qualification, \(\chi(x)=0\) is equivalent to the existence of multipliers satisfying KKT stationarity, dual feasibility, and complementarity. Feasibility is an invariant of the accepted sequence, whereas stationarity is the asymptotic convergence target.
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: A feasible-SQP method starts from a feasible point and accepts only points satisfying the original nonlinear constraints. Corrections or retractions may be used to turn an SQP trial direction into a feasible displacement. Its global-convergence property requires every admissible infinite run to approach constrained first-order criticality along a subsequence, measured by the maximum feasible descent, unless it terminates at a critical point.
knowledge_statements.conclusion_latex: \[x_0\in\mathcal X\Rightarrow(\forall k\ x_k\in\mathcal X),\qquad \liminf_{k\to\infty}\chi(x_k)=0\] for every admissible nonterminating run.
equivalent_formulations_latex: If \(\mathcal X\) is convex, \(\chi(x)=0\) is equivalent to \(-\nabla f(x)\in N_{\mathcal X}(x)\).
Under LICQ for a smooth nonlinear program, \(\chi(x)=0\) at a feasible point is equivalent to the KKT first-order conditions.
special_cases_latex: For equality constraints defining a smooth manifold, a retraction \(R_x(s)\in\mathcal X\) may replace the additive correction.
For bound constraints, projection or an active-set step can enforce feasibility exactly.
immediate_consequences_latex: The feasibility residual is identically zero on accepted iterates.
No restoration phase is needed to recover feasibility after an accepted step, although feasibility-preserving step construction may itself fail.
boundary_notes: Linearized feasibility alone does not make an SQP method feasible-SQP.
No inspected source in the supplied corpus established this exact named family and residual formulation.

notation.meaning: Tangent cone to the feasible set.

children.title: SQP Complexity-Termination Theorem Family
children.top_down_role: Modern deterministic work measures and computable termination evidence for SQP.

knowledge_statements.slot_contract: State the canonical mathematical definition of the source node, with its domain, quantifiers, notation, and a precise source locator.
knowledge_statements.ambient_context_latex: Let an SQP algorithm generate information states \(z_k=(x_k,y_k,\mathcal M_k)\). Let \(R(z_k)\geq0\) be a computable optimality or infeasibility residual, and let \(W_k\geq0\) count a specified unit of work through iteration \(k\).
knowledge_statements.scope_note: Deterministic finite-dimensional SQP. This is a definition of a family of quantitative results, not a particular complexity theorem or exponent.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex:
An SQP complexity–termination result is a statement indexed by tolerances \(\varepsilon\in\mathcal E\subset\mathbb R_+^q\) that specifies: (i) a stopping set
\[\mathcal T(\varepsilon)=\{z:R_i(z)\leq\varepsilon_i\ \text{for all required residuals }i\};\]
(ii) a work measure \(W_k\), such as iterations, evaluations, matrix–vector products, or inner QP work; (iii) a bound \(B(\varepsilon,\mathcal D)\), depending only on tolerances and stated problem/algorithm data \(\mathcal D\); and (iv) a certificate map \(C(z_k)\) identifying the termination status. The result belongs to the family when it guarantees
\[\exists k:\ z_k\in\mathcal T(\varepsilon),\qquad W_k\leq B(\varepsilon,\mathcal D),\]
or returns a separately defined failure certificate, such as stationary infeasibility. The work unit, residuals, oracle, and failure outcomes are part of the mathematical specification; changing any of them defines a different complexity–termination result.
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: An SQP complexity–termination result defines a tolerance-dependent stopping set, an explicit unit of computational work, a worst-case bound on that work, and a computable status certificate. It guarantees that an admissible run reaches the stopping set within the bound or returns one of the separately defined failure certificates. Evaluation, iteration, and inner-solve bounds are distinct members of the family because they count different work.
knowledge_statements.conclusion_latex: \[W_{k(\varepsilon)}\leq B(\varepsilon,\mathcal D),\qquad k(\varepsilon)=\inf\{k:z_k\in\mathcal T(\varepsilon)\},\] unless a specified alternative certificate is returned first.
equivalent_formulations_latex: A bound on the hitting time \(k(\varepsilon)\) is iteration complexity when \(W_k=k\).
If each iteration uses at most \(q\) oracle calls, an iteration bound \(k(\varepsilon)\leq B\) implies the evaluation bound \(N_{\mathrm{eval}}(\varepsilon)\leq qB\).
special_cases_latex: First-order results use feasibility and KKT-stationarity residuals.
Second-order results add a constrained-curvature residual.
Inexact-work results include residual-dependent inner-solve costs in \(W_k\).
immediate_consequences_latex: A termination tolerance has no complexity meaning until the counted work unit is fixed.
A certificate can be valid without providing a sharp work bound, and a work bound can target only one certificate class.
boundary_notes: The definition does not assign a universal polynomial order to SQP.
No supplied inspected source supported this exact modern taxonomy.

notation.meaning: Cumulative specified work through iteration k.

review_flags: The supplied classical SQP sources do not provide an exact source for the stated modern complexity-and-certificate family.
knowledge_statements.title: SQP Complexity–Termination Result Family

children.title: Deterministic SQP Evaluation Complexity
children.top_down_role: Worst-case evaluation families for deterministic SQP frameworks.

knowledge_statements.slot_contract: State the canonical mathematical definition of the source node, with its domain, quantifiers, notation, and a precise source locator.
knowledge_statements.ambient_context_latex: Fix a deterministic SQP algorithm and an oracle returning specified quantities among \(f(x)\), \(c(x)\), their first derivatives, and possibly Lagrangian second derivatives. Let \(R(x,y)\) be the chosen termination residual.
knowledge_statements.scope_note: Worst-case oracle evaluation count for deterministic smooth constrained optimization; linear algebra and inner iterations are excluded unless explicitly charged as oracle calls.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex:
For tolerance \(\varepsilon>0\), define the first successful termination index
\[k_\varepsilon=\inf\{k:R(x_k,y_k)\leq\varepsilon\}.\]
If \(e_k\) is the number of prescribed oracle evaluations performed through iteration \(k\), the deterministic SQP evaluation complexity is
\[N_{\mathrm{eval}}(\varepsilon;\mathcal P)=\sup_{P\in\mathcal P}\sup_{z_0\in\mathcal I(P)} e_{k_\varepsilon},\]
where \(\mathcal P\) is the stated problem class and \(\mathcal I(P)\) the admissible initial states. A bound \(N_{\mathrm{eval}}(\varepsilon;\mathcal P)\leq B(\varepsilon)\) is valid only when the oracle contents, caching convention, unsuccessful-trial evaluations, derivative order, problem constants, and termination residual are fixed. If no qualifying iterate is produced, the value is \(+\infty\) unless the specification admits and separately counts a failure certificate.
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: Deterministic SQP evaluation complexity is the worst-case number of calls to a fixed derivative oracle before the algorithm first meets a specified termination tolerance. The maximum ranges over a declared problem class and admissible initial states. The oracle contents and counting conventions are part of the definition, so bounds counting only function values cannot be compared directly with bounds counting functions and derivatives together.
knowledge_statements.conclusion_latex: \[N_{\mathrm{eval}}(\varepsilon;\mathcal P)=\sup_{P,z_0}e_{k_\varepsilon},\qquad k_\varepsilon=\inf\{k:R(x_k,y_k)\leq\varepsilon\}.\]
equivalent_formulations_latex: If every iteration uses at most \(q\) oracle calls and the iteration complexity is \(K(\varepsilon)\), then \(N_{\mathrm{eval}}(\varepsilon)\leq qK(\varepsilon)\).
Separate counts \(N_f,N_c,N_J,N_H\) may replace a scalar count; a scalarization requires declared weights or a maximum convention.
special_cases_latex: A first-order oracle returns \(f,c,\nabla f,\nabla c\).
A second-order oracle additionally returns Hessian or Hessian–vector information.
immediate_consequences_latex: Rejected trial points contribute to evaluation complexity whenever they require new oracle calls.
Warm starts can reduce algebraic work without changing the evaluation count.
boundary_notes: The definition is deterministic and excludes expectations and high-probability bounds.
No exact authoritative SQP evaluation-complexity source was established from the supplied corpus.

notation.meaning: First index satisfying the termination tolerance.
Cumulative oracle evaluations through iteration k.
Problem class over which worst-case complexity is taken.

review_flags: A precise source fixing the SQP oracle, residual, and evaluation-count convention is required.
knowledge_statements.title: Deterministic SQP Evaluation Complexity

children.title: First-Order SQP Complexity
children.top_down_role: Evaluation-complexity families for approximate first-order constrained criticality.

knowledge_statements.title: First-Order SQP Complexity
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: Quadratic decrease in the KKT residual yields an order epsilon-to-the-minus-two bound on accepted SQP iterations and function-constraint evaluations.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex: Let \(M_k\ge M_{\inf}\) be the globalization measure of a deterministic SQP method and let \(\chi_k\ge0\) be its first-order KKT residual. Suppose every accepted iteration with \(\chi_k>\varepsilon\) satisfies \(M_k-M_{k+1}\ge\kappa\chi_k^2\), and at most \(q\) objective-constraint evaluations occur per accepted iteration. With \(\Delta=M_0-M_{\inf}\), an iterate satisfying \(\chi_k\le\varepsilon\) is obtained after at most \(\lceil\Delta/(\kappa\varepsilon^2)\rceil\) accepted iterations and at most \(q\lceil\Delta/(\kappa\varepsilon^2)\rceil+q\) evaluations.
assumptions_latex: \(M_k\ge M_{\inf}\) for every iteration.
\(M_k-M_{k+1}\ge\kappa\chi_k^2\) whenever \(\chi_k>\varepsilon\), with \(\kappa>0\).
Each accepted iteration uses at most \(q\) objective-constraint evaluations.
knowledge_statements.conclusion_latex: \(N_{\mathrm{eval}}(\varepsilon)\le q\lceil\Delta/(\kappa\varepsilon^2)\rceil+q=O(\varepsilon^{-2})\).
knowledge_statements.scope_note: Conditional evaluation bound derived from uniform decrease in a first-order KKT residual.

notation.meaning: merit, filter-envelope, or potential value used in the decrease accounting

enrichment_metadata.review_comment: The conditional summation bound is plausible and the complexity-bound kind fits the leaf, but no source identifies an SQP family for which the assumed decrease and uniform evaluation cost hold. The meaning and counting of an objective-constraint evaluation also require a family-specific source.

knowledge_statements.slot_contract: State the canonical mathematical definition of the source node, with its domain, quantifiers, notation, and a precise source locator.
knowledge_statements.ambient_context_latex:
For equality constraints \(c(x)=0\), define
\[r_F(x)=\|c(x)\|,\qquad r_S(x,y)=\|\nabla f(x)+\nabla c(x)^Ty\|.\]
For inequalities, augment these by dual-feasibility and complementarity residuals.
knowledge_statements.scope_note: Approximate first-order KKT criticality for deterministic smooth finite-dimensional SQP; the definition does not select a universal complexity exponent.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex:
Given tolerances \(\varepsilon_F,\varepsilon_S>0\), a pair \((x,y)\) is an \((\varepsilon_F,\varepsilon_S)\)-first-order SQP point when
\[r_F(x)\leq\varepsilon_F,
\qquad r_S(x,y)\leq\varepsilon_S,\]
and, for inequality constraints, the stated approximate sign and complementarity conditions also hold. For a fixed SQP algorithm and work count \(W_k\), its first-order complexity is the worst-case hitting-work function
\[N_1(\varepsilon_F,\varepsilon_S)=\sup_{P,z_0}W_{k_1},\quad
k_1=\inf\{k:(x_k,y_k)\text{ is an }(\varepsilon_F,\varepsilon_S)\text{-first-order point}\}.\]
A claimed order such as \(O(\varepsilon^{-p})\) is meaningful only after specifying how \(\varepsilon_F\) and \(\varepsilon_S\) are coupled and what \(W_k\) counts.
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: First-order SQP complexity measures the worst-case work required to produce an approximately feasible primal point and a multiplier estimate with a small Lagrangian-gradient residual. Inequality-constrained formulations must also control multiplier signs and complementarity. The tolerance relation and the counted work unit are part of the definition; no universal exponent follows from the phrase first-order SQP complexity alone.
knowledge_statements.conclusion_latex: \[N_1(\varepsilon_F,\varepsilon_S)=\sup_{P,z_0}W_{\inf\{k:r_F(x_k)\leq\varepsilon_F,\ r_S(x_k,y_k)\leq\varepsilon_S\}}.\]
equivalent_formulations_latex: A scalar residual \(R_1(x,y)=\max\{r_F(x),r_S(x,y)\}\) yields the single-tolerance target \(R_1(x,y)\leq\varepsilon\).
For regular equality constraints, minimizing over multipliers gives \(r_S^{\min}(x)=\inf_y\|\nabla f(x)+\nabla c(x)^Ty\|\).
special_cases_latex: For unconstrained optimization, \(r_F\equiv0\) and \(r_S=\|\nabla f\|\).
For feasible-SQP, \(r_F(x_k)=0\) for all accepted iterates.
immediate_consequences_latex: A small stationarity residual without small feasibility residual is not an approximate KKT certificate.
Different multiplier-selection rules can yield different measured stationarity residuals at the same primal point.
boundary_notes: The definition does not include second-order curvature information.
No source supporting a particular SQP first-order complexity exponent was identified.
review_flags: The residual target is standard, but the exact SQP complexity framework and any rate require an independently inspected modern source.
knowledge_statements.title: First-Order SQP Complexity Target

children.title: Second-Order SQP Complexity
children.top_down_role: Evaluation-complexity families for approximate second-order constrained criticality.

knowledge_statements.title: Second-Order SQP Complexity
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: Under quadratic gradient-residual decrease and cubic negative-curvature decrease, approximate second-order criticality needs order epsilon-g minus two plus epsilon-H minus three evaluations.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex: Let \(\chi_k\) be a first-order KKT residual and \(\theta_k\) the smallest Lagrangian-Hessian curvature on the computed critical subspace. Suppose each accepted nonterminal iteration decreases a lower-bounded potential by at least \(\kappa_g\varepsilon_g^2\) when \(\chi_k>\varepsilon_g\), or by at least \(\kappa_H\varepsilon_H^3\) when \(\theta_k<-\varepsilon_H\). If the initial potential gap is \(\Delta\) and each accepted iteration costs at most \(q\) evaluations, then a point with \(\chi_k\le\varepsilon_g\) and \(\theta_k\ge-\varepsilon_H\) occurs within \(q\lceil\Delta(\kappa_g^{-1}\varepsilon_g^{-2}+\kappa_H^{-1}\varepsilon_H^{-3})\rceil+q\) evaluations.
assumptions_latex: The globalization potential is bounded below with initial gap \(\Delta<\infty\).
Every nonterminal accepted iteration achieves one of the stated uniform decreases.
At most \(q\) evaluations are used per accepted iteration.
knowledge_statements.conclusion_latex: \(N_{\mathrm{eval}}=O(\varepsilon_g^{-2}+\varepsilon_H^{-3})\) for \(\chi_k\le\varepsilon_g\) and \(\theta_k\ge-\varepsilon_H\).
knowledge_statements.scope_note: Conditional evaluation bound for approximate first- and second-order constrained criticality.

notation.meaning: least computed Lagrangian curvature on the critical subspace

enrichment_metadata.review_comment: The displayed order follows conditionally from the asserted decreases, but no authoritative source identifies an SQP variant, critical-subspace construction, or evaluation model satisfying them. Those details materially determine the second-order complexity claim.

knowledge_statements.slot_contract: State the canonical mathematical definition of the source node, with its domain, quantifiers, notation, and a precise source locator.
knowledge_statements.ambient_context_latex: Let \(L(x,y)=f(x)+y^Tc(x)\) for equality constraints, and let \(Z(x)\) have orthonormal columns spanning \(\ker\nabla c(x)\). Define the reduced Lagrangian Hessian \(H_R(x,y)=Z(x)^T\nabla_{xx}^2L(x,y)Z(x)\).
knowledge_statements.scope_note: Smooth twice-differentiable finite-dimensional SQP near a regular constraint manifold. Inequality cases require a declared critical cone rather than merely the equality null space.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex:
For tolerances \(\varepsilon_F,\varepsilon_S,\varepsilon_H>0\), a pair \((x,y)\) is an approximate second-order SQP point when
\[\|c(x)\|\leq\varepsilon_F,\qquad
\|\nabla_xL(x,y)\|\leq\varepsilon_S,\qquad
\lambda_{\min}(H_R(x,y))\geq-\varepsilon_H.\]
For inequalities, the last condition is imposed on the declared approximate critical cone and the first-order conditions include dual feasibility and complementarity. Given a work count \(W_k\), second-order SQP complexity is
\[N_2(\varepsilon_F,\varepsilon_S,\varepsilon_H)=\sup_{P,z_0}W_{k_2},\]
where \(k_2\) is the first index satisfying all three tolerance conditions. The definition requires an implementable convention for estimating the smallest constrained curvature and charging that computation to \(W_k\).
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: Second-order SQP complexity is the worst-case work needed to obtain approximate feasibility, approximate KKT stationarity, and near-nonnegative Lagrangian curvature in feasible critical directions. For equality constraints, curvature is measured by the smallest eigenvalue of the reduced Hessian. Inequality constraints require a critical-cone convention. Computing or estimating negative curvature must be included in the stated work model.
knowledge_statements.conclusion_latex: \[N_2(\varepsilon_F,\varepsilon_S,\varepsilon_H)=\sup_{P,z_0}W_{\inf\{k:r_F\leq\varepsilon_F,\ r_S\leq\varepsilon_S,\ \lambda_{\min}(H_R)\geq-\varepsilon_H\}}.\]
equivalent_formulations_latex: The curvature condition is equivalent to \(d^T\nabla_{xx}^2L(x,y)d\geq-\varepsilon_H\|d\|^2\) for every \(d\in\ker\nabla c(x)\).
A negative-curvature residual is \(r_H(x,y)=\max\{0,-\lambda_{\min}(H_R(x,y))\}\).
special_cases_latex: For unconstrained optimization, \(Z=I\) and the condition becomes \(\lambda_{\min}(\nabla^2f(x))\geq-\varepsilon_H\).
At exact tolerances, the conditions reduce to second-order necessary KKT conditions under regularity.
immediate_consequences_latex: Every approximate second-order point is also an approximate first-order point at the same first-order tolerances.
A first-order certificate alone cannot exclude a strict feasible saddle.
boundary_notes: Positive semidefiniteness is necessary, not sufficient, for a constrained local minimum.
No exact modern SQP second-order complexity source was found among the supplied hints.

notation.meaning: Orthonormal basis for equality-feasible tangent directions.

review_flags: An authoritative source is required for the exact approximate critical cone, curvature computation, and complexity bound.
knowledge_statements.title: Second-Order SQP Complexity Target

children.title: Inexact SQP Work Complexity
children.top_down_role: Complexity accounting for approximate QP and KKT solves.

knowledge_statements.title: Inexact SQP Work Complexity
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: Inexact SQP work equals the outer evaluation count plus the accumulated cost of residual-controlled approximate KKT or QP solves.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex: Suppose an SQP method terminates within \(N(\varepsilon)\) outer iterations when each quadratic-program KKT system is solved to residual tolerance \(\eta_k\le\bar\eta\chi_k\), where \(0<\bar\eta<1\). If the inner solver uses at most \(W_k(\eta_k)\) Hessian- or Jacobian-vector products at iteration \(k\), then total inner work before termination is at most \(\sum_{k=0}^{N(\varepsilon)-1}W_k(\eta_k)\), while derivative-evaluation work is at most \(N(\varepsilon)\) batches. In particular, if \(W_k(\eta)\le a_k+b_k\log(1/\eta)\), the corresponding sum gives the explicit work bound.
assumptions_latex: The forcing rule satisfies \(\eta_k\le\bar\eta\chi_k\) with \(0<\bar\eta<1\).
The exact stated outer guarantee remains valid under this forcing rule.
\(W_k(\eta_k)\) bounds inner matrix-vector products at iteration \(k\).
knowledge_statements.conclusion_latex: \(W_{\mathrm{total}}(\varepsilon)\le\sum_{k=0}^{N(\varepsilon)-1}W_k(\eta_k)\), with at most \(N(\varepsilon)\) derivative-evaluation batches.
knowledge_statements.scope_note: Outer evaluations plus accumulated inner linear-algebra work under residual-controlled SQP solves.

notation.meaning: inner KKT or QP residual tolerance

enrichment_metadata.review_comment: The accumulated inner-work expression is largely accounting by definition. A source is needed for the forcing rule, preservation of the outer guarantee, the inner iteration model, and the assertion of at most one derivative-evaluation batch per outer iteration.

children.title: SQP Termination Certificates
children.top_down_role: Computable evidence distinguishing constrained stationarity, feasibility failure, and unresolved model failure.

knowledge_statements.slot_contract: State the canonical mathematical definition of the source node, with its domain, quantifiers, notation, and a precise source locator.
knowledge_statements.ambient_context_latex: Let \(z=(x,y,\mathcal M,\mathcal I)\) be the computed SQP state, including primal and dual estimates, current model information, and inner-solver diagnostics. Let \(\mathcal S\) be a finite set of status labels.
knowledge_statements.scope_note: Computable deterministic termination evidence. The system separates approximate solution, feasibility failure, and unresolved numerical or model failure.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex:
An SQP termination-certificate system is a partial map
\[C:\mathcal Z\to\mathcal S\times\mathcal W,\qquad C(z)=(s,w),\]
where \(w\) is finite computed witness data and each status \(s\) has a validity predicate \(V_s(z,w)\). A certificate is valid only if
\[C(z)=(s,w)\quad\Longrightarrow\quad V_s(z,w)=\mathrm{true}.\]
At minimum, distinct predicates may represent: approximate primal-dual stationarity; approximate second-order criticality; stationary infeasibility of a restoration problem; and unresolved model or inner-solve failure. The predicates must be mutually interpretable and must expose their tolerances. A run terminates certifiably only when some predicate is verified from available data; exhaustion of an iteration limit is an unresolved status unless it independently satisfies another predicate.
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: An SQP termination-certificate system maps the computed algorithm state to a status and finite witness data. Every status has an explicit predicate that can be checked from those data. Approximate stationarity, second-order criticality, stationary infeasibility, and unresolved numerical failure are distinct outcomes. Reaching an iteration limit is not by itself an optimization certificate.
knowledge_statements.conclusion_latex: \[C(z)=(s,w)\Rightarrow V_s(z,w),\qquad s\in\mathcal S.\]
equivalent_formulations_latex: The certificate system may be viewed as a disjoint union of computable acceptance sets \(\mathcal C_s=\{z:\exists w\ V_s(z,w)\}\).
A Boolean stopping test is the special case \(|\mathcal S|=2\) with statuses certified and continue.
special_cases_latex: A KKT residual vector and tolerances form a primal-dual stationarity witness.
A negative-curvature estimate augments the witness for a second-order status.
A restoration criticality residual with positive violation supports a stationary-infeasibility status.
immediate_consequences_latex: Statuses with different mathematical meanings must not share an undifferentiated success flag.
Certificate tolerances permit downstream users to assess the quality of termination.
boundary_notes: A certificate validates a stated predicate, not global optimality unless that predicate and its assumptions imply it.
No inspected source supported this exact certificate-system taxonomy.

notation.meaning: Validity predicate associated with status s.

review_flags: The exact multi-status SQP certificate taxonomy requires an authoritative source.
knowledge_statements.title: SQP Termination-Certificate System

children.title: Primal-Dual Stationarity Certificates
children.top_down_role: Termination evidence based on approximate constrained stationarity.

knowledge_statements.title: Primal-Dual Stationarity Certificates
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: For explicitly dimensioned smooth equality and inequality constraints, a point and its multipliers certify approximate KKT stationarity when primal feasibility, dual feasibility, Lagrangian-gradient, and complementarity residuals satisfy the declared tolerance.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex: Let \(f:\mathbb{R}^n\to\mathbb{R}\), \(h:\mathbb{R}^n\to\mathbb{R}^m\), and \(g:\mathbb{R}^n\to\mathbb{R}^p\) be continuously differentiable, and consider minimizing \(f(x)\) subject to \(h(x)=0\) and \(g(x)\le 0\). For \(\varepsilon\ge 0\), a tuple \((x,\lambda,\mu)\in\mathbb{R}^n\times\mathbb{R}^m\times\mathbb{R}^p\) is an \(\varepsilon\)-primal-dual stationarity certificate if \(\mu\ge0\) and \[\max\!\left\{\|h(x)\|,\|[g(x)]_+\|,\|\nabla f(x)+J_h(x)^{\mathsf T}\lambda+J_g(x)^{\mathsf T}\mu\|,\|\mu\odot g(x)\|\right\}\le\varepsilon.\] The quantities in this test are evaluable from the reported point, multipliers, function values, and first derivatives. For \(\varepsilon=0\), these conditions are exactly the KKT system under the inequality convention \(g(x)\le0\).
assumptions_latex: \(f:\mathbb{R}^n\to\mathbb{R}\), \(h:\mathbb{R}^n\to\mathbb{R}^m\), and \(g:\mathbb{R}^n\to\mathbb{R}^p\) are continuously differentiable at \(x\).
Inequalities use the convention \(g(x)\le0\).
The tolerance satisfies \(\varepsilon\ge0\).
knowledge_statements.conclusion_latex: The tuple certifies \(\varepsilon\)-approximate primal feasibility, dual feasibility, stationarity, and complementarity; when \(\varepsilon=0\), it satisfies the KKT conditions.
knowledge_statements.scope_note: Residual certificate for approximate KKT conditions in finite-dimensional smooth nonlinear programming.

notation.meaning: componentwise positive part of a vector

source_witnesses.locator: 2.6 Primal-Dual Methods Not Utilizing a Penalty Function p. 153

locator_traceability.matched_excerpt: - 2.6 Primal-Dual Methods Not Utilizing a Penalty Function p. 153

knowledge_statements.slot_contract: State the canonical mathematical definition of the source node, with its domain, quantifiers, notation, and a precise source locator.
knowledge_statements.ambient_context_latex:
Consider \(\min f(x)\) subject to \(c(x)=0\) and \(h(x)\geq0\), with Lagrangian
\[L(x,y,z)=f(x)+y^Tc(x)-z^Th(x),\qquad z\geq0.\]
knowledge_statements.scope_note: Smooth finite-dimensional nonlinear programming with equality and inequality constraints; residual norms and scaling must be declared.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex:
For tolerances \(\varepsilon_F,\varepsilon_D,\varepsilon_C,\varepsilon_S\geq0\), a tuple \((x,y,z)\) is a primal-dual stationarity certificate when
\[\|c(x)\|\leq\varepsilon_F,\qquad
\|[-h(x)]_+\|\leq\varepsilon_F,\]
\[\|[-z]_+\|\leq\varepsilon_D,\qquad
\|z\odot h(x)\|\leq\varepsilon_C,\]
and
\[\|\nabla f(x)+\nabla c(x)^Ty-\nabla h(x)^Tz\|\leq\varepsilon_S.\]
The certificate consists of the primal point, multiplier estimates, residual vector, tolerances, norm, and any scaling used. At zero tolerances these conditions are the KKT feasibility, dual-feasibility, complementarity, and stationarity equations. With positive tolerances, the certificate asserts only membership in the stated approximate KKT set.
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: A primal-dual stationarity certificate records a primal point and multiplier estimates whose equality violation, inequality violation, dual-sign violation, complementarity residual, and Lagrangian-gradient residual are all within declared tolerances. It must also record the norm and scaling used. Zero tolerances recover the KKT equations; positive tolerances certify only approximate KKT stationarity.
knowledge_statements.conclusion_latex: \[(x,y,z)\in\mathcal C_{\mathrm{KKT}}(\varepsilon_F,\varepsilon_D,\varepsilon_C,\varepsilon_S)\] exactly when all five displayed residual inequalities hold.
equivalent_formulations_latex: The five conditions may be combined as \(\max\{r_F,r_D,r_C,r_S\}\leq\varepsilon\) under a common tolerance.
For equality-only problems, the dual-sign and complementarity conditions disappear.
special_cases_latex: For unconstrained optimization, the certificate reduces to \(\|\nabla f(x)\|\leq\varepsilon_S\).
For a feasible-SQP iterate, the primal-feasibility residual may be identically zero.
immediate_consequences_latex: The multiplier vector is part of the witness; a primal point alone does not verify the displayed stationarity residual.
Small complementarity without dual feasibility does not constitute an approximate KKT certificate.
boundary_notes: Without a constraint qualification, exact KKT conditions need not characterize every local minimizer.
No source was inspected that supports precisely this tolerance-scaled certificate definition.
review_flags: The exact residual scaling and tolerance convention needs a precise source, despite the underlying KKT equations being standard.
knowledge_statements.title: Approximate Primal-Dual Stationarity Certificate

children.title: Feasibility Status Certificate System
children.top_down_role: Termination evidence distinguishing acceptable feasibility from persistent incompatibility.

knowledge_statements.slot_contract: State the canonical mathematical definition of the source node, with its domain, quantifiers, notation, and a precise source locator.
knowledge_statements.ambient_context_latex: Let \(\vartheta(x)\geq0\) be a computable constraint-violation measure and let \(\chi_F(x)\geq0\) be a first-order criticality measure for the feasibility problem \(\min_x\vartheta(x)\).
knowledge_statements.scope_note: Algorithmic status classification for SQP and restoration procedures. Stationary infeasibility is distinguished from a proof that the nonlinear constraints have no feasible point.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex:
Given tolerances \(\varepsilon_F,\varepsilon_C>0\), a feasibility-status certificate assigns exactly one supported label from:
\[\begin{aligned}
\mathrm{FEASIBLE}&:\quad \vartheta(x)\leq\varepsilon_F,\\
\mathrm{STATIONARY\_INFEASIBLE}&:\quad \vartheta(x)>\varepsilon_F,
\quad \chi_F(x)\leq\varepsilon_C,\\
\mathrm{UNRESOLVED}&:\quad \text{neither preceding predicate is verified}.
\end{aligned}\]
The witness contains \(x\), the evaluated violation, the feasibility-criticality residual, tolerances, and derivative or subgradient data used to compute \(\chi_F\). A stronger label \(\mathrm{INFEASIBLE}\) may be emitted only when an independent mathematical witness proves that no point satisfies the constraints; stationary infeasibility alone does not provide that implication for a nonconvex feasibility problem.
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: A feasibility-status system distinguishes an acceptably feasible point, an infeasible point that is approximately stationary for the violation-minimization problem, and an unresolved state. The witness records both violation and feasibility-criticality residuals. A true infeasibility label requires a separate global certificate; local stationary failure of restoration is not enough in a nonconvex problem.
knowledge_statements.conclusion_latex: \[\operatorname{status}(x)=\begin{cases}\mathrm{FEASIBLE},&\vartheta(x)\leq\varepsilon_F,\\\mathrm{STATIONARY\_INFEASIBLE},&\vartheta(x)>\varepsilon_F\ \land\ \chi_F(x)\leq\varepsilon_C,\\\mathrm{UNRESOLVED},&\text{otherwise.}\end{cases}\]
equivalent_formulations_latex: For differentiable \(\vartheta\), one may take \(\chi_F(x)=\|\nabla\vartheta(x)\|\).
For nonsmooth maximum violation, \(\chi_F(x)=\operatorname{dist}(0,\partial\vartheta(x))\) is an admissible stationarity measure.
special_cases_latex: If \(\varepsilon_F=0\), the feasible label requires exact feasibility.
For convex constraints with a valid separating dual witness, a genuine infeasibility status may be available.
immediate_consequences_latex: A restoration iteration limit normally produces UNRESOLVED, not STATIONARY_INFEASIBLE.
Positive violation and small feasibility criticality identify a locally least-infeasible candidate.
boundary_notes: The predicates do not establish global infeasibility for general nonlinear constraints.
No authoritative source for this exact three-way SQP status system was found.
review_flags: The distinction between stationary infeasibility and proven infeasibility is mathematically important, but the exact status taxonomy lacks a supplied source.
knowledge_statements.title: Feasibility-Status Certificate System
Feasibility Certificates
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: For explicitly dimensioned equality, inequality, and finite bound constraints, a reported point certifies feasibility to tolerance epsilon when every maximum-norm violation is at most epsilon.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex: Let \(h:\mathbb{R}^n\to\mathbb{R}^m\), \(g:\mathbb{R}^n\to\mathbb{R}^p\), and \(\ell,u\in\mathbb{R}^n\) with \(\ell\le u\). For the constraints \(h(x)=0\), \(g(x)\le0\), and \(\ell\le x\le u\), a reported point \(x\in\mathbb{R}^n\) is an \(\varepsilon\)-feasibility certificate, where \(\varepsilon\ge0\), if \[\max\!\left\{\|h(x)\|_\infty,\|[g(x)]_+\|_\infty,\|[\ell-x]_+\|_\infty,\|[x-u]_+\|_\infty\right\}\le\varepsilon.\] The certificate is checked by evaluating all displayed residuals under the declared residual-evaluation convention. At \(\varepsilon=0\), the displayed conditions certify exact feasibility.
assumptions_latex: \(h:\mathbb{R}^n\to\mathbb{R}^m\) and \(g:\mathbb{R}^n\to\mathbb{R}^p\) are defined at the reported point \(x\in\mathbb{R}^n\).
\(\ell,u\in\mathbb{R}^n\) are finite bound vectors satisfying \(\ell\le u\).
The tolerance satisfies \(\varepsilon\ge0\), and the residual-evaluation convention is declared.

knowledge_statements.statement_latex: Let \(h:\mathbb{R}^n\to\mathbb{R}^m\), \(g:\mathbb{R}^n\to\mathbb{R}^p\), and \(\ell,u\in\mathbb{R}^n\) with \(\ell\le u\). At \(\varepsilon=0\), the displayed conditions certify exact feasibility.
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: For explicitly dimensioned equality, inequality, and finite bound constraints, a reported point certifies feasibility to tolerance epsilon when every maximum-norm violation is at most epsilon.

knowledge_statements.title: Infeasibility Certificates
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: For an explicitly dimensioned SQP affine constraint system, a nonnegative Farkas multiplier with zero combined linear coefficient and positive combined constant term certifies infeasibility of the linearized constraints.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex: Let \(A\in\mathbb{R}^{m\times n}\), \(b\in\mathbb{R}^m\), \(C\in\mathbb{R}^{p\times n}\), and \(q\in\mathbb{R}^p\), and consider the SQP linearized system \(Ad+b=0\) and \(Cd+q\le0\) in \(d\in\mathbb{R}^n\). Vectors \(y\in\mathbb{R}^m\) and \(z\in\mathbb{R}^p\) form an infeasibility certificate if \[z\ge0,\qquad A^{\mathsf T}y+C^{\mathsf T}z=0,\qquad b^{\mathsf T}y+q^{\mathsf T}z>0.\] These finitely verifiable relations imply that no \(d\in\mathbb{R}^n\) satisfies the linearized constraints. Conversely, infeasibility of this finite-dimensional affine system admits such a certificate under the inequality convention \(Cd+q\le0\).
assumptions_latex: \(A\in\mathbb{R}^{m\times n}\), \(b\in\mathbb{R}^m\), \(C\in\mathbb{R}^{p\times n}\), and \(q\in\mathbb{R}^p\).
The step satisfies \(d\in\mathbb{R}^n\), and the multiplier candidates satisfy \(y\in\mathbb{R}^m\) and \(z\in\mathbb{R}^p\).
The linearized inequalities use the convention \(Cd+q\le0\).
knowledge_statements.conclusion_latex: \(\{d\in\mathbb{R}^n:Ad+b=0,\ Cd+q\le0\}=\varnothing\).

knowledge_statements.title: Ambiguous Feasibility Evidence
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: Constraint residuals whose error interval crosses the tolerance are inconclusive, and solver failure alone does not certify infeasibility.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex: Let \(v(x)\) be the maximum computed constraint violation, with certified evaluation error at most \(\delta\), and let \(\varepsilon\) be the feasibility tolerance. If \(v(x)+\delta\le\varepsilon\), the point is certified feasible; if \(v(x)-\delta>\varepsilon\), that point is certified nonfeasible. When \(v(x)-\delta\le\varepsilon<v(x)+\delta\), the evaluation is ambiguous. Moreover, failure of an SQP restoration phase or QP solver, without a valid separating or Farkas multiplier, is not an infeasibility certificate.
assumptions_latex: The residual evaluation satisfies \(|v_{\mathrm{true}}(x)-v(x)|\le\delta\).
The tolerance \(\varepsilon\ge0\) is fixed before classification.
knowledge_statements.conclusion_latex: \(v(x)-\delta\le\varepsilon<v(x)+\delta\) yields neither a feasibility certificate nor an infeasibility certificate.
knowledge_statements.scope_note: Boundary separating inconclusive numerical evidence from valid feasibility or infeasibility certificates.

enrichment_metadata.review_comment: The interval classification is plausible and the failure-boundary kind fits the leaf, but no source supports the certified residual-error model or the distinction between restoration/QP failure and a valid infeasibility certificate. The latter must remain explicitly limited to absence of a recognized certificate for the relevant subproblem or NLP model.

children.title: Second-Order Criticality Certificates
children.top_down_role: Termination evidence incorporating constrained curvature information.

knowledge_statements.title: Second-Order Criticality Certificates
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: Approximate KKT residuals plus a nearly positive-semidefinite Lagrangian Hessian on the critical subspace certify approximate second-order criticality.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex: Let \((x,\lambda,\mu)\) satisfy the \(\varepsilon_g\)-primal-dual KKT residual conditions, and let columns of \(Z\) form an orthonormal basis for a declared linearized critical subspace. With \(L(x,\lambda,\mu)=f(x)+\lambda^{\mathsf T}h(x)+\mu^{\mathsf T}g(x)\), the tuple \((x,\lambda,\mu,Z)\) is an \((\varepsilon_g,\varepsilon_H)\)-second-order criticality certificate if \[\lambda_{\min}\!\left(Z^{\mathsf T}\nabla_{xx}^2L(x,\lambda,\mu)Z\right)\ge-\varepsilon_H.\] Verification requires checking the first-order residuals, the defining linearized relations for \(Z\), and the eigenvalue bound.
assumptions_latex: \(f,h,g\) are twice continuously differentiable at \(x\).
\(Z\) has orthonormal columns spanning the declared critical subspace.
The first-order primal-dual residual is at most \(\varepsilon_g\).
knowledge_statements.conclusion_latex: The Lagrangian curvature is at least \(-\varepsilon_H\) in every unit direction in \(\operatorname{range}(Z)\).
knowledge_statements.scope_note: Approximate KKT certificate augmented by projected Lagrangian curvature.

enrichment_metadata.review_comment: Positive semidefiniteness on an arbitrary declared subspace is not by itself a standard second-order criticality certificate. For inequality-constrained problems the relevant object is generally a critical cone, not necessarily a subspace; additional active-set and multiplier conditions are needed before a null-space eigenvalue test is equivalent. The cited locator must be inspected to determine the correct formulation.

knowledge_statements.ambient_context_latex: For equality constraints \(c(x)=0\), let \(L(x,y)=f(x)+y^Tc(x)\), and let \(Z\) have orthonormal columns spanning \(\ker\nabla c(x)\). Assume second derivatives needed to form \(\nabla_{xx}^2L(x,y)\) are available or estimable.

knowledge_statements.statement_latex:
A second-order criticality certificate with tolerances \((\varepsilon_F,\varepsilon_S,\varepsilon_H)\) consists of \((x,y,Z,\widehat\lambda)\) satisfying
\[\|c(x)\|\leq\varepsilon_F,
\qquad \|\nabla_xL(x,y)\|\leq\varepsilon_S,
\qquad \|\nabla c(x)Z\|\leq\varepsilon_Z,\]
\[\|Z^TZ-I\|\leq\varepsilon_Z,

e\qquad \widehat\lambda\leq\lambda_{\min}(Z^T\nabla_{xx}^2L(x,y)Z)+\delta_\lambda,
\qquad \widehat\lambda\geq-\varepsilon_H.\]
Equivalently, the witness must provide a certified lower bound no smaller than \(-\varepsilon_H\), up to the declared eigenvalue error \(\delta_\lambda\), for Lagrangian curvature in feasible tangent directions. For inequalities, \(Z\) is replaced by a representation or oracle for the critical cone and the certificate includes first-order dual and complementarity residuals.
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: A second-order certificate augments approximate feasibility and stationarity with a verified lower bound on Lagrangian curvature in feasible critical directions. For equality constraints, it records an approximately orthonormal null-space basis and an eigenvalue bound for the reduced Hessian. Approximation errors in the basis and eigenvalue computation must be included in the witness.
knowledge_statements.conclusion_latex:
\[r_F\leq\varepsilon_F,
\quad r_S\leq\varepsilon_S,
\quad \lambda_{\min}(Z^T\nabla_{xx}^2LZ)\geq-\varepsilon_H-\delta_\lambda\] with the declared tangent-space accuracy.
equivalent_formulations_latex: Exact reduced-Hessian positive semidefiniteness is equivalent to \(d^T\nabla_{xx}^2L(x,y)d\geq0\) for every \(d\) satisfying \(\nabla c(x)d=0\).
A certified negative-curvature direction \(d\) with \(d^T\nabla_{xx}^2Ld< -\varepsilon_H\|d\|^2\) refutes the certificate.

With exact arithmetic and zero tolerances, the certificate becomes the second-order necessary KKT condition.
immediate_consequences_latex: A valid second-order certificate includes a first-order certificate.

knowledge_statements.slot_contract: State the canonical mathematical definition of the source node, with its domain, quantifiers, notation, and a precise source locator.
knowledge_statements.ambient_context_latex:
At iteration \(k\), an SQP method requires approximate solution of a structured KKT system
\[\begin{pmatrix}H_k&A_k^T\\A_k&0\end{pmatrix}\begin{pmatrix}s_k\\y_{k+1}\end{pmatrix}=\begin{pmatrix}-g_k\\-c_k\end{pmatrix}\]
or an equivalent quadratic subproblem, where problem dimensions and sparsity may vary across a family of instances.
knowledge_statements.scope_note: Algorithmic family definition for large sparse or matrix-free smooth nonlinear programming. Scalability is stated relative to declared storage and primitive-operation models.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex:
An SQP implementation is scalable on an instance family \(\{P_N\}\) if its iteration can be expressed using declared primitives—sparse factorizations, Jacobian and Hessian products, preconditioner applications, and warm-start state—whose storage \(M_N\) and work \(W_N\) satisfy specified growth bounds as the representation size \(N\to\infty\), while the inexact step obeys the algorithm’s globalization accuracy conditions. A matrix-free member requires access to products
\[v\mapsto H_kv,
\qquad v\mapsto A_kv,
\qquad w\mapsto A_k^Tw,
\]
without forming the corresponding dense matrices. A sparse-direct member requires storage and factorization bounds expressed in terms of nonzeros and fill. A warm-started member carries prior primal, dual, active-set, or factorization information but must preserve the mathematical acceptance and residual tests. Thus scalability is a quantified resource property, not merely the ability to run on one large instance.
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: A scalable SQP implementation is defined relative to a growing family of problem representations and an explicit resource model. It uses sparse, matrix-free, preconditioned, or warm-started primitives whose storage and work obey declared growth bounds, while still satisfying the inexactness and globalization conditions of the underlying SQP method. Calling an implementation large-scale without such resource bounds is not a mathematical scalability claim.
knowledge_statements.conclusion_latex: \[M_N\leq\mathcal M(N),\qquad W_N\leq\mathcal W(N),\qquad N\to\infty,\] with every computed step satisfying the declared SQP residual and model-decrease conditions.
equivalent_formulations_latex: Matrix-free scalability may be stated by bounds on numbers of \(H_kv\), \(A_kv\), and \(A_k^Tw\) products per accepted step.
Sparse-direct scalability may be stated using symbolic and numerical factorization storage and fill bounds.
special_cases_latex: Limited-memory quasi-Newton SQP avoids storing a dense Hessian approximation.
Warm-started active-set SQP reuses the preceding working set for a related problem sequence.
Iterative KKT SQP uses preconditioned Krylov solves with residual forcing conditions.
immediate_consequences_latex: Sparse storage alone does not guarantee low factorization work because fill may be large.
Warm starts affect resource use but do not alter certificate validity requirements.
boundary_notes: Scalability depends on the problem family, ordering, conditioning, and preconditioner model.
No single inspected source supported the entire sparse, matrix-free, warm-started, and software-oriented taxonomy.

children.title: Sparse Direct SQP
children.top_down_role: SQP implementations based on sparse KKT and QP factorizations.

knowledge_statements.slot_contract: State the canonical mathematical definition of the source node, with its domain, quantifiers, notation, and a precise source locator.
knowledge_statements.ambient_context_latex: Consider the finite-dimensional nonlinear program \(\min_{x\in\mathbb R^n} f(x)\) subject to \(c(x)=0\) and \(g(x)\leq 0\), where the derivatives used below exist. At iterate \((x_k,\lambda_k,\mu_k)\), let \(B_k\) approximate the Hessian of the Lagrangian, \(A_k=\nabla c(x_k)^T\), and \(G_k=\nabla g(x_k)^T\).
knowledge_statements.scope_note: This definition classifies finite-dimensional SQP implementations by sparse storage and direct factorization of each quadratic-programming or KKT system; it does not assert convergence.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex: A sparse direct SQP method is an SQP method whose step \(d_k\) is obtained from the quadratic program \[\min_d\;\nabla f(x_k)^Td+\tfrac12 d^TB_kd\quad\text{subject to}\quad c(x_k)+A_kd=0,\quad g(x_k)+G_kd\leq0,\] and for which the assembled QP matrices are stored sparsely and the equality-constrained system associated with every selected working set \(W_k\), \[K_k\binom{d_k}{y_k}=-\binom{\nabla f(x_k)}{r_k},\qquad K_k=\begin{pmatrix}B_k&J_{W_k}^T\\J_{W_k}&0\end{pmatrix},\] is solved by a finite direct factorization of a sparse permutation of \(K_k\), possibly with symmetric pivoting and regularization.
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: A sparse direct SQP method forms the usual quadratic model with linearized constraints, stores its Hessian and Jacobians sparsely, and computes each working-set step by a direct sparse factorization of the corresponding coupled KKT matrix. Permutations, pivoting, and regularization may be used, but the defining linear solve is a direct sparse solve rather than an iterative operator-only solve.
knowledge_statements.conclusion_latex: The defining properties are sparse explicit matrix representation and direct factorization of the QP or working-set KKT equations.
equivalent_formulations_latex: For an equality-constrained QP, the defining solve may equivalently be written as \(B_kd_k+J_k^Ty_k=-\nabla f(x_k)\) and \(J_kd_k=-r_k\), followed by a sparse direct solution of the combined saddle-point equations.
special_cases_latex: If \(B_k\) and \(J_k\) are dense, the method is direct SQP but not sparse direct SQP under this definition.
A sparse active-set QP solver is included when each working-set change is handled through sparse factorization or sparse factor updates.
immediate_consequences_latex: The numerical cost and storage depend on fill-in in the factors, not only on the number of nonzeros in \(B_k\) and \(J_k\).
The full-space and reduced-space sparse variants are distinguished by whether the coupled KKT variables are retained or eliminated before the principal factorization.
boundary_notes: Matrix-free Krylov solution of the KKT equations is excluded, even if sparse matrices are available.
Sparse storage alone is insufficient if the principal subproblem solve is iterative rather than direct.
No definiteness, nonsingularity, globalization, or convergence condition is imposed by the classification.

notation.meaning: Jacobian of equality constraints together with inequalities selected in the QP working set.
Working-set saddle-point or KKT coefficient matrix.
Corresponding vector of current constraint residuals.

knowledge_statements.title: Sparse Full-Space SQP
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: Full-space sparse SQP obtains the primal step and multiplier correction together by factoring the coupled sparse KKT matrix.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex: For QP gradient \(r\), symmetric Hessian approximation \(B\), constraint Jacobian \(A\), and linearized residual \(c\), the full-space SQP step and multiplier correction solve \[\begin{pmatrix}B&A^{\mathsf T}\\A&0\end{pmatrix}\begin{pmatrix}p\\y\end{pmatrix}=-\begin{pmatrix}r\\c\end{pmatrix}.\] A sparse full-space implementation preserves the sparsity of \(A\) and \(B\), computes a fill-reducing symmetric-indefinite factorization of the displayed KKT matrix, and returns \((p,y)\) whose scaled linear residual meets the prescribed tolerance. Active inequalities enter through the selected active rows of \(A\).
assumptions_latex: \(B\) is symmetric and \(A\) is the Jacobian of equalities plus selected active inequalities.
The displayed KKT matrix is nonsingular or a declared regularization is applied.
knowledge_statements.conclusion_latex: The computed pair \((p,y)\) satisfies the coupled SQP optimality equations to the prescribed residual tolerance.
knowledge_statements.scope_note: Coupled sparse KKT representation of an equality-constrained or active-set SQP step.

enrichment_metadata.review_comment: The coupled KKT representation is standard and fits full-space SQP, but the cited general SQP locator does not inspectably support preservation of sparsity, fill-reducing symmetric-indefinite factorization, or the stated residual policy. A sparse-direct SQP source is required for this exact terminal container.

knowledge_statements.title: Sparse Reduced-Space SQP
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: Reduced-space SQP first satisfies linearized constraints, solves the Hessian equation in the Jacobian null space, then recovers multipliers.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex: Assume \(A\) has full row rank. Choose \(Z\) with \(AZ=0\) and a complementary matrix \(Y\) such that \(AY\) is nonsingular. Writing \(p=Yp_Y+Zp_Z\), the linearized constraints give \(p_Y=-(AY)^{-1}c\), and the SQP stationarity equations reduce to \[\left(Z^{\mathsf T}BZ\right)p_Z=-Z^{\mathsf T}\left(r+BYp_Y\right).\] After solving this sparse reduced-Hessian system, recover \(p\), then obtain \(y\) from \(A^{\mathsf T}y=-(r+Bp)\).
assumptions_latex: \(A\) has full row rank.
\(AZ=0\), \(AY\) is nonsingular, and the columns of \((Y,Z)\) span the primal space.
\(Z^{\mathsf T}BZ\) is nonsingular or is regularized.
knowledge_statements.conclusion_latex: The reconstructed \((p,y)\) satisfies \(Bp+A^{\mathsf T}y=-r\) and \(Ap=-c\).
knowledge_statements.scope_note: Null-space decomposition reducing the SQP KKT equations to a projected Hessian system.

notation.meaning: null-space basis for the active constraint Jacobian

knowledge_statements.slot_contract: State the canonical mathematical definition of the source node, with its domain, quantifiers, notation, and a precise source locator.
knowledge_statements.ambient_context_latex: At SQP iteration \(k\), let \(B_k\) be the quadratic-model operator, \(J_k\) the active or equality-constraint Jacobian, and \(K_k(d,y)=(B_kd+J_k^Ty,J_kd)\) the associated saddle-point operator.
knowledge_statements.scope_note: The definition covers large finite-dimensional SQP implementations whose dominant subproblem linear algebra is iterative and operator based.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex: A matrix-free iterative SQP method is an SQP method that computes an exact or inexact step by an iterative procedure applied to the QP optimality equations while accessing \(B_k\), \(J_k\), and \(J_k^T\) through products \(v\mapsto B_kv\), \(v\mapsto J_kv\), and \(w\mapsto J_k^Tw\), without requiring explicit assembly or direct factorization of the complete matrices \(B_k\), \(J_k\), or \(K_k\). A preconditioner \(P_k\) may be assembled or factored, provided it is an auxiliary approximation and not the exact full KKT matrix whose factorization itself determines the step.
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: Matrix-free iterative SQP computes SQP steps with an iterative linear or quadratic solver using Hessian and Jacobian products. It does not need the complete model or KKT matrix to be assembled or directly factored. An explicit approximate preconditioner is allowed.
knowledge_statements.conclusion_latex: The defining interface consists of model-operator products and an iterative stopping rule, with no required direct factorization of the complete SQP system.
equivalent_formulations_latex: For equality constraints, the method may iteratively solve \(K_k(d_k,y_k)=(-q_k,-r_k)\) using only evaluations of the block operator.
A projected implementation is matrix-free when null-space projection and reduced-Hessian products are themselves supplied as operator actions.
special_cases_latex: A Hessian-free method may use \(B_kv\) from automatic differentiation or finite-difference directional derivatives.
Limited-memory quasi-Newton recursion is matrix-free when it supplies \(B_kv\) without assembling a dense \(B_k\).
immediate_consequences_latex: Storage can be governed by vectors, operator state, and the preconditioner rather than by all entries of the KKT matrix.
The computed step may be inexact because the iterative solve can terminate at a prescribed residual or model criterion.
boundary_notes: Merely calling an iterative refinement routine after an exact direct KKT factorization does not make the SQP method matrix-free.
An explicitly assembled sparse Krylov solve is iterative SQP but is not fully matrix-free with respect to that assembled operator.
The definition supplies no convergence guarantee for arbitrary inner stopping tolerances.

children.title: Krylov SQP
children.top_down_role: SQP step computation using Krylov subspace linear algebra.

knowledge_statements.title: Krylov SQP
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: Krylov SQP applies matrix-free KKT products and preconditioning until the relative linear residual reaches the prescribed forcing tolerance.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex: Given operators for \(Bv\), \(Av\), and \(A^{\mathsf T}w\), form the KKT operator \(K(p,y)=(Bp+A^{\mathsf T}y,Ap)\) and right-hand side \(b=-(r,c)\). Choose a symmetric positive-definite preconditioner \(P\), initialize \(s_0=(0,0)\), and apply a symmetry-compatible Krylov method such as MINRES to \(Ks=b\). Stop at the first iterate \(s_j=(p_j,y_j)\) satisfying \(\|b-Ks_j\|_{P^{-1}}\le\eta\|b\|_{P^{-1}}\), or at a declared iteration limit; return \(p_j\) as the inexact SQP step and report the residual status.
assumptions_latex: \(B\) is symmetric, so the full KKT operator \(K\) is symmetric.
\(P\) is symmetric positive definite.
The stopping tolerance satisfies \(0<\eta<1\).
knowledge_statements.conclusion_latex: On successful termination, \(\|b-K(p_j,y_j)\|_{P^{-1}}\le\eta\|b\|_{P^{-1}}\).
knowledge_statements.scope_note: Matrix-free Krylov computation of an approximate SQP KKT step.

enrichment_metadata.review_comment: The algorithm kind fits the Krylov SQP leaf and the conditional residual stopping test is coherent, but the cited locator concerns construction of a Krylov-space basis rather than preconditioned MINRES for an SQP KKT operator. A source must support the KKT specialization, SPD preconditioning convention, and residual norm used here.

knowledge_statements.title: Preconditioned SQP Systems
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: SQP KKT or null-space systems can be transformed by nonsingular preconditioners and solved with matrix-free Krylov iterations without changing their exact solutions.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex:
For the SQP system 
\[
K_k\begin{pmatrix}p\\y\end{pmatrix}=-\begin{pmatrix}g_k\\c_k\end{pmatrix},\qquad K_k=\begin{pmatrix}B_k&A_k^{\mathsf T}\\A_k&0\end{pmatrix},
\]
a nonsingular full-space preconditioner \(P_k\) gives the equivalent system \(P_k^{-1}K_k(p,y)^{\mathsf T}=-P_k^{-1}(g_k,c_k)^{\mathsf T}\). If the columns of \(Z_k\) span \(\ker A_k\) and \(p=p_N+Z_kq\), a nonsingular reduced preconditioner \(M_k\) gives \(M_k^{-1}Z_k^{\mathsf T}B_kZ_kq=-M_k^{-1}Z_k^{\mathsf T}(g_k+B_kp_N)\). Either system may be solved by a compatible Krylov method without forming its coefficient matrix explicitly.
assumptions_latex: \(B_k\in\mathbb R^{n\times n}\) is symmetric and \(A_k\in\mathbb R^{m\times n}\) has full row rank.
\(P_k\) and \(M_k\) are nonsingular, and \(A_kp_N=-c_k\).
knowledge_statements.conclusion_latex: The preconditioned full-space and reduced-space systems are algebraically equivalent to their unpreconditioned SQP systems.

children.title: Truncated SQP Subproblem Solves
children.top_down_role: Large-scale SQP terminating iterative inner solves before exact completion.

knowledge_statements.title: Truncated SQP Subproblem Solves
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: An iterative SQP subproblem solve stops once a forcing residual or iteration limit is reached, then passes its inexact step to the outer globalization procedure.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex:
At outer iterate \(x_k\), apply an iterative solver to the linearized SQP KKT equations and obtain \((p_k,y_k)\) with residual
\[
r_k=\begin{pmatrix}B_kp_k+g_k+A_k^{\mathsf T}y_k\\A_kp_k+c_k\end{pmatrix}.
\]
Terminate the inner solve when \(\lVert r_k\rVert\leq\eta_k\lVert(g_k,c_k)\rVert\), or earlier at a prescribed iteration limit after producing an acceptable descent or model-reduction step. Globalize the resulting inexact step by the parent SQP acceptance mechanism. Output \(p_k\), the multiplier estimate \(y_k\), and the achieved residual norm; exact solution of the quadratic subproblem is not required.
assumptions_latex: \(0\leq\eta_k<1\) is the prescribed inner forcing tolerance.
The iterative method returns a finite step and reports its KKT residual.
knowledge_statements.conclusion_latex: The outer SQP iteration receives an explicitly controlled inexact quadratic-subproblem solution.
knowledge_statements.scope_note: Inexact inner termination for equality-constrained, large-scale SQP quadratic subproblems.

notation.meaning: KKT residual of the inner solve

enrichment_metadata.review_comment: The algorithm kind fits truncated inner SQP solves, but the cited general SQP section does not inspectably support the forcing-residual rule or termination at an iteration limit. The phrase “acceptable descent or model-reduction step” also requires a precise test from an inexact-SQP source.

knowledge_statements.slot_contract: State the canonical mathematical definition of the source node, with its domain, quantifiers, notation, and a precise source locator.
knowledge_statements.ambient_context_latex: Let \(Q_k(d)=q_k^Td+\tfrac12d^TB_kd\) be the SQP quadratic model over a linearized feasible set \(\mathcal F_k\), and let an iterative inner method produce candidates \(d_{k,0},d_{k,1},\ldots\) with associated residual or stationarity measure \(\rho_{k,j}\).
knowledge_statements.scope_note: The definition concerns intentional early termination of an iterative QP, KKT, or projected subproblem solve; it does not prescribe a convergence-forcing sequence.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex: A truncated SQP subproblem solve accepts \(d_k=d_{k,j_k}\) at a finite inner index \(j_k\) selected before exact solution of the QP is required, according to a stated rule such as \[\rho_{k,j_k}\leq\eta_k,\qquad Q_k(0)-Q_k(d_{k,j_k})\geq\kappa_k,\qquad \|d_{k,j_k}\|=\Delta_k,\] or detection of nonpositive curvature \(p_{k,j_k}^TB_kp_{k,j_k}\leq0\). The returned step must satisfy whatever feasibility, projected-feasibility, or normal-tangential conditions are imposed by that rule, but need not satisfy the exact QP KKT equations.
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: A truncated SQP solve stops an iterative subproblem solver at a finite inner iterate using an explicit residual, model-decrease, trust-region-boundary, or curvature condition. The returned step can be inexact and need not solve the quadratic program's KKT equations exactly.
knowledge_statements.conclusion_latex: The defining distinction is acceptance by an explicit finite inner stopping event rather than a requirement of exact QP optimality.
equivalent_formulations_latex: For a linear KKT solve, truncation may be expressed by a nonzero residual \(r_{k,j_k}=b_k-K_kz_{k,j_k}\) satisfying a prescribed tolerance.
For a projected quadratic solve, truncation may instead be expressed through the projected gradient or a Cauchy-decrease condition.
special_cases_latex: Truncated conjugate gradients stops at a residual tolerance, the trust-region boundary, or a direction of nonpositive curvature.
A fixed cap \(j_k\leq j_{\max}\) is a truncation rule when the current inner iterate is accepted at the cap.
immediate_consequences_latex: Exact and truncated solves coincide if the inner method reaches an exact solution before any other stopping event.
Outer convergence theory must account for the resulting inexactness through conditions not supplied by this definition.
boundary_notes: Failure of an inner solver without an acceptance criterion is not, by itself, a defined truncated solve.
A direct solve followed only by iterative refinement is not truncated SQP unless refinement may terminate under an inexact acceptance rule.
The constants \(\eta_k\), \(\kappa_k\), and \(\Delta_k\) require separate algorithmic specification.

children.title: Structure-Exploiting SQP
