knowledge_statements.slot_contract: State the canonical mathematical definition of the source node, with its domain, quantifiers, notation, and a precise source locator.
knowledge_statements.ambient_context_latex: Consider an NLP whose variables, objective, or constraints possess a specified decomposition \(x=(x_1,\ldots,x_N)\), incidence pattern, temporal ordering, or elimination structure. Let \(B_k\) and \(J_k\) be the SQP Hessian approximation and constraint Jacobian.
knowledge_statements.scope_note: This definition covers exact exploitation of algebraic problem structure in formulating or solving SQP subproblems; generic sparsity alone is not the intended distinguishing feature.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex: A structure-exploiting SQP method is an SQP method for which the subproblem representation and step computation preserve and use a declared decomposition \(\mathscr S\) of the nonlinear program, so that \(B_k\), \(J_k\), or the KKT operator is assembled, applied, eliminated, decomposed, or factorized according to \(\mathscr S\). Formally, there must exist structure maps or index sets determining blocks \(x_i\) and local functions such that the SQP matrices inherit a corresponding block, bordered, banded, separable, scenario, or temporal pattern, and the principal linear-algebra operation is defined on that pattern rather than treating the subproblem as an unstructured dense QP.
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: Structure-exploiting SQP preserves a declared block, separable, temporal, scenario, or application-derived decomposition from the nonlinear model into the SQP matrices and uses that decomposition in the principal subproblem solve. The method is distinguished by more than incidental zero entries.
knowledge_statements.conclusion_latex: A method belongs to this class when a declared model decomposition induces the SQP algebraic pattern and the step computation operates explicitly on that pattern.
equivalent_formulations_latex: The structure may be represented by element-variable incidence sets, a block graph, a temporal chain, a scenario tree, or a block-bordered KKT matrix.
Condensing, decomposition, Riccati recursion, structured Schur complements, and elementwise Hessian assembly are included when derived from the declared decomposition.
special_cases_latex: Partially separable SQP uses element-function incidence structure.
Block-structured SQP uses decomposable or bordered KKT blocks.
Dynamic-optimization SQP uses state-transition and stage ordering.
immediate_consequences_latex: Two methods applied to the same sparse NLP can differ in classification if only one exposes and uses the generating decomposition.
The definition permits either direct or iterative structured linear algebra.
boundary_notes: Ordinary sparse storage with a generic ordering is not necessarily structure-exploiting in the stronger sense used here.
The declaration of structure alone is insufficient unless it changes formulation or computation of the SQP step.
No complexity reduction follows without additional quantitative assumptions on block sizes and coupling.

children.title: Partially Separable SQP
children.top_down_role: SQP preserving elementwise objective and constraint structure.

knowledge_statements.title: Partially Separable SQP
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: Partially separable SQP represents the quadratic model as a sum of small element models, preserving the global SQP subproblem while enabling local derivative operations.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex:
Suppose
\[
f(x)=\sum_{e=1}^{E}f_e(U_ex),\qquad B_k=\sum_{e=1}^{E}U_e^{\mathsf T}B_{e,k}U_e,
\]
where each \(U_e\) selects a small subset of variables. The SQP objective model is
\[
g_k^{\mathsf T}p+\tfrac12p^{\mathsf T}B_kp
=\sum_{e=1}^{E}\left(\nabla f_e(U_ex_k)^{\mathsf T}U_ep+\tfrac12(U_ep)^{\mathsf T}B_{e,k}(U_ep)\right).
\]
Together with the linearized constraints \(c(x_k)+A_kp=0\), this defines the same quadratic subproblem as global assembly, while objective values, gradients, and Hessian-vector products can be evaluated elementwise and accumulated.
assumptions_latex: Each \(f_e\) is twice continuously differentiable on a neighborhood of \(U_ex_k\).
Each element matrix \(B_{e,k}\) is symmetric and dimensionally compatible with \(U_e\).
knowledge_statements.conclusion_latex: Elementwise accumulation reproduces the global SQP quadratic objective and its matrix-vector products.
knowledge_statements.scope_note: Elementwise assembly of objective derivatives and SQP curvature while retaining partial separability.
review_flags: standard_field_rationale: finite-element-style partial separability gives the displayed exact assembly identities

children.title: Block-Structured SQP
children.top_down_role: SQP exploiting block-bordered and decomposable KKT systems.

knowledge_statements.title: Block-Structured SQP
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: A conformably block-bordered SQP KKT system with nonsingular local blocks reduces to independent local eliminations and one coupling Schur-complement system, followed by local back-substitution.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex:
Let \(r\geq 1\) be the number of local blocks. Partition an SQP KKT system as
\[
\begin{pmatrix}
K_{11}&&&E_1^{\mathsf T}\\
&K_{22}&&E_2^{\mathsf T}\\
&&\ddots&\vdots\\
E_1&E_2&\cdots&K_0
\end{pmatrix}
\begin{pmatrix}w_1\\w_2\\\vdots\\w_0\end{pmatrix}
=-\begin{pmatrix}b_1\\b_2\\\vdots\\b_0\end{pmatrix}.
\]
For each \(i\in\{1,\ldots,r\}\), suppose \(K_{ii}\) is nonsingular. Eliminating the local variable gives
\[
w_i=-K_{ii}^{-1}(b_i+E_i^{\mathsf T}w_0).
\]
The coupling variable therefore satisfies
\[
\left(K_0-\sum_{i=1}^{r}E_iK_{ii}^{-1}E_i^{\mathsf T}\right)w_0
=-b_0+\sum_{i=1}^{r}E_iK_{ii}^{-1}b_i.
\]
After solving this Schur-complement system, the displayed local formulas recover the full SQP primal-dual step; the local solves can be performed independently once \(w_0\) is fixed.
assumptions_latex: \(r\in\mathbb N\), \(K_{ii}\in\mathbb R^{n_i\times n_i}\), and \(K_{ii}\) is nonsingular for every \(i\in\{1,\ldots,r\}\).
\(K_0\in\mathbb R^{n_0\times n_0}\), \(E_i\in\mathbb R^{n_0\times n_i}\), \(w_i,b_i\in\mathbb R^{n_i}\), and \(w_0,b_0\in\mathbb R^{n_0}\).
knowledge_statements.conclusion_latex: The Schur-complement system together with \(w_i=-K_{ii}^{-1}(b_i+E_i^{\mathsf T}w_0)\) is algebraically equivalent to the displayed full block-bordered KKT system.
knowledge_statements.scope_note: Block-bordered KKT representation and Schur-complement elimination for decomposable SQP subproblems.

children.title: Dynamic-Optimization SQP Interfaces

knowledge_statements.title: Dynamic-Optimization SQP Interfaces
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: Multiple shooting retains state and control increments; condensing eliminates state increments recursively and yields an equivalent control-space SQP quadratic program.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex:
For dynamics \(x_{i+1}=F_i(x_i,u_i)\), multiple-shooting SQP retains increments \((\delta x_i,\delta u_i)\) and imposes
\[
\delta x_{i+1}-A_i\delta x_i-B_i\delta u_i=-d_i,
\]
where \(A_i=\nabla_xF_i\), \(B_i=\nabla_uF_i\), and \(d_i=x_{i+1}-F_i(x_i,u_i)\). Forward substitution expresses every state increment affinely as \(\delta x_i=S_i\delta x_0+T_i\delta u+s_i\). Substitution into the quadratic objective and remaining linearized constraints yields a condensed quadratic program in \((\delta x_0,\delta u)\). Any condensed solution, lifted by this recursion, satisfies the multiple-shooting linearized dynamics and has the same model objective value.
assumptions_latex: Each stage map \(F_i\) is continuously differentiable at the current trajectory.
The multiple-shooting SQP model is quadratic with affine linearized constraints.
knowledge_statements.conclusion_latex: Condensing and recursive lifting establish equivalent reduced and multiple-shooting SQP representations.
knowledge_statements.scope_note: Multiple-shooting and condensed representations of a discrete-time dynamic-optimization SQP subproblem.

knowledge_statements.title: QP Warm Starting in SQP
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: Each SQP quadratic program reuses the preceding working set, multipliers, and compatible factors, while retaining the ordinary QP optimality tests.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex: For SQP quadratic program \(Q_k\), initialize its active-set solver with the preceding working set \(W_{k-1}\), mapped multiplier estimate \(\lambda_{k-1}\), and any still-compatible factorization. Remove indices absent from \(Q_k\), add constraints violated by the initial trial point, and refactorize whenever dimensions or numerical tests invalidate the stored factors. Run the active-set iterations until the QP KKT conditions meet their prescribed tolerances. Output the QP step \(p_k\), multipliers \(\lambda_k\), final working set \(W_k\), and reusable factorization state for \(Q_{k+1}\). Warm starting changes initialization only, not the termination conditions defining a solved subproblem.
assumptions_latex: Successive SQP quadratic programs use consistently identifiable constraints.
Stored factors are reused only after compatibility and numerical-validity checks.
knowledge_statements.conclusion_latex: The warm-started QP solver returns the same class of KKT-qualified output as a cold-started solve.

knowledge_statements.title: Parametric Warm-Start SQP
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: For nearby parameter values, SQP starts from the preceding primal-dual solution, optionally extrapolated by KKT sensitivity, and then performs globalized correction iterations.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex: For parameter sequence \(\theta_0,\theta_1,\ldots\) and problems \(\min_x f(x;\theta_j)\) subject to \(c(x;\theta_j)=0\) and \(h(x;\theta_j)\leq0\), initialize the SQP solve at \(\theta_j\) from the preceding primal-dual solution \((x_{j-1}^*,\lambda_{j-1}^*,\mu_{j-1}^*)\). Optionally compute a predictor by solving the differentiated active KKT system for \(dz/d\theta\) and set \(z_j^0=z_{j-1}^*+(dz/d\theta)(\theta_j-\theta_{j-1})\). Apply ordinary globalized SQP corrections at \(\theta_j\) until its termination tests hold. If predictor construction fails, use the preceding solution without extrapolation.

A sensitivity predictor is used only when the selected active KKT Jacobian is nonsingular.

children.title: Classical SQP Software Lineages

knowledge_statements.slot_contract: State the canonical mathematical definition of the source node, with its domain, quantifiers, notation, and a precise source locator.
knowledge_statements.ambient_context_latex: Consider software methods for smooth finite-dimensional constrained nonlinear programs that repeatedly form quadratic Lagrangian models with linearized constraints. knowledge_statements.scope_note: This is a taxonomy definition for implementation families, not a named convergence theorem or a claim about particular software packages.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex: A classical SQP software lineage is an implementation family whose members share the SQP core \[\min_d\;\nabla f(x_k)^Td+\tfrac12d^TB_kd\quad\text{subject to linearized constraints},\] together with a persistent architecture \(\mathcal A=(\mathcal Q,\mathcal L,\mathcal H,\mathcal G)\), where \(\mathcal Q\) specifies the QP formulation and solver class, \(\mathcal L\) specifies dense, sparse, full-space, or reduced-space linear algebra, \(\mathcal H\) specifies exact or quasi-Newton Lagrangian curvature, and \(\mathcal G\) specifies line-search, merit/filter, or trust-region globalization. knowledge_statements.statement_plain: A classical SQP software lineage is a family of solver versions sharing the standard SQP quadratic model and a persistent architecture: the QP solver, linear-algebra representation, Hessian strategy, and globalization mechanism. children.title: Dense Active-Set SQP Software
children.top_down_role: Classical dense SQP implementations centered on active-set QP solves.

knowledge_statements.title: Dense Active-Set SQP Software
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: Classical dense SQP forms full derivative arrays, solves each quadratic model by an active-set QP method, globalizes the step, and updates curvature and multipliers.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex:
Given \((x_k,\lambda_k,\mu_k)\), form dense arrays for the constraint Jacobian and symmetric Lagrangian-Hessian approximation \(B_k\). Solve the linearly constrained quadratic program
\[
\min_p\ g_k^{\mathsf T}p+\tfrac12p^{\mathsf T}B_kp
\quad\text{subject to}\quad c_k+A_kp=0,\quad h_k+G_kp\leq0
\]
by an active-set method, obtaining \((p_k,\widehat\lambda_k,\widehat\mu_k)\). Choose a globalized step length \(\alpha_k\), set \(x_{k+1}=x_k+\alpha_kp_k\), update multipliers and \(B_k\), and stop when feasibility and stationarity tolerances hold. Dense factorizations are used for the QP working-set systems.

The dense QP solver detects or regularizes singular working-set systems.

knowledge_statements.title: Sparse Reduced-Hessian SQP Software
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: Sparse reduced-Hessian SQP computes a feasible normal component, solves curvature equations only in the constraint null space, and recovers the full step and multipliers.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex: At iterate \(x_k\), choose sparse matrices \(Y_k,Z_k\) such that \(A_kY_k\) is nonsingular and \(A_kZ_k=0\). Compute a normal component \(p_{N,k}=-Y_k(A_kY_k)^{-1}c_k\), then solve the reduced quadratic problem for \(q_k\) with Hessian \(R_k=Z_k^{\mathsf T}B_kZ_k\) and step \(p_k=p_{N,k}+Z_kq_k\). Recover multiplier estimates from the full stationarity equations, globalize \(p_k\), and update a sparse representation of \(R_k\) or its factors. Stop when nonlinear feasibility and stationarity satisfy their tolerances.
assumptions_latex: \(A_k\) has full row rank and the chosen \(A_kY_k\) is nonsingular.
The reduced quadratic problem is regularized when \(R_k\) lacks suitable curvature.
knowledge_statements.conclusion_latex: The assembled step satisfies \(A_kp_k=-c_k\) and uses reduced-space curvature \(R_k\).
knowledge_statements.scope_note: Sparse null-space SQP using a reduced Lagrangian-Hessian model.

enrichment_metadata.review_comment: The null-space construction is algebraically plausible and the algorithm kind fits the container, but the cited sparse-linear-system and general-SQP sections do not inspectably support the complete sparse reduced-Hessian SQP software procedure, multiplier recovery, or sparse factor updates.

knowledge_statements.slot_contract: State the canonical mathematical definition of the source node, with its domain, quantifiers, notation, and a precise source locator.
knowledge_statements.ambient_context_latex: Consider a smooth finite-dimensional nonlinear program in \(\mathbb R^n\). At an SQP iterate \(x\), let \(c(x)=0\) denote the equality constraints together with any inequalities selected as active, let \(A(x)=\nabla c(x)\in\mathbb R^{m\times n}\), and let \(H\in\mathbb S^n\) approximate the Hessian of the Lagrangian. Assume \(A(x)\) has full row rank. Choose \(N\in\mathbb R^{n\times(n-m)}\) with \(A(x)N=0\), and choose \(R\in\mathbb R^{n\times m}\) so that \([R\ N]\) is nonsingular and \(A(x)R\) is nonsingular.
knowledge_statements.scope_note: This definition covers large-scale equality-constrained SQP and active-set SQP after a working set has been fixed. Sparsity refers to the linear-algebra realization of the range-space systems and any structured curvature information; it does not require the reduced matrix itself to be sparse.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex: \[\mathfrak S_{\mathrm{RH}}:=\left\{\mathcal A:\ s=Rs_r+Ns_n,\quad A(x)R s_r=-c(x),\quad H_{nn}s_n=-N^T\nabla_x\ell(x,y)-H_{nr}s_r,\quad H_{nn}=N^THN,\quad H_{nr}=N^THR\right\}.\] A sparse reduced-Hessian SQP implementation is an algorithm \(\mathcal A\in\mathfrak S_{\mathrm{RH}}\) that represents or updates the curvature required on \(\ker A(x)\), solves the systems involving \(A(x)R\) and its transpose with sparsity-exploiting linear algebra, and avoids forming or factoring a general dense \(n\times n\) Hessian. In the canonical reduced-Hessian specialization, \(H_{nr}=0\) and \(H_{rr}:=R^THR=0\), while a positive-definite secant approximation to \(H_{nn}\) is maintained. The resulting \(s\) is the SQP correction associated with the linearized constraints and the reduced quadratic model.
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: A sparse reduced-Hessian SQP implementation is an SQP algorithm for a smooth finite-dimensional constrained problem that decomposes every step as a range-space component plus a null-space component. The range-space coordinates solve the linearized feasibility equation, while the null-space coordinates solve a system whose coefficient is the reduced Hessian. The implementation stores or updates the curvature needed only on the null space, uses sparse factorizations for the constraint-related systems, and avoids a general dense full-Hessian factorization. In the canonical reduced-Hessian variant, the range/null cross block and range/range block are set to zero and a positive-definite secant approximation is maintained for the null-space block.
assumptions_latex: \(f:\mathbb R^n\to\mathbb R\) and the constraints defining the current equality or working-set model are sufficiently differentiable to form \(A(x)\), \(\nabla_x\ell(x,y)\), and a symmetric model \(H\).
\(A(x)\) has full row rank, \(A(x)N=0\), and \(A(x)R\) is nonsingular.

The implementation has access to sparse or structured representations for the constraint-related systems; this is a defining implementation condition, not a claim that \(H_{nn}\) is necessarily sparse.
knowledge_statements.conclusion_latex: \[s=Rs_r+Ns_n,\qquad A(x)R s_r=-c(x),\qquad N^THN s_n=-N^T\nabla_x\ell(x,y)-N^THR s_r,\] with the canonical reduced-Hessian specialization setting \(N^THR=0\) and \(R^THR=0\) and maintaining curvature on \(\ker A(x)\).
equivalent_formulations_latex: The null-space equation is the stationarity condition of the quadratic SQP model restricted to affine-feasible directions \(s=Rs_r+Nz\).
When \(H_{nr}=H_{rr}=0\), the curvature model in coordinates \((s_r,s_n)\) is \(\operatorname{diag}(0,H_{nn})\), so only \(H_{nn}\) is updated.
special_cases_latex: If \(m\) is close to \(n\), then \(H_{nn}\in\mathbb R^{(n-m)\times(n-m)}\) is small even when the original problem is large.
For an inequality-constrained problem, the definition applies to the equality constraints augmented by the current working set; the dimension of \(N\) may change when that set changes.
immediate_consequences_latex: If \(H_{nn}\succ0\), the null-space coordinate \(s_n\) is unique for each computed \(s_r\).
The principal linear solves involve the reduced system \(H_{nn}\) and the constraint-related systems \(A(x)R\) and \(R^TA(x)^T\), rather than an unrestricted dense Hessian system.
boundary_notes: The definition does not identify a particular software package, programming interface, globalization rule, or sparse matrix ordering.
Full-row-rank failure requires rank-revealing, regularized, or restoration techniques outside this canonical definition.
A method that merely uses a sparse full Hessian but does not form a null-space reduced model belongs to a nearby sparse SQP family, not necessarily this reduced-Hessian family.

knowledge_statements.slot_contract: State the canonical mathematical definition of the source node, with its domain, quantifiers, notation, and a precise source locator.
knowledge_statements.statement_title: Filter or composite trust-region globalized SQP family
knowledge_statements.ambient_context_latex: Let \(f:\mathbb R^n\to\mathbb R\) and smooth constraints \(c_i:\mathbb R^n\to\mathbb R\) define \(c_i(x)=0\) for \(i\in\mathcal E\) and \(c_i(x)\geq0\) for \(i\in\mathcal I\). At iteration \(k\), let \(g_k=\nabla f(x_k)\), let \(A_{\mathcal E}(x_k)\) and \(A_{\mathcal I}(x_k)\) be the corresponding Jacobian blocks, let \(H_k\in\mathbb S^n\) model Lagrangian curvature, and let \(\Delta_k>0\) be a trust-region radius.
knowledge_statements.scope_note: This is a deterministic, finite-dimensional, smooth SQP definition. It covers two closely related globalization architectures: composite-step trust-region acceptance through a merit-model comparison, and penalty-free filter acceptance through the bicriteria pair consisting of constraint violation and objective value.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex: Define \(m_k(s)=f(x_k)+g_k^Ts+\tfrac12s^TH_ks\) and \[\vartheta(x)=\max\left\{0,\max_{i\in\mathcal E}|c_i(x)|,\max_{i\in\mathcal I}(-c_i(x))\right\}.\] A globalized SQP implementation belongs to this family when it constructs \(s_k=n_k+t_k\), where \(n_k\) seeks linearized feasibility, \(t_k\) reduces \(m_k\) while preserving the feasibility attained by \(n_k\), and \(\|s_k\|\leq\Delta_k\). Its globalization must use at least one of the following defining rules. Composite trust-region rule: accept or reject \(x_k+s_k\) by comparing actual change in a specified merit function with the predicted change in its SQP model, and update \(\Delta_k\) according to that agreement. Filter rule: maintain a set \(\mathcal F\) of mutually nondominating pairs \((\vartheta_j,f_j)\), choose \(\gamma_\vartheta\in(0,1)\), and declare a trial point \(x^+\) acceptable exactly when, for every \((\vartheta_j,f_j)\in\mathcal F\cup\{(\vartheta(x_k),f(x_k))\}\), \[\vartheta(x^+)<(1-\gamma_\vartheta)\vartheta_j\quad\text{or}\quad f(x^+)<f_j-\gamma_\vartheta\vartheta(x^+).\] If the trust-region quadratic model is incompatible, a restoration step instead seeks to reduce \(\vartheta\).
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: A globalized SQP implementation in this family builds a trust-region SQP model and decomposes its trial step into a normal component directed toward linearized feasibility and a tangential component directed toward reduction of the quadratic objective model without losing the achieved linearized feasibility. The complete step must remain in the current trust region. Global acceptance is then controlled either by agreement between actual and predicted reduction in a merit function, or by a penalty-free filter. A filter stores mutually nondominating constraint-violation/objective pairs and accepts a trial point only if it improves constraint violation by the prescribed margin or improves the objective by the prescribed margin relative to every stored pair and the current iterate. When the linearized trust-region problem is incompatible, the family invokes a restoration phase aimed at reducing constraint violation.
assumptions_latex: The objective and constraint functions are smooth enough to form \(g_k\), the constraint Jacobians, and a symmetric Lagrangian-Hessian model \(H_k\).
The normal and tangential components satisfy \(s_k=n_k+t_k\) and \(\|s_k\|\leq\Delta_k\); when the linearized constraints are compatible, both \(n_k\) and \(s_k\) satisfy those constraints.
For filter globalization, \(\gamma_\vartheta\in(0,1)\), and \(\mathcal F\) contains no distinct pairs for which one is no worse in both \(\vartheta\) and \(f\).
For composite merit globalization, the merit function and its model are explicitly specified so that actual and predicted changes are comparable.
knowledge_statements.conclusion_latex: \[s_k=n_k+t_k,\qquad \|s_k\|\leq\Delta_k,\] with acceptance governed either by an actual-versus-predicted merit-model test or by the filter condition \[\forall(\vartheta_j,f_j)\in\mathcal F\cup\{(\vartheta_k,f_k)\}:\quad \vartheta(x_k+s_k)<(1-\gamma_\vartheta)\vartheta_j\ \lor\ f(x_k+s_k)<f_j-\gamma_\vartheta\vartheta(x_k+s_k).\]
equivalent_formulations_latex: The unmarginized filter condition is Pareto nondominance for the bicriteria minimization of \((\vartheta(x),f(x))\); the displayed rule adds a strict acceptance margin.
For equality constraints, a canonical tangential subproblem is to reduce \(\tfrac12t^TH_kt+(g_k+H_kn_k)^Tt\) subject to \(A(x_k)t=0\) and \(\|n_k+t\|\leq\Delta_k\).
special_cases_latex: With only equality constraints, \(\vartheta(x)=\|c(x)\|_\infty\), and a tangential step in \(\ker A(x_k)\) preserves the linearized infeasibility produced by \(n_k\).
A pure filter implementation uses no penalty parameter in its primary acceptance test.
When the linearized constraints and trust region have no common point, restoration may approximately minimize \(\vartheta(x)\) before returning to the SQP model.
immediate_consequences_latex: A filter-acceptable trial point must make a margin-qualified improvement in at least one of feasibility or objective value relative to every comparison pair.

The zero tangential step is feasible whenever the selected normal step itself satisfies the trust-region and linearized constraints, so the composite formulation separates feasibility from model optimization.
Trust-region contraction controls step size, while restoration handles incompatibility that contraction alone cannot cure.
boundary_notes: Filter acceptability alone is not a complete algorithm: model-decrease safeguards, radius updates, restoration termination, and filter insertion rules must also be specified by an implementation.
The definition does not assert global convergence without additional boundedness, regularity, sufficient-decrease, and restoration assumptions.
Line-search SQP globalized solely by a scalar merit function is a neighboring globalized SQP family but is outside the stated filter-or-composite-trust-region focus.

notation.meaning: Quadratic SQP objective model at iteration \(k\).
Tangential step seeking quadratic-model reduction while retaining linearized feasibility.

knowledge_statements.title: Filter-Based SQP Software
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: A filter accepts SQP trials that sufficiently improve objective or feasibility without being dominated, using restoration or step reduction after rejection.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex: Maintain a filter \(\mathcal F_k\) of pairs \((\theta_i,f_i)\), where \(\theta(x)\geq0\) measures constraint violation. After computing an SQP trial point \(x_k^+=x_k+\alpha_kp_k\), accept it only if it is not dominated, with prescribed margins, by any filter entry and it satisfies the implementation's switching or sufficient-decrease test. On acceptance, insert \((\theta(x_k^+),f(x_k^+))\) when required and delete entries it dominates; otherwise reduce \(\alpha_k\) or invoke restoration. Terminate when feasibility and stationarity tests hold. Thus acceptance need not require decrease of one fixed penalty function.
assumptions_latex: \(\theta(x)=0\) exactly when the constraints are satisfied.
Filter margins and switching tests are fixed by the implementation and are strictly positive where required.
knowledge_statements.conclusion_latex: Every accepted trial satisfies the filter acceptance rules or the designated sufficient-decrease switching condition.
knowledge_statements.scope_note: SQP globalization using a dominance filter in objective value and constraint violation.
review_flags: standard_field_rationale: nondominance in objective-violation space is the defining filter-globalization mechanism

knowledge_statements.title: Trust-Region SQP Software
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: Trust-region SQP bounds each step, compares actual with predicted model reduction, and accepts or rejects the trial while adapting the radius.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex:
At \(x_k\), compute an SQP step \(p_k\) satisfying the linearized constraints and \(\lVert D_kp_k\rVert\leq\Delta_k\). For a merit or composite model \(\Phi_k\), form
\[
\rho_k=\frac{\Phi_k(0)-\Phi_k(p_k)}{\Phi_k(0)-m_k(p_k)}
\]
when the denominator is positive. Accept the trial point if \(\rho_k\geq\eta_1\); shrink \(\Delta_k\) after poor agreement and permit enlargement when \(\rho_k\geq\eta_2\) and the step is near the boundary, where \(0<\eta_1<\eta_2<1\). Recompute rejected steps and stop when feasibility and stationarity tolerances hold.
assumptions_latex: The predicted reduction denominator is positive whenever \(\rho_k\) is evaluated.
The step norm scaling \(D_k\) is nonsingular and the trust radius satisfies \(\Delta_k>0\).
knowledge_statements.conclusion_latex: Trial acceptance and trust-radius updates are determined by the agreement ratio and fixed thresholds.
knowledge_statements.scope_note: SQP globalization by a trust-region bound and actual-to-predicted reduction ratio.

enrichment_metadata.review_comment: The algorithm kind fits the container, but the cited basic trust-region section is not an inspectable constrained-SQP specialization. Requiring every step to satisfy the linearized constraints needs an explicit compatibility assumption or a specified composite-step/relaxation mechanism; otherwise such a step may not exist within the trust region.

knowledge_statements.title: Hybrid Globalization SQP Software
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: A hybrid SQP solver switches between specified globalization modes when their acceptance or failure triggers fire, while sharing the current primal-dual and model state.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex: Let \(s_k\) denote a globalization mode from a finite set containing at least two of line search, trust region, filter, and restoration. Compute the SQP trial according to mode \(s_k\), evaluate feasibility, objective or merit change, and model agreement, and accept only when that mode's stated test holds. If its rejection or model-failure trigger occurs, change \(s_k\) according to a fixed transition rule, transfer the current primal-dual iterate and compatible model data, and compute a new trial. After acceptance, update derivatives, multipliers, curvature, and mode state. Stop only when common feasibility and stationarity tolerances are satisfied.
assumptions_latex: Every mode has explicit acceptance, rejection, and transition predicates.
Mode transitions preserve a well-defined current primal-dual iterate.
knowledge_statements.conclusion_latex: Each accepted iterate is certified by the active mode's acceptance test, and every switch follows the prescribed transition rule.
knowledge_statements.scope_note: SQP software switching among line-search, trust-region, filter, or restoration mechanisms.

notation.meaning: trial SQP step generated in the active mode
